pages.title: Objectives
pages.page_title: U1 Objectives

units.heading: Objectives

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The purpose of New Zealand's student instructions is to contribute to New Zealand's sustainable economic development by:

children.label: a
children.text: facilitating the entry of genuine students, with a focus on attracting and developing students who have the skills and talent New Zealand needs;

children.label: b
children.text: increasing global connectedness;

children.label: c
children.text: supporting the sustainable growth of export education capability;

children.label: d
children.text: earning foreign exchange; and

children.label: e
children.text: strengthening New Zealand education, while managing risk to New Zealand and maintaining social cohesion.

units.heading: Persons requiring a student visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A person must obtain a student visa in order to undertake study or training in New Zealand, unless they are:

children.label: a
children.text: a New Zealand citizen; or

children.label: b
children.text: the holder of a residence class visa; or

children.label: c
children.text: the holder of a student visa; or

children.label: d
children.text: the holder of a limited visa granted for the express purpose of attending a programme of study or training; or

children.label: e
children.text: the holder of any other type of temporary entry class visa whose conditions have been varied to authorise the holder to undertake a programme of study in New Zealand; or

children.label: f
children.text: covered by the provisions of U2.5.

units.heading: When a student visa is not required

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa or variation of conditions is not required in order to undertake:

children.label: a
children.text: in order to undertake any training (other than an apprenticeship or a cadetship) provided by an employer as part of the normal conditions of employment offered to the holder of a work visa, other than a work visa granted under a Working Holiday Scheme; or

children.label: b
children.text: to undertake one or more courses of study or training of not more than three calendar months’ duration in total per visa stay conditions, or in each 12 month period if the visa stay conditions is valid for a minimum of 24 months; or

children.label: c
children.text: where V2.35 applies.

pages.title: Summary

units.heading: Summary

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless otherwise specified, to be granted a student visa to attend a course of more than three months, applicants must:

children.label: i
children.text: have an offer of a place in an approved course with an education provider in New Zealand that meets student visa requirements (see U3.5 and U5.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: be exempted from or have paid course fees; and

children.label: iii
children.text: have a guarantee of accommodation (see U3.15); and

children.label: iv
children.text: meet the conditions set out in E3.20; and

children.label: v
children.text: not be the holder of a current visitor visa granted under Guardians accompanying students to New Zealand instructions (see V3.100).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All applicants must meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for:

children.label: i
children.text: lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa as set out at E4; and

children.label: ii
children.text: bona fide applicants as set out at E5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: health and character as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have not completed, or will not be completing the course of study endorsed on their student visa and who wish to change their course of study and/or education provider must:

children.label: i
children.text: meet requirements (a) and (b) above; and

children.label: ii
children.text: meet the requirements set out at U3.40. Note: Applicants who are progressing to further study, for example a student in Year 13 who is progressing to tertiary studies, will not need to meet U3.40.

pages.page_title: U3.5 Offer of a place (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Offer of a place

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Applicants must have an offer of a place with a New Zealand education provider, which shows:

children.label: a
children.text: the name of the course and the minimum time required for completing it; and

children.label: b
children.text: evidence that the course and education provider meet foreign student requirements (see U5); and

children.label: c
children.text: the amount of the fee for the complete course, or, if the course is longer than one year, the annual fee; and

children.label: d
children.text: whether or not the student has to pay course fees and whether the fees are domestic or foreign fees; and

children.label: e
children.text: whether the student is full-time or part-time.

pages.title: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand
pages.page_title: U3.20 Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that they have sufficient funds available to maintain themselves throughout the period of their stay in New Zealand. Evidence may include but is not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: a notice of the award of a full scholarship; or

children.label: ii
children.text: the form Sponsorship for Temporary Entry (INZ 1025) completed by a person who is an acceptable sponsor (see E6.5 and E6.5.1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: funds held by or on behalf of the student; or

children.label: iv
children.text: before the student’s arrival in New Zealand, the form Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) (which covers a stay in New Zealand of up to 12 months) completed by a person who is in the applicant’s home country, in New Zealand or in a third country; or

children.label: v
children.text: after the student's arrival in New Zealand, the form Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) (which covers a stay in New Zealand of up to 12 months) completed by a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: When determining whether a student has sufficient funds to maintain themselves throughout their stay in New Zealand, immigration officers may consider the period of time for which funds have been held by the student and/or their ability to access funds for the period that they are in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking courses lasting less than 36 weeks

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students taking courses lasting less than 36 weeks must provide:

children.label: a
children.text: evidence that funds of the amount required for visitor visa holders have been deposited in New Zealand, or

children.label: b
children.text: a letter from an education provider confirming that accommodation and other living expenses are included as part of a prepaid package.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: This evidence may be sighted after the application has been approved in principle.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking courses lasting 36 weeks or longer

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students taking courses lasting 36 weeks or longer must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that:

children.label: a
children.text: they have NZ$10,000.00 per year available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (travellers' cheques or bank documents in the student's name are acceptable); or

children.label: b
children.text: (if they are citizens of Samoa and Tonga), a written guarantee of maintenance from a relative in New Zealand who is either a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder.

pages.title: Outward travel
pages.page_title: U3.25 Outward travel

units.heading: Outward travel

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Applicants for student visas are required to provide evidence that they have the means while their visa is current to travel to a country to which they have right of entry, in the form of:

children.label: a
children.text: a fully paid travel ticket to any such country; or

children.label: b
children.text: sufficient funds held in New Zealand i.e. funds additional to any sum required under U3.20, to purchase any such ticket; or

children.label: c
children.text: an acceptable form of undertaking by a third party supplied to an immigration officer before arrival in New Zealand; or

children.label: d
children.text: the form Sponsorship for Temporary Entry (INZ 1025) completed by a person who is an acceptable sponsor (see E6.5 and E6.5.1); or

children.label: e
children.text: financial assistance available to the holder under any multilateral or bilateral aid programme administered in New Zealand by a government department or statutory body.

pages.title: Students aged 13 and under and students enrolled in Years 1 to 8
pages.page_title: U3.30 Students aged 13 and under and students enrolled in Years 1 to 8 (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Students aged 13 and under and students enrolled in Years 1 to 8

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Student visas will only be granted to students enrolled in school years 1 to 8 and students aged 13 and under who are enrolled in any other provider (see U3.30.5 below) if they will be living in New Zealand with their legal guardian (see U3.30.1) unless:

children.label: i
children.text: they are domestic students (see U3.35); or

children.label: ii
children.text: they are enrolled in a school hostel (see U3.30.10 below) approved by the Code Administrator; or

children.label: iii
children.text: they are enrolled in Years 7 or 8 of a school, or are aged 11 to 13 years and enrolled in any other provider (see U3.30.5), which has prior programme approval from the Code Administrator.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All visas granted under these instructions are subject to the condition that the holder live with their legal guardian (see U3.30.1) in New Zealand, unless the student visa holder has been granted a variation of conditions under U7.25.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The Code Administrator is the Ministry of Education.

units.heading: Definition of 'legal guardian'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of these instructions a 'legal guardian' is the person with the legal right and responsibility to provide for the care (including education and health) of an international student, and provides for the care of the student in the student's home country. This definition includes the student's biological or adoptive parents, testamentary guardian, or court-appointed guardian.

units.heading: Definition of 'other provider'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of these instructions 'other provider' is a private training establishment.

units.heading: Definition of 'school hostel'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of these instructions 'school hostel' means a hostel as defined in section 2 of the Education Act 1989, and:

children.label: a
children.text: licensed under regulations made under section 144C of the Education Act 1989 (if any); or

children.label: b
children.text: approved and monitored by the Code Administrator, for international students enrolled in Years 1 to 6 of a school, or aged 10 and under and enrolled in any other provider.

pages.title: Definition of 'domestic student'
pages.page_title: U3.35 Definition of 'domestic student' (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Definition of 'domestic student'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of student instructions a 'domestic student' means a domestic student as defined in section 2 of the Education Act 1989. The Ministry of Education holds a complete list of who is considered to be a domestic student for the purpose of fee payment and enrolment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary schooling domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending primary and secondary schools and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue;

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents;

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents;

children.label: d
children.text: People who are for the time being accorded privileges and immunities under the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations or the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, pursuant to the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunity Act 1968, or the Consular Privileges and Immunity Act 1971. Approval for dependent children of diplomatic, consular or official staff to study in New Zealand must be granted by the Protocol Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (see H2.5). Protocol division will also confirm whether fees are payable;

children.label: e
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending primary and secondary schools and are exempt from paying foreign course fees:

children.label: a
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is in New Zealand to study under an exchange programme approved by the New Zealand Government.

children.label: b
children.text: Children whose application for a residence class visa is under consideration and who are the dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand resident visa, or permanent resident visa.

children.label: c
children.text: Children whose application for New Zealand citizenship is under consideration and who are the dependent children of a New Zealand citizen.

children.label: d
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is onshore and the holder of a valid work visa other than those excluded under U8.20.

children.label: e
children.text: Students who have, or dependent children of any person who has, made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009.

children.label: f
children.text: Dependent children of a foreign student enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme in a New Zealand university.

children.label: g
children.text: Dependent children of any person who, during the current calendar year, last ceased to hold a special temporary visa (see H2).

children.label: h
children.text: Students who have entered New Zealand for the purposes of adoption and:

children.label: i
children.text: whose adoption application before the New Zealand Family Court (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student) is supported by the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services and who has a letter from the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services confirming this support; or

children.label: ii
children.text: who are the subject of an Interim Order of Adoption granted by the New Zealand Family Court under section 5 of the Adoption Act 1955 (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student).

children.label: i
children.text: People who are in the custody of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development pursuant to any of the following orders:

children.label: i
children.text: an order, pursuant to sections 78, 101 or 238(1)(d) of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, in favour of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 110 of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, appointing the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development as sole guardian; or

children.label: iii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 33 of the Care of Children Act 2004, whereby a child or young person is placed under the Guardianship of the Family Court or the High Court and the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development is appointed as agent of the court with power and discretion to place the child.

children.label: j
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a NZAID Scholarship.

children.label: k
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a visitor visa granted under V3.115.

children.label: l
children.text: Dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

units.heading: Exchange Students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students who are in New Zealand to study under an exchange scheme approved by the New Zealand Government (see E11.45) are considered to be international students and must attend a primary or secondary school which is a signatory to the Ministry of Education's Code of Practice for Pastoral Care of International Students (see U5.1), or a tertiary institution.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Such students require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa but do not have to pay course fees for foreign students.

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector (see U5.20) and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions or limited visa in order to undertake a course of study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue.

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents.

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents.

children.label: d
children.text: People who are for the time being entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction by or under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunity Act 1968, other than a person referred to in section 10D(2)(d) of that Act, or the Consular Privileges and Immunity Act 1971 who hold a special temporary visa (see H2). Approval for partners and dependent children of diplomatic, consular or official staff to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand must be granted by the Protocol Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (see H2.1). Protocol Division will also confirm whether fees are payable.

children.label: e
children.text: Despite (d) above, the accompanying partners and dependent children aged 21 and over of Diplomatic, Consular or Official staff, who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand, may not be eligible for domestic student status and may be required to pay foreign student fees (see H2.1(b).

children.label: f
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector and are exempt from paying foreign course fees for foreign students:

children.label: a
children.text: Students enrolled for the first time in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme, after 19 April 2005, in any New Zealand university (see U5.20).

children.label: b
children.text: Partners and dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

pages.title: Students who wish to change their course of study and/or education provider
pages.page_title: U3.40 Students who wish to change their course of study and/or education provider (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Students who wish to change their course of study and/or education provider

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A further student visa or variation of conditions, for the purpose of changing course and/or education provider, will only be granted if an immigration officer is satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant meets the student requirements set out at U3.1; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant has not breached their visa conditions as set out at E3.20; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the original student visa would have been granted for the proposed course and/or education provider; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the applicant remains a bona fide applicant (see E5.1).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Factors that an immigration officer may take into consideration when determining (a)(iii) and (a)(iv) above include, but are not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: the time elapsed since the original visa was granted;

children.label: ii
children.text: whether the level and/or subject area of the proposed course are significantly different from the original course; and

children.label: iii
children.text: any relevant information held about the previous application(s) including advice from the original issuing branch (see E7.1.1).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have received NZAID funding within the two years prior to their application to change course and/or education provider being made, must also provide evidence that NZAID supports the change of course or education provider and that any scholarship continues.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Applicants who wish to change their course and/or education provider may provide evidence of payment of course fees after the application has been approved in principle.

units.heading: Fee-paying foreign students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students must meet the full costs of their programme of study, whether by themselves or with the help of family members, friends, home governments, or others (such as the United Nations).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: This category includes students studying at private training establishments, such as those offering English language courses.

pages.title: Private training establishments

units.heading: Private training establishments

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Private training establishments may offer course places to foreign students provided the course meets the criteria for one in which a foreign student may be enrolled in accordance with the provisions of the Education Act 1989 (see sections 232 and 233).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The definition of a foreign student is contained in section 159 of the Education Act 1989.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The primary requirements for satisfying sections 232 and 233 of the Education Act 1989, in respect of courses of study are that:

children.label: i
children.text: the private training establishment providing the course has been registered by the New Zealand Qualifications Authority, and

children.label: ii
children.text: the course is an approved course, and

children.label: iii
children.text: the private training establishment has been accredited to provide the course.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: These requirements apply to all courses with the exception of those courses that are exempt as provided for in section 232(2) of the Education Act 1989.

units.heading: Tertiary institutions (Universities, Polytechnics, Colleges of Education, Wananga)

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Tertiary institutions may offer course places to foreign students provided the course meets the criteria for one in which a foreign student may be enrolled in accordance with the provisions of the Education Act 1989 (see section 224(7)–(12)).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The definition of a foreign student is contained in section 159 of the Education Act 1989.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The primary requirements for section 224(7)–(12) of the Education Act 1989 in respect of courses of study that are or are likely to be longer than 3 months are that:

children.label: i
children.text: the course is an approved course, and

children.label: ii
children.text: the institution is accredited to provide the course, and

children.label: iii
children.text: the effect of the enrolment is not to deprive a domestic or exempt student of a place at the institution or on the course of study unless the student is an NZAID assisted student or the place has been established by the Council of the institution for a foreign student and its continued availability is dependent on the fees payable by the foreign student enrolled in it.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Polytechnics also include institutes of technology, technical institutes or community colleges established before 1 January 1991.

pages.title: Courses of study lasting longer than 3 months
pages.page_title: U6.1 Courses of study lasting longer than 3 months (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Courses of study lasting longer than 3 months

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: People who require a visa to visit New Zealand and who wish to come to New Zealand to study full-time for a period longer than 3 months, must hold a student visa.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Potential students who are nationals of countries to whom a visitor visa waiver applies (see E2.1.5) may enter New Zealand as visitors and apply for a student visa after their arrival.

units.heading: Definition of 'full-time study'

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For private training establishments full-time study is generally considered to be enrolment in a course of study that requires attendance for a minimum of 20 hours per week.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: For other tertiary institutions enrolment in at least 3 papers, or equivalent, per semester is indicative of full-time study.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Any course of study that does not meet (a) or (b) above is usually considered to be part-time (see U7.20).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The final decision on whether or not a student may be considered to be undertaking full-time study rests with immigration officers. If necessary, immigration officers should confirm whether or not the proposed course of study could be considered to be full-time or not by consulting the Ministry of Education, Wellington which has a qualifications database and/or the education provider itself.

pages.title: Distance education (correspondence) students
pages.page_title: U6.5 Distance education (correspondence) students

units.heading: Distance education (correspondence) students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Distance education students may attend the New Zealand education provider at which they are enrolled so that they can undertake practical study or sit examinations, or for any other educational reason that requires their presence at the provider.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Students who apply to come to New Zealand for more than 3 months for this purpose may be granted a student visa for the necessary period.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Students who wish to come to New Zealand for this purpose for less than 3 months may do so on a visitor visa.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Immigration officers should sight evidence that distance students who apply for student or visitor visas:

children.label: i
children.text: are distance education students; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have an offer of a place at an education provider (if they are in New Zealand for more than 3 months); and

children.label: iii
children.text: have paid the tuition fees or are exempt from having to pay them.

units.heading: Variations to work visas and visitor visas to allow study

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of work or visitor visas must apply for a variation of conditions to their current visa if:

children.label: i
children.text: they wish to undertake a course of study longer than 3 months (see also U7.20.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: it is inappropriate for some other reason to apply for a student visa.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Immigration officers with Schedule 3 delegations and above may give a special direction varying the conditions of the current visa to allow study, provided that they sight evidence that the applicant has:

children.label: i
children.text: an offer of a place at an education provider; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a signed training agreement with an Industry Training Organisation; and

children.label: iii
children.text: paid the course fees or is exempt from having to pay them.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Holders of visitor visas granted under the special category V3.100 may only be given a special direction varying conditions to allow part-time study.

pages.title: Further temporary visas
pages.page_title: U6.25 Further temporary visas (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Further temporary visas

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Temporary entry class visa holders may be granted further temporary entry class visas in the following situations:

children.label: a
children.text: If an applicant for a student visa was not required to provide evidence of health and character before arriving in New Zealand, and must now do so (see A4 and A5), but is unable to while their existing visa is current, officers with Schedule 3 delegations and above have discretion to grant a temporary visa for an interim period of a maximum of 3 months, provided that the applicant is:

children.label: i
children.text: in New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: holds another type of temporary entry class visa.

children.label: b
children.text: When the student visa requirements in paragraph (a) above have been met, a further visa may be granted for the full period requested without the applicant having to make a further application.

children.label: c
children.text: If a student visa holder has applied for a residence class visa while lawfully in New Zealand, immigration officers may grant a further student visa for 3 months provided that:

children.label: i
children.text: a final decision on the residence class visa application is unlikely before the current student visa expires; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the mandatory requirements for a further visa are met.

pages.title: Currency of student visas
pages.page_title: U6.30 Currency of student visas

units.heading: Currency of student visas

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Student visas may be granted for the following periods:

children.label: a
children.text: for holders of full scholarships and fees scholarships who do not meet the requirements under U6.35, the period of the student's award (up to a maximum of 4 years); and

children.label: i
children.text: for fee-paying foreign students who do not meet the requirements under U6.35, the period for which the student has paid the tuition fees (up to a maximum of 4 years); and

children.label: ii
children.text: for fee-paying foreign students and full scholarship students, who meet the requirements under U6.35, for the length of their programme of study, regardless of the period for which they have paid tuition fees (up to a maximum of 4 years).

children.label: b
children.text: If the programme of study is based on the New Zealand academic year, the visa may be granted for the academic year for which the student has paid, to expire on 31 March of the following year.

children.label: c
children.text: If the programme of study lasts for less than one year, or can begin at any time during the year, the visa may be granted to expire no more than two months after the period for which the student has paid.

units.heading: Visas for the length of a course of study

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Student visas may be granted for the length of a student's course of study, regardless of the period for which they have paid their course fees, where:

children.label: i
children.text: the student has an offer of a place with an education provider with which INZ has a Memorandum of Understanding for the Students Online Initiative which allows for the grant of visas for the length of course of study, and

children.label: ii
children.text: the education provider supports the grant of a length of course visa.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of the education provider's support to grant a length of course visa must be provided. Acceptable evidence may include written confirmation from the education provider, such as an offer of a place which indicates the education provider's support.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: All applicants for visas for the length of their course (if that course is for more than 12 months) must, at the time of application for their visa provide a fully completed Medical and Chest X-ray Certificate (INZ 1007). All applicants for visas for the length of their course (if that course is for more than 24 months) must, at the time of application for their visa, provide police certificates from their country of citizenship and from any country in which they have lived for 5 or more years since attaining the age of 17 years (see A4 and A5).

units.heading: Conditions of student visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All visas for school students must state primary, intermediate, or secondary studies.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the student has provided acceptable guarantees of funds and onward travel, the visa must state: ‘Evidence of financial support not required’ and ‘return/onward ticket not required’.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: All student visas must allow multiple journeys.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Two currency dates must be specified on student visas:

children.label: i
children.text: the date on which the visa expires; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the date on which the permission to travel expires.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions allowing the student to work (see U13).

units.heading: Student visa holders liable for deportation

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa holder who breaches any of the conditions of their visa (in particular those relating to attendance, employment, and living with their legal guardian) may become liable for deportation (see E3.60).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Where the student is required to live with a legal guardian (see U3.30) and that legal guardian becomes liable for deportation, the student will also become liable for deportation (see E3.60).

pages.title: Students undertaking employment
pages.page_title: U7.15 Students undertaking employment (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Students undertaking employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students may apply for a variation of conditions to work:

children.label: i
children.text: to fulfil practical course requirements (see U7.15.1); and/or

children.label: ii
children.text: for up to 20 hours in any given week during the academic year, and during any holidays within the academic year if they are an eligible student (see U7.15.5); and/or

children.label: iii
children.text: full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period if they are an eligible student (see U7.15.10); and/or

children.label: iv
children.text: on completing their course (see WD).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Students are not permitted to:

children.label: i
children.text: work in self-employment; or

children.label: ii
children.text: provide commercial sexual services; or

children.label: iii
children.text: act as an operator of a New Zealand business of prostitution; or

children.label: iv
children.text: invest in a business of prostitution (see E7.40).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: U7.15(a) does not apply to New Zealand Agency for International Development (NZAID) supported students; see U11.1 for NZAID supported students work entitlements.

units.heading: Course requirements

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of student visas may apply for a variation of conditions to allow them to work in order to fulfil a requirement of practical experience for their course.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If satisfied that practical experience is a course requirement, an immigration officer may grant a student visa with the conditions varied to allow employment. Note: If an applicant's main activity will be work, they must apply for a work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where the variation of conditions is sought in conjunction with an application for a student visa, the fee for a variation of conditions may be waived.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The variation of conditions will be effective only for the period of the student's current student visa and ceases on completion of the relevant course of study.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: The variation of conditions may be applied for at any time the visa is current or when applying for a further student visa.

units.heading: Twenty hours in any given week for eligible students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of student visas may be granted a variation of conditions to allow them to work during the academic year, and during any holidays within the academic year for up to 20 hours in any given week if they are:

children.label: i
children.text: undertaking a full-time course of study, at a private training establishment or tertiary institution (see U5.15 - U5.20), of at least two academic years’ duration; or

children.label: ii
children.text: undertaking a full-time course of study in New Zealand, culminating in a New Zealand qualification that would qualify for points under the Skilled Migrant Category (see SM14); or

children.label: iii
children.text: undertaking a full-time tertiary course of study of at least one academic year's duration as part of an approved tertiary student exchange scheme (see E11.45); or

children.label: iv
children.text: undertaking a full-time, full secondary school year course of study in Years 12 or 13, provided they have written permission from their school and written parental consent; or

children.label: v
children.text: engaged in a full-time course of study of at least six months’ duration at a private training establishment or tertiary institution (see U5.15 - U5.20); and

children.label: b1
children.text: an immigration officer is satisfied that the primary purpose of the course of study is to develop English language skills; and

children.label: b2
children.text: the student can provide a certificate (no more than 2 years old at the time the application is lodged) from the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) which shows an overall band score of at least 5.0 in the IELTS (General or Academic Module).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of an offer of employment is not required.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where the variation of conditions is sought in conjunction with an application for a student visa, the fee for a variation of conditions may be waived.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The variation of conditions will be effective only for the period of the student's current student visa and ceases on completion of the relevant course of study.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: The variation of conditions may be applied for at any time the visa is current or when applying for a further student visa.

units.heading: Christmas-New Year holiday period

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of student visas may be granted a variation of conditions to allow them to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period at the end of each academic year, provided they are undertaking a full-time course of study of 12 months or more duration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Any school student who does not meet the requirements set out at U7.15.5a(iv) is not eligible to work under the provisions of U7.15.10. Note: Written permission from the school is not required for students who are 18 years of age or over, under the provisions of U7.15.10.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence of an offer of employment is not required.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Where the variation of conditions is sought in conjunction with an application for a student visa, the fee for a variation of conditions may be waived.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: The variation of conditions will be effective only for the period of the student's current student visa.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: The variation of conditions may be applied for at any time the visa is current or when applying for a further student visa.

pages.page_title: U7.20 Part-time study

units.heading: Part-time study

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: People who are not considered to be full-time students (see U6.1.1) may apply for a visitor visa with a variation of conditions to allow study on a part-time basis.

units.heading: Programmes of study lasting up to 9 months

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: People outside New Zealand may apply for and be granted a variation of conditions to allow study on a part-time basis for a maximum of 9 months from the date of their arrival in New Zealand, provided that they are enrolled in a part-time programme of study certified as one that complies with foreign student requirements (see U3.1) and lasts no more than 9 months, and comply with visitor requirements (see V2.1).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: People already in New Zealand may apply for and be granted a visitor visa with a variation of conditions to allow study on a part-time basis for the balance of their stay up to a maximum of 9 months from the date of their arrival.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If study is the main reason for the applicant being in New Zealand, immigration officers must decline any application to undertake part-time programmes of study lasting longer than 9 months, unless the officers are satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the application has special merit that warrants the application being approved, and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant will comply with the conditions of their visa.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Immigration officers must be satisfied that applicants who wish to undertake part-time programmes of study lasting up to 9 months after their date of arrival:

children.label: i
children.text: are enrolled in and have paid the fees for such a programme of study; and

children.label: ii
children.text: are able to satisfy the standard visitor requirements (see V2.1).

units.heading: Students completing their programme of study

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Despite U7.20 above and U6.1.1, a person who is: may be considered to be a full-time student and may be granted a student visa for the remaining duration of their programme of study if they can meet student requirements (see U3.1).

children.label: i
children.text: in their final semester of a programme of study in New Zealand, that is of at least 2 academic years’ duration; or

children.label: ii
children.text: in their final semester of a programme of study in New Zealand, culminating in a New Zealand qualification at level four or higher on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: To be eligible for a student visa under these instructions, applicants must not previously have been granted a visa under these instructions.

pages.page_title: U7.25 Temporary exemption from the requirement to live with a legal guardian in New Zealand

units.heading: Temporary exemption from the requirement to live with a legal guardian in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students who are required to live with their legal guardian in New Zealand (see U3.30) may apply for a variation of conditions to their student visa to temporarily exempt them from this requirement.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A variation of conditions will only be granted where an immigration officer is satisfied that an emergency exists that requires the legal guardian to temporarily return to their home country.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The applicant must provide evidence that:

children.label: i
children.text: an emergency exists that requires the legal guardian to temporarily return to their home country; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the education provider has approved the alternative caregiving arrangements, consistent with its obligations under the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the legal guardian has purchased a return travel ticket.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The variation of conditions may be granted for the period of time required, up to a maximum of four weeks.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Any failure of the legal guardian to return to New Zealand within the approved period may result in the student visa holder becoming liable for deportation (see U7.10).

units.heading: Partners and dependent children of diplomatic, consular or official staff

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Partners (see E4.1.20) and dependent children (see E4.1.10) of diplomatic, consular or official staff who wish to study in New Zealand must obtain approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade Protocol Division (see H2).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If a diplomatic tour of duty terminates during the academic year, and the partner or dependent child ceases to hold a special temporary visa (see H2.1), they must obtain a student visa to continue studying.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade Protocol Division will confirm whether partners and dependent children of diplomatic personnel, who themselves hold a special temporary visa, are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all course fees. If they are regarded as domestic students, this will continue until the end of the calendar year in which the diplomat's tour of duty terminates, and they are not required to provide evidence of having paid course fees in order to complete the academic year.

pages.title: Partners and dependent children of military visa holders
pages.page_title: U8.15 Partners and dependent children of military visa holders (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Partners and dependent children of military visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Partners (see E4.1.20) and dependent children (see E4.1.10) of military visa holders may be granted student visas for the same period as the military visa held, or deemed to be held, by the applicant's partner or parent.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Applicants meet temporary entry class requirements for lodging an application as set out at E4, bona fide applicants as set out at E5, and health and character requirements as set out at A4.5 and A5.5, but are exempt from:

children.label: i
children.text: providing evidence of enrolment; and

children.label: ii
children.text: providing guarantees of accommodation and maintenance; and

children.label: iii
children.text: meeting onward travel requirements.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children of military visa holders are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) in the following respects:

children.label: i
children.text: for the purpose of all course fees for the period of secondment; and

children.label: ii
children.text: until the end of the calendar year in which their partner or parent completes their posting in New Zealand.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The student visas granted must be current for the period of enrolment or until the parent or partner holding a military visa departs, whichever occurs first.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: If the student wishes to continue studying in New Zealand after their parent or partner departs, they must meet the requirements under the immigration instructions for a temporary visa and obtain one accordingly.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Before granting a student visa an immigration officer must be satisfied that the applicant's partner or parent:

children.label: i
children.text: holds a military visa; or

children.label: ii
children.text: is eligible to be granted a military visa; or

children.label: iii
children.text: is deemed to be granted a military visa.

units.heading: Partners of military visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Partners of military visa holders must prove to the satisfaction of an immigration officer that:

children.label: i
children.text: they are living together with their partner in a genuine and stable partnership at the time their application is made; and

children.label: ii
children.text: they comply with the minimum requirements for recognition of partnerships (see E4.1.20 and F2.15); and

children.label: iii
children.text: their partner supports the application.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of the applicant’s relationship to the military visa holder must be provided in the following forms:

children.label: i
children.text: evidence of their relationship with their partner, and

children.label: ii
children.text: evidence that demonstrates they are living together with that partner in a genuine and stable partnership at the time their application is made (F2.20 sets out the types of evidence that are required).

pages.title: Partners and dependent children of holders of work visas
pages.page_title: U8.20 Partners and dependent children of holders of work visas (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Partners and dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Crew of foreign chartered fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all course fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for partners and dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the partner or parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the partner or parent (see W2.15).

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent/s meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is $33,675 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent/s meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent/s:

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent/s do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent/s and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: note1

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The only programme of study refugee or protection status claimants or their partner or dependent children may undertake without the need for a student visa is an English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL) programme of study at a New Zealand technical institute.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Permission to attend an ESOL programme of study may be given by special direction varying the conditions of the claimant's temporary entry class visa, and an immigration officer must inform the claimant of the special direction by letter.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Claimants not eligible for a student visa under these provisions may apply under the provisions for student visas at U3, but must meet all the requirements, including payment of the appropriate fee.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Claimants are exempt from paying the immigration levy (see A6.11.20).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: For information on the eligibility of refugee or protection status claimants for other temporary visas (see E8.10).

units.heading: Claimants' school-aged children

blocks.label: a

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Applications must be made in the prescribed manner (see E4.50); but an appropriately delegated immigration officer may waive:

children.label: i
children.text: the application fee; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the requirement to produce evidence of funds or sponsorship; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the requirement to produce evidence of travel tickets or onward travel arrangements.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Claimants' school-aged children are exempt from paying the immigration levy.

units.heading: New Zealand Agency for International Development- (NZAID-) supported students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: An NZAID-funded student is a student who receives funding from the New Zealand Government under the following schemes:

children.label: i
children.text: Aotearoa Scholarships;

children.label: ii
children.text: New Zealand Development Scholarships (formerly known as Study Awards Schemes and Postgraduate Scholarship Schemes);

children.label: iii
children.text: Short-Term Training Awards;

children.label: iv
children.text: Commonwealth Scholarships;

children.label: v
children.text: New Zealand Regional Development Scholarships (formerly known as Pacific Regional Awards);

children.label: vi
children.text: English Language Training for Officials (ELTO).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The objective of NZAID Scholarships and Awards is to promote human resource development. NZAID scholars are generally required to return to their home countries immediately on completion of their studies (for at least 2 years) to contribute to economic and social progress through the transfer of knowledge and skills.

units.heading: New Zealand Agency for International Development- (NZAID-) supported students undertaking employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: NZAID-supported students may be granted a variation of conditions to their student visa to allow them to work during the academic year, and during any holidays within the academic year for up to 20 hours in any given week, if NZAID and the relevant education provider both support the application in writing and the work is:

children.label: i
children.text: a compulsory requirement to fulfil practical experience for their course of study; or

children.label: ii
children.text: related to their postgraduate course of study.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: NZAID-supported students may be granted a variation of conditions to their student visa to allow them to work during the Christmas-New Year holiday period if it is a course requirement and NZAID supports the application in writing.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: NZAID-supported students on Aotearoa Scholarships may be granted a variation of conditions to their student visa to allow them to work for up to 20 hours in any given week during the academic year, and during any holidays within the academic year and full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: NZAID scholars may be granted work visas at the completion of their studies for qualification-related work experience for the minimum time needed to complete practical work requirements. Note: NZAID-supported senior medical and pharmacy students may be granted work visa for their internship/registration year.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: NZAID-supported students are not permitted to:

children.label: i
children.text: work in self-employment; or

children.label: ii
children.text: provide commercial sexual services; or

children.label: iii
children.text: act as an operator of a New Zealand business of prostitution; or

children.label: iv
children.text: invest in a business of prostitution (see E7.40).

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Any NZAID-supported student, or their partner or dependent children may only be granted a visa for New Zealand in the 2 year period following completion of the NZAID student's scholarship, with written approval from NZAID (with the exception of a work visa to complete course requirements or a short-term visitor visa).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: See WF4.5 for work instructions for partners of holders of student visas who are NZAID-supported.

pages.title: Guardians accompanying students to New Zealand
pages.page_title: V3.100 Guardians accompanying students to New Zealand

units.heading: Guardians accompanying students to New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A person may be granted a visitor visa under these instructions for the purpose of living with and caring for, a foreign fee paying student in New Zealand, if they are the legal guardian of a person who:

children.label: i
children.text: is the holder of a current student visa and is 17 years old or younger; or

children.label: ii
children.text: is the holder of a current student visa and is enrolled in school years 1-13.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Only one legal guardian of the holder of a student visa will be granted a visa under these instructions at any one time.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: To be granted a visa under these instructions applicants must meet the requirements for bona fide applicants as set out at E5.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If a student visa is granted to more than one person in a particular family, only one legal guardian of those holders of student visas will be granted a visa under these instructions at any one time during the validity of those student visas.

units.heading: Deportation liability

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The holder of a visa granted under these instructions will become liable for deportation if the student whom the applicant accompanied to New Zealand becomes liable for deportation.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All visas granted under these instructions are subject to the condition that the holder lives in New Zealand with the student they are accompanying, unless the student’s visa has been varied as set out at U7.25. If this condition is breached, the visa holder may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: If the presence of a student's legal guardian in New Zealand (and that legal guardian's support for the student) is material to the decision of a New Zealand education provider to enrol that student, any failure of the legal guardian (see V3.100.5) to live with and care for that student (either through withdrawal of their support or absence from New Zealand) may result in the holder of the student visa being made liable for deportation (see U7.10).

units.heading: Definition of 'legal guardian'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of these instructions, a 'legal guardian' is:

children.label: a
children.text: the person with the legal right and responsibility to provide for the care (including education and health) of an international student. This includes the student's biological or adoptive parents, testamentary guardian, or court-appointed guardian; and

children.label: b
children.text: the person who provides for the care of the student in the student's home country.

units.heading: Length of permitted stay

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Successful applicants under these instructions will be granted a multiple entry visitor visa valid for the same period as the student visa held by the student they are accompanying.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: If the student visa holder is not enrolled in school years 1-13 and turns 18 years of age during the validity of their student visa, the legal guardian may only be granted a visitor visa valid until the day before the student turns 18.

units.heading: Grant of further visitor visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Further visitor visas may be granted to the applicant, if they are accompanying the student and continuing to meet the requirements of V3.100, upon application and payment of the fee.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: In determining whether further visas may be granted, immigration officers must take into consideration whether, during the currency of a previous visa granted under these instructions, the legal guardian lived with and cared for the student on the basis of whose stay in New Zealand they were granted a visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The length of permitted stay for further visitor visas should be granted in line with V3.100.10 above.

units.heading: Funds for maintenance in New Zealand

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Applicants for a visitor visa under these instructions must have funds of at least NZ$1,000 per month for maintenance and accommodation, or NZ$400 per month if their accommodation has been prepaid.

units.heading: Evidence of onward travel arrangements

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence of travel tickets, onward travel arrangements or sufficient funds for the purchase of onward travel tickets (see V2.25).

units.heading: Health and character requirements

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Applicants must meet health and character requirements for temporary entry as set out in A4 and A5.

units.heading: Guardians who wish to work or study once in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Guardian visa holders are not eligible for:

children.label: i
children.text: the grant of a work visa under Accredited Employer work visa instructions or Specific Purpose or Event instructions; or

children.label: ii
children.text: the grant of a student visa under Student instructions.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Guardian visa holders who wish to work or study may apply for a variation of conditions to their visitor visa to allow for part-time work between the hours of 9:30am and 2:30pm Monday to Friday (inclusive), or part time study.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applications for variations of conditions by guardians must meet general work requirements (with the exception of the labour market test requirement) or student requirements.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Variations of conditions will not be granted if the proposed employer (including any person associated with the employer who is able to influence the recruitment, employment or supervision of workers of that employer) does not have a history of compliance with employment standards or is currently included on a list of non-compliant employers maintained by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (see W2.10.15, Appendix 10 and Appendix 18).

units.heading: Work visa holders dismissed during a trial period

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of current work visas who: may be granted a visitor visa for up to three months.

children.label: i
children.text: hold a visa subject to the condition that they may only take up employment with a specific employer; and

children.label: ii
children.text: had provision for a trial period of up to 90 days under section 67A of the Employment Relations Act 2000 included in their employment agreement; and

children.label: iii
children.text: have been notified within the duration of the trial period that they are to be dismissed; and

children.label: iv
children.text: have not previously been the principal applicant in a successful application under these instructions;

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Applicants for a visitor visa under these instructions must:

children.label: i

children.label: ii
children.text: provide evidence of travel tickets, onward travel arrangements or sufficient funds for the purchase of onward travel tickets (see V2.25);

children.label: iii
children.text: meet health and character requirements for temporary entry (see A4 and A5).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children may also be included in the principal applicant's visitor visa application.

pages.title: Definition of 'bona fide applicant'
pages.page_title: E5.1 Definition of 'bona fide applicant'

units.heading: Definition of 'bona fide applicant'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A bona fide applicant for temporary entry is a person who:

children.label: a
children.text: genuinely intends a temporary stay in New Zealand for a lawful purpose; and

children.label: b
children.text: in the opinion of an immigration officer is not likely:

children.label: i
children.text: to remain in New Zealand unlawfully; or

children.label: ii
children.text: to breach the conditions of any visa granted; or

children.label: iii
children.text: to be unable to leave or be deported from New Zealand (see E5.10).

pages.title: Processing an application
pages.page_title: E7.1 Processing an application

units.heading: Processing an application

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Immigration officers must be satisfied that applicants for temporary entry and entry permission have met the health and character requirements for temporary entry (see A4 and A5); and the requirements for the particular category of visa; and that they are bona fide applicants (see E5).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Applicants may be required to present further documents, a medical examination or attend an interview.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: An immigration officer determining a temporary application from a person who is offshore must have no reason to believe that person would be refused entry permission, if the visa is granted.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: In making the determination set out at (c) above, the immigration officer should take into account:

children.label: i
children.text: for applications subject to temporary entry instructions, the most recent version of the relevant Border Entry instructions.

children.label: ii
children.text: for applications subject to restricted temporary entry instructions, the relevant Border Entry instructions in effect at the time the application was made.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: An immigration officer making the determination set out at (c) above is not required to consider whether the applicant is likely to be granted entry permission as an exception to instructions.

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matter) Regulations 2010 regs 10, 11, 12, 13

units.heading: Checking for information from previous applications

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Immigration officers should check previous applications for relevant information, and if necessary contact the branches or offices that processed the previous applications, especially if applicants are applying outside their home country.

units.heading: Referral to appropriate receiving office

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: When assessing applications lodged at an office other than the designated receiving office for the applicant's country of nationality, immigration officers should refer to Z5 and where necessary refer the application to the appropriate receiving office before making a decision on the application.

pages.title: Considering an application
pages.page_title: E7.10 Considering an application

units.heading: Considering an application

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Immigration officers must first determine applications for temporary entry in accordance with:

children.label: i
children.text: the requirements of the Immigration Act 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the temporary entry instructions in force at the time the application is made or any general instructions given by the chief executive; and

children.label: iii
children.text: any relevant special directions.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If an application fails to meet the requirements of temporary entry instructions, officers must then consider all the circumstances of the application to see if an exception to temporary entry instructions is justified, taking into account the objectives of temporary entry instructions and the situation and purpose of the applicant. See also section E7.32 which refers to the grant of a limited visa or the imposition of bonds.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Officers must be satisfied that applicants for temporary entry are bona fide applicants (see E5.1 and E5.10).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If applicants do not respond within the specified time to a request from an immigration officer for further information, evidence or documents, or an interview, the application will be assessed on the relevant information available to INZ at the time.

units.heading: Requesting a passport for applications made online

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Where an application is made on an electronic form in accordance with Regulation 23A or 23AA of the Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission and Related Matters) Regulations 2010, the applicant may be required to provide their original passport or travel document to an immigration officer if they are:

children.label: i
children.text: outside of New Zealand at the time they make the application; and

children.label: ii
children.text: not subject to a visa waiver to travel to New Zealand (E2.1); and

children.label: iii
children.text: not a person intending to travel on a People’s Republic of China passport.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: An automated system may request an original passport or travel document from a person to whom E7.10.1(a) above applies.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Regardless of E7.10.1(a), an immigration officer determining the application may request any applicant to supply their passport or travel document.

see_also: See also Immigration Act 2009 s 28 and the Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010, Reg 23A and Reg 23AA.

pages.title: Effect of provisions of the Prostitution Reform Act 2003
pages.page_title: E7.40 Effect of provisions of the Prostitution Reform Act 2003

units.heading: Effect of provisions of the Prostitution Reform Act 2003

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: No temporary entry visa or entry permission may be granted in contravention of the Prostitution Act 2003. That Act provides that:

children.label: a
children.text: No visa may be granted to a person on the basis that the person;

children.label: i
children.text: has provided, or intends to provide, commercial sexual services; or

children.label: ii
children.text: has acted, or intends to act as an operator of a business of prostitution; or

children.label: iii
children.text: has invested, or intends to invest, in a business of prostitution.

children.label: b
children.text: It is a condition of every temporary entry class visa granted under the Immigration Act 2009 that the holder of the visa may not, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: provide commercial sexual services; or

children.label: ii
children.text: act as an operator of a New Zealand business of prostitution; or

children.label: iii
children.text: invest in a New Zealand business of prostitution.

children.label: c
children.text: A temporary entry class visa holder may become liable for deportation if the holder does any of the things listed in (b) above.

blocks.label: p2
blocks.text: E7.40 applies to all visas and permits held and all requirements and conditions imposed under the Immigration Act 1987 or the Immigration Act 2009, whether granted or imposed before or after the commencement of the 2009 Act.

pages.title: Conditions to which holders of temporary entry class visas are subject
pages.page_title: E3.15 Conditions to which holders of temporary entry class visas are subject

units.heading: Conditions to which holders of temporary entry class visas are subject

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The holder of a temporary entry class visa may:

children.label: i
children.text: visit New Zealand consistent with the conditions of the visa, for any lawful purpose; or Examples: Holidaying, sightseeing, family and social visits, amateur sport, business consultations, undergoing medical treatment.

children.label: ii
children.text: work in New Zealand, or within the exclusive economic zone of New Zealand, only if the conditions of the visa allow, and only consistently with those conditions; or

children.label: iii
children.text: study in New Zealand, only if the conditions of the visa allow, and only consistently with those conditions; or

children.label: iv
children.text: undertake the express purpose for which they were approved to travel to New Zealand, and only consistently with the express purpose conditions, if granted a limited visa.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: An interim visa holder may work, study or visit only as authorised by the terms or conditions of their interim visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Subject to any special direction to the contrary, every visitor, work and interim and limited visa that is not an interim or limited visa granted for the purpose of study, is subject to the following conditions:

children.label: i
children.text: at all times during the currency of the visa to be in New Zealand, the holder has sufficient funds available for the holder’s maintenance in New Zealand, or a current approved sponsorship undertaking (see E6); and

children.label: ii
children.text: at all times during the currency of the visa to be in New Zealand, the holder has the means to travel to a country to which the holder has a right of entry, such means to be in the form of:

children.label: b1
children.text: a fully paid travel ticket to any such country; or

children.label: b2
children.text: sufficient funds held in New Zealand by or on behalf of or in trust for the holder to purchase any such ticket; or

children.label: b3
children.text: a current approved sponsorship (see E6).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Every temporary entry class visa is subject to the condition that the holder comply with:

children.label: i
children.text: any order made under section 70 of the Health Act 1956; and

children.label: ii
children.text: any instruction from a Medical Officer of Health which relates to a notifiable or quarantinable disease.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Despite E7.10(a)(ii), (d) above applies to all visas granted (including in an immigration control area) on and after 18 March 2020.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: A notifiable or quarantinable disease is any disease referred to in Part 1 and Part 3, respectively, of Schedule 1 of the Health Act 1956.

units.heading: Remote work for visitor visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: It is a condition of all visitor visas that the holder may undertake remote work in New Zealand.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Remote work undertaken by a visitor visa holder is work that:

children.label: i
children.text: is not for a New Zealand employer; and

children.label: ii
children.text: does not offer goods or services in New Zealand in exchange for gain or reward from either New Zealand businesses or persons in New Zealand (see W2.2.1); and

children.label: iii
children.text: does not require the visitor to be physically present at a place of work in New Zealand (see W2.2.5).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Remote work is not, in and of itself, a lawful purpose for visiting New Zealand (see V2.1.1 and E5.5), however intending to work remotely while undertaking another purpose (such as sightseeing or visiting family) is acceptable.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Visitors who wish to undertake work in New Zealand that does not meet the requirements of (b) above must apply for a work visa, unless they are:

children.label: i
children.text: granted a visitor visa under a special category (see V3) that allows a specific type of work under that category; or

children.label: ii
children.text: undertaking an activity for gain or reward listed at W2.2.1(a).
