pages.title: Deportation liability of temporary entry class visa holder for cause
pages.page_title: E3.60 Deportation liability of temporary entry class visa holder for cause

units.heading: Deportation liability of temporary entry class visa holder for cause

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A temporary entry class visa holder is liable for deportation if the Minister determines that there is sufficient reason to deport the temporary entry class visa holder (see (e) below).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The person has 14 days from the date of service of the deportation liability notice to give good reason why deportation should not proceed.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: E3.60 (b) above does not apply if:

children.label: i
children.text: the person is the holder of a limited visa; or

children.label: ii
children.text: the Minister determines that the person is an excluded person.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: A temporary visa holder or interim visa holder who is liable for deportation under E3.60 may, no later than 28 days after the date of service of the deportation liability notice, appeal to the Tribunal on humanitarian grounds against his or her liability for deportation.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: For the purposes of E3.60 (a) above, sufficient reason includes, but is not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: breach of conditions of the person’s visa;

children.label: ii
children.text: criminal offending;

children.label: iii
children.text: other matters relating to character;

children.label: iv
children.text: concealment of relevant information in relation to the person’s application for a visa;

children.label: v
children.text: a situation where the person’s circumstances no longer meet the rules or criteria under which the visa was granted.

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: (See section D2) for deportation procedures.)

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Examples: the holder of a student visa who fails to attend their place of study without reasonable excuse, or the holder of a visitor visa who undertakes employment without authority.

units.heading: Diplomatic, Consular, and Official staff, and accompanying dependants

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The Protocol Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) must confirm all applications for visas made by people who are for the time being accorded privileges and immunities under the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations or the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, pursuant to the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunity Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunity Act 1971.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: MFAT Protocol Division also advises on the validity period and the type (Diplomatic, Consular or Official) of visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Visas granted may allow travel to New Zealand on multiple journeys.

pages.title: Accompanying dependants
pages.page_title: H2.1 Accompanying dependants

units.heading: Accompanying dependants

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Accompanying partners or dependent children are eligible for a special temporary visa (Diplomatic, Consular or Official) upon confirmation from MFAT Protocol Division.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children aged 21 and over are not normally eligible for a special temporary visa except in their own right, unless confirmation of eligibility is provided by MFAT Protocol Division.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Accompanying partners or dependent children who have been granted a special temporary visa and who wish to work or study in New Zealand must also obtain approval from MFAT Protocol Division.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Accompanying partners or dependent children aged 21 and over, who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand may be liable for foreign student fees and should contact MFAT Protocol Division to establish whether or not they are eligible for domestic student status or would attract foreign student fees.

pages.title: Students undertaking employment
pages.page_title: U7.15 Students undertaking employment (07/02/2011)

units.heading: Students undertaking employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students may apply for a variation of conditions to work:

children.label: i
children.text: to fulfil practical course requirements (see U7.15.1); and/or

children.label: ii
children.text: for up to 20 hours in any given week during the academic year, and during any holidays within the academic year if they are an eligible student (see U7.15.5); and/or

children.label: iii
children.text: full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period if they are an eligible student (see U7.15.10); and/or

children.label: iv
children.text: on completing their course (see WD).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Students are not permitted to:

children.label: i
children.text: work in self-employment; or

children.label: ii
children.text: provide commercial sexual services; or

children.label: iii
children.text: act as an operator of a New Zealand business of prostitution; or

children.label: iv
children.text: invest in a business of prostitution (see E7.40).

units.heading: Course requirements

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of student visas may apply for a variation of conditions to allow them to work in order to fulfil a requirement of practical experience for their course.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If satisfied that practical experience is a course requirement, an immigration officer may grant a student visa with the conditions varied to allow employment. Note: If an applicant's main activity will be work, they must apply for a work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where the variation of conditions is sought in conjunction with an application for a student visa, the fee for a variation of conditions may be waived.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The variation of conditions will be effective only for the period of the student's current student visa and ceases on completion of the relevant course of study.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: The variation of conditions may be applied for at any time the visa is current or when applying for a further student visa.

units.heading: Twenty hours in any given week for eligible students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of student visas may be granted a variation of conditions to allow them to work during the academic year, and during any holidays within the academic year for up to 20 hours in any given week if they are:

children.label: i
children.text: undertaking a full-time course of study, at a private training establishment or tertiary institution (see U5.15 - U5.20), of at least two academic years’ duration; or

children.label: ii
children.text: undertaking a full-time course of study in New Zealand, culminating in a New Zealand qualification that would qualify for points under the Skilled Migrant Category (see SM14); or

children.label: iii
children.text: undertaking a full-time tertiary course of study of at least one academic year's duration as part of an approved tertiary student exchange scheme (see E11.45); or

children.label: iv
children.text: undertaking a full-time, full secondary school year course of study in Years 12 or 13, provided they have written permission from their school and written parental consent; or

children.label: v
children.text: engaged in a full-time course of study of at least six months’ duration at a private training establishment or tertiary institution (see U5.15 - U5.20); and

children.label: b1
children.text: an immigration officer is satisfied that the primary purpose of the course of study is to develop English language skills; and

children.label: b2
children.text: the student can provide a certificate (no more than 2 years old at the time the application is lodged) from the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) which shows an overall band score of at least 5.0 in the IELTS (General or Academic Module).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of an offer of employment is not required.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where the variation of conditions is sought in conjunction with an application for a student visa, the fee for a variation of conditions may be waived.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The variation of conditions will be effective only for the period of the student's current student visa and ceases on completion of the relevant course of study.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: The variation of conditions may be applied for at any time the visa is current or when applying for a further student visa.

units.heading: Christmas-New Year holiday period

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of student visas may be granted a variation of conditions to allow them to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period at the end of each academic year, provided they are undertaking a full-time course of study of 12 months or more duration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Any school student who does not meet the requirements set out at U7.15.5a(iv) is not eligible to work under the provisions of U7.15.10. Note: Written permission from the school is not required for students who are 18 years of age or over, under the provisions of U7.15.10.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence of an offer of employment is not required.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Where the variation of conditions is sought in conjunction with an application for a student visa, the fee for a variation of conditions may be waived.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: The variation of conditions will be effective only for the period of the student's current student visa.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: The variation of conditions may be applied for at any time the visa is current or when applying for a further student visa.

pages.page_title: U11 New Zealand Aid Programme-supported students (07/02/2011)

units.heading: New Zealand Aid Programme-supported students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A New Zealand Aid Programme-supported student is a student who receives funding from the New Zealand Government under the following schemes:

children.label: i
children.text: New Zealand Development Scholarships (formerly known as Study Awards Schemes and Postgraduate Scholarship Schemes);

children.label: ii
children.text: Short-Term Training Awards;

children.label: iii
children.text: Commonwealth Scholarships;

children.label: iv
children.text: New Zealand Regional Development Scholarships (formerly known as Pacific Regional Awards);

children.label: v
children.text: English Language Training for Officials (ELTO).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The objective of the scholarships and awards is for candidates to gain knowledge and skills in specific subject areas that will assist in the development of their home country. Awardees are required to return to their home country for at least two years after the completion of their scholarship/award to apply these new skills and knowledge in government, civil society or private business organisations.

units.heading: New Zealand Aid Programme (NZAP)-supported students undertaking employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: New Zealand Aid Programme (NZAP)-supported students may be granted conditions on their student visa to allow them to work during the academic year for up to 20 hours per week, during any holidays within the academic year for up to 20 hours per week, and full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: NZAP scholars may be granted work visas at the completion of their studies for qualification-related work experience for the minimum time needed to complete practical work requirements. Note: NZAP-supported senior medical and pharmacy students may be granted work visa for their internship/registration year.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: NZAP-supported students are not permitted to:

children.label: i
children.text: work in self-employment; or

children.label: ii
children.text: provide commercial sexual services; or

children.label: iii
children.text: act as an operator of a New Zealand business of prostitution; or

children.label: iv
children.text: invest in a business of prostitution (see E7.40).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Any NZAP-supported student, or their partner or dependent children may only be granted a visa for New Zealand in the two-year period following completion of the NZAP student's scholarship, with written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (with the exception of a work visa to complete course requirements or a short-term visitor visa).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: See WF4.5 for work instructions for partners of holders of student visas who are NZAP-supported.

pages.title: Definition of 'domestic student'
pages.page_title: U3.35 Definition of 'domestic student' (07/02/2011)

units.heading: Definition of 'domestic student'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of student instructions a 'domestic student' means a domestic student as defined in section 2 of the Education Act 1989. The Ministry of Education holds a complete list of who is considered to be a domestic student for the purpose of fee payment and enrolment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary schooling domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending primary and secondary schools and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue;

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents;

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents;

children.label: d
children.text: People who are for the time being accorded privileges and immunities under the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations or the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, pursuant to the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunity Act 1968, or the Consular Privileges and Immunity Act 1971. Approval for dependent children of diplomatic, consular or official staff to study in New Zealand must be granted by the Protocol Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (see H2.5). Protocol division will also confirm whether fees are payable;

children.label: e
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending primary and secondary schools and are exempt from paying foreign course fees:

children.label: a
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is in New Zealand to study under an exchange programme approved by the New Zealand Government.

children.label: b
children.text: Children whose application for a residence class visa is under consideration and who are the dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand resident visa, or permanent resident visa.

children.label: c
children.text: Children whose application for New Zealand citizenship is under consideration and who are the dependent children of a New Zealand citizen.

children.label: d
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is onshore and the holder of a valid work visa other than those excluded under U8.20.

children.label: e
children.text: Students who have, or dependent children of any person who has, made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009.

children.label: f
children.text: Dependent children of a foreign student enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme in a New Zealand university.

children.label: g
children.text: Dependent children of any person who, during the current calendar year, last ceased to hold a special temporary visa (see H2).

children.label: h
children.text: Students who have entered New Zealand for the purposes of adoption and:

children.label: i
children.text: whose adoption application before the New Zealand Family Court (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student) is supported by the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services and who has a letter from the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services confirming this support; or

children.label: ii
children.text: who are the subject of an Interim Order of Adoption granted by the New Zealand Family Court under section 5 of the Adoption Act 1955 (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student).

children.label: i
children.text: People who are in the custody of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development pursuant to any of the following orders:

children.label: i
children.text: an order, pursuant to sections 78, 101 or 238(1)(d) of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, in favour of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 110 of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, appointing the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development as sole guardian; or

children.label: iii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 33 of the Care of Children Act 2004, whereby a child or young person is placed under the Guardianship of the Family Court or the High Court and the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development is appointed as agent of the court with power and discretion to place the child.

children.label: j
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand Aid Programme Scholarship.

children.label: k
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a visitor visa granted under V3.115.

children.label: l
children.text: Dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

units.heading: Exchange Students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students who are in New Zealand to study under an exchange scheme approved by the New Zealand Government (see E11.45) are considered to be international students and must attend a primary or secondary school which is a signatory to the Ministry of Education's Code of Practice for Pastoral Care of International Students (see U5.1), or a tertiary institution.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Such students require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa but do not have to pay course fees for foreign students.

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector (see U5.20) and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions or limited visa in order to undertake a course of study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue.

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents.

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents.

children.label: d
children.text: People who are for the time being entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction by or under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunity Act 1968, other than a person referred to in section 10D(2)(d) of that Act, or the Consular Privileges and Immunity Act 1971 who hold a special temporary visa (see H2). Approval for partners and dependent children of diplomatic, consular or official staff to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand must be granted by the Protocol Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (see H2.1). Protocol Division will also confirm whether fees are payable.

children.label: e
children.text: Despite (d) above, the accompanying partners and dependent children aged 21 and over of Diplomatic, Consular or Official staff, who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand, may not be eligible for domestic student status and may be required to pay foreign student fees (see H2.1(b)).

children.label: f
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector and are exempt from paying foreign course fees for foreign students:

children.label: a
children.text: Students enrolled for the first time in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme, after 19 April 2005, in any New Zealand university (see U5.20).

children.label: b
children.text: Partners and dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

pages.title: Students who wish to change their study conditions
pages.page_title: U3.40 Students who wish to change their study conditions

units.heading: Students who wish to change their study conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A further student visa or variation of conditions, for the purpose of changing programme of study, education provider and/or study location, will only be granted if an immigration officer is satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant meets the student requirements set out at U3.1; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant has not breached their visa conditions as set out at E3.20; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the original student visa would have been granted for the proposed programme of study, education provider, and/or study location; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the applicant remains a bona fide applicant (see E5.1); and

children.label: v
children.text: the applicant is not seeking to vary conditions to enable them to enrol in a lower-level programme of study or to enrol with a different education provider (see E3.26.10).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Factors that an immigration officer may take into consideration when determining (a)(iii) and (a)(iv) above include, but are not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: the time elapsed since the original visa was granted;

children.label: ii
children.text: whether the level and/or subject area of the proposed programme of study are significantly different from the original programme of study; and

children.label: iii
children.text: any relevant information held about the previous application(s) including advice from the original issuing branch (see E7.1.1).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have received New Zealand Scholarship funding within the two years prior to their application to change programme of study and/or education provider being made, must also provide evidence that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade supports the change of programme of study or education provider and that any scholarship continues.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Applicants who wish to change their programme of study and/or education provider may provide evidence of payment of tuition fees after the application has been approved in principle.

units.heading: Primary and secondary schools (state and integrated)

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Primary and secondary schools are accredited by the Ministry of Education for admitting fee-paying foreign students and may offer them places, within any limits imposed by that Ministry on levels and subjects, after all New Zealand domestic and New Zealand Aid Programme scholarship students have been placed.

blocks.label: b

units.heading: Tertiary institutions (Universities, Polytechnics, Colleges of Education, Wananga)

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Tertiary institutions may offer course places to foreign students provided the course meets the criteria for one in which a foreign student may be enrolled in accordance with the provisions of the Education Act 1989 (see section 224(7)–(12)).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The definition of a foreign student is contained in section 159 of the Education Act 1989.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The primary requirements for section 224(7)–(12) of the Education Act 1989 in respect of courses of study that are or are likely to be longer than 3 months are that:

children.label: i
children.text: the course is an approved course, and

children.label: ii
children.text: the institution is accredited to provide the course, and

children.label: iii
children.text: the effect of the enrolment is not to deprive a domestic or exempt student of a place at the institution or on the course of study unless the student is an New Zealand Aid Programme scholarship student or the place has been established by the Council of the institution for a foreign student and its continued availability is dependent on the fees payable by the foreign student enrolled in it.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Polytechnics also include institutes of technology, technical institutes or community colleges established before 1 January 1991.

Training may involve placement with a New Zealand government department, a private training establishment, or at a tertiary institution. Trainees are provided with entitlements for accommodation and maintenance whilst on this scheme.

blocks.label: b

units.heading: New Zealand Aid Programme (NZAP)-supported students undertaking employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: New Zealand Aid Programme (NZAP)-supported students may be granted conditions on their student visa to allow them to work during the academic year for up to 20 hours per week, during any holidays within the academic year for up to 20 hours per week, and full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: NZAP scholars may be granted work visas at the completion of their studies for qualification-related work experience for the minimum time needed to complete practical work requirements. Note: NZAP-supported senior medical and pharmacy students may be granted work visa for their internship/registration year.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: NZAP-supported students are not permitted to:

children.label: i
children.text: work in self-employment; or

children.label: ii
children.text: provide commercial sexual services; or

children.label: iii
children.text: act as an operator of a New Zealand business of prostitution; or

children.label: iv
children.text: invest in a business of prostitution (see E7.40).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Any NZAP-supported student, or their partner or dependent children may only be granted a visa for New Zealand in the two-year period following completion of the NZAP student's scholarship, with written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (with the exception of a work visa to complete course requirements or, if the applicant is outside New Zealand, a short-term visitor visa).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: See WF4.5 for work instructions for partners of holders of student visas who are NZAP-supported.

pages.title: Student visas and permission to study for child victims of people trafficking
pages.page_title: U10.5 Student visas and permission to study for child victims of people trafficking

units.heading: Student visas and permission to study for child victims of people trafficking

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Child victims of people trafficking wishing to study at primary or secondary school may be granted student visas valid for 12 months.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The applicant must have certification from the New Zealand Police that they are believed to be a victim of people trafficking.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applications must be made in the prescribed manner (see E4.50) but an appropriately delegated immigration officer may waive:

children.label: i
children.text: the application fee; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the requirement to produce evidence of funds or sponsorship.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Student visas granted under this category may be endorsed with conditions that allow study as a domestic student at any primary or secondary school.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: - A child victim of people trafficking is a person who was under the age of 18 at the time they were identified as a victim of people trafficking. - A child victim may be in New Zealand unaccompanied, or may be a victim of people trafficking together with their parent(s).

units.heading: When a student visa is not required

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa or variation of conditions is not required:

children.label: a
children.text: for work visa holders to undertake any course of study, or other training, authorised by their employer as part of their employment; or

children.label: b
children.text: for all temporary visa holders, to undertake one or more courses of study of not more than three calendar months’ duration in total per visa stay conditions, or in each 12 month period if the visa stay conditions is valid for a minimum of 24 months; or

children.label: c
children.text: where V2.35 applies.

pages.title: Summary

units.heading: Summary

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless otherwise specified, to be granted a student visa to attend a course of more than three months, applicants must:

children.label: i
children.text: have an offer of a place or, if returning to continue a course of study, a confirmation of enrolment in an approved course with an education provider in New Zealand that meets student visa requirements (see U3.5, U3.10, and U5.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: be exempted from or have paid course fees; and

children.label: iii
children.text: if aged under 18, meet accommodation requirements (see U3.15); and

children.label: iv
children.text: have fulfilled the purpose and met the conditions for any previous or current temporary visas held as set out in E3.15 and E3.20; and

children.label: v
children.text: meet the conditions set out in E3.20; and

children.label: vi
children.text: not be the holder of a current visitor visa granted under Guardians accompanying students to New Zealand instructions (see V3.100).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All applicants must meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for:

children.label: i
children.text: lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa as set out at E4; and

children.label: ii
children.text: bona fide applicants as set out at E5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: health and character as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have not completed, or will not be completing the course of study endorsed on their student visa and who wish to change their course of study and/or education provider must:

children.label: i
children.text: meet requirements (a) and (b) above; and

children.label: ii
children.text: meet the requirements set out at U3.40.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Applicants who are progressing to further study, for example a student in Year 13 who is progressing to tertiary studies, will not need to meet U3.40.

pages.title: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand
pages.page_title: U3.20 Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand (25/07/2011)

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that they have sufficient funds available to maintain themselves throughout the period of their stay in New Zealand.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence may include but is not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: a notice of the award of a full scholarship; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a completed Sponsorship for Temporary Entry (INZ 1025) form (see U3.20.5); or

children.label: iii
children.text: a completed Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form, which covers a stay in New Zealand for the length of the visa (see U3.20.10); or

children.label: iv
children.text: funds held by or on behalf of the student (see U3.20.20).

units.heading: Sponsorship

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A sponsor for a student visa application must be an acceptable sponsor (see E6.5) and be either:

children.label: i
children.text: a natural person who is a relative or a friend of the applicant; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an organisation or government agency (an individual must be nominated as the authorised contact).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Sponsors must satisfy an immigration officer that they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet sponsorship obligations); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are sponsoring.

units.heading: Financial Undertaking

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Before the student’s arrival in New Zealand, a financial undertaking may be provided by a third party.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the third party is a person, they must be a relative or a friend of the applicant.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If the third party is not a person, they must nominate an individual as an authorised contact.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The third party providing the financial undertaking must satisfy an immigration officer they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet their financial obligations as set out on the Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are supporting.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Where a third party wishes to continue providing a financial undertaking for the student’s subsequent onshore student visa applications, they may do so if they continue to meet (d).

units.heading: Determining whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To determine whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide, immigration officers may consider:

children.label: a
children.text: the relationship between the applicant and the sponsor or third party;

children.label: b
children.text: any previous breaches of financial obligations set out in undertakings;

children.label: c
children.text: the number of student visa applications they are currently supporting;

children.label: d
children.text: the period of time for which funds have been held by the sponsor or third party; and

children.label: e
children.text: the student’s ability to access funds from the sponsor or third party while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds held by or on behalf of the student

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Where funds are held by or on behalf of the student, immigration officers must be satisfied that the funds are from a genuine source and are genuinely available for the purposes of the applicant’s maintenance requirements.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: When determining whether a student has sufficient funds to maintain themselves throughout their stay in New Zealand, immigration officers may consider the period of time for which funds have been held by the student and the student’s ability to access funds while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking courses lasting less than 36 weeks

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students taking courses lasting less than 36 weeks must provide:

children.label: a
children.text: evidence that funds of the amount required for visitor visa holders are held by or on behalf of the student; or

children.label: b
children.text: a letter from an education provider confirming that accommodation and other living expenses are included as part of a prepaid package.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: This evidence may be sighted after the application has been approved in principle.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking courses lasting 36 weeks or longer

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students taking courses lasting 36 weeks or longer must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that:

children.label: a
children.text: they have NZ$10,000.00 per year available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (travellers' cheques or bank documents in the student's name are acceptable); or

children.label: b
children.text: (if they are citizens of Samoa and Tonga) a written guarantee of maintenance from a relative in New Zealand who is either a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder.

pages.title: Definition of 'domestic student'
pages.page_title: U3.35 Definition of 'domestic student' (25/07/2011)

units.heading: Definition of 'domestic student'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of student instructions a 'domestic student' means a domestic student as defined in section 2 of the Education Act 1989. The Ministry of Education holds a complete list of who is considered to be a domestic student for the purpose of fee payment and enrolment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary schooling domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending primary and secondary schools and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue;

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents;

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents;

children.label: d
children.text: People who are for the time being accorded privileges and immunities under the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations or the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, pursuant to the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunity Act 1968, or the Consular Privileges and Immunity Act 1971. Approval for dependent children of diplomatic, consular or official staff to study in New Zealand must be granted by the Protocol Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (see H2.5). Protocol division will also confirm whether fees are payable;

children.label: e
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending primary and secondary schools and are exempt from paying foreign course fees:

children.label: a
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is in New Zealand to study under an exchange programme approved by the New Zealand Government.

children.label: b
children.text: Children whose application for a residence class visa is under consideration and who are the dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand resident visa, or permanent resident visa.

children.label: c
children.text: Children whose application for New Zealand citizenship is under consideration and who are the dependent children of a New Zealand citizen.

children.label: d
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is onshore and the holder of a valid work visa other than those excluded under U8.20.

children.label: e
children.text: Students who have, or dependent children of any person who has, made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009.

children.label: f
children.text: Dependent children of a foreign student enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme in a New Zealand university.

children.label: g
children.text: Dependent children of any person who, during the current calendar year, last ceased to hold a special temporary visa (see H2).

children.label: h
children.text: Students who have entered New Zealand for the purposes of adoption and:

children.label: i
children.text: whose adoption application before the New Zealand Family Court (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student) is supported by the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services and who has a letter from the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services confirming this support; or

children.label: ii
children.text: who are the subject of an Interim Order of Adoption granted by the New Zealand Family Court under section 5 of the Adoption Act 1955 (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student).

children.label: i
children.text: People who are in the custody of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development pursuant to any of the following orders:

children.label: i
children.text: an order, pursuant to sections 78, 101 or 238(1)(d) of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, in favour of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 110 of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, appointing the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development as sole guardian; or

children.label: iii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 33 of the Care of Children Act 2004, whereby a child or young person is placed under the Guardianship of the Family Court or the High Court and the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development is appointed as agent of the court with power and discretion to place the child.

children.label: j
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand Aid Programme Scholarship.

children.label: k
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a visitor visa granted under V3.115.

children.label: l
children.text: Dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

children.label: m
children.text: Children granted a student visa under U10.5.

units.heading: Exchange Students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students who are in New Zealand to study under an exchange scheme approved by the New Zealand Government (see E11.45) are considered to be international students and must attend a primary or secondary school which is a signatory to the Ministry of Education's Code of Practice for Pastoral Care of International Students (see U5.1), or a tertiary institution.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Such students require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa but do not have to pay course fees for foreign students.

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector (see U5.20) and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions or limited visa in order to undertake a course of study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue.

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents.

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents.

children.label: d
children.text: People who are for the time being entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction by or under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunity Act 1968, other than a person referred to in section 10D(2)(d) of that Act, or the Consular Privileges and Immunity Act 1971 who hold a special temporary visa (see H2). Approval for partners and dependent children of diplomatic, consular or official staff to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand must be granted by the Protocol Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (see H2.1). Protocol Division will also confirm whether fees are payable.

children.label: e
children.text: Despite (d) above, the accompanying partners and dependent children aged 21 and over of Diplomatic, Consular or Official staff, who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand, may not be eligible for domestic student status and may be required to pay foreign student fees (see H2.1(b)).

children.label: f
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector and are exempt from paying foreign course fees for foreign students:

children.label: a
children.text: Students enrolled for the first time in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme, after 19 April 2005, in any New Zealand university (see U5.20).

blocks.label: p2
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

units.heading: Offer of a place

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Applicants must have an offer of a place with a New Zealand education provider, which shows:

children.label: a

children.label: b

children.label: c

children.label: d

children.label: e
children.text: whether or not the student has to pay course fees and whether the fees are domestic or foreign fees; and

children.label: f
children.text: whether the student is full-time (see U6.1.1) or part-time (see U7.20).

pages.title: Status of education providers and courses
pages.page_title: U5.1 Status of education providers and courses (25/07/2011)

units.heading: Status of education providers and courses

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All education providers must certify in their offers of places to foreign students (see U3.5) that the course of study offered complies with foreign student requirements for different kinds of education providers (see U5.5 - U5.20).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All education providers offering places to foreign students must be signatories to the Ministry of Education's Code of Practice for Pastoral Care of International Students.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Any queries on the status of courses offered by primary and secondary schools (state, integrated or private) and private training establishments should be referred to the Approvals and Accreditations Service, New Zealand Qualifications Authority, PO Box 160, Wellington.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Immigration New Zealand (INZ) may suspend the processing of applications for student visas for study at an education provider where at least one of the following applies:

children.label: i
children.text: the offered course of study does not comply with foreign student requirements as set out in U5.5 to U5.20;

children.label: ii
children.text: the education provider is not complying with its obligations under the Immigration Act, immigration regulations, or immigration instructions;

children.label: iii
children.text: INZ has been informed by education agencies that the education provider is not complying with its obligations under the Education Act and education regulations.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Before a decision is made to suspend the processing of student visas, the following will be taken into account:

children.label: i
children.text: evidence of the non-compliance; and

children.label: ii
children.text: reasons for the non-compliance; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the duration, frequency, and severity of the non-compliance.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: INZ may resume the processing of student visas if it is satisfied that the education provider is complying with its obligations.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Despite (d), where an applicant fails to meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for health, character or bona fide applicants, the application may be declined.

pages.page_title: U6.20 Variations to work visas and visitor visas to allow study (25/07/2011)

units.heading: Variations to work visas and visitor visas to allow study

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless U2.5(a) applies, holders of work or visitor visas must apply for a variation of conditions to their current visa, if:

children.label: i
children.text: they wish to undertake a course of study longer than 3 months (see also U7.20.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: it is inappropriate for some other reason to apply for a student visa.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Immigration officers with Schedule 3 delegations and above may give a special direction varying the conditions of the current visa to allow study, provided that they sight evidence that the applicant has:

children.label: i
children.text: an offer of a place at an education provider; and

children.label: ii
children.text: paid the course fees or is exempt from having to pay them.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Holders of visitor visas granted under the special category V3.100 may only be given a special direction varying conditions to allow part-time study.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If the variation of conditions is applied for at the same time as the work or visitor visa then a separate fee for the variation of conditions is not required.

pages.title: Partners and dependent children of holders of work visas
pages.page_title: U8.20 Partners and dependent children of holders of work visas (25/07/2011)

units.heading: Partners and dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Crew of foreign chartered fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2); or

children.label: v
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all course fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for partners and dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the partner or parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the partner or parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.15 to A5.25.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Despite (a) (v) partners and dependent children of Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) Job Search visa holders may be granted student visas if the related SMC application was under consideration on or before 24 July 2011.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent/s meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is $33,675 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent/s meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent/s:

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent/s do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent/s and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

pages.title: Further temporary visas
pages.page_title: U6.25 Further temporary visas

units.heading: Further temporary visas

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Temporary entry class visa holders may be granted further temporary entry class visas in the following situations:

children.label: a
children.text: If an applicant for a student visa was not required to provide evidence of health and character before arriving in New Zealand, and must now do so (see A4 and A5), but is unable to while their existing visa is current, officers with Schedule 3 delegations and above have discretion to grant a temporary visa for an interim period of a maximum of 3 months, provided that the applicant is:

children.label: i
children.text: in New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: holds another type of temporary entry class visa.

children.label: b
children.text: When the student visa requirements in paragraph (a) above have been met, a further visa may be granted for the full period requested without the applicant having to make a further application.

children.label: c
children.text: If a student visa holder has applied for a residence class visa while lawfully in New Zealand, immigration officers may grant a further student visa for 3 months provided that:

children.label: i
children.text: a final decision on the residence class visa application is unlikely before the current student visa expires; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the mandatory requirements for a further visa are met.

pages.page_title: U11 New Zealand Aid Programme-supported students (07/11/2011)

units.heading: New Zealand Aid Programme-supported students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A New Zealand Aid Programme-supported student is a student who receives funding from the New Zealand Government under the following schemes:

children.label: i
children.text: New Zealand Development Scholarships;

children.label: ii
children.text: Short-Term Training Awards;

children.label: iii
children.text: Commonwealth Scholarships;

children.label: iv
children.text: New Zealand Regional Development Scholarships;

children.label: v
children.text: English Language Training for Officials;

children.label: vi
children.text: New Zealand Pacific Scholarships;

children.label: vii
children.text: New Zealand Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) Scholars Award.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The objective of the scholarships and awards is for candidates to gain knowledge and skills in specific subject areas that will assist in the development of their home country. Awardees are required to return to their home country for at least two years after the completion of their scholarship/award to apply these new skills and knowledge in government, civil society or private business organisations.

pages.title: Students holding a New Zealand scholarship undertaking employment
pages.page_title: U11.1 Students holding a New Zealand scholarship undertaking employment

units.heading: Students holding a New Zealand scholarship undertaking employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: New Zealand scholarship students may be granted conditions on their student visa to allow them to work during the academic year for up to 25 hours per week, during any holidays within the academic year for up to 25 hours per week, and full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period unless they are studying under the following schemes:

children.label: i
children.text: Short Term Training Scholarships; or

children.label: ii
children.text: English Language Training for Officials Scholarships Note: New Zealand scholarship students may also be eligible for full-time work rights during scheduled vacation periods. See U13.15.10

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: With the exception of the schemes listed under (a), New Zealand scholarship students may be granted work visas at the completion of their programmes of study for qualification-related work experience for the minimum time needed to complete practical work requirements. Note: New Zealand scholarship senior medical and pharmacy students may be granted a work visa for their internship/registration year.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: New Zealand scholarship students are not permitted to:

children.label: i
children.text: work in self-employment; or

children.label: ii
children.text: provide commercial sexual services; or

children.label: iii
children.text: act as an operator of a New Zealand business of prostitution; or

children.label: iv
children.text: invest in a business of prostitution (see E7.40).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Any New Zealand scholarship student, or their partner or dependent children, may only be granted a visa for New Zealand in the two-year period following completion of the student's scholarship, with written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or Education New Zealand (with the exception of a work visa to complete programme of study requirements or, if the applicant is outside New Zealand, a short-term visitor visa).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Despite (d) above, where a New Zealand scholarship student has completed a Short Term Training Scholarships or English Language Training for Officials of twelve months or less in duration, the New Zealand scholarship student, their partner or dependent children may only be granted a visa for New Zealand in the one year period following completion of their scholarship or training, with the written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or Education New Zealand (with the exception of a work visa to complete programme of study requirements or, if the applicant is outside New Zealand, a short-term visitor visa).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: See WF4.5 for work instructions for partners of holders of student visas who are holding a New Zealand scholarship.

pages.title: Definition of 'domestic student'
pages.page_title: U3.35 Definition of 'domestic student' (07/11/2011)

units.heading: Definition of 'domestic student'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of student instructions a 'domestic student' means a domestic student as defined in section 2 of the Education Act 1989. The Ministry of Education holds a complete list of who is considered to be a domestic student for the purpose of fee payment and enrolment.

blocks.label: p2
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending primary and secondary schools and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue;

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents;

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents;

children.label: d
children.text: People who are for the time being accorded privileges and immunities under the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations or the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, pursuant to the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunity Act 1968, or the Consular Privileges and Immunity Act 1971. Approval for dependent children of diplomatic, consular or official staff to study in New Zealand must be granted by the Protocol Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (see H2.5). The Protocol division will also confirm whether fees are payable;

children.label: e
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

blocks.label: p3
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending primary and secondary schools and are exempt from paying foreign course fees:

children.label: a
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is in New Zealand to study under an exchange programme approved by the New Zealand Government.

children.label: b
children.text: Children whose application for a residence class visa is under consideration and who are the dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand resident visa, or permanent resident visa.

children.label: c
children.text: Children whose application for New Zealand citizenship is under consideration and who are the dependent children of a New Zealand citizen.

children.label: d
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is onshore and the holder of a valid work visa other than those excluded under U8.20.

children.label: e
children.text: Students who have, or dependent children of any person who has, made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009.

children.label: f
children.text: Dependent children of a foreign student enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme in a New Zealand university.

children.label: g
children.text: Dependent children of any person who, during the current calendar year, last ceased to hold a special temporary visa (see H2).

children.label: h
children.text: Students who have entered New Zealand for the purposes of adoption and:

children.label: i
children.text: whose adoption application before the New Zealand Family Court (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student) is supported by the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services and who has a letter from the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services confirming this support; or

children.label: ii
children.text: who are the subject of an Interim Order of Adoption granted by the New Zealand Family Court under section 5 of the Adoption Act 1955 (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student).

children.label: i
children.text: People who are in the custody of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development pursuant to any of the following orders:

children.label: i
children.text: an order, pursuant to sections 78, 101 or 238(1)(d) of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, in favour of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 110 of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, appointing the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development as sole guardian; or

children.label: iii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 33 of the Care of Children Act 2004, whereby a child or young person is placed under the Guardianship of the Family Court or the High Court and the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development is appointed as agent of the court with power and discretion to place the child.

children.label: j
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand Aid Programme Scholarship.

children.label: k
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a visitor visa granted under V3.115.

children.label: l
children.text: Dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

children.label: m
children.text: Children granted a student visa under U10.5.

children.label: n
children.text: Students who are in New Zealand to study under an exchange scheme approved by the Ministry of Education (see E11.45).

blocks.label: p4
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector (see U5.20) and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions or limited visa in order to undertake a course of study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue.

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents.

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents.

children.label: d
children.text: People who are for the time being entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction by or under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunity Act 1968, other than a person referred to in section 10D(2)(d) of that Act, or the Consular Privileges and Immunity Act 1971 who hold a special temporary visa (see H2). Approval for partners and dependent children of diplomatic, consular or official staff to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand must be granted by the Protocol Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (see H2.1). Protocol Division will also confirm whether fees are payable.

children.label: e
children.text: Despite (d) above, the accompanying partners and dependent children aged 21 and over of Diplomatic, Consular or Official staff, who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand, may not be eligible for domestic student status and may be required to pay foreign student fees (see H2.1(b)).

children.label: f
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

blocks.label: p5
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector and are exempt from paying foreign course fees for foreign students:

children.label: a
children.text: Students enrolled for the first time in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme, after 19 April 2005, in any New Zealand university (see U5.20).

children.label: b
children.text: Partners and dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

pages.title: Programmes of study lasting longer than 3 months
pages.page_title: U6.1 Programmes of study lasting longer than 3 months

units.heading: Programmes of study lasting longer than 3 months

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: People who require a visa to visit New Zealand and who wish to come to New Zealand to study full-time for a period longer than three months, must hold a student visa.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Potential students who are nationals of countries to whom a visitor visa waiver applies (see E2.1) may enter New Zealand as visitors and apply for a student visa after their arrival.

units.heading: Definition of 'full-time study'

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For private training establishments full-time study is generally considered to be enrolment in:

children.label: i
children.text: a programme of study that requires attendance for a minimum of 20 hours per week; or

children.label: ii
children.text: at least three papers, or equivalent, per semester if the offered programme of study is at Level 7 or above on the New Zealand Qualification Framework.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: For other tertiary institutions enrolment in at least three papers, or equivalent, per semester is indicative of full-time study.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Any programme of study that does not meet (a) or (b) above is usually considered to be part-time (see U7.20).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The final decision on whether or not a student may be considered to be undertaking full-time study rests with immigration officers.

pages.title: Students undertaking employment
pages.page_title: U7.15 Students undertaking employment (07/11/2011)

units.heading: Students undertaking employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students may apply for a variation of conditions to work:

children.label: i
children.text: to fulfil practical course requirements (see U7.15.1); and/or

children.label: ii
children.text: for up to 20 hours in any given week during the academic year, and during any holidays within the academic year if they are an eligible student (see U7.15.5); and/or

children.label: iii
children.text: full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period if they are an eligible student (see U7.15.10).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Students are not permitted to:

children.label: i
children.text: work in self-employment; or

children.label: ii
children.text: provide commercial sexual services; or

children.label: iii
children.text: act as an operator of a New Zealand business of prostitution; or

children.label: iv
children.text: invest in a business of prostitution (see E7.40).

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of student visas may apply for a variation of conditions to allow them to work in order to fulfil a requirement of practical experience for their course.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If satisfied that practical experience is a course requirement, an immigration officer may grant a student visa with the conditions varied to allow employment. Note: If an applicant's main activity will be work, they must apply for a work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where the variation of conditions is sought in conjunction with an application for a student visa, the fee for a variation of conditions may be waived.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The variation of conditions will be effective only for the period of the student's current student visa and ceases on completion of the relevant course of study.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: The variation of conditions may be applied for at any time the visa is current or when applying for a further student visa.

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of student visas may be granted a variation of conditions to allow them to work during the academic year, and during any holidays within the academic year for up to 20 hours in any given week if they are:

children.label: i
children.text: undertaking a full-time course of study, at a private training establishment or tertiary institution (see U5.15 - U5.20), of at least two academic years’ duration; or

children.label: ii
children.text: undertaking a full-time course of study in New Zealand, culminating in a New Zealand qualification that would qualify for points under the Skilled Migrant Category (see SM14); or

children.label: iii
children.text: undertaking a full-time tertiary course of study of at least one academic year's duration as part of an approved tertiary student exchange scheme (see E11.45); or

children.label: iv
children.text: undertaking a full-time, full secondary school year course of study in Years 12 or 13, provided they have written permission from their school and written parental consent; or

children.label: v
children.text: engaged in a full-time course of study of at least six months’ duration at a private training establishment or tertiary institution (see U5.15 - U5.20); and

children.label: b1
children.text: an immigration officer is satisfied that the primary purpose of the course of study is to develop English language skills; and

children.label: b2
children.text: the student can provide a certificate (no more than 2 years old at the time the application is lodged) from the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) which shows an overall band score of at least 5.0 in the IELTS (General or Academic Module).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of an offer of employment is not required.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where the variation of conditions is sought in conjunction with an application for a student visa, the fee for a variation of conditions may be waived.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The variation of conditions will be effective only for the period of the student's current student visa and ceases on completion of the relevant course of study.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: The variation of conditions may be applied for at any time the visa is current or when applying for a further student visa.

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of student visas may be granted a variation of conditions to allow them to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period at the end of each academic year, provided they are undertaking a full-time course of study of 12 months or more duration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Any school student who does not meet the requirements set out at U7.15.5a(iv) is not eligible to work under the provisions of U7.15.10. Note: Written permission from the school is not required for students who are 18 years of age or over, under the provisions of U7.15.10.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence of an offer of employment is not required.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Where the variation of conditions is sought in conjunction with an application for a student visa, the fee for a variation of conditions may be waived.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: The variation of conditions will be effective only for the period of the student's current student visa.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: The variation of conditions may be applied for at any time the visa is current or when applying for a further student visa.

units.heading: Dependent children of holders of student visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas if their parent is a student visa holder who is:

children.label: i
children.text: any person who is in New Zealand to study under an exchange programme approved by the New Zealand Government; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a foreign student enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme in a New Zealand university; or

children.label: iii
children.text: any person who is the holder of a New Zealand scholarship administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of student visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's student visa (see U3.35).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of student visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment (see E4.1).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and evidence of maintenance funds are required (see U3.20).
