pages.title: Acceptable sponsors
pages.page_title: E6.5 Acceptable sponsors

units.heading: Acceptable sponsors

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Whether sponsorship is required for any type of temporary entry class application will be determined in immigration instructions for that type of application (see V2.20 and V2.25 for visitors, U3.20 and U3.25 for students, W2.15, W2.20, WM3 and WR2.15 for workers, and H8).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A sponsor for a temporary entry class application must be deemed acceptable by the Minister of Immigration or an immigration officer.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: An acceptable sponsor must either be a natural person, an organisation, or a government agency (including Crown entities and State Owned Enterprises), defined as follows:

children.label: i
children.text: a natural person must be a New Zealand citizen or the holder of a current residence class visa that is not subject to conditions, other than conditions relating to travel, under section 49(1)(a) or section 50 of the Immigration Act 2009; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an organisation must be registered in New Zealand as a company, incorporated society or charitable trust; or

children.label: iii
children.text: a government agency must be a government department named in Schedule 1 of the State Sector Act 1988, or a Crown entity as defined in section 7(1) of the Crown Entities Act 2004.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Whether natural persons, organisations or government agencies can sponsor a specific type of application will be determined in immigration instructions for that type of application.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: A sponsor who is not a natural person must nominate an individual as the authorised contact for the purpose of sponsorship.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: All acceptable sponsors must:

children.label: i
children.text: provide written undertakings for the maintenance, the accommodation, and the cost of deportation or repatriation of the applicant (see E6.15); and

children.label: ii
children.text: meet any other sponsorship requirements specified in the relevant immigration instructions (if any).

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: It is a matter for the absolute discretion of the Minister of immigration or the immigration officer whether a person (or organisation or government agency) is acceptable as a sponsor, and no appeal lies against their decision, whether to any court, the Tribunal, the Minister of Immigration, or otherwise.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: for the purpose of sponsorship requirements, Crown entities as defined in section 7(1) of the Crown Entities Act 2004 include Crown agents, autonomous Crown entities and independent Crown entities, Crown entity companies, Crown entity subsidiaries, school boards of trustees, and tertiary institutions.

units.heading: Additional criteria for natural persons

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: In addition to the requirement of E6.5(c)(i), to be an acceptable sponsor for a temporary entry class visa application a natural person must:

children.label: i
children.text: be ordinarily resident in New Zealand during the term of sponsorship, unless stated otherwise in specific instructions; and

children.label: ii
children.text: not sponsor for the purpose of receiving a financial reward or fee; and

children.label: iii
children.text: not have been convicted at any time of an offence under immigration law; and

children.label: iv
children.text: not have an outstanding debt to the Crown or other third parties as a result of another sponsorship arrangement; and

children.label: v
children.text: not sponsor a person if they have previously breached sponsorship obligations; and

children.label: vi
children.text: not have entered insolvency procedures or be adjudicated bankrupt; and

children.label: vii
children.text: not be liable for deportation; and

children.label: viii
children.text: not be a person whose liability for deportation is currently suspended; and

children.label: ix
children.text: not be serving a custodial sentence or be awaiting sentencing after being convicted of a crime which carries a custodial sentence.

units.heading: Additional criteria for organisations

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: In addition to the requirement of E6.5(c)(ii), to be an acceptable sponsor for a temporary entry class visa application an organisation must:

children.label: i
children.text: identify a clear link between the organisation’s activities and the purpose for which the applicant is coming to New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: not sponsor for the purpose of receiving a financial reward or fee; and

children.label: iii
children.text: not have been convicted of an offence under immigration law; and

children.label: iv
children.text: not have any listed directors, trustees or management who have been convicted of an offence under immigration law; and

children.label: v
children.text: not have an outstanding debt to the Crown or other third parties as a result of another sponsorship arrangement; and

children.label: vi
children.text: not have previously breached sponsorship obligations; and

children.label: vii
children.text: not be in receivership or liquidation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: financial reward does not preclude an employer from sponsoring an employee where the financial reward is the expected profit the employer will make from the employee’s work.

pages.title: Partners and dependent children of holders of work visas
pages.page_title: U8.20 Partners and dependent children of holders of work visas (07/11/2011)

units.heading: Partners and dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Crew of foreign chartered fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2); or

children.label: v
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all course fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for partners and dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the partner or parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the partner or parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.15 to A5.25.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Despite (a) (v) partners and dependent children of Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) Job Search visa holders may be granted student visas if the related SMC application was under consideration on or before 24 July 2011.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent/s meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is $33,675 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent/s meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent/s:

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent/s do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent/s and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$33,675 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary or wages of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary or wages of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

units.heading: Confirmation of enrolment

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Applicants who are returning to the same New Zealand education provider to continue a programme of study or training scheme may, instead of an offer of a place, provide a confirmation of enrolment from the education provider which shows:

children.text: the name of the programme of study; and

children.label: b

children.label: c
children.text: whether the student is full-time (see U6.1.1) or part-time (see U7.20); and

children.label: d
children.text: the dates and duration of all scheduled vacations if the programme of study or training scheme is one academic year or more.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: For the information specified at U3.7(d), this can be provided in a separate document accompanying the Offer of Place or Confirmation of Enrolment.

pages.title: Summary

units.heading: Summary

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless otherwise specified, to be granted a student visa to attend a course of more than three months, applicants must:

children.label: i
children.text: have an offer of a place in an approved course with an education provider in New Zealand that meets student visa requirements (see U3.5 and U5.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: be exempted from or have paid course fees; and

children.label: iii
children.text: if aged under 18, meet accommodation requirements (see U3.15); and

children.label: iv
children.text: have fulfilled the purpose and met the conditions for any previous or current temporary visas held as set out in E3.15 and E3.20; and

children.label: v
children.text: meet the conditions set out in E3.20; and

children.label: vi
children.text: not be the holder of a current visitor visa granted under Guardians accompanying students to New Zealand instructions (see V3.100).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All applicants must meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for:

children.label: i
children.text: lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa as set out at E4; and

children.label: ii
children.text: bona fide applicants as set out at E5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: health and character as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have not completed, or will not be completing the course of study endorsed on their student visa and who wish to change their course of study and/or education provider must:

children.label: i
children.text: meet requirements (a) and (b) above; and

children.label: ii
children.text: meet the requirements set out at U3.40.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Applicants who are progressing to further study, for example a student in Year 13 who is progressing to tertiary studies, will not need to meet U3.40.

pages.title: Offer of a place
pages.page_title: U3.5 Offer of a place (25/07/2011)

units.heading: Offer of a place

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Applicants must have an offer of a place with a New Zealand education provider, which shows:

children.label: a
children.text: the name of the course and the minimum time required for completing it; and

children.label: b
children.text: evidence that the course and education provider meet foreign student requirements (see U5); and

children.label: c
children.text: confirmation that the education provider has assessed and is satisfied the student meets the course competencies and enrolment provision (section 7.1) as set out in the Code of Practice for the Pastoral Care of International Students; and

children.label: d
children.text: the amount of the fee for the complete course, or, if the course is longer than one year, the annual fee; and

children.label: e
children.text: whether or not the student has to pay course fees and whether the fees are domestic or foreign fees; and

children.label: f
children.text: whether the student is full-time (see U6.1.1) or part-time (see U7.20).

pages.title: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand
pages.page_title: U3.20 Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand (21/11/2011)

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that they have sufficient funds available to maintain themselves throughout the period of their stay in New Zealand.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence may include but is not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: a notice of the award of a full scholarship; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a completed Sponsorship for Temporary Entry (INZ 1025) form (see U3.20.5); or

children.label: iii
children.text: a completed Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form, which covers a stay in New Zealand for the length of the visa (see U3.20.10); or

children.label: iv
children.text: funds held by or on behalf of the student (see U3.20.20).

units.heading: Sponsorship

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A sponsor for a student visa application must be an acceptable sponsor (see E6.5) and be either:

children.label: i
children.text: a natural person who is a relative or a friend of the applicant; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an organisation or government agency (an individual must be nominated as the authorised contact).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Sponsors must satisfy an immigration officer that they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet sponsorship obligations); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are sponsoring.

units.heading: Financial Undertaking

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Before the student’s arrival in New Zealand, a financial undertaking may be provided by a third party.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the third party is a person, they must be a relative or a friend of the applicant.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If the third party is not a person, they must nominate an individual as an authorised contact.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The third party providing the financial undertaking must satisfy an immigration officer they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet their financial obligations as set out on the Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are supporting.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Where a third party wishes to continue providing a financial undertaking for the student’s subsequent onshore student visa applications, they may do so if they continue to meet (d).

units.heading: Determining whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To determine whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide, immigration officers may consider:

children.label: a
children.text: the relationship between the applicant and the sponsor or third party;

children.label: b
children.text: any previous breaches of financial obligations set out in undertakings;

children.label: c
children.text: the number of student visa applications they are currently supporting;

children.label: d
children.text: the period of time for which funds have been held by the sponsor or third party; and

children.label: e
children.text: the student’s ability to access funds from the sponsor or third party while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds held by or on behalf of the student

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Where funds are held by or on behalf of the student, immigration officers must be satisfied that the funds are from a genuine source and are genuinely available for the purposes of the applicant’s maintenance requirements.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: When determining whether a student has sufficient funds to maintain themselves throughout their stay in New Zealand, immigration officers may consider the period of time for which funds have been held by the student and the student’s ability to access funds while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking courses lasting less than 36 weeks

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students taking courses lasting less than 36 weeks must provide:

children.label: a
children.text: evidence that funds of the amount required for visitor visa holders are held by or on behalf of the student; or

children.label: b
children.text: a letter from an education provider confirming that accommodation and other living expenses are included as part of a prepaid package. Note: This evidence may be sighted after the application has been approved in principle.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking courses lasting 36 weeks or longer

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students taking courses lasting 36 weeks or longer must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that:

children.label: a
children.text: they have NZ$10,000.00 per year available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (travellers' cheques or bank documents in the student's name are acceptable); or

children.label: b
children.text: (if they are citizens of Samoa and Tonga) a written guarantee of maintenance from a relative in New Zealand who is either a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder.

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maternity health services

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Pregnant applicants for a student visa who are due to give birth while in New Zealand must provide evidence that they:

children.label: a
children.text: have funds of at least NZ$9,000 available to pay for maternity health services; or

children.label: b
children.text: have sponsorship by a person, an organisation or a Government agency which meets generic sponsorship requirements set out at E6.5, to cover maternity health services; or

children.label: c
children.text: have a guarantee of financial undertaking by a third party which covers maternity health services (see U3.20.10); or

children.label: d
children.text: are eligible for publicly-funded maternity health services.

units.heading: Funds requirements

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless specifically stated otherwise, applicants for work visas are required to provide:

children.label: i
children.text: a proposed salary that an immigration officer considers sufficient to cover maintenance and accommodation; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a guarantee of maintenance and accommodation by their employer for the currency of the visa; or

children.label: iii
children.text: sufficient funds for maintenance and accommodation for the currency of the visa; or

children.label: iv
children.text: sponsorship by a relative or friend in New Zealand (see E6).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Officers with schedule 2 delegations and above are authorised to waive the requirement for evidence of funds or sponsorship.

units.heading: Evidence of sufficient funds

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Evidence of sufficient funds includes but is not limited to:

children.label: b1
children.text: cash;

children.label: b2
children.text: New Zealand bank accounts showing the current balance;

children.label: b3
children.text: travellers' cheques;

children.label: b4
children.text: bank drafts;

children.label: b5
children.text: recognised credit cards with sufficient credit available;

children.label: b6
children.text: for group visas, certification from a reputable travel agency.

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maternity health services

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: In addition to W2.15(a) pregnant applicants for a work visa who are due to give birth while in New Zealand must provide evidence that they:

children.label: a
children.text: have funds of at least NZ$9,000 available to pay for maternity health services; or

children.label: b
children.text: have sponsorship by a person, which meets generic sponsorship requirements set out at E6.5, to cover maternity health services; or

children.label: c
children.text: are eligible for publicly-funded maternity health services.

pages.title: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand
pages.page_title: U3.20 Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that they have sufficient funds available to maintain themselves throughout the period of their stay in New Zealand.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence may include but is not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: a notice of the award of a full scholarship; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a completed Sponsorship for Temporary Entry (INZ 1025) form (see U3.20.5); or

children.label: iii
children.text: a completed Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form, which covers a stay in New Zealand for the length of the visa (see U3.20.10); or

children.label: iv
children.text: funds held by or on behalf of the student (see U3.20.20).

units.heading: Sponsorship

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A sponsor for a student visa application must be an acceptable sponsor (see E6.5) and be either:

children.label: i
children.text: a natural person who is a relative or a friend of the applicant; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an organisation or government agency (an individual must be nominated as the authorised contact).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A sponsor for a fee-paying foreign tertiary or non-compulsory education student who is applying from within New Zealand must have sponsored that student’s initial student visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Sponsors must satisfy an immigration officer that they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet sponsorship obligations); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are sponsoring.

units.heading: Financial Undertaking

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Before the student’s arrival in New Zealand, a financial undertaking may be provided by a third party.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the third party is a person, they must be a relative or a friend of the applicant.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If the third party is not a person, they must nominate an individual as an authorised contact.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The third party providing the financial undertaking must satisfy an immigration officer they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet their financial obligations as set out on the Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are supporting.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Where a third party wishes to continue providing a financial undertaking for the student’s subsequent onshore student visa applications, they may do so if they continue to meet (d).

units.heading: Determining whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To determine whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide, immigration officers may consider:

children.label: a
children.text: the relationship between the applicant and the sponsor or third party;

children.label: b
children.text: any previous breaches of financial obligations set out in undertakings;

children.label: c
children.text: the number of student visa applications they are currently supporting;

children.label: d
children.text: the period of time for which funds have been held by the sponsor or third party; and

children.label: e
children.text: the student’s ability to access funds from the sponsor or third party while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds held by or on behalf of the student

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Where funds are held by or on behalf of the student, immigration officers must be satisfied that the funds are from a genuine source and are genuinely available for the purposes of the applicant’s maintenance requirements.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: When determining whether a student has sufficient funds to maintain themselves throughout their stay in New Zealand, immigration officers may consider the period of time for which funds have been held by the student and the student’s ability to access funds while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking programmes of study lasting less than 36 weeks

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students taking programmes of study lasting less than 36 weeks must provide evidence they have funds of:

children.label: i
children.text: at least NZ$1,667 per month of study available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses) if they are undertaking tertiary or non-compulsory education study; or

children.label: ii
children.text: at least NZ$1,417 per month of study available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses) if they are undertaking compulsory education study.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the student is invited to apply for a student visa on the basis of having a critical purpose for travelling to New Zealand under H5.25.15(c) because they belong to a class of individuals that meets the requirements of H5.30.21(c)(iv), the student must provide evidence they have funds of at least NZ$1,667 per month of study available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a)(ii) and (b) above, if the student is invited to apply for a student visa to undertake secondary study on the basis of having a critical purpose for travelling to New Zealand under H5.25.15(c) because they belong to a class of individuals that meets the requirements of H5.30.21(c)(vi), the student must provide evidence they have funds of at least NZ$1,250 per month of study available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Notes: - This evidence may be sighted after the application has been approved in principle. - Compulsory education study is primary, intermediate, or secondary school study from years 1 to 13.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking programmes of study lasting 36 weeks or longer

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students taking programmes of study lasting 36 weeks or longer must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that:

children.label: i
children.text: they have NZ$20,000.00 per year available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses) if they are undertaking tertiary or non-compulsory education study; or

children.label: ii
children.text: they have NZ$17,000.00 per year available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses) if they are undertaking compulsory education study; or

children.label: iii
children.text: if they are citizens of Samoa and Tonga a written guarantee of maintenance from a relative in New Zealand who is either a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the student is invited to apply for a student visa on the basis of having a critical purpose for travelling to New Zealand under H5.25.15(c) because they belong to a class of individuals that meets the requirements of H5.30.21(c)(iv), the student must provide evidence they have funds of at least NZ$1,667 per month of study available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a)(ii) and (b) above, if the student is invited to apply for a student visa to undertake secondary study on the basis of having a critical purpose for travelling to New Zealand under H5.25.15(c) because they belong to a class of individuals that meets the requirements of H5.30.21(c)(vi), they must have NZ$15,000.00 per year available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses).

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maternity health services

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Pregnant applicants for a student visa who are due to give birth while in New Zealand must provide evidence that they:

children.label: a
children.text: have funds of at least NZ$9,000 available to pay for maternity health services; or

children.label: b
children.text: have sponsorship by a person, an organisation or a Government agency which meets generic sponsorship requirements set out at E6.5 to cover maternity health services; or

children.label: c
children.text: have a guarantee of financial undertaking by a third party which covers maternity health services (see U3.20.10); or

children.label: d
children.text: are eligible for publicly-funded maternity health services.

pages.title: Overview of health instructions
pages.page_title: A4.5 Overview of health instructions

units.heading: Overview of health instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All applicants for visas must have an acceptable standard of health unless:

children.label: i
children.text: they are entering New Zealand for specific medical treatment and have been granted a visa for this purpose; or

children.label: ii
children.text: they are applying for a further residence class visa under RV2 or RV4.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A person has an acceptable standard of health if they are:

children.label: i
children.text: unlikely to be a danger to public health; and

children.label: ii
children.text: unlikely to impose significant costs or demands on New Zealand's health services or special education services; and

children.label: iii
children.text: able to undertake the work or study on the basis of which they are applying for a visa, or which is a requirement for the grant of the visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: For the purposes of these instructions, 'Health services' includes all health and disability support services funded through Vote Health.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Applicants for residence class visas and applicants for temporary entry class visas are assessed to determine whether they have an acceptable standard of health using separate sets of criteria. Assessment of whether a temporary entry class visa applicant has an acceptable standard of health takes into account their length of intended stay in New Zealand (see A4.10 and A4.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Applicants are required to provide evidence of their health status as follows, unless specifically exempt:

children.label: i
children.text: applicants for temporary entry class visas intending a stay in New Zealand of more than six months and who have risk factors for tuberculosis must provide a Chest X-ray Certificate (see A4.25.1);

children.label: ii
children.text: applicants for residence class visas, and applicants for temporary entry class visas intending a stay in New Zealand of more than 12 months must provide a Medical Certificate and a Chest X-ray Certificate (see A4.20 and A4.25);

children.label: iii
children.text: applicants for a Global Workforce Seasonal Visa must provide a Medical Certificate and a Chest X-ray Certificate, regardless of their intended length of stay in New Zealand (see A4.25).

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Where an applicant is required to provide a Medical Certificate and/or Chest X-ray Certificate by A4.20 or A4.25, they must:

children.label: i
children.text: if the application is not made online, provide evidence of completion of the required certificate(s) with the application;

children.label: ii
children.text: if the application is made online and evidence of completion of the required certificate(s) is required to submit the application, provide that evidence in the manner specified by the online application form; or

children.label: iii
children.text: if the application is made online and evidence of completion of the required certificate(s) is not required to submit the application, complete the required certificate(s) when requested after submission of the application and provide evidence of completion in the manner specified in the request. Note: Requests for certificates under (f)(iii) may be made by an automated system. INZ’s automated system determines when to request a Medical or Chest X-ray certificate in line with instructions and based on the information provided by the applicant in the application form and information INZ holds about the applicant, such as the date and outcome of any previously provided Medical or Chest X-ray certificates.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Evidence of completion of a Medical Certificate and Chest X-ray Certificate includes:

children.label: i
children.text: a completed Medical Certificate and Chest X-ray Certificate; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an eMedical reference code (NZER); or

children.label: iii
children.text: confirmation that a physician has directly submitted the applicant’s Medical Certificate and Chest X-ray Certificate to Immigration New Zealand.

blocks.label: h
blocks.text: An immigration officer may however, request a Chest X-ray Certificate or a Medical Certificate regardless of the period of intended stay in New Zealand, if they consider this is necessary to establish whether the applicant has an acceptable standard of health.

blocks.label: i
blocks.text: Generally, an applicant's Chest X-ray Certificate or Medical Certificate will be valid for any temporary entry class or residence class visa application they make within 36 months of the certificate(s) having been completed by the radiologist and physician respectively (see A4.25(c) and A4.20(d)).

blocks.label: j
blocks.text: Some applicants who are assessed as having an unacceptable standard of health may be granted a medical waiver (see A4.60 and A4.65).

blocks.label: k
blocks.text: If any person included in the application fails to meet the necessary health requirements and does not qualify for a medical waiver, the application may be declined.

pages.title: Conditions of student visa, limited visa and interim visa for study purposes
pages.page_title: E3.20 Conditions of student visa, limited visa and interim visa for study purposes

units.heading: Conditions of student visa, limited visa and interim visa for study purposes

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Subject to any special direction to the contrary, every student visa, limited visa and interim visa granted for the purpose of study is subject to the following conditions:

children.label: a
children.text: At all times during the currency of the visa to be in New Zealand, the holder has the means to maintain himself or herself in New Zealand, in the form of:

children.label: i
children.text: funds held in New Zealand by or on behalf of or in trust for the holder; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an acceptable form of financial undertaking by an eligible third party; or

children.label: iii
children.text: a current approved sponsorship undertaking (see E6); or

children.label: iv
children.text: financial assistance available to the holder under any multilateral or bilateral aid programme administered in New Zealand by a Government department or statutory body; and

children.label: b
children.text: At all times during the currency of the visa to be in New Zealand, the holder has the means to travel to a country to which the holder has a right of entry, such means to be in the form of:

children.label: i
children.text: a fully paid travel ticket to any such country; or

children.label: ii
children.text: sufficient funds held in New Zealand by or on behalf of or in trust for the holder (being funds additional to any sum required under paragraph (a)) to purchase any such ticket; or

children.label: iii
children.text: an acceptable form of financial undertaking by an eligible third party; or

children.label: iv
children.text: a current approved sponsorship (see E6); or

children.label: v
children.text: financial assistance available to the holder under any multilateral or bilateral aid programme administered in New Zealand by a Government department or statutory body; and

children.label: c
children.text: The holder attends the programme of study at all times as required, at the place of study endorsed on the visa, unless there are genuine reasons for absences; and

children.label: d
children.text: The holder makes satisfactory progress in the programme of study, which is primarily determined by the education provider offering the programme of study, and assessed against its academic progress policies; and

children.label: e
children.text: The holder pays all or any fees that may be fixed from time to time and that are payable by the holder in respect of the programme of study undertaken or to be undertaken; and

children.label: f
children.text: The holder has insurance (see U3.45) if required to do so (see U3.1(vii)).

pages.title: When a student visa is not required
pages.page_title: U2.5 When a student visa is not required (30/07/2012)

units.heading: When a student visa is not required

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa or variation of conditions is not required:

children.label: a
children.text: for work visa holders to undertake any programme of study, or other training, authorised by their employer as part of their employment; or

children.label: b
children.text: for all temporary visa holders, to undertake one or more programmes of study of not more than three calendar months’ duration in total per visa stay conditions, or in each 12 month period if the visa stay conditions is valid for a minimum of 24 months; or

children.label: c
children.text: where V2.35 or WI2.1.1 (f) applies.

section_listing: U2.5 When a student visa is not required (25/07/2011)
U2.5 When a student visa is not required (29/11/2010)

pages.title: Summary
pages.page_title: U3.1 Summary

units.heading: Summary

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless otherwise specified, to be granted a student visa to attend a programme of study of more than three months, applicants must:

children.label: i
children.text: have an offer of a place or, if returning to continue a programme of study, a confirmation of enrolment in an approved programme of study with an education provider in New Zealand that meets student visa requirements (see U3.5, U3.10, and U5.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: be exempted from or have paid tuition fees; and

children.label: iii
children.text: if aged under 18, meet accommodation requirements (see U3.15); and

children.label: iv
children.text: have fulfilled the purpose and met the conditions for any previous or current temporary visas held as set out in E3.15 and E3.20; and

children.label: v
children.text: meet the conditions set out in E3.20; and

children.label: vi
children.text: not be the holder of a current visitor visa granted under Guardians accompanying students to New Zealand instructions (see V3.100); and

children.label: vii
children.text: hold insurance (see U3.45), unless they are a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) student or a student holding a New Zealand scholarship administered through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All applicants must meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for:

children.label: i
children.text: lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa as set out at E4; and

children.label: ii
children.text: bona fide applicants as set out at E5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: health and character as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: A student visa will not be granted to an applicant who holds or has held a Short-term Graduate work visa, unless the proposed study is:

children.label: i
children.text: a programme of study at a higher level on the New Zealand Qualifications and Credentials Framework (NZQCF) than the level of the qualification/s their Short-term Graduate work visa was based on; and

children.label: ii
children.text: a qualification eligible for a Post-Study work visa (see WD3.1).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (c)(i) above, an applicant who holds or has held a Short-term Graduate work visa based on a non-degree NZQCF level 7 qualification may apply for and be granted a student visa to study a Bachelor’s degree.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: To determine whether an applicant is likely to breach the condition of a student visa (see E5.1.b(ii)) that the holder must make satisfactory progress in their proposed programme of study, an immigration officer may:

children.label: i
children.text: consider whether the applicant has English language ability consistent with the level and nature of that study; and

children.label: ii
children.text: request the applicant provide evidence of their English language ability as part of this assessment.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Applicants who have not completed, or will not be completing the programme of study endorsed on their student visa and who wish to change their programme of study and/or education provider must:

children.label: i
children.text: meet requirements (a) and (b) above; and

children.label: ii
children.text: meet requirements at (c) above (unless U3.1(d) applies), if the applicant has held a Short-term Graduate work visa before their student visa was granted; and

children.label: iii
children.text: meet the requirements set out at U3.40.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Applicants who are progressing to further study, for example a student in Year 13 who is progressing to tertiary studies, will not need to meet U3.40.

units.heading: Tuition fees

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence of:

children.label: i
children.text: exemption from tuition fees, or

children.label: ii
children.text: payment of tuition fees, or

children.label: iii
children.text: a notice of the award of a full New Zealand Aid Programme scholarship. Note: For applications processed outside New Zealand, evidence of payment is not required until after the application has been approved in principle.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, evidence of payment of tuition fees need not be provided if an immigration officer is satisfied that the student is awaiting home country government loan approval to pay their tuition fees once the student enrols in person at the New Zealand Tertiary Education Institution (TEI). The student must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: evidence the loan has been applied for, and

children.label: ii
children.text: confirmation from the enrolling New Zealand TEI that they expect to receive the fee directly once the student is onshore and has completed enrolment at that TEI.

pages.page_title: U3.35 Definition of 'domestic student' (30/07/2012)

units.heading: Definition of 'domestic student'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of student instructions a 'domestic student' means a domestic student as defined in section 2 of the Education Act 1989. The Ministry of Education holds a complete list of who is considered to be a domestic student for the purpose of fee payment and enrolment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary schooling domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending primary and secondary schools and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue;

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents;

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents;

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current school year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending primary and secondary schools and are exempt from paying foreign course fees:

children.label: a
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is in New Zealand to study under an exchange programme approved by the New Zealand Government.

children.label: b
children.text: Children whose application for a residence class visa is under consideration and who are the dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand resident visa, or permanent resident visa.

children.label: c
children.text: Children whose application for New Zealand citizenship is under consideration and who are the dependent children of a New Zealand citizen.

children.label: d
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is onshore and the holder of a valid work visa other than those excluded under U8.20.

children.label: e
children.text: Students who have, or dependent children of any person who has, made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009.

children.label: f
children.text: Dependent children of a foreign student enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme in a New Zealand university.

children.label: g
children.text: Dependent children of any person who, during the current calendar year, last ceased to hold a special temporary visa (see H2).

children.label: h
children.text: Students who have entered New Zealand for the purposes of adoption and:

children.label: i
children.text: whose adoption application before the New Zealand Family Court (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student) is supported by the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services and who has a letter from the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services confirming this support; or

children.label: ii
children.text: who are the subject of an Interim Order of Adoption granted by the New Zealand Family Court under section 5 of the Adoption Act 1955 (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student).

children.label: i
children.text: People who are in the custody of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development pursuant to any of the following orders:

children.label: i
children.text: an order, pursuant to sections 78, 101 or 238(1)(d) of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, in favour of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 110 of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, appointing the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development as sole guardian; or

children.label: iii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 33 of the Care of Children Act 2004, whereby a child or young person is placed under the Guardianship of the Family Court or the High Court and the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development is appointed as agent of the court with power and discretion to place the child.

children.label: j
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand Aid Programme Scholarship.

children.label: k
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a visitor visa granted under V3.115.

children.label: l
children.text: Dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

children.label: m
children.text: Children granted a student visa under U10.5.

children.label: n
children.text: Students who are in New Zealand to study under an exchange scheme approved by the Ministry of Education (see E11.45).

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector (see U5.20) and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions or limited visa in order to undertake a course of study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue.

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents.

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents.

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current academic year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Despite (d) above, dependent children aged 21 and over of Diplomatic, Consular or Official staff, who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand, may not be eligible for domestic student status and may be required to pay foreign student fees (see H2.1(b)).

children.label: f
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

children.label: g
children.text: A person who has made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and who is the holder of a valid temporary entry class visa.

children.label: h
children.text: A person who has been recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and whose application for residence is being processed.

children.label: i
children.text: A person who is enrolled at a tertiary education provider for the purpose of participating in industry training funded under the Industry Training Act 1992.

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector and are exempt from paying foreign course fees for foreign students:

children.label: a
children.text: Students enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme, in any New Zealand university (see U5.20).

children.label: b
children.text: A person who is in New Zealand to study under a New Zealand Government approved exchange programme at a tertiary education provider.

children.label: c
children.text: Partners and dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

pages.title: Insurance requirements for fee-paying foreign students
pages.page_title: U3.45 Insurance requirements for fee-paying foreign students

units.heading: Insurance requirements for fee-paying foreign students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Fee-paying foreign students must hold insurance as a condition of their visa (see E3.20 (f)) unless (d) below applies.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A fee-paying foreign student must declare that they will arrange and hold insurance, which complies with the insurance requirements of the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021 and is acceptable to the student’s education provider, from the period of their enrolment until the expiry of their student visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: A student may be required to provide evidence that they held insurance from the time of their enrolment until the expiry of their student visa with any further visa application made.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The requirement to hold insurance does not apply to Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) students or students holding New Zealand scholarships administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

pages.title: Offer of a place
pages.page_title: U3.5 Offer of a place

units.heading: Offer of a place

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Applicants must have an offer of a place with a New Zealand education provider, which shows:

children.label: a
children.text: the name of the programme of study or training scheme and the minimum time required for completing it; and

children.label: b
children.text: evidence that the programme of study or training scheme and education provider meet foreign student requirements (see U5); and

children.label: c
children.text: confirmation that the education provider has assessed and is satisfied that the programme is appropriate for the student’s expectations, and that the prospective student has the English language proficiency and academic capability to succeed in the programme offered; and

children.label: d
children.text: the amount of the tuition fee, or, if the programme of study is longer than one year, the annual fee; and

children.label: e
children.text: whether or not the student has to pay programme of study or training scheme fees and whether the fees are domestic or foreign fees; and

children.label: f
children.text: whether the student is full-time (see U6.1.1) or part-time (see U7.20); and

children.label: g
children.text: the dates and duration of all scheduled vacations if the programme of study or training scheme is one academic year or more.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: ~For the information specified at U3.5(g), this can be provided in a separate document accompanying the Offer of Place or Confirmation of Enrolment. ~ An academic year means a programme of study of a minimum of 120 credits during a period of at least eight months (minimum of two semesters). ~From January 2014, students seeking to enrol in a programme of study or training scheme offered at an education provider that holds a Category Four status under the NZQA’s External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system will not be granted a student visa

pages.title: Status of education providers and programmes
pages.page_title: U5.1 Status of education providers and programmes

units.heading: Status of education providers and programmes

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All education providers must certify in their offers of places to foreign students (see U3.5) that the programme of study or training scheme offered complies with foreign student requirements for different kinds of education providers (see U5.5 - U5.20).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All education providers offering places to foreign students must be signatories to the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Any queries on the status of programmes or training schemes offered by private training establishments should be referred to the Service Delivery Unit, Quality Assurance Division, New Zealand Qualifications Authority (NZQA), PO Box 160, Wellington.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Students will not be granted a student visa to undertake a programme of study or training scheme offered at an education provider that holds a Category Four status under the NZQA’s External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Immigration New Zealand (INZ) may suspend the processing of applications for student visas for study at an education provider where at least one of the following applies:

children.label: i
children.text: the offered programme of study or training scheme does not comply with foreign student requirements as set out in U5.5 to U5.20;

children.label: ii
children.text: the education provider is not complying, or is under investigation by INZ for non-compliance, with its obligations under the Immigration Act, immigration regulations, or immigration instructions;

children.label: iii
children.text: the education provider is not complying, or is under investigation by education agencies for non-compliance, with its obligations under the Education Act and education regulations including the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021;

children.label: iv
children.text: the education provider is under investigation for a matter that may result in it:

children.label: b1
children.text: no longer being recognised as being able to provide New Zealand qualifications by the relevant regulatory agency; or

children.label: b2
children.text: the programme of study or training scheme the applicant is seeking a visa to study may no longer result in a qualification recognised in New Zealand. Note: for the purposes of these instructions, "education agencies" include any agencies identified by the Ministry of Education, as well as the Ministry of Education itself – see Education agencies - Ministry of Education

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Where (e) above applies, INZ may:

children.label: i
children.text: suspend processing for an initial period of up to six months while awaiting the outcome of the investigation of the provider, and if the investigation has not been completed within that period, extend the initial suspension period to allow for the outcome of the investigation; or

children.label: ii
children.text: continue processing any such applications where INZ is not satisfied the requirements of immigration instructions have been met and decline the application.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Depending on the nature of the non-compliance or potential non-compliance, processing may be suspended for

children.label: i
children.text: all applications to study at the provider; or

children.label: ii
children.text: applications to study particular programmes at the provider; or

children.label: iii
children.text: a group of applications to study at the provider that share one or more common characteristics (such as education agent) relevant to the non-compliance or potential non-compliance.

blocks.label: h
blocks.text: Before a decision is made to suspend the processing of student visas, the following will be taken into account:

children.label: i
children.text: evidence of the non-compliance; and

children.label: ii
children.text: reasons for the non-compliance; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the duration, frequency, and severity of the non-compliance.

blocks.label: i
blocks.text: INZ may resume the processing of student visas if it is satisfied that the education provider is complying with its obligations.

units.heading: Applicants whose applications are suspended due to provider non-compliance or investigation

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: If the processing of a student visa application is suspended where U5.1(e) above applies, the applicant may submit an Offer of Place to study with a different education provider (see (c) below) or withdraw their application.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Processing may be suspended on any application that has not been completed through the grant of a visa, decline, or withdrawal by the applicant. For avoidance of doubt this includes applications that have been approved in principle where a visa has not been granted.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Processing may resume if the applicant provides a new Offer of Place for a programme with a different education provider, provided:

children.label: i
children.text: the new offer of place meets all relevant requirements for the grant of a student visa; and either

children.label: ii
children.text: the Offer of Place is for the same programme; or

children.label: iii
children.text: the immigration officer is satisfied that there is a valid reason for the Offer of Place being for a different programme (for example, the programme is not offered by another provider).

units.heading: Private training establishments

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Private training establishments may offer programme of study places to international students provided the programme of study or training scheme meets the criteria for one in which an international student may be enrolled in accordance with the provisions of the Education and Training Act 2020 (see section 527).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The definition of an international student is contained in section 10(1) of the Education and Training Act 2020.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The primary requirements for satisfying section 527 of the Education and Training Act 2020, in respect of programme of study or training schemes are that:

children.label: i
children.text: the private training establishment providing the programme of study or training scheme has been registered by the New Zealand Qualifications Authority, and

children.label: ii
children.text: the programme of study or training scheme is an approved programme of study or training scheme, and

children.label: iii
children.text: the private training establishment has been accredited to provide the programme of study.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: These requirements apply to all programmes of study and training schemes with the exception of those programmes of study or training scheme that are exempt as provided for in section 528 of the Education and Training Act 2020.

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Tertiary institutions may offer programmes of study or training scheme places to international students provided the programme of study or training scheme meets the criteria for one in which a international student may be enrolled in accordance with the provisions of the Education and Training Act 2020 (see section 525).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The definition of an international student is contained in section 10(1) of the Education and Training Act 2020.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The primary requirements for section 525 of the Education and Training Act 2020 in respect of programmes of study or training schemes that are or are likely to be longer than 3 months are that:

children.label: i

children.label: ii

children.label: iii

children.label: b1

children.label: b2
children.text: the place has been established by the Council of the institution for a foreign student and its continued availability is dependent on the fees payable by the foreign student enrolled in it.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: ~ Polytechnics also include institutes of technology, technical institutes or community colleges established before 1 January 1991. ~ These requirements apply to all programmes of study and training schemes with the exception of those programmes of study or training schemes that are exempt as provided for in section 528 of the Education and Training Act 2020.

units.heading: Visas for the length of a programme of study: Aviation students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Aviation students may be granted a student visa for the length of their programme of study if:

children.label: i
children.text: the student has an offer of place from an aviation training provider that is:

children.label: b1

children.label: iii

blocks.label: b

blocks.label: c

units.heading: Partners and dependent children of diplomatic, consular or official staff

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Partners (see E4.1.20) and dependent children (see E4.1.10) of diplomatic, consular or official staff who wish to study in New Zealand must obtain approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade Protocol Division (see H2).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If a diplomatic or consular tour of duty terminates during the academic year, and the partner or dependent child ceases to hold a special temporary visa (see H2.1), they must obtain a student visa to continue studying.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children of diplomatic or consular personnel will be regarded as domestic students until the end of the calendar year in which the diplomat's or consular official’s tour of duty terminates, and they are not required to provide evidence of having paid tuition fees in order to complete the school or academic year (see U3.35).

units.heading: Partners and dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Crew of foreign chartered fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2); or

children.label: v
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: vi
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or.

children.label: vii
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all course fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for partners and dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the partner or parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the partner or parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.15 to A5.25.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Despite (a) (v) partners and dependent children of Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) Job Search visa holders may be granted student visas if the related SMC application was under consideration on or before 24 July 2011.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent/s meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is $33,675 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent/s meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent/s:

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent/s do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent/s and child may become liable for deportation. Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$33,675 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation. Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

pages.title: Visitor visa requirements
pages.page_title: V2.1 Visitor visa requirements

units.heading: Visitor visa requirements

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To be granted a visitor visa applicants must:

children.label: a
children.text: meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry instructions for:

children.label: i
children.text: lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa as set out at E4; and

children.label: ii
children.text: bona fide applicants as set out at E5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: health and character as set out at A4 and A5; and

children.label: b
children.text: meet the funds or sponsorship requirements (see V2.20); and

children.label: c
children.text: meet the onward travel requirements, if relevant (see V2.25); and

children.label: d
children.text: be coming to New Zealand for a lawful purpose.

units.heading: Definition of 'lawful purpose' for visitors

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For the purposes of applying the 'lawful purpose' test in the provision relating to bona fide applicants (see E5.1), visitors are considered to be coming to New Zealand for a lawful purpose if: they are coming for such purposes as:

children.label: b1
children.text: holidaying;

children.label: b2
children.text: sightseeing;

children.label: b3
children.text: family and social visits;

children.label: b4
children.text: amateur sport;

children.label: b5
children.text: business consultation (see V3.5);

children.label: b6
children.text: medical treatment (see V3.40); or

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: guest of government visits (guest of government status is granted by the Visits and Ceremonial Office, Department of Internal Affairs); or they are staying in New Zealand for the purpose of arranging travel to depart, where the applicant is unable to leave because of COVID-19 (see V3.155); and

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: they are not intending to undertake employment (see W2.2.1) or a programme of study or training, with the exception of short-term study (see V2.35 and U2.5(b)).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: - If the programme is offered by a private training establishment, the applicant must ensure that the primary requirements for satisfying sections 342, 343, 345 and 527 of the Education and Training Act 2020, in respect of programmes of study, are met (see U5.15). - All education providers offering places to international students must be signatories to the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021 (see U5.1(b)).

units.heading: Applying using the online system

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Applications for a visitor visa from an applicant who is in, and applying from, a Pacific Forum country (excluding Australia) must be made using the approved online form provided on the Immigration New Zealand website.

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010 Reg 23AA

pages.title: Short-term study in schools
pages.page_title: V2.35 Short-term study in schools

units.heading: Short-term study in schools

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Visitor visa holders can study without the need to obtain a student visa or a variation of conditions if they attend primary, intermediate, secondary, or composite school for a single period of study of up to three months per calendar year. The single period of study:

children.label: i
children.text: must start and finish within a calendar year; and

children.label: ii
children.text: must not be in term 1 if a visitor visa was held and a single period of study was undertaken in term 4 of the previous year.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Visitor visa holders undertaking a single period of study in (a) above must attend a school that is a signatory to the Education (Pastoral Care Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021, if at least one of the following applies:

children.label: i
children.text: they attend for more than two weeks; or

children.label: ii
children.text: they are fee-paying foreign students.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (b)(i) above, attendance at a school that is a signatory to the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021 is not required where the visitor visa holder is studying under a reciprocal exchange scheme managed by an Exchange Programme Organisation (EPO) approved by the Ministry of Education (see U4.15).
