pages.title: Character checks
pages.page_title: A5.5 Character checks

units.heading: Character checks

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Character checks must be carried out for the following categories of applicant:

children.label: i
children.text: those aged 17 and over applying for residence class visas; and

children.label: ii
children.text: those aged 17 and over applying for temporary entry class visas who intend to stay in New Zealand for 24 months or longer; and

children.label: iii
children.text: other applicants for temporary entry class visas who warrant a character check if the immigration officer decides it is necessary; and

children.label: iv
children.text: those aged 17 and over applying for a Global Workforce Seasonal Visa, regardless of their intended length of stay in New Zealand. Note: the 24-month period in A5.5(a)(ii) above includes time already spent in New Zealand prior to the application being made.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: It is a mandatory requirement (see R2.40) for first time applicants for a residence class visa aged 17 and over to obtain a police or similar certificate from: Applicants for a further residence class visa under RV2 or RV4 will not usually need to submit a police or similar certificate, unless specifically asked to by an immigration officer. Applicants for a further residence class visa applying under any other category are required to submit a police or similar certificate as if they were applying for residence for the first time. Note: the requirement in A5.5(b) above does not apply to Australian citizens, holders of a current Australian permanent residence visa and holders of a current Australian resident return visa, applying for a resident visa at an immigration control area.

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant's country of citizenship; and

children.label: ii
children.text: each country in which the applicant has lived for 12 months or more (whether on one visit or intermittently) in the last 10 years (but see A5.10.1).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If required, applicants aged 17 and over applying for a temporary entry class visa must obtain a police or similar certificate from:

children.label: i
children.text: their country of citizenship; and

children.label: ii
children.text: from any country in which they have lived for five or more years (whether on one visit or intermittently) since attaining the age of 17 years.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (c) above, student visa applicants do not have to provide a police or similar certificate until they are aged 20 or over if they:

children.label: i
children.text: held a student visa when they turned 17; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have held consecutive student visas (or interim visas with study conditions) since the date they turned 17; and

children.label: iii
children.text: are applying for a further student visa.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Despite (c) above, applicants for the following temporary entry class visas do not need to provide a police or similar certificate:

children.label: i
children.text: applicants (and their partner and dependent child(ren), if any) for a Migrant Exploitation Protection work visa (see WI20);

children.label: ii
children.text: applicants (and their partner and dependent child(ren), if any) for an Essential Skills work visa who provided a certificate with a previous visa application;

children.label: iii
children.text: applicants for a 2022 Special Ukraine Visa.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, applicants for an Afghan Emergency Resettlement Category permanent resident visa (see S4.35) do not need to provide a police or similar certificate if they are unable to obtain the required document.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, applicants aged 17 and over applying for residence under the 2021 Resident Visa Category (S6) are not required to provide a police certificate or similar from their country of citizenship or any country they have lived in 12 months or more (whether on one visit or intermittently) in the last 10 years, except for a New Zealand Police Check. This will be required regardless of the duration they have lived in New Zealand. INZ will request this from the New Zealand Police on the applicant’s behalf.

blocks.label: h
blocks.text: Despite (d), (e), (f) and (g) above, a police or similar certificate is required if an immigration officer decides it is necessary.

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010 Regs 5(2)(d)(iii), 6(2)(d)(iv),10(2)(e)(iii)

units.heading: Impact of the Criminal Records (Clean Slate) Act 2004

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: When assessing whether a person meets an applicable character requirement, an immigration officer must be aware that New Zealand convictions may be covered by the Criminal Records (Clean Slate) Act 2004 (Clean Slate Scheme) and that if so, an eligible individual is not required to declare New Zealand convictions.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If Immigration New Zealand (INZ) holds any information that a person has these New Zealand convictions, and that person is an eligible individual under the Clean Slate Scheme, this information cannot be used when assessing whether the person meets the applicable character requirements.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The information referred to in (b), above, includes any prior police certificates, any information INZ holds in its records (including its Application Management System), and any other information which may have been gathered from a public source.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If a person is an eligible individual under the Clean Slate Scheme, immigration officers cannot, under any circumstances, request or require that an individual disregard the effect of the Clean Slate Scheme when answering questions about his or her New Zealand criminal record, or disregard the effect of the Clean Slate Scheme and disclose, or give consent to the disclosure of, his or her criminal record. Doing so is an offence under the Criminal Records (Clean Slate) Act 2004. However, if the persons voluntarily declares criminal convictions that are subject to the Clean Slate Scheme, this information can be used to assess whether the person meets the applicable character requirements.

pages.title: Requirements for participants in approved student exchange schemes
pages.page_title: E11.55 Requirements for participants in approved student exchange schemes

units.heading: Requirements for participants in approved student exchange schemes

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Participants in approved student exchange schemes may be granted student visas for the length of their exchange provided they:

children.label: a
children.text: meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry instructions for lodging an application for a temporary entry visa as set out at E4; and

children.label: b
children.text: apply from outside of New Zealand; and

children.label: c
children.text: are bona fide applicants as set out at E5

children.label: d
children.text: meet health and character requirements as set out at A4 and A5.

units.heading: Evidence

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Participants must provide evidence to show that:

children.label: a
children.text: they have been accepted into an approved student exchange scheme by the scheme organiser; and

children.label: b
children.text: they meet outward travel requirements.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Evidence of the travel arrangements to leave New Zealand at the end of the intended stay is: - actual travel tickets (confirmed or open-dated) out of New Zealand to a destination to which the applicant has right of entry; or - a written guarantee from the New Zealand guarantor that they will ensure that participants (and any dependants) will have outward bookings at the end of their stay in New Zealand, regardless of whether they complete the full term of the exchange.

units.heading: Participants who arrive in New Zealand without a student visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: If participants arrive in New Zealand without a student visa, immigration officers may grant a student visa for the maximum period of stay for their scheme, provided that:

children.label: a
children.text: there are special reasons why they have not obtained a visa; and

children.label: b
children.text: they meet the requirements set out at E11.55.

units.heading: Partners and dependent children of student exchange scheme participants

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children of student exchange scheme participants may be granted visas that are current for the same period as the participants' visas, provided they meet the requirements for the particular category of visa they are applying for.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Immigration officers must be satisfied that the exchange scheme allows participants to be accompanied to New Zealand by their partner and dependent children.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Participants' partners may apply for work visas after their arrival, but they are subject to work visa criteria.

units.heading: Extending the stay for tourist reasons

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Participants who wish to remain in New Zealand for a further period as tourists may be granted visitor visas for a maximum of 3 months, provided that they meet the requirements and conditions for a visitor visa.

units.heading: Pastoral Care of International Students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Attendance at a school that is a signatory to the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021 is required where the student is studying under a school-to-school exchange scheme (U4.15(b)(i)).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Attendance at a school that is a signatory to the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021 is not required for:

children.label: i
children.text: school students studying under a reciprocal exchange scheme managed by an Exchange Programme Organisation (EPO) approved by the Ministry of Education (see U4.15(b)(ii); and

children.label: ii
children.text: tertiary students on approved exchanges.

pages.title: Requirements for lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa
pages.page_title: E4.50 Requirements for lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa

units.heading: Requirements for lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: These requirements apply to the lodgement of the following types of temporary entry class visa applications:

children.label: i
children.text: Applications lodged on an approved paper form (E4.50.1, E4.50.15).

children.label: ii
children.text: Applications lodged under a Working Holiday Scheme (WI2) and under Silver Fern instructions (WL) which must be made online using the electronic form provided on the Immigration website (https://onlineservices.immigration.govt.nz/?whs) (E4.50.2, E4.50.15).

children.label: iii
children.text: Applications not covered by (a)(ii), made on an electronic form (E4.50.2, E4.50.15).

children.label: iv
children.text: Applications lodged otherwise than on an approved form (E4.50.5, E4.50.10, E4.50.15).

children.label: v
children.text: Applications for a temporary entry class visa or entry permission in an immigration control area (E4.50.35, E4.50.40).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The requirements for applications for Diplomatic, consular, and official staff, and their dependants are at H4.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The requirements for the reconsideration of decision to decline further temporary entry class visa are at E7.35.1.

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010 reg 10, 11, 13, 14, 23A

units.heading: Mandatory requirements for applications lodged on an approved paper form

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of temporary entry instructions, mandatory requirements for applications lodged on an approved paper form means that applications must be made on the application form relevant to the type of visa required which must be completed in English, in full and submitted to an immigration officer, together with:

children.label: a
children.text: the applicant's passport (or a certified copy) or certificate of identity (or a certified copy), or if this is unavailable, his or her original birth certificate (or a certified copy) or other identity document (or a certified copy); and

children.label: b
children.text: two passport-sized photographs of the applicant’s head and shoulders; and

children.label: c
children.text: the appropriate fee and levies (if any); and

children.label: d
children.text: (all temporary entry class applications apart from military visa applications (see M2.1)) evidence of funds for maintenance in New Zealand or evidence of sponsorship (see E6); and

children.label: e
children.text: such information and evidence as is required by the relevant immigration instructions to demonstrate that the applicant fits the category or categories of immigration instructions under which the application is being made; and

children.label: f
children.text: any other information, evidence and submissions the applicant considers show that he or she is eligible to be granted a temporary entry class visa in terms of the relevant immigration instructions.

blocks.label: p2
blocks.text: Applications must be signed by the applicant (unless the applicant is less than 18 years old, in which case it must be signed by a parent or guardian of the applicant).

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010, reg 10

units.heading: Mandatory requirements for applications made on an electronic form

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applications for a second Working Holiday Scheme work visa (where a scheme allows for this) must be lodged according to E4.50.1.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: An application made on an electronic form must be completed in English, and requires the applicant to:

children.label: i
children.text: state his or her full name; and

children.label: ii
children.text: state his or her date and place of birth; and

children.label: iii
children.text: state the details of his or her passport or other certificate of identity; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if prompted by the online system, upload a photograph of the applicant’s head and shoulders, that complies with the standards specified for the purpose; and

children.label: v
children.text: produce the information and evidence required by immigration instructions to demonstrate he or she fits the category under which the application is being made; and

children.label: vi
children.text: acknowledge that the details supplied in support of their application are true and correct to the best of their knowledge; and

children.label: vii
children.text: agree that if their circumstances change before a visa is granted or before the application is determined, they will notify an immigration officer of the change; and

children.label: viii
children.text: pay the prescribed fee for the type of visa applied for or arrange for its payment in a manner acceptable to the immigration officer processing the application; and

children.label: ix
children.text: pay the immigration levy that is payable (if any), or arrange for its payment in a manner acceptable to the immigration officer processing the application; and

children.label: x
children.text: pay the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL) (if applicable), or arrange for its payment in a manner acceptable to the immigration officer processing the application.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The specified standards for the photograph can be obtained from the INZ website.

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010, reg 23A

units.heading: Mandatory requirements for applications lodged otherwise than on an approved form

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Despite E4.50.1, a person or their advisor may request an immigration officer to consider an application for a visa made without using the relevant approved form and an immigration officer may agree to the request.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Where an immigration officer agrees to that request, the applicant must supply the following information in English and in any way appropriate to the circumstances:

children.label: i
children.text: his or her full name; and

children.label: ii
children.text: his or her date and place of birth; and

children.label: iii
children.text: details of his or her passport or certificate of identity, including country of citizenship; and

children.label: iv
children.text: details of any current or previous visa (or permit as the case may be) held by him or her; and

children.label: v
children.text: details of the type of visa he or she is applying for; and

children.label: vi
children.text: any other information that he or she considers shows that the temporary entry class visa application should be granted; and

children.label: vii
children.text: such information and evidence that the immigration officer thinks necessary for him or her to determine the application.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The application must be completed by the applicant:

children.label: i
children.text: acknowledging that the details supplied in support of the application are true and correct to the best of his or her knowledge; and

children.label: ii
children.text: agreeing that if his or her circumstances change before a visa is granted, he or she will notify an immigration officer of the change in circumstances; and

children.label: iii
children.text: paying the prescribed fee (if any) for the type of visa applied for, or arranging for the payment of that fee in a manner satisfactory to the immigration officer; and

children.label: iv
children.text: paying the immigration levy and/or IVL that is payable by the applicant (if any), or arranging for its payment in a manner acceptable to the immigration officer processing the application; and

children.label: v
children.text: signing the application (except if the application is made in an electronic format).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If the applicant is less than 18 years old, (c)(v) does not apply. Instead, the application must be signed by his or her parent or guardian, except if the application is made in an electronic format or at an immigration control area (in which case the form must be signed by the parent or guardian only if the applicant is accompanied by that person).

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010, reg 21, 22

units.heading: Processing of applications made otherwise than on an approved form

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Where an immigration officer has agreed to a request to consider an application for a visa made otherwise than on an approved form, the immigration officer may at any time before a visa is granted as a result of the application:

children.label: i
children.text: refuse to consider the application, or continue to consider the application; and

children.label: ii
children.text: inform the applicant that if he or she wishes to pursue the application, he or she must do so using the relevant approved form.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If an immigration officer refuses to consider an application for a visa made otherwise than on an approved form then:

children.label: i
children.text: the application will be treated as not having been made; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant must apply for the visa in the normal way; and

children.label: iii
children.text: in the event the person pursues an application for a visa in the normal way, the mandatory requirements as set out at E4.50.1 and E4.50.5 will apply; and

children.label: iv
children.text: any application fee, Immigration Levy and IVL; will either be refunded or applied towards any visa application made by the same person.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: In the event an application for a visa is made otherwise than on an approved form and has been accepted for processing but cannot be finalised without further information or documentation being obtained, an immigration officer may transfer the application to another INZ office for finalisation. In such cases the application may, at the discretion of the immigration officer considering it, continue to be finalised without the applicant needing:

children.label: i
children.text: to complete the approved form; or

children.label: ii
children.text: pay any additional fee, Immigration Levy and IVL.

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010 reg 21 and 22

units.heading: Additional requirements

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Before determining an application made on an approved paper form or on an electronic form or otherwise than on an approved form, the immigration officer processing the application may do one or more of the following:

children.label: a
children.text: require the applicant to be interviewed by an immigration officer;

children.label: b
children.text: require the applicant to produce further information or evidence (including photographs) that the officer thinks necessary for him or her to determine the application;

children.label: c
children.text: require the applicant to undergo a medical examination or another medical examination, as the case may be;

children.label: d
children.text: require the applicant to produce travel tickets to a country that the person has right of entry to or evidence of onward travel arrangements that the officer thinks necessary for him or her to determine the application;

children.label: e
children.text: require the applicant to produce evidence of the applicant’s funds for maintenance while in New Zealand or evidence of the applicant’s sponsorship that the officer thinks necessary for him or her to determine the application;

children.label: f
children.text: if not already provided, require the applicant to produce his or her passport or other certificate of identity.

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010, reg 10, 21, 23A

units.heading: Children under the age of 16 travelling alone or with one parent

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: If a child under the age of 16 years is travelling to New Zealand alone or with one parent only, officers may request evidence that both the child's parents have consented to the child being removed from the child's country of residence.

units.heading: No acceptance of immigration applications or requests from unlicensed immigration advisers

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: No immigration application or request put forward on behalf of another person by an unlicensed immigration adviser may be accepted, unless the immigration adviser is exempt from the requirement to be licensed under the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007. If an application or request is accepted automatically, in error, or for any other reason, the application must be refused.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Where an immigration application or request on behalf of another person is not accepted, or is refused, because it contravenes E4.50.25 (a) the relevant person or body must notify that person in writing of that fact, and advise the person as to how the application or request may be re-lodged or advanced in an acceptable manner.

see_also: See also Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007 s 9

units.heading: Persons exempt from licensing

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following persons are exempt from the requirement to be licensed under the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007:

children.label: a
children.text: a person who provides immigration advice in an informal or family context only, where the advice is not provided systematically or for a fee;

children.label: b
children.text: a Member of Parliament, or their staff, who provides immigration advice within the scope of their employment agreement;

children.label: c
children.text: a foreign diplomat or consular staff accorded protection as such under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971;

children.label: d
children.text: an employee of the New Zealand public service who provides immigration advice within the scope of their employment agreement;

children.label: e
children.text: a lawyer who holds a current practising certificate as a barrister or as a barrister and solicitor of the High Court of New Zealand;

children.label: f
children.text: a person employed by or working as a volunteer for a New Zealand community law centre, as defined in section 6 of the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006, where at least one lawyer is on the employing body of the community law centre or is employed by or working as a volunteer for the community law centre in a supervisory capacity;

children.label: g
children.text: a person employed by or working as a volunteer for a New Zealand citizens advice bureau; or

children.label: h
children.text: a person who provides immigration advice only in respect of applications for temporary entry class visas with conditions authorising study in New Zealand, but subject to any regulations made under section 12(1)(b) of the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007; or

children.label: i
children.text: a person exempted by regulations made under section 12 of the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007.

see_also: See also Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007 ss 11, 12

units.heading: Requirements for lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa or entry permission in an immigration control area

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: An application for a temporary entry class visa or entry permission made at an immigration control area must:

children.label: i
children.text: be made on the approved form; and

children.label: ii
children.text: be completed in English; and

children.label: iii
children.text: relate to only one person; and

children.label: iv
children.text: be signed by the applicant.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: E4.50.35 (a)(iv) applies unless the applicant is less than 18 years old, in which case:

children.label: i
children.text: the arrival card must be signed by a parent or guardian of the applicant, if the applicant is accompanied by that person; or

children.label: ii
children.text: the arrival card is not required to be signed, if the applicant is not accompanied by a parent or guardian.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The application must be given to an immigration officer at an immigration control area, together with the applicant's passport or certificate of identity and, if appropriate, evidence of any temporary entry class visa that the applicant holds (except in the case of an application for a military visa in which case M2.1 will apply).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: A person who is eligible to use the automated electronic system may meet the requirements at (c) above by giving their passport to the automated electronic system.

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010 reg 11, 25, 28C

units.heading: Additional requirements

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Before determining the application, the immigration officer processing the application may do one or more of the following:

children.label: a
children.text: require the applicant to be interviewed by an immigration officer; or

children.label: b
children.text: require the applicant to produce further information or evidence (including photographs) that the officer thinks necessary for him or her to determine the application; or

children.label: c
children.text: require the applicant to undergo a medical examination or another medical examination, as the case may be; or

children.label: d
children.text: require the applicant to produce travel tickets to a country that the person has right of entry to or evidence of onward travel arrangements that the officer thinks necessary for him or her to determine the application; or

children.label: e
children.text: require the applicant to produce evidence of the applicant’s funds for maintenance while in New Zealand or evidence of the applicant’s sponsorship that the officer thinks necessary for him or her to determine the application.

units.heading: Applicant to specify address for communication

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Everyone who applies for a visa or entry permission must specify in their application for a visa a physical address in New Zealand to which any communication relating to the application, or to which advice of any visa that may be granted pursuant to that application may be sent, or at which any notice may be served under the Immigration Act 2009.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: An applicant for or holder of a visa or entry permission may at any time, by written notice to an immigration officer, substitute a different address for that specified under E4.50.45 (a).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: An applicant for a visa or entry permission may also specify in an application an electronic address to which any communication relating to the application, or to which advice of any visa that may be granted pursuant to the application, may be sent.

see_also: See also Immigration Act 2009 ss 57(2), (3) and (4), 110, 387

pages.title: New Zealand scholarship students
pages.page_title: U11 New Zealand scholarship students

units.heading: New Zealand scholarship students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A New Zealand scholarship student receives funding from the New Zealand Government through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade under the following schemes:

children.label: i
children.text: New Zealand Scholarships;

children.label: ii
children.text: New Zealand Short Term Training Scholarships;

children.label: iii
children.text: New Zealand Commonwealth Scholarships;

children.label: iv
children.text: New Zealand English Language Training for Officials;

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The objective of the scholarships is for candidates to gain knowledge and skills in specific subject areas that will assist in the development of their home country.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Recipients are required to return to their home country for at least two years after the completion of their scholarship to apply these new skills and knowledge in government, civil society or private business organisations.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (c) above, New Zealand scholarship students who have completed Short Term Training Scholarships or English Language Training for Officials of twelve months or less in duration are required to return to their home country for at least one year after the completion of their scholarship.

units.heading: Foreign government-supported students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A foreign government-supported student receives funding from their home country government to support their study in New Zealand.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A foreign government-supported student must meet the general student requirements under U3.1, and is exempt from having to provide evidence of paying their tuition fees.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: In addition to the requirements at U3.1, a foreign government-supported student must provide a letter from the foreign government:

children.label: i
children.text: that sets out the terms of the student’s sponsorship and undertakes to pay the tuition fees directly to the education provider and pay the student’s living expenses; and

children.label: ii
children.text: states that the student is of good character.

units.heading: Tuition fees

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence of full payment of tuition fees for one year or one programme, whichever is shorter.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: For applicants living outside New Zealand, evidence of payment is not required until after the application has been approved in principle.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, aviation students may provide evidence of full payment of the first term as set out under U6.35.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (a), the following students are not required to provide evidence of tuition fee payment if they can meet the required exemption and provide evidence as below:

blocks.label: table1
blocks.text: | Exemption | Evidence required ; i | Exempt from tuition fees | Confirmation that the programme of study is exempt from fees or that the student is exempt from paying any fees. ; ii | Students participating in a Study Abroad or Non-award scheme under a study abroad partner agreement with a New Zealand Tertiary education institution | Confirmation from the New Zealand tertiary institution that tuition fees are being paid directly to them from a foreign tertiary institution or authorised third party provider on behalf of the foreign tertiary institution. ; iii | Students holding a New Zealand scholarship administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade | Notice of the award of a full New Zealand scholarship. ; iv | Home country government loan approval at a tertiary institution | Evidence that the loan has been applied for and confirmation from the tertiary institution that the fees will be paid directly to them. ; v | Home country government loan approval at a private training establishment (PTE) for study at Bachelor’s degree and above | Evidence that the loan has been applied for and confirmation from the PTE that the fees will be paid directly to them. ; vi | Foreign government-supported student | Meet all requirements as applicable under U12.

pages.title: Definition of 'domestic student'
pages.page_title: U3.35 Definition of 'domestic student'

units.heading: Definition of 'domestic student'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of student instructions a 'domestic student' means a domestic student as defined in section 10(1) of the Education and Training Act 2020. The Ministry of Education holds a complete list of who is considered to be a domestic student for the purpose of fee payment and enrolment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary schooling domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending primary and secondary schools and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue;

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents;

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents;

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current school year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending primary and secondary schools and are exempt from paying foreign tuition fees:

children.label: a
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is in New Zealand to study under an exchange programme approved by the New Zealand Government.

children.label: b
children.text: Children whose application for a residence class visa is under consideration and who are the dependent children of any person who is a New Zealand citizen or the holder of a residence class visa.

children.label: c
children.text: Children whose application for New Zealand citizenship is under consideration and who are the dependent children of a New Zealand citizen.

children.label: d
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is onshore and the holder of a valid work visa other than those excluded under U8.20.

children.label: e
children.text: Students who have, or dependent children of any person who has, made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009.

children.label: f
children.text: Dependent children of a foreign student enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme in a New Zealand university.

children.label: g
children.text: Dependent children of any person who, during the current calendar year, last ceased to hold a special temporary visa (see H2).

children.label: h
children.text: Students who have entered New Zealand for the purposes of adoption and:

children.label: i
children.text: whose adoption application before the New Zealand Family Court (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student) is supported by the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki and who has a letter from the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki confirming this support; or

children.label: ii
children.text: who are the subject of an Interim Order of Adoption granted by the New Zealand Family Court under section 5 of the Adoption Act 1955 (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student); or

children.label: iii
children.text: whose adoption application is through an intercountry adoption process under the Hague Convention on Protection of Children and Co-operation in Respect of Intercountry Adoption 1993 as given effect in New Zealand through the Adoption (Intercountry) Act 1997 and:

children.label: b1
children.text: where at least one of the adoptive parents is a New Zealand citizen, or the holder of a New Zealand residence class visa granted under the Immigration Act 2009; and

children.label: b2
children.text: who has a letter from Oranga Tamariki–Ministry for Children confirming support for the adoption.

children.label: i
children.text: People who are in the custody of the Chief Executive of the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki; pursuant to any of the following orders:

children.label: i
children.text: an order, pursuant to sections 78, 101 or 238(1)(d) of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989, in favour of the Chief Executive of the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 110 of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989, appointing the Chief Executive of the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki as sole guardian; or

children.label: iii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 33 of the Care of Children Act 2004, whereby a child or young person is placed under the Guardianship of the Family Court or the High Court and the Chief Executive of the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki is appointed as agent of the court with power and discretion to place the child.

children.label: j
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand scholarship administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

children.label: k
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a visitor visa granted under V3.115.

children.label: l
children.text: Dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

children.label: m
children.text: Children granted a student visa under U10.5.

children.label: n
children.text: Students who are in New Zealand to study under an exchange scheme approved by the Ministry of Education (see E11.45).

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector (see U5.20) and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions or limited visa in order to undertake a programme of study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue.

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents.

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents.

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current academic year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Despite (d) above, dependent children aged 21 and over of Diplomatic, Consular or Official staff, who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand, may not be eligible for domestic student status and may be required to pay foreign student fees (see H2.1(b)).

children.label: f
children.text: A person who has made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and who is the holder of a valid temporary entry class visa.

children.label: g
children.text: A person who has been recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and whose application for residence is being processed.

children.label: h
children.text: A person who is enrolled at a tertiary education provider for the purpose of participating in industry training funded under the Industry Training Act 1992.

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector and are exempt from paying foreign tuition fees for foreign students:

children.label: a
children.text: Students enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme, in any New Zealand university (see U5.20).

children.label: b
children.text: A person who is in New Zealand to study under a New Zealand Government approved exchange programme at a tertiary education provider.

units.heading: Exchange students

units.heading: Partners and dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2); or

children.label: v
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: vi
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or.

children.label: vii
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all course fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for partners and dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the partner or parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the partner or parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.15 to A5.25.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Despite (a) (v) partners and dependent children of Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) Job Search visa holders may be granted student visas if the related SMC application was under consideration on or before 24 July 2011.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent/s meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is $33,675 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent/s meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent/s:

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent/s do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent/s and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$33,675 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Students aged under 10

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Student visas will only be granted to students aged under 10 who are enrolled in any provider if they will be living in New Zealand with their legal guardian (see U3.30.1) unless:

children.label: i
children.text: they are domestic students (see U3.35); or

children.label: ii
children.text: they are enrolled in a school hostel (see U3.30.10 below) approved by the Code Administrator.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All visas granted under these instructions are subject to the condition that the holder live with their legal guardian (see U3.30.1) in New Zealand, unless the student visa holder has been granted a variation of conditions under U7.25 or one of the exceptions listed in U3.30(a) i-ii applies.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The Code Administrator is the New Zealand Qualifications Authority.

units.heading: Definition of 'legal guardian'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of these instructions a 'legal guardian' is the person with the legal right and responsibility to provide for the care (including education and health) of an international student, and provides for the care of the student in the student's home country. This definition includes the student's biological or adoptive parents, testamentary guardian, or court-appointed guardian.

units.heading: Definition of 'hostel'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of these instructions 'hostel' means a hostel as defined in section 10(1) of the Education and Training Act 2020, and:

children.label: a
children.text: licensed under regulations made under section 643 of the Education and Training Act 2020 (if any); or

children.label: b
children.text: approved and monitored by the Code Administrator, for international students enrolled in Years 1 to 6 of a school, or aged 10 and under and enrolled in any other provider.

pages.title: Who may be included in an application
pages.page_title: E4.1 Who may be included in an application

units.heading: Who may be included in an application

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Each principal applicant must lodge a separate application.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The partner of a principal applicant, and dependent children less than 20 years old, may be included in an application for a:

children.label: i
children.text: visitor visa if intending to travel to and be in New Zealand together; or

children.label: ii
children.text: limited visa in certain circumstances (see L4.5.1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: transit visa if intending to transit through New Zealand together.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: For the purpose of inclusion in an application, a partner is a person who meets the definition of partner in E4.1.20 below. Those who do not meet this definition must apply for a temporary entry class visa in their own right.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children of student, work, diplomatic or military visa applicants must lodge a separate application for a temporary entry class visa appropriate to their needs (see E4.5). Example: A dependent child of an applicant for a work visa intending to attend school in New Zealand must apply for a student visa.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: For the purpose of lodging an application, 'children of the principal applicant' means biological or adopted children of the principal applicant and/or the principal applicant's partner (if the partner is included in the application).

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Evidence of the relationship of each applicant to the principal applicant must be given with the application.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: The requirements in relation to the application (including any that an immigration officer may require an applicant to meet before determining an application) must be met in relation to the principal applicant and each applicant, except that any applicant less than 18 years old is not required to sign the application.

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010 reg 20

units.heading: Who may not be included in an application

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Unless otherwise specified, the following people may not be included in a temporary entry class visa application:

children.label: a
children.text: any child aged 20 and over (whether dependent or not); and

children.label: b
children.text: any child aged 19 and under who is not a dependent child.

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010, reg 20

units.heading: Definition of 'principal applicant'

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For visitor visa and transit visa applications the principal applicant is the person who is declared to be the principal applicant on that application.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: For a work, student, diplomatic or military visa application, the principal applicant is the person applying for the work, student, diplomatic or military visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: For a limited visa the principal applicant is identified as follows:

children.label: i
children.text: the principal applicant is the person who is declared to be the principal applicant on that application; or

children.label: ii
children.text: for applications for a limited visa to be granted for the purpose of study, the principal applicant is the person whose express purpose is study; or

children.label: iii
children.text: if the express purpose of one or more persons in an application is to accompany another person also in the application, the principal applicant must be that other person; or

children.label: iv
children.text: if two or more persons in an application share the same express purpose and that express purpose does not depend on the express purpose of any other person also in the application, the principal applicant may be any one of those two or more persons. Example: A husband and wife, both doctors, wish to attend a medical conference in New Zealand. Their dependent child is to accompany them. Either the husband or the wife may be the principal applicant.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: When an application is assessed, all persons included in the application will be assessed against relevant instructions.

units.heading: Definition of 'dependent child'

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For the purpose of lodging an application, and despite the definition in section 4 of the Immigration Act 2009, a child is dependent if:

children.label: i
children.text: they are under 18 years of age; and

children.label: b1
children.text: they are single; and

children.label: b2
children.text: (if included in an application for a visitor visa, limited visa or transit visa) they are totally or substantially reliant on the principal applicant and/or the principal applicant's partner for financial support, whether living with them or not; or

children.label: b3
children.text: (if applying for a temporary entry class visa under E4.5) they are totally or substantially reliant on that student, work or military visa holder for financial support.

children.label: ii
children.text: they are aged 18 or 19 years; and

children.label: b1
children.text: they are single with no child(ren) of their own; and

children.label: b2
children.text: (if included in an application for a visitor visa, limited visa or transit visa), they are totally or substantially reliant on the principal applicant and/or the principal applicant's partner for financial support, whether living with them or not; or

children.label: b3
children.text: (if applying for a temporary entry class visa under E4.5) they are totally or substantially reliant on that student, work or military visa holder for financial support.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: An unmarried child under 18 years of age is presumed to be dependent unless there is evidence to the contrary.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: For children aged 18 or 19 years of age, evidence of actual dependence may be required.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: For the purpose of lodging an application for a dependent child visitor visa under V3.10 (Partners and dependent children of student or work visa holders) or V3.20 (Dependent children of New Zealand citizens or residence class visa holders), and despite the definition in section 4 of the Immigration Act 2009, a child is also dependent if they meet the specifications under V3.10.20 or V3.20.5.

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010, reg 20

units.heading: Custody of children under the age of 16 years

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: If an applicant is applying for a visa to enter New Zealand for the purpose of marriage to a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder (see V3.35), or for any temporary entry class visa with the intention of remaining in New Zealand for a period of 12 months or more and: immigration officers must be satisfied that the applicant parent has the right to remove the child from its country of residence or from the country in which rights of custody or visitation have been granted, or that the other parent consents to such removal.

children.label: i
children.text: a child under the age of 16 years is included in their application; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a child under the age of 16 years is applying for a different type of visa in order to accompany that parent as provided by E4.5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: that child's other parent is not included in the application or accompanying the child to New Zealand,

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of the right to remove the child from its country of residence, or from the country in which rights of custody or visitation have been granted includes, but is not limited to, legal documents showing that the applicant or accompanying parent has sole custody of the child and the other parent has no visitation rights, and/or a signed statement from the other parent, witnessed in accordance with local practice or law, agreeing to allow the child to remain in New Zealand for their period of intended stay if their entry is approved.

units.heading: Definition of 'partner'

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For the purpose of inclusion in an application, or where a person otherwise relies on such a relationship for the purpose of obtaining a temporary entry class visa, 'partner' means:

children.label: i
children.text: a person who is legally married to; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a person who is in a civil union relationship with; or

children.label: iii
children.text: a person who is in a de facto relationship with

children.label: b1
children.text: a principal applicant in an application for a temporary entry class visa; or

children.label: b2
children.text: a person who is a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder; or

children.label: b3
children.text: a person who is an applicant for, or the holder of a student, work, or military visa; and

children.label: iv
children.text: they are in a genuine and stable partnership (see E4.5.25).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite the definition of partner contained in regulation 4 of the Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010, references to 'partner' in temporary entry instructions mean 'partner' as defined in (a) above.

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010, reg 4, reg 20

units.heading: Eligibility of partners in polygamous relationships

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: In the case of polygamous partnerships (as an exception to the exclusivity requirement which forms part of the definition of a genuine and stable partnership (see E4.5.25)) only one partner will be eligible for a temporary entry class visa on the basis of their partnership with a person described in E4.1.20(a)(i-iii).

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A visa waiver means a waiver of the requirement to hold a visa permitting travel to New Zealand in relation to any class of persons. A person travelling to New Zealand visa waiver is required to hold an Electronic Travel Authority (ETA) unless exempt (see E12 Electronic Travel Authority). A visa waiver applies to, but is not limited to, the following people:

children.label: a
children.text: citizens of the Commonwealth of Australia; and

children.label: b
children.text: people who hold:

children.label: i
children.text: a current permanent residence visa issued by the Government of Australia; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a current resident return visa issued by the Government of Australia; and

children.label: c
children.text: people granted a visa waiver by special direction; and

children.label: d
children.text: members of a visiting force (including members of the civilian component of the visiting force) but only if:

children.label: i
children.text: each person is travelling to New Zealand in the ordinary course of the person’s duty or employment; and

children.label: ii
children.text: each person is seeking a temporary entry class visa at an immigration control area; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the craft transporting the visiting force is a commercial craft; and

children.label: e
children.text: members of, or any person associated with, a scientific programme or expedition under the auspices of a Contracting Party to the Antarctic Treaty (within the meaning of the Antarctica Act 1960) or any person to whom section 5 of that Act applies, but only if:

children.label: i
children.text: the person concerned is seeking a temporary entry class visa; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the application is made at an immigration control area; and

children.label: f
children.text: cruise ship passengers; and

children.label: g
children.text: cruise ship crew travelling in the ordinary course of business of the ship; and

children.label: h
children.text: positioning cruise ship crew; and

children.label: i
children.text: aircraft crew of an aircraft on a flight between any other country and New Zealand in the course of a scheduled international service; and

children.label: j
children.text: positioning aircraft crew; and

children.label: k
children.text: cargo ship passengers travelling between any foreign port and New Zealand (from 1 April 2025 onwards); and

children.label: l
children.text: cargo ship crew travelling in the ordinary course of business of the ship between any foreign port and New Zealand (from 1 April 2025 onwards); and

children.label: m
children.text: crew on a foreign ship authorised by the Minister of Transport under section 198(2) of the Maritime Transport Act 1994 to carry coastal cargo within the meaning of section 198(6) of that Act (from 1 April 2025 onwards); and

children.label: n
children.text: positioning cargo ship crew (from 1 April 2025 onwards); and

children.label: o
children.text: British citizens, and other British passport holders who produce evidence of the right to reside permanently in the United Kingdom, but only if the person concerned is seeking a visitor visa current for not more than six months and the purposes of the visit do not include medical consultation or treatment; and

children.label: p
children.text: people travelling on a United Nations (UN) laissez-passer who are seeking a visitor visa current for not more than three months; and

children.label: q
children.text: any other class of persons specified in the Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010; and

children.label: r
children.text: citizens of the following countries, but only if the person concerned is seeking a visitor visa current for not more than three months and the purposes of the visit is not for medical consultation or treatment: Andorra Argentina Austria Bahrain Belgium Brazil Brunei Bulgaria Canada Chile Croatia Cyprus Czech Republic Denmark Estonia 1 Finland France Germany Greece 2 Hong Kong 3 Hungary Iceland Ireland Israel Italy Japan Korea (South) Kuwait (suspended 8) Latvia 1 Liechtenstein Lithuania 1 Luxembourg Macau 4 Malaysia Malta Mauritius Mexico Monaco Netherlands Norway Oman Poland Portugal 5 Qatar Romania San Marino Saudi Arabia Seychelles Singapore Slovak Republic Slovenia Spain Sweden Switzerland Taiwan 6 United Arab Emirates United States of America 7 Uruguay Vatican City 1 Visa waiver does not apply to people travelling on alien's (non-citizen's) passports issued by these countries. 2 Greek passport holders whose passports were issued on and after 1 January 2006. (Greek passports issued before 1 January 2006 are not acceptable for travel after 1 January 2007, see A2.10.50) 3 Residents of Hong Kong travelling on Hong Kong Special Administrative Region or British National (Overseas) passports. 4 Residents of Macau travelling on Macau Special Administrative Region passports. 5 Portuguese passport holders must also have the right to live permanently in Portugal. 6 Permanent residents of Taiwan travelling on Taiwan passports. A personal identity number printed within the visible section of the biographical page of the Taiwan passport demonstrates that the holder is a permanent resident of Taiwan (see A2.10.40). 7 including nationals of the USA. 8 Kuwait’s visa waiver status is suspended from 11:59pm on 12 November 2026 to 11:59pm on 11 February 2027 as per a special direction made by the Minister of Immigration on 4 November 2026.

children.label: s
children.text: citizens of the following countries, but only if:

children.label: i
children.text: the person concerned is seeking a visitor visa current for not more than three months; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the purpose of the visit is not for medical consultation or treatment; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the person is travelling from Australia; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the person holds one of the eligible Australian visa types as set out at E2.1.1 below.

pages.title: Dependent children of military visa holders
pages.page_title: U8.15 Dependent children of military visa holders

units.heading: Dependent children of military visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of military visa holders may be granted student visas for the same period as the military visa held, or deemed to be held, by the applicant's parent.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Applicants meet temporary entry class requirements for lodging an application as set out at E4, bona fide applicants as set out at E5, and health and character requirements as set out at A4.5 and A5.5, but are exempt from:

children.label: i
children.text: providing evidence of enrolment; and

children.label: ii
children.text: providing guarantees of accommodation and maintenance; and

children.label: iii
children.text: meeting onward travel requirements.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of military visa holders are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) in the following respects:

children.label: i
children.text: for the purpose of all tuition fees for the period of secondment; and

children.label: ii
children.text: until the end of the calendar year in which their parent completes their posting in New Zealand.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The student visas granted must be current for the period of enrolment or until the parent holding a military visa departs, whichever occurs first.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: If the student wishes to continue studying in New Zealand after their parent departs, they must meet the requirements under the immigration instructions for a temporary visa and obtain one accordingly.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Before granting a student visa an immigration officer must be satisfied that the applicant's parent:

children.label: i
children.text: holds a military visa; or

children.label: ii
children.text: is eligible to be granted a military visa; or

children.label: iii
children.text: is deemed to be granted a military visa.
