pages.title: Dependent children of work visa holders
pages.page_title: U8.20 Dependent children of work visa holders

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: v
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or

children.label: vi
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4); or

children.label: vii
children.text: seasonal workers under Specific Purpose Instructions; or

children.label: viii
children.text: seasonal workers under seasonal AEWV pathways (see WA1.10(a)(ii)); or

children.label: ix
children.text: Short-term Graduate work visa instructions (see WD5); or

children.label: x
children.text: India Iconic Work Instructions (see WI21); or

children.label: xi
children.text: India Skilled Work Instructions (see WI22); or

children.label: xii
children.text: Independent Professional, or Contractual Service Supplier under Specific Purpose instructions (see WS).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, the eligibility of dependent children of Accredited Employer work visa holders and Specific Purpose work visa holders under the NOL subcategory (see WS2.1.1(o) – instructions effective 8 September 2025) for student visas is set out at U8.20.2 below.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, a dependent child of the holder of a Migrant Exploitation Protection work visa (MEPV) may be granted a student visa under these instructions only if, as at the time they apply, the dependent child is in New Zealand on a visa that was granted on the basis of the visa held by the MEPV holder immediately prior to the MEPV holder’s current visa. If granted, the visa’s duration must be for the same period as the MEPV holder’s visa, and will not include multiple entry travel conditions.

units.heading: Dependent children of Accredited Employer work visa holders and certain Specific Purpose work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of an Accredited Employer work visa holder or a Specific Purpose work visa holder under the NOL subcategory (see WS2.1.1(o) – instructions effective 8 September 2025) may be granted a student visa if their supporting parent is:

children.label: i
children.text: in a role classified as ANZSCO skill level 1, 2 or 3 (including roles treated at a higher skill level under WA3.16(d) at the Job Check); or

children.label: ii
children.text: in a role classified as NOL skill level 1, 2 or 3 and listed at Appendix 20; or

children.label: iii
children.text: paid at or above 1.5x the Skilled Migrant Category median wage (see SR3.20(a)(ii)); or

children.label: iv
children.text: in a role on the Green List and meets the applicable requirements (see Appendix 13); or

children.label: v
children.text: in acceptable employment under the Transport Sector or Care Sector Work to Residence policies as defined in SR6.10 or SR7.10 with the exception of the requirement to have completed 24 months of work in New Zealand in that occupation.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite the requirement to determine applications for temporary entry in accordance with the instructions in effect at the time an application is made (E7.10(a)(ii)), the exception set out at (a)(v) above applies to any application that was submitted before 6 October 2024 and as of that date had not been decided.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of an Accredited Employer work visa holder working in a role at ANZSCO skill level 4 or 5 cannot be granted a student visa as a dependent child, unless:

children.label: i
children.text: on 26 June 2024, they held a visa as a dependent child of the Accredited Employer work visa holder; or

children.label: ii
children.text: on 26 June 2024, they had an application in progress for a visa as a dependent child of the Accredited Employer work visa holder and that application was subsequently granted; or

children.label: iii
children.text: their Accredited Employer work visa holder parent is described in (a)(iii) to (v) above.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: An Accredited Employer work visa holder or a Specific Purpose work visa holder under the NOL subcategory (see WS2.1.1(o) – instructions effective 8 September 2025) whose dependent child is applying for a student visa under these instructions must meet the minimum income threshold specified in U8.20.6 below.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Despite (d) above, the minimum income threshold does not apply if the supporting work visa holder(s) currently meet the previous income threshold in place on 9 March 2025 (as per U8.20(a)), and on 9 March 2025:

children.label: i
children.text: the dependent child held a visa as a dependent child of the AEWV holder, or had applied for a visa as a dependent of the AEWV holder on or before 9 March 2025 and that application has not been completed; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the dependent child’s parent(s) held an AEWV or Essential Skills work visa, or had applied for an Accredited Employer work visa on or before 9 March 2025 that was subsequently granted; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the maximum continuous stay period that applied to their parent on 9 March 2025 has not yet been reached.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold (see U8.20.6 below).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite U8.20.6(a), dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

units.heading: Minimum income threshold

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$58,240 gross per annum.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of the parent or parents holding an Accredited Employer work visa, Specific Purpose work visa holder under the NOL subcategory (see WS2.1.1(o) – instructions effective 8 September 2025) or an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the supporting work visa holder’s current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant’s parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child’s visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Accredited Employer work visas, or Specific Purpose work visas under the NOL subcategory (see WS2.1.1(o) – instructions effective 8 September 2025) or Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$58,240 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a)(i) above, the minimum income threshold does not apply if the parent(s) currently meet the previous income threshold in place on 9 March 2025 (as per U8.20.6 (a)), and on 9 March 2025:

children.label: i
children.text: the dependent child held a visa as a dependent child of the Religious work visa holder, or had applied on or before that date for a visa as a dependent of the Religious work visa holder and that application has not been completed; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the dependent child’s parent(s) held a Religious Work visa, or had applied on or before that date for a Religious Work visa that was subsequently granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

pages.title: Samoan Quota Scheme
pages.page_title: S1.10 Samoan Quota Scheme

units.heading: Samoan Quota Scheme
Objective

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The Samoan Quota Scheme allows up to 1,100 Samoan citizens to be granted a resident visa each year. The total number of Samoan citizens granted resident visas under this category includes principal applicants, their partners, and dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, an additional 550 resident visas may be granted to Samoan citizens each year for the four years from 2023 to 2026 following the closure of the registration period and the electronic draw of the ballot registrations in each year. Note: This reallocation of unused places is due the closure of the scheme between 2020-2021. This additional 550 resident visas that may be granted each year to Samoan citizens under this category includes principal applicants, their partners, and dependent children.

units.heading: Criteria for a resident visa

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: To qualify for a resident visa under the Samoan Quota Scheme, the principal applicant must:

children.label: i
children.text: be a Samoan citizen (having been born in Samoa or born overseas to a Samoan citizen who was born in Samoa); and

children.label: ii
children.text: be either in Samoa or lawfully in New Zealand at the time their application for a resident visa is made; and

children.label: iii
children.text: have their registration drawn from the Samoan Quota Scheme pool; and

children.label: iv
children.text: lodge their application for a resident visa under the Samoan Quota Scheme within eight months of written advice from INZ that their registration has been drawn from the Samoan Quota Scheme pool; and

children.label: v
children.text: have been aged between 18 and 45 (inclusive) at the registration closing date; and

children.label: vi
children.text: have an acceptable offer of employment, or have a partner included in the application who has an acceptable offer of employment (see S1.10.30 below); and

children.label: vii
children.text: (if they have dependent children) meet the minimum income requirement (see S1.10.35 below); and

children.label: viii
children.text: meet a minimum level of English language ability (see S1.10.45 below); and

children.label: ix
children.text: meet health and character requirements (see A4 and A5).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children of the principal applicant who are included in the resident visa application must also meet health and character requirements for a resident visa (see A4 and A5).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: An immigration officer may extend the eight month timeframe referred to in paragraph (a)(iv) if the officer believes the special circumstances of the applicant justify such an extension.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: A Director Visa, or Operations Director (or a person in a higher line management position) may extend the eight month timeframe referred to in paragraph (a)(iv) in relation to a class of applicants if they believe the special circumstances of the class of applicants justify such an extension.

units.heading: Registration process

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Principal registrants may register for entry into the Samoan Quota pool within a set registration period. The dates of the registration period will be announced each year prior to the registration opening.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Principal registrants must be aged between 18 and 45 (inclusive) at the registration closing date for their registration to be accepted into the ballot.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Registrations must be made on the appropriate registration form for the Samoan Quota Scheme.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Registrations must be submitted during the registration period to the appropriate receiving office specified in the appropriate registration guide for the Samoan Quota Scheme.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Registrations will be accepted for entry into the ballot only if they are fully completed, signed by the principal registrant, and accompanied by any documents or evidence specified as required by the registration form.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Any person included in a registration must either:

children.label: i
children.text: be in New Zealand lawfully at the time the registration is made; or

children.label: ii
children.text: be offshore at the time the registration is made.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Any person who has previously overstayed in New Zealand, but has departed voluntarily, and is not subject to a removal order or period of prohibition on entry, can register under the Samoan Quota Scheme.

units.heading: Definition of 'principal registrant'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The principal registrant is the person who is declared to be the principal registrant on the registration application form and who intends to be the principal applicant of any resulting resident visa application.

units.heading: Inclusion in registration of immediate family members of the principal registrant

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Where the principal registrant has a partner and/or dependent children all of those people must be included in the registration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If a registration is successful in the pool draw, only a partner and/or dependent children included in the registration may be included in the resulting application for a resident visa under the Samoan Quota Scheme. This limitation applies despite R2.1 concerning the inclusion of family members in an application.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Any partner and/or dependent children who were eligible for inclusion in the registration but were not included must not subsequently be granted a residence class visa under the Partnership or Dependent Child Categories.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) and (c) above, a partner or dependent child who was included in the registration but not in the resulting application for a resident visa may be granted a residence class visa as a principal applicant under the Partnership or Dependent Child Categories.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Notwithstanding (b) above, in the event an applicant includes any partner and/or dependent child in their application who was not included in their registration, officers should allow the principal applicant an opportunity to explain the non-declaration in accordance with R5.15 before applying the limitation referred to in (b).

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Where a person is not eligible to be included at the time of registration but is eligible at the time of the application for a resident visa (e.g. in the case of a new-born child), they may be included in the resident visa application provided R2.1 is met.

units.heading: Number of registrations that may be lodged

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Registrants must lodge (or be included in) only one registration within the registration period. If a registration is lodged that includes registrants who are already included in a registration accepted by INZ, the subsequent registration(s) will not be accepted.

units.heading: Selection process following closure of registration

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: As soon as practicable following the closure of the registration period, INZ will conduct an electronic draw.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Registrations will be randomly drawn from the pool until the appropriate number of potential applicants to fill the number of available places within the annual period has been drawn.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Principal registrants whose registrations have been drawn from the pool will be notified by INZ in the month following the draw that their registration has been successful, and will be invited to lodge an application for a resident visa under the Samoan Quota Scheme at the appropriate receiving office of INZ not more than eight months after the date of that advice.

units.heading: Acceptable offers of employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Acceptable offers of employment may be in either a skilled or unskilled occupation but must be for on-going and sustainable employment. On-going and sustainable employment is:

children.label: i
children.text: an offer of employment or current employment with a single employer which is permanent, or indefinite, and of which the employer is in a position to meet the terms specified; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an offer of employment or current employment, with a single employer for a stated term of at least 12 months. Note: When assessing whether employment is sustainable, officers may consider, but are not limited to, such factors as the residence status of the employer, the period for which the employing organisation has been established as a going concern, and the financial sustainability of the employing organisation. Where an offer of employment or current employment is for a stated term of at least 12 months, the stated term must be valid both at the time the application is lodged and when the application is decided, in particular: ~ if the applicant has current employment, he or she must be in that employment, or ~ if the applicant has an offer of employment, the offer must continue to be valid.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Acceptable offers of employment must also be:

children.label: i
children.text: for full-time employment (employment is full-time if it amounts to, on average, at least 30 hours per week) unless S1.10.35.1(c) applies; and

children.label: ii
children.text: current at the time of assessing the application and at the time of grant of the visa; and

children.label: iii
children.text: genuine; and

children.label: iv
children.text: for a position that is paid by salary or wages (i.e. positions of self-employment, payment by commission and/or retainer are not acceptable); and

children.label: v
children.text: accompanied by evidence of professional or technical registration if this is required by law to take up the offer; and

children.label: vi
children.text: compliant with all relevant employment law in force in New Zealand.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: An acceptable offer of employment must be from an employer who complies with all relevant employment and immigration law in force in New Zealand. Compliance with relevant New Zealand employment and immigration law will be assessed on the basis of past and current behaviour, and includes, but is not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: paying employees no less than the applicable minimum wage rate; and

children.label: ii
children.text: meeting holiday and leave entitlements and other minimum statutory requirements; and

children.label: iii
children.text: meeting occupational safety and health obligations; and

children.label: iv
children.text: only employing people who are entitled to work in New Zealand.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: An employer is considered to not have a history of compliance with employment law if it fails to meet the requirements set out at R5.110 or if it is included on a list of non-compliant employers maintained by the Labour Inspectorate (see Appendix 10).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: For the purposes of S1.10.30(a) (ii), INZ must be satisfied that the employer:

children.label: i
children.text: has genuine reasons based on reasonable grounds for specifying that the employment is for a stated term; and

children.label: ii
children.text: has advised the employee of when or how their employment will end and the reasons for their employment ending; and

children.label: iii
children.text: is in a position to meet the terms specified.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: ‘Genuine reasons’ for the purposes of S1.10.30(e)(i) do not include reasons:

children.label: i
children.text: that exclude or limit the rights of a person under employment law; or

children.label: ii
children.text: to determine the suitability of a person for permanent or indefinite employment Note: In order meet employment law, employment agreements that are for a stated term must specify in writing the way in which the employment will end and the reasons for ending the employment.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the principal applicant has dependent children, the offer of employment must also meet the minimum income requirement set out at S1.10.35 below.

units.heading: Minimum income requirement

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Principal applicants with dependent children must show that they will meet the minimum income requirement if they come to New Zealand, which is intended to ensure they can support themselves and their dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The gross minimum income requirement is NZ$55,404.96. This is based on the Jobseeker Support (married and civil union rate) plus the maximum Accommodation Supplement (as set by the New Zealand Government).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The minimum income requirement must be derived from an acceptable offer of employment - see S1.10.30.

units.heading: Ability to include partner's income as part of the minimum income requirement

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: If both the principal applicant and their partner included in their application have an acceptable offer of employment in New Zealand, both of their wages or salaries may be taken into account when determining if the minimum income requirement is met.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: In such cases the partner's employment and income will only be taken into account if, at the time the application is assessed, an immigration officer is satisfied the principal applicant and partner have been living together for 12 months or more in a partnership that is genuine and stable (R2.1.15.1(b) and R2.1.15.5(a)(i))).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where the employment (and income) of both the principal applicant and their partner is used to meet the minimum income requirement, both offers of employment must meet all the requirements in S1.10.30 except that only one has to meet the requirement that the offer be for full-time employment.

units.heading: Evidence of employment offer

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Evidence of an offer of employment is original or certified copies of the following documents:

children.label: i
children.text: a written offer of employment; and

children.label: ii
children.text: a detailed job description; and

children.label: iii
children.text: an employment agreement entered into by the employer and the principal applicant, stating:

children.label: b1
children.text: the terms of employment; and

children.label: b2
children.text: the hours of work; and

children.label: b3
children.text: the period during which employment may begin.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Additional evidence may include, but is not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: any information requested by INZ; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the results of any verification undertaken by INZ; and

children.label: iii
children.text: information from the employer or recruitment agency.

units.heading: Minimum English language requirement

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The immigration officer determines whether principal applicants meet the minimum English language requirement by assessing whether they are able to:

children.label: a
children.text: read English; and

children.label: b
children.text: understand and respond to questions in English; and

children.label: c
children.text: maintain an English language conversation about themselves, their family or their background.

units.heading: Determining applications

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The immigration officer must sight the original job offer and verify that it is genuine and current by checking:

children.label: i
children.text: directly with the employer; or

children.label: ii
children.text: through the nearest office of INZ to the employer in New Zealand; or

children.label: iii
children.text: by some other appropriate arrangement.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The immigration officer must then assess the applicant's English language ability against the criteria at S1.10.45 above.

units.heading: Grant of visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: If an application for a resident visa under the Samoan Quota Scheme is approved and the applicant is in New Zealand lawfully, a resident visa will be granted.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If an application for a resident visa under the Samoan Quota Scheme is approved and the applicant is in Samoa, the principal applicant will be granted with a resident visa with travel conditions allowing first entry within three months, while the partner and dependent children will be granted resident visas with travel conditions allowing first entry within 12 months.

pages.title: Pacific Access Category
pages.page_title: S1.40 Pacific Access Category

units.heading: Pacific Access Category
Objective

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The Pacific Access Category allows up to 250 citizens of Fiji, 250 citizens of Tonga, 75 citizens of Tuvalu, and 75 citizens of Kiribati to be granted residence class visas in New Zealand each year. The total number of individuals granted resident visas under each category includes principal applicants, their partners and dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, an additional 650 resident visas may be granted to citizens of the participating countries each year for 2023 and 2024 following the closure of the registration period and the electronic draw of the ballot registrations in each year. The additional resident visas for each year and country are as follows:

children.label: i
children.text: Fiji – 250 citizens

children.label: ii
children.text: Tonga – 250 citizens

children.label: iii
children.text: Tuvalu - 75 citizens

children.label: iv
children.text: Kiribati – 75 citizens

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: This reallocation of unused places is due the closure of the scheme between 2020-2021. The additional 650 resident visas may be granted each year to individuals from the participating countries under each category includes principal applicants, their partners and dependent children.

units.heading: Criteria for a resident visa

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: To qualify for a resident visa under the Pacific Access Category, the principal applicant must:

children.label: i
children.text: be a citizen of Fiji, Tonga, Tuvalu, or Kiribati; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have their Pacific Access Category registration drawn from the relevant Fiji, Tonga, Tuvalu, or Kiribati pool of the Pacific Access Category; and

children.label: iii
children.text: lodge their application for a resident visa under the Pacific Access Category within eight months of written advice from INZ that their registration has been drawn from the relevant Fiji, Tonga, Tuvalu, or Kiribati pool of the Pacific Access Category; and

children.label: iv
children.text: have been aged between 18 and 45 (inclusive) at the registration closing date; and

children.label: v
children.text: have an acceptable offer of employment or have a partner, included in the application, who has an acceptable offer of employment (see S1.40.30 below); and

children.label: vi
children.text: (if they have dependent children) meet the minimum income requirement set out at S1.40.35 below; and

children.label: vii
children.text: meet a minimum level of English language ability (see S1.40.45 below); and

children.label: viii
children.text: meet health and character requirements (see A4 and A5).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Principal applicants who are citizens of Fiji:

children.label: i
children.text: must be either in Fiji or lawfully in New Zealand at the time their application under the Pacific Access Category is made; and

children.label: ii
children.text: must have been born in Fiji or born overseas to a Fijian citizen who was born in Fiji.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Principal applicants who are citizens of Tonga:

children.label: i
children.text: must be either in Tonga or lawfully in New Zealand at the time their application under the Pacific Access Category is made; and

children.label: ii
children.text: must have been born in Tonga or born overseas to a Tongan citizen who was born in Tonga.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Principal applicants who are citizens of Kiribati:

children.label: i
children.text: must be either in Kiribati or Fiji or lawfully in New Zealand at the time their application under the Pacific Access Category is made; and

children.label: ii
children.text: must have been born in Kiribati or born overseas to a Kiribati citizen who was born in Kiribati.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Principal applicants who are citizens of Tuvalu:

children.label: i
children.text: must be either in Tuvalu or Fiji or lawfully in New Zealand at the time their application under the Pacific Access Category is made; and

children.label: ii
children.text: must have been born in Tuvalu or born overseas to a Tuvaluan citizen who was born in Tuvalu.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children included in applications under the Pacific Access Category must also meet health and character requirements (see A4 and A5).

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: An immigration officer may extend the eight-month timeframe referred to in paragraph (a)(iii) if the officer believes the special circumstances of the applicant justify such an extension.

blocks.label: h
blocks.text: A Director Visa, or Operations Director (or a person in a higher line management position) may extend the eight-month timeframe referred to in paragraph (a)(iii) in relation to a class of applicants if they believe the special circumstances of the class of applicants justify such an extension.

units.heading: Registration process

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Principal registrants may register for entry into the relevant Fiji, Tonga, Tuvalu, or Kiribati pool of the Pacific Access Category within a set registration period. The dates of the registration period will be announced each year prior to the registration opening.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Principal registrants must be aged between 18 and 45 (inclusive) at the registration closing date for their registration to be accepted into the ballot.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Registrations must be made on the appropriate registration form for the Pacific Access Category.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Registrations must be submitted during the registration period to the appropriate receiving office specified on the Pacific Access Category registration guide applicable to the country.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Registrations will be accepted for entry into the ballot only if they are fully completed, signed by the principal registrant, submitted together with the appropriate fee and accompanied by any documents or evidence as required by the registration form.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Any person included in a registration must either:

children.label: i
children.text: be in New Zealand lawfully at the time the registration is made; or

children.label: ii
children.text: be offshore at the time the registration is made.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Any person who has previously overstayed in New Zealand, but has departed voluntarily, and is not subject to a removal order or period of prohibition on entry, can register under the Pacific Access Category.

units.heading: Definition of 'principal registrant'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The principal registrant is the person who is declared to be the principal registrant on the registration application form and who intends to be the principal applicant of any resulting residence class visa application.

units.heading: Inclusion in registration of immediate family members of the principal registrant

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Where the principal registrant has a partner and/or dependent children all of those people must be included in the registration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If a registration is successful in the pool draw, only a partner and/or dependent children included in the registration may be included in the resulting application for a resident visa under the Pacific Access Category. This limitation applies despite R2.1 concerning the inclusion of family members in an application.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Any partner and/or dependent children who were eligible for inclusion in the registration but were not included must not subsequently be granted a residence class visa under the Partnership or Dependent Child Categories.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) and (c) above, a partner or dependent child who was included in the registration but not in the resulting application for a resident visa may be granted a residence class visa as a principal applicant under the Partnership or Dependent Child Categories.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Notwithstanding (b) above, in the event an applicant includes any partner and/or dependent child in their application who was not included in their registration, officers should allow the principal applicant an opportunity to explain the non-declaration in accordance with R5.15 before applying the limitation referred to in (b).

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Where a person is not eligible to be included at the time of registration but is eligible at the time of the application for a resident visa (e.g. in the case of a new-born child), they may be included in the resident visa application provided R2.1 is met.

units.heading: Number of registrations that may be lodged

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Registrants must lodge (or be included in) only one registration within the registration period. If a registration is lodged that includes registrants who are already included in a registration accepted by INZ, the subsequent registration(s) will not be accepted.

units.heading: Selection process following closure of registration

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: INZ will conduct an electronic draw as soon as practicable after the closure of the registration period.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Registrations will be randomly drawn from the pool of registrations, until the appropriate number of potential registrants to meet the various quotas of available places within the annual period has been drawn.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Principal registrants whose registrations have been drawn from the various pools will be notified by INZ in the month following the draw that their registration has been successful and that they must lodge a full application under the Pacific Access Category to the appropriate receiving office of INZ not more than eight months after the date of that advice.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Principal registrants who are unsuccessful in the registration process within a particular registration period are able to re-register within subsequent registration periods at a reduced fee.

units.heading: Acceptable offers of employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Acceptable offers of employment may be in either a skilled or unskilled occupation but must be for on-going and sustainable employment. On-going and sustainable employment is:

children.label: i
children.text: an offer of employment or current employment with a single employer which is permanent, or indefinite, and of which the employer is in a position to meet the terms specified; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an offer of employment or current employment, with a single employer for a stated term of at least 12 months. Note: When assessing whether employment is sustainable, officers may consider, but are not limited to, such factors as the residence status of the employer, the period for which the employing organisation has been established as a going concern, and the financial sustainability of the employing organisation. Where an offer of employment or current employment is for a stated term of at least 12 months, the stated term must be valid both at the time the application is lodged and when the application is decided, in particular: ~ if the applicant has current employment, he or she must be in that employment, or ~ if the applicant has an offer of employment, the offer must continue to be valid.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Acceptable offers of employment must also be:

children.label: i
children.text: for full-time employment (employment is full-time if it amounts to, on average, at least 30 hours per week) unless S1.40.35.1 (c) applies; and

children.label: ii
children.text: current at the time of assessing the application and at the time of grant the visa; and

children.label: iii
children.text: genuine; and

children.label: iv
children.text: for a position that is paid by salary or wages (i.e. positions of self-employment, payment by commission and/or retainer are not acceptable); and

children.label: v
children.text: accompanied by evidence of professional or technical registration if this is required by law to take up the offer; and

children.label: vi
children.text: compliant with all relevant employment law in force in New Zealand.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: An acceptable offer of employment must be from an employer who complies with all relevant employment and immigration law in force in New Zealand. Compliance with relevant New Zealand employment and immigration law will be assessed on the basis of past and current behaviour, and includes, but is not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: paying employees no less than the applicable minimum wage rate; and

children.label: ii
children.text: meeting holiday and leave entitlements and other minimum statutory requirements; and

children.label: iii
children.text: meeting occupational safety and health obligations; and

children.label: iv
children.text: only employing people who are entitled to work in New Zealand.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: An employer is considered to not have a history of compliance with employment law if it fails to meet the requirements set out at R5.110 or if it is included on a list of non-compliant employers maintained by the Labour Inspectorate (see Appendix 10).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: For the purposes of S1.40.30(a)(ii), INZ must be satisfied that the employer:

children.label: i
children.text: has genuine reasons based on reasonable grounds for specifying that the employment is for a stated term; and

children.label: ii
children.text: has advised the employee of when or how their employment will end and the reasons for their employment ending; and

children.label: iii
children.text: is in a position to meet the terms specified.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: ‘Genuine reasons’ for the purposes of S1.40.30(e)(i) do not include reasons:

children.label: i
children.text: that exclude or limit the rights of a person under employment law; or

children.label: ii
children.text: to determine the suitability of a person for permanent or indefinite employment. Note: In order to meet employment law, employment agreements that are for a stated term must specify in writing the way in which the employment will end and the reasons for ending the employment.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the principal applicant has dependent children, the offer of employment must also meet the minimum income requirement set out at S1.40.35 below.

units.heading: Minimum income requirement

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Principal applicants with dependent children must show that they will meet the minimum income requirement if they come to New Zealand, which is intended to ensure they can support themselves and their dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The gross minimum income requirement is NZ $55,404.96. This is based on the Jobseeker Support (married and civil union rate) plus the maximum Accommodation Supplement (as set by the New Zealand Government).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The minimum income requirement must be derived from the acceptable offer of employment - see S1.40.30.

units.heading: Ability to include the partner's income as part of the minimum income requirement

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: If both the principal applicant and their partner included in their application have an acceptable offer of employment in New Zealand, both of their wages or salaries may be taken into account when determining if the minimum income requirement is met.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: In such cases the partner's employment and income will only be taken into account if, at the time the application is assessed, an immigration officer is satisfied the principal applicant and partner have been living together for 12 months or more in a partnership that is genuine and stable (see R2.1.15.1(b) and R2.1.15.5(a)(i)).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where the employment (and income) of both the principal applicant and their partner is used to meet the minimum income requirement, both offers of employment must meet all the requirements in S1.40.30, except that only one has to meet the requirement that the offer be for full-time employment.

units.heading: Evidence of employment offer

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Evidence of an offer of employment is original or certified copies of the following documents:

children.label: i
children.text: a written offer of employment; and

children.label: ii
children.text: a detailed job description; and

children.label: iii
children.text: a letter from the employer stating whether or not any occupational registration is required by law for the principal applicant to take up the position; and

children.label: iv
children.text: an employment agreement entered into by the employer and the principal applicant, stating:

children.label: b1
children.text: the terms of employment; and

children.label: b2
children.text: the hours of work; and

children.label: b3
children.text: the period during which employment may begin.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Additional evidence may include, but is not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: any information requested by INZ; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the results of any verification undertaken by INZ; and

children.label: iii
children.text: information from the employer or recruitment agency.

units.heading: Minimum English language requirement

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Immigration officers determine whether principal applicants meet the minimum English language requirement by assessing whether they are able to:

children.label: a
children.text: read English; and

children.label: b
children.text: understand and respond to questions in English; and

children.label: c
children.text: maintain an English language conversation about themselves, their family, or their background.

units.heading: Determining applications

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Immigration officers must sight the original job offer and verify that it is genuine and current by checking:

children.label: i
children.text: directly with the employer; or

children.label: ii
children.text: through the nearest office of INZ to the employer in New Zealand; or

children.label: iii
children.text: by some other appropriate arrangement.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Immigration officers must assess the applicant's English language ability against the criteria at S1.40.45 above.

units.heading: Grant of visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: If an application for a resident visa under the Pacific Access Category is approved and the applicant is in New Zealand lawfully, a resident visa will be granted.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If an application for a resident visa under the Pacific Access Category is approved and the applicant is in Fiji, Tonga, Kiribati, or Tuvalu, the principal applicant will be granted a resident visa with travel conditions allowing first entry within three months, while the partner and dependent children will be granted resident visas with travel conditions allowing first entry within 12 months.

pages.title: Persons requiring a student visa
pages.page_title: U2.1 Persons requiring a student visa (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Persons requiring a student visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A person must obtain a student visa in order to undertake study or training in New Zealand, unless they are:

children.label: a
children.text: a New Zealand citizen; or

children.label: b
children.text: the holder of a residence class visa; or

children.label: c
children.text: the holder of a student visa; or

children.label: d
children.text: the holder of a limited visa granted for the express purpose of attending a course of study or training; or

children.label: e
children.text: the holder of any other type of temporary entry class visa whose conditions have been varied to authorise the holder to undertake a course of study in New Zealand; or

children.label: f
children.text: covered by the provisions of U2.5.

pages.title: Offer of a place
pages.page_title: U3.5 Offer of a place (30/07/2012)

units.heading: Offer of a place

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Applicants must have an offer of a place with a New Zealand education provider, which shows:

children.label: a
children.text: the name of the programme or training scheme and the minimum time required for completing it; and

children.label: b
children.text: evidence that the programme or training scheme and education provider meet foreign student requirements (see U5); and

children.label: c
children.text: confirmation that the education provider has assessed and is satisfied the prospective student meets the course competencies and enrolment provision (section 7.1) as set out in the Code of Practice for the Pastoral Care of International Students; and

children.label: d
children.text: the amount of the fee for the complete programme or training scheme, or, if the programme is longer than one year, the annual fee; and

children.label: e
children.text: whether or not the student has to pay programme or training scheme fees and whether the fees are domestic or foreign fees; and

children.label: f
children.text: whether the student is full-time (see U6.1.1) or part-time (see U7.20).

units.heading: Confirmation of enrolment

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Applicants who are returning to the same New Zealand education provider to continue a course of study may, instead of an offer of a place, provide a confirmation of enrolment from the education provider which shows:

children.label: a
children.text: the name of the course; and

children.label: b

children.label: c
children.text: whether the student is full-time (see U6.1.1) or part-time (see U7.20).

pages.title: Conditions of student visas
pages.page_title: U6.40 Conditions of student visas (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Conditions of student visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All visas for school students must state: 'primary or secondary school studies'.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the student has provided acceptable guarantees of funds and onward travel, the visa must state: ‘Evidence of financial support not required’ and ‘return/onward ticket not required’.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: All student visas must allow multiple journeys.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Two currency dates must be specified on student visas:

children.label: i
children.text: the date on which the visa expires; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the date on which the permission to travel expires.

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: See also E3.20 for further conditions.

units.heading: Student visa holders liable for deportation

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa holder who breaches any of the conditions of their visa (in particular those relating to attendance, employment, holding acceptable insurance and living with their legal guardian) may become liable for deportation (see E3.60).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Where the student is required to live with a legal guardian (see U3.30) and that legal guardian becomes liable for deportation, the student will also become liable for deportation (see E3.60).

pages.title: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment
pages.page_title: U13.15 Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment

units.heading: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment, a student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work during the academic year, and during any scheduled vacations, including within the academic year.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Students aged 16 or 17 years of age enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment must have written permission from their education provider and written parental consent to be granted conditions allowing work.

units.heading: Work conditions for up to twenty-five hours in any given week

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa holder may be granted with conditions to work for up to 25 hours in any given week during the validity of the visa if the student is:

children.label: i
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1) of at least two academic years’ duration; or

children.label: ii
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study, culminating in a New Zealand qualification at level four or higher on the New Zealand Qualification Framework; or Note: Micro-credentials are not qualifications, even if they are listed on the NZQCF. They are therefore excluded when assessing eligibility for work rights under (ii).

children.label: iii
children.text: undertaking full-time study as part of an approved tertiary student exchange scheme (see E11.45); or

children.label: iv
children.text: engaged in a full-time programme of study of at least 24 teaching weeks duration; and

children.label: b1
children.text: an immigration officer is satisfied that the primary purpose of the programme of study is to develop English language skills; and

children.label: b2
children.text: the student can provide acceptable English language test results, as set out at U13.15.20 (no more than 2 years old at the time the application is lodged); or

children.label: v
children.text: undertaking full-time English language study of at least 14 consecutive weeks’ duration at an education provider that:

children.label: b1
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: b2
children.text: holds Category One status under the NZQA EER quality assurance system; or Note: When assessing eligibility for work rights under (v) for an applicant who holds a current student visa, all consecutive previous English language study undertaken on this and any previous student visa can be counted towards the 14 consecutive week period provided the programme of study the applicant is applying for: - follows directly from their current study and - is with the same provider as that on their current and any previous student visa.

children.label: vi
children.text: undertaking a full-time Study Abroad programme under a study abroad partner agreement with a New Zealand Tertiary education institution.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite E7.10(a)(ii), immigration officers may apply these instructions to any eligible student visa application that was submitted before 3 November 2025 and as of that date had not been decided.

units.heading: Full time work rights during Christmas-New Year vacation period

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation (summer vacation) period provided that the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: studying full-time (see U6.1.1); and

children.label: b
children.text: enrolled in a programme of study that has a minimum duration of at least two semesters during a period of at least eight months.

units.heading: Full time work rights during scheduled vacations

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during all scheduled vacations, if the student is undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1); and of at least one academic year’s duration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) where scheduled vacations are more than one third of the programme of study duration for programmes of study offered by tertiary providers other than universities, full-time work rights may not be granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: An academic year means a programme of study of a minimum of 120 credits during a period of at least eight months (minimum of two semesters)

units.heading: Work conditions for doctoral students

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder unlimited work rights if:

children.label: a
children.text: the student is undertaking a Doctoral degree, and

children.label: b
children.text: the qualification is awarded by a New Zealand tertiary institution.

units.heading: Acceptable English language test results

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following English language test results are acceptable:

blocks.label: table1
blocks.text: Test | Minimum score required ; International English Language Testing System (IELTS) - General or Academic Module | Overall score of 5.0 or more ; Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-based Test (TOEFL iBT) | Overall score of 35 or more ; Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic) | Overall score of 36 or more ; B2 First (First Certificate in English) (formerly Cambridge English: First (FCE)) or B2 First for Schools (First Certificate in English) (formerly Cambridge English: First (FCE) for Schools) | Overall score of 154 or more ; Occupational English Test (OET) | Grade C or higher in all four skills (Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking)*

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: * A score of Grade C or higher in all four skills is required for the OET as there is no overall grade for this test.

pages.page_title: U13.1 Work conditions for all students

units.heading: Work conditions for all students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions allowing the student to work if the:

children.label: i
children.text: student is aged 16 or over, and

children.label: ii
children.text: requirements at U13.5 or U13.10 or U13.15 are met.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: An offer of employment is not required for a student visa to be granted with conditions allowing the student to work.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The holder of a student visa with work conditions is not permitted to: as indicated in E7.40.

children.label: i
children.text: work in self-employment; or

children.label: ii
children.text: provide commercial sexual services; or

children.label: iii
children.text: act as an operator of a New Zealand business of prostitution; or

pages.page_title: U13.5 Work conditions for practical experience requirements

units.heading: Work conditions for practical experience requirements

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the student to work in order to fulfil a requirement of practical experience for their programme of study in New Zealand if an immigration officer is satisfied that practical experience is a course requirement.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If it is determined that an applicant’s main activity will be work, that applicant may be directed to apply for a work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Students studying in any other country that want to undertake practical work experience in New Zealand should apply for a student and trainee work visa (see WE1).

pages.title: Work conditions for secondary school students
pages.page_title: U13.10 Work conditions for secondary school students

units.heading: Work conditions for secondary school students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For secondary school students, a student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work, for up to 25 hours in any given week and full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation period where the student:

children.label: i
children.text: is a full-time student in Years 12 or 13; and

children.label: ii
children.text: has provided written permission from their school; and

children.label: iii
children.text: has written parental consent.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Where a secondary school student is undertaking a student exchange with an Exchange Provider Organisation (EPO), written permission from the EPO is also required (see E11.55.20).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a)(ii), (iii) and (b) above, secondary school students aged 18 years of age or older do not require parental consent or written permission to be granted conditions allowing full-time work during the Christmas-New Year vacation period.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite E7.10(a)(ii), immigration officers may apply these instructions to any eligible student visa application for secondary school students that was submitted before 3 November 2025 and as of that date had not been decided.

pages.title: Foreign government-supported students

units.heading: Foreign government-supported students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A foreign government-supported student receives funding from their home country government to support their study in New Zealand.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A foreign government-supported student must meet the general student requirements under U3.1, and is exempt from having to provide evidence of paying their course fees.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: In addition to the requirements at U3.1, a foreign government-supported student must provide a letter from the foreign government:

children.label: i
children.text: that sets out the terms of the student’s sponsorship and undertakes to pay the course fees directly to the education provider and pay the student’s living expenses; and

children.label: ii
children.text: states that the student is of good character.

pages.title: New Zealand Aid Programme (NZAP)-supported students undertaking employment
pages.page_title: U11.1 New Zealand Aid Programme (NZAP)-supported students undertaking employment (07/11/2011)

units.heading: New Zealand Aid Programme (NZAP)-supported students undertaking employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: New Zealand Aid Programme (NZAP)-supported students may be granted conditions on their student visa to allow them to work during the academic year for up to 20 hours per week, during any holidays within the academic year for up to 20 hours per week, and full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period unless they are studying under the following schemes:

children.label: i
children.text: Short-Term Training Awards; or

children.label: ii
children.text: New Zealand Regional Development Scholarships; or

children.label: iii
children.text: English Language Training for Officials.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: With the exception of the schemes listed under (a), NZAP scholars may be granted work visas at the completion of their studies for qualification-related work experience for the minimum time needed to complete practical work requirements. Note: NZAP-supported senior medical and pharmacy students may be granted a work visa for their internship/registration year.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: NZAP-supported students are not permitted to:

children.label: i
children.text: work in self-employment; or

children.label: ii
children.text: provide commercial sexual services; or

children.label: iii
children.text: act as an operator of a New Zealand business of prostitution; or

children.label: iv
children.text: invest in a business of prostitution (see E7.40).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Any NZAP-supported student, or their partner or dependent children may only be granted a visa for New Zealand in the two-year period following completion of the NZAP student's scholarship, with written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (with the exception of a work visa to complete course requirements or, if the applicant is outside New Zealand, a short-term visitor visa). Note: See WF4.5 for work instructions for partners of holders of student visas who are NZAP-supported.

pages.title: Student visas and permission to study for refugee or protection status claimants
pages.page_title: U10.1 Student visas and permission to study for refugee or protection status claimants (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Student visas and permission to study for refugee or protection status claimants

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The only course of study refugee or protection status claimants or their partner or dependent children may undertake without the need for a student visa is an English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL) course at a New Zealand technical institute.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Permission to attend an ESOL course may be given by special direction varying the conditions of the claimant's temporary entry class visa, and an immigration officer must inform the claimant of the special direction by letter.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Claimants not eligible for a student visa under these provisions may apply under the provisions for student visas at U3, but must meet all the requirements, including payment of the appropriate fee.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: For information on the eligibility of refugee or protection status claimants for other temporary visas see E8.10.

units.heading: Claimants' school-aged children

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Claimants' school-aged children wishing to study at primary or secondary school may be granted student visas.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Applications must be made in the prescribed manner (see E4.50); but an appropriately delegated immigration officer may waive:

children.label: i
children.text: the application fee; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the requirement to produce evidence of funds or sponsorship; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the requirement to produce evidence of travel tickets or onward travel arrangements.

units.heading: Religious trainees

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Foreign students accepted for training in New Zealand to prepare them for entry to religious orders or the ministry are generally trained at one of the following institutions:

children.label: b1
children.text: College of St John the Evangelist (Anglican and Methodist)

children.label: b2
children.text: Knox College (Presbyterian)

children.label: b3
children.text: Holy Cross Seminary (Catholic).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Such students may be granted a student visa for the requested period.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: written confirmation of a place, and

children.label: ii
children.text: a guarantee of accommodation, maintenance and repatriation by the sponsoring church for the length of the course, and

children.label: iii
children.text: if the student is undertaking university courses, evidence of an offer of a place from the university and evidence that the course fees have been paid.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Applications for further visas must meet the same requirements as in paragraph (c) above and be supported by both the religious organisation and the training provider.

pages.page_title: U9.5 Nautical students (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Nautical students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Foreign students may be granted a student visa to attend nautical courses for the requested period at Manukau Polytechnic.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Applicants must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: a letter from the shipping company that employs them, guaranteeing maintenance and repatriation for the length of the course (this guarantee may be accepted instead of a financial undertaking or other evidence of funds for maintenance and onward travel), and

children.label: ii
children.text: evidence that they have a place at Manukau Polytechnic, and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence that they have paid the course fees or are exempt from having to pay them.

pages.title: Air New Zealand trainees
pages.page_title: U9.1 Air New Zealand trainees (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Air New Zealand trainees

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Trainees from any airline that has made a special arrangement with Air New Zealand to accept its trainees may be granted a student visa for training for the requested period with Air New Zealand at an Air New Zealand Training Centre in New Zealand.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Applicants must provide a guarantee from Air New Zealand confirming placement, maintenance, accommodation and repatriation, for the length of the training, but they do not have to produce evidence that they have paid the course fee.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: A letter of support from Air New Zealand must accompany any application for a further student visa.

pages.title: Dependent children of holders of work visas
pages.page_title: U8.20 Dependent children of holders of work visas (01/07/2013)

units.heading: Dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2); or

children.label: v
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: vi
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or.

children.label: vii
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all course fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.15 to A5.25.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Despite (a)(v) dependent children of Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) Job Search visa holders may be granted student visas if the related SMC application was under consideration on or before 24 July 2011.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$35,019 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$35,019 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

pages.title: Dependent children of military visa holders
pages.page_title: U8.15 Dependent children of military visa holders (01/07/2013)

units.heading: Dependent children of military visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of military visa holders may be granted student visas for the same period as the military visa held, or deemed to be held, by the applicant's parent.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Applicants meet temporary entry class requirements for lodging an application as set out at E4, bona fide applicants as set out at E5, and health and character requirements as set out at A4.5 and A5.5, but are exempt from:

children.label: i
children.text: providing evidence of enrolment; and

children.label: ii
children.text: providing guarantees of accommodation and maintenance; and

children.label: iii
children.text: meeting onward travel requirements.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of military visa holders are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) in the following respects:

children.label: i
children.text: for the purpose of all course fees for the period of secondment; and

children.label: ii
children.text: until the end of the calendar year in which their parent completes their posting in New Zealand.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The student visas granted must be current for the period of enrolment or until the parent holding a military visa departs, whichever occurs first.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: If the student wishes to continue studying in New Zealand after their parent departs, they must meet the requirements under the immigration instructions for a temporary visa and obtain one accordingly.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Before granting a student visa an immigration officer must be satisfied that the applicant's parent:

children.label: i
children.text: holds a military visa; or

children.label: ii
children.text: is eligible to be granted a military visa; or

children.label: iii
children.text: is deemed to be granted a military visa.

pages.title: Part-time study
pages.page_title: U7.20 Part-time study (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Part-time study

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: People who are not considered to be full-time students (see U6.1.1) may apply for a visitor visa with a variation of conditions to allow study on a part-time basis.

units.heading: Courses lasting up to 9 months

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: People outside New Zealand may apply for and be granted a variation of conditions to allow study on a part-time basis for a maximum of 9 months from the date of their arrival in New Zealand, provided that they are enrolled in a part-time course certified as one that complies with foreign student requirements (see U3.1) and lasts no more than 9 months, and comply with visitor requirements (see V2.1).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: People already in New Zealand may apply for and be granted a visitor visa with a variation of conditions to allow study on a part-time basis for the balance of their stay up to a maximum of 9 months from the date of their arrival.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If study is the main reason for the applicant being in New Zealand, immigration officers must decline any application to undertake part-time courses lasting longer than 9 months, unless the officers are satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the application has special merit that warrants the application being approved, and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant will comply with the conditions of their visa.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Immigration officers must be satisfied that applicants who wish to undertake part-time courses lasting up to 9 months after their date of arrival:

children.label: i
children.text: are enrolled in and have paid the fees for such a course; and

children.label: ii
children.text: are able to satisfy the standard visitor requirements (see V2.1).

units.heading: Students completing their course of study

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Despite U7.20 above and U6.1.1, a person who is: may be considered to be a full-time student and may be granted a student visa for the remaining duration of their course if they can meet student requirements (see U3.1).

children.label: i
children.text: in their final semester of a course of study in New Zealand, that is of at least 2 academic years’ duration; or

children.label: ii
children.text: in their final semester of a course of study in New Zealand, culminating in a New Zealand qualification that would qualify for points under the Skilled Migrant Category (see SM14)

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: To be eligible for a student visa under these instructions, applicants must not previously have been granted a visa under these instructions.
