pages.title: Partners and dependent children of diplomatic, consular or official staff
pages.page_title: U8.10 Partners and dependent children of diplomatic, consular or official staff (30/07/2012)

units.heading: Partners and dependent children of diplomatic, consular or official staff

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Partners (see E4.1.20) and dependent children (see E4.1.10) of diplomatic, consular or official staff who wish to study in New Zealand must obtain approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade Protocol Division (see H2).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If a diplomatic or consular tour of duty terminates during the academic year, and the partner or dependent child ceases to hold a special temporary visa (see H2.1), they must obtain a student visa to continue studying.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Partners and dependent children of diplomatic or consular personnel will be regarded as domestic students until the end of the calendar year in which the diplomat's or consular official’s tour of duty terminates, and they are not required to provide evidence of having paid course fees in order to complete the school or academic year (see U3.35).

pages.title: Second and subsequent courses
pages.page_title: U7.5 Second and subsequent courses (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Second and subsequent courses

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: There is no limit on the number of courses foreign students may undertake in New Zealand.

pages.title: Visas for the length of a course of study
pages.page_title: U6.35 Visas for the length of a course of study (30/07/2012)

units.heading: Visas for the length of a course of study

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Student visas may be granted for the length of a student's course of study, regardless of the period for which they have paid their course fees, where:

children.label: i
children.text: the student has an offer of a place with an education provider with which INZ has a Memorandum of Understanding for the Students Online Initiative which allows for the grant of visas for the length of course of study, and

children.label: ii
children.text: the education provider supports the grant of a length of course visa.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of the education provider's support to grant a length of course visa must be provided. Acceptable evidence may include written confirmation from the education provider, such as an offer of a place which indicates the education provider's support.

pages.title: Currency of student visas
pages.page_title: U6.30 Currency of student visas (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Currency of student visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Student visas may be granted for the following periods:

children.label: i
children.text: for holders of full scholarships and fees scholarships who do not meet the requirements under U6.35, the period of the student's award (up to a maximum of 4 years); and

children.label: ii
children.text: for fee-paying foreign students who do not meet the requirements under U6.35, the period for which the student has paid the course fees (up to a maximum of 4 years); and

children.label: iii
children.text: for fee-paying foreign students and full scholarship students, who meet the requirements under U6.35, for the length of their course of study, regardless of the period for which they have paid course fees (up to a maximum of 4 years).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the course is based on the New Zealand academic year, the visa may be granted for the academic year for which the student has paid, to expire on 31 March of the following year.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If the course lasts for less than one year, or can begin at any time during the year, the visa may be granted to expire no more than one month after the period for which the student has paid.

pages.title: Variations to work visas and visitor visas to allow study
pages.page_title: U6.20 Variations to work visas and visitor visas to allow study (08/04/2013)

units.heading: Variations to work visas and visitor visas to allow study

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless U2.5(a) applies, holders of work or visitor visas must apply for a variation of conditions to their current visa, if:

children.label: i
children.text: they wish to undertake a course of study longer than 3 months (see also U7.20.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: it is inappropriate for some other reason to apply for a student visa.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Immigration officers with Schedule 3 delegations and above may vary the conditions of the current visa to allow study, provided that they sight evidence that the applicant has:

children.label: i
children.text: an offer of a place at an education provider; and

children.label: ii
children.text: paid the course fees or is exempt from having to pay them.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Holders of visitor visas granted under the special category V3.100 may only be granted a variation of conditions to allow part-time study.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If the variation of conditions is applied for at the same time as the work or visitor visa then a separate fee for the variation of conditions is not required.

pages.title: Distance education (correspondence) students
pages.page_title: U6.5 Distance education (correspondence) students (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Distance education (correspondence) students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Distance education students may attend the New Zealand education provider at which they are enrolled so that they can undertake practical study or sit examinations, or for any other educational reason that requires their presence at the provider.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Students who apply to come to New Zealand for more than 3 months for this purpose may be granted a student visa for the necessary period.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Students who wish to come to New Zealand for this purpose for less than 3 months may do so on a visitor visa.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Immigration officers should sight evidence that distance students who apply for student or visitor visas:

children.label: i
children.text: are distance education students; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have an offer of a place at an education provider (if they are in New Zealand for more than 3 months); and

children.label: iii
children.text: have paid the course fees or are exempt from having to pay them.

pages.title: Courses of study lasting longer than 3 months
pages.page_title: U6.1 Courses of study lasting longer than 3 months (07/11/2011)

units.heading: Courses of study lasting longer than 3 months

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: People who require a visa to visit New Zealand and who wish to come to New Zealand to study full-time for a period longer than three months, must hold a student visa.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Potential students who are nationals of countries to whom a visitor visa waiver applies (see E2.1) may enter New Zealand as visitors and apply for a student visa after their arrival.

units.heading: Definition of 'full-time study'

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For private training establishments full-time study is generally considered to be enrolment in:

children.label: i
children.text: a course of study that requires attendance for a minimum of 20 hours per week; or

children.label: ii
children.text: at least three papers, or equivalent, per semester if the offered course is at Level 7 or above on the New Zealand Qualification Framework.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: For other tertiary institutions enrolment in at least three papers, or equivalent, per semester is indicative of full-time study.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Any course of study that does not meet (a) or (b) above is usually considered to be part-time (see U7.20).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The final decision on whether or not a student may be considered to be undertaking full-time study rests with immigration officers.

section_listing: U6.1 Courses of study lasting longer than 3 months (29/11/2010)

pages.title: Summary

units.heading: Summary

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless otherwise specified, to be granted a student visa to attend a course of more than three months, applicants must:

children.label: i
children.text: have an offer of a place or, if returning to continue a course of study, a confirmation of enrolment in an approved course with an education provider in New Zealand that meets student visa requirements (see U3.5, U3.10, and U5.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: be exempted from or have paid course fees; and

children.label: iii
children.text: if aged under 18, meet accommodation requirements (see U3.15); and

children.label: iv
children.text: have fulfilled the purpose and met the conditions for any previous or current temporary visas held as set out in E3.15 and E3.20; and

children.label: v
children.text: meet the conditions set out in E3.20; and

children.label: vi
children.text: not be the holder of a current visitor visa granted under Guardians accompanying students to New Zealand instructions (see V3.100).); and

children.label: vii
children.text: hold acceptable insurance (see U3.45), unless they are a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) student or a New Zealand Aid Programme-supported student.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All applicants must meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for:

children.label: i
children.text: lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa as set out at E4; and

children.label: ii
children.text: bona fide applicants as set out at E5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: health and character as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have not completed, or will not be completing the course of study endorsed on their student visa and who wish to change their course of study and/or education provider must:

children.label: i
children.text: meet requirements (a) and (b) above; and

children.label: ii
children.text: meet the requirements set out at U3.40. Note: Applicants who are progressing to further study, for example a student in Year 13 who is progressing to tertiary studies, will not need to meet U3.40.

pages.title: Students undertaking employment
pages.page_title: U7.15 Students undertaking employment (27/08/2012)

units.heading: Students undertaking employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students may apply for a variation of conditions to work:

children.label: i
children.text: to fulfil practical course requirements (see U7.15.1); and/or

children.label: ii
children.text: for up to 20 hours in any given week during the academic year, and during any holidays within the academic year if they are an eligible student (see U7.15.5); and/or

children.label: iii
children.text: full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period if they are an eligible student (see U7.15.10).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Students are not permitted to:

children.label: i
children.text: work in self-employment; or

children.label: ii
children.text: provide commercial sexual services; or

children.label: iii
children.text: act as an operator of a New Zealand business of prostitution; or

children.label: iv
children.text: invest in a business of prostitution (see E7.40).

units.heading: Course requirements

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of student visas may apply for a variation of conditions to allow them to work in order to fulfil a requirement of practical experience for their course.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If satisfied that practical experience is a course requirement, an immigration officer may grant a student visa with the conditions varied to allow employment. Note: If an applicant's main activity will be work, they must apply for a work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where the variation of conditions is sought in conjunction with an application for a student visa, the fee for a variation of conditions may be waived.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The variation of conditions will be effective only for the period of the student's current student visa and ceases on completion of the relevant course of study.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: The variation of conditions may be applied for at any time the visa is current or when applying for a further student visa.

units.heading: Twenty hours in any given week for eligible students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of student visas may be granted a variation of conditions to allow them to work during the academic year, and during any holidays within the academic year for up to 20 hours in any given week if they are:

children.label: i
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study, at a private training establishment or tertiary institution (see U5.15 - U5.20), of at least two academic years’ duration; or

children.label: ii
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study in New Zealand, culminating in a New Zealand qualification that would qualify for points under the Skilled Migrant Category (see SM14); or

children.label: iii
children.text: undertaking a full-time tertiary programme of study of at least one academic year's duration as part of an approved tertiary student exchange scheme (see E11.45); or

children.label: iv
children.text: undertaking a full-time, full secondary school year programme of study in Years 12 or 13, provided they have written permission from their school and written parental consent; or

children.label: v
children.text: engaged in a full-time programme of study of at least six months’ duration at a private training establishment or tertiary institution (see U5.15 - U5.20); and

children.label: b1
children.text: an immigration officer is satisfied that the primary purpose of the programme of study is to develop English language skills; and

children.label: b2
children.text: the student can provide a certificate (no more than 2 years old at the time the application is lodged) from the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) which shows an overall band score of at least 5.0 in the IELTS (General or Academic Module); or

children.label: vi
children.text: undertaking a full-time English language programme of at least 14 weeks duration or a full-time foundation programme of at least one academic year’s duration at level four or higher on the New Zealand Qualification Framework where either programme is at an education provider in Canterbury that:

children.label: b1
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: b2
children.text: holds Category One status under the New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system; or

children.label: b3
children.text: is on a three year audit cycle. Note: For (vi) the programme of study must have been commenced on or before 28 February 2014. To be eligible for work rights under (vi), students aged 16 and 17 years must have written permission from their education provider and written parental consent. Students below the age of 16 are not eligible. A list of qualifying education providers can be found at www.nzqa.govt.nz/audience-pages/quake/

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of an offer of employment is not required.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where the variation of conditions is sought in conjunction with an application for a student visa, the fee for a variation of conditions may be waived.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The variation of conditions will be effective only for the period of the student's current student visa and ceases on completion of the relevant course of study.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: The variation of conditions may be applied for at any time the visa is current or when applying for a further student visa.

units.heading: Christmas-New Year holiday period

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of student visas may be granted a variation of conditions to allow them to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period at the end of each academic year, provided they are undertaking a full-time course of study of 12 months or more duration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Any school student who does not meet the requirements set out at U7.15.5a(iv) is not eligible to work under the provisions of U7.15.10. Note: Written permission from the school is not required for students who are 18 years of age or over, under the provisions of U7.15.10.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence of an offer of employment is not required.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Where the variation of conditions is sought in conjunction with an application for a student visa, the fee for a variation of conditions may be waived.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: The variation of conditions will be effective only for the period of the student's current student visa.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: The variation of conditions may be applied for at any time the visa is current or when applying for a further student visa.

pages.title: Tuition fees
pages.page_title: U3.10 Tuition fees (26/11/2012)

units.heading: Tuition fees

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence of:

children.label: i
children.text: exemption from tuition fees, or

children.label: ii
children.text: payment of tuition fees, or

children.label: iii
children.text: a notice of the award of a full New Zealand Aid Programme scholarship. Note: For applications processed outside New Zealand, evidence of payment is not required until after the application has been approved in principle.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, evidence of payment of tuition fees need not be provided if an immigration officer is satisfied that the student is awaiting home country government loan approval to pay their tuition fees once the student enrols in person at the New Zealand Tertiary Education Institution (TEI). The student must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: evidence the loan has been applied for, and

children.label: ii
children.text: confirmation from the enrolling New Zealand TEI that they expect to receive the fee directly once the student is onshore and has completed enrolment at that TEI.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The exception set out in (b) above also applies to students who are undertaking a bachelor degree programme or higher at a private training establishment (PTE) if an immigration officer is satisfied that the student is awaiting home country government loan approval to pay their tuition fees once the student enrols in person at the PTE. The student must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: evidence the loan has been applied for,

children.label: ii
children.text: confirmation from the enrolling New Zealand PTE that they expect to receive the fee directly once the student is onshore and has completed enrolment at that PTE, and

children.label: iii
children.text: confirmation from the PTE that the course the student is enrolling in is a bachelor degree programme or higher.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where the course is offered by a PTE, the applicant must ensure that the primary requirements for satisfying sections 232 and 233 of the Education Act 1989, in respect of courses of study, are met (see U5.15).

pages.title: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand
pages.page_title: U3.20 Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand (26/03/2012)

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that they have sufficient funds available to maintain themselves throughout the period of their stay in New Zealand.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence may include but is not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: a notice of the award of a full scholarship; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a completed Sponsorship for Temporary Entry (INZ 1025) form (see U3.20.5); or

children.label: iii
children.text: a completed Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form, which covers a stay in New Zealand for the length of the visa (see U3.20.10); or

children.label: iv
children.text: funds held by or on behalf of the student (see U3.20.20).

units.heading: Sponsorship

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A sponsor for a student visa application must be an acceptable sponsor (see E6.5) and be either:

children.label: i
children.text: a natural person who is a relative or a friend of the applicant; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an organisation or government agency (an individual must be nominated as the authorised contact).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Sponsors must satisfy an immigration officer that they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet sponsorship obligations); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are sponsoring.

units.heading: Financial Undertaking

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Before the student’s arrival in New Zealand, a financial undertaking may be provided by a third party.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the third party is a person, they must be a relative or a friend of the applicant.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If the third party is not a person, they must nominate an individual as an authorised contact.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The third party providing the financial undertaking must satisfy an immigration officer they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet their financial obligations as set out on the Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are supporting.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Where a third party wishes to continue providing a financial undertaking for the student’s subsequent onshore student visa applications, they may do so if they continue to meet (d).

units.heading: Determining whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To determine whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide, immigration officers may consider:

children.label: a
children.text: the relationship between the applicant and the sponsor or third party;

children.label: b
children.text: any previous breaches of financial obligations set out in undertakings;

children.label: c
children.text: the number of student visa applications they are currently supporting;

children.label: d
children.text: the period of time for which funds have been held by the sponsor or third party; and

children.label: e
children.text: the student’s ability to access funds from the sponsor or third party while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds held by or on behalf of the student

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Where funds are held by or on behalf of the student, immigration officers must be satisfied that the funds are from a genuine source and are genuinely available for the purposes of the applicant’s maintenance requirements.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: When determining whether a student has sufficient funds to maintain themselves throughout their stay in New Zealand, immigration officers may consider the period of time for which funds have been held by the student and the student’s ability to access funds while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking courses lasting less than 36 weeks

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students taking courses lasting less than 36 weeks must provide evidence they have funds of at least NZ$1,250 per month of study available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: This evidence may be sighted after the application has been approved in principle.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking courses lasting 36 weeks or longer

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students taking courses lasting 36 weeks or longer must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that:

children.label: a
children.text: they have NZ$15,000.00 per year available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses); or

children.label: b
children.text: if they are citizens of Samoa and Tonga a written guarantee of maintenance from a relative in New Zealand who is either a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder.

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maternity health services

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Pregnant applicants for a student visa who are due to give birth while in New Zealand must provide evidence that they:

children.label: a
children.text: have funds of at least NZ$9,000 available to pay for maternity health services; or

children.label: b
children.text: have sponsorship by a person, an organisation or a Government agency which meets generic sponsorship requirements set out at E6.5, to cover maternity health services; or

children.label: c
children.text: have a guarantee of financial undertaking by a third party which covers maternity health services (see U3.20.10); or

children.label: d
children.text: are eligible for publicly-funded maternity health services.

pages.title: Definition of 'domestic student'
pages.page_title: U3.35 Definition of 'domestic student' (26/11/2012)

units.heading: Definition of 'domestic student'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of student instructions a 'domestic student' means a domestic student as defined in section 2 of the Education Act 1989. The Ministry of Education holds a complete list of who is considered to be a domestic student for the purpose of fee payment and enrolment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary schooling domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending primary and secondary schools and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue;

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents;

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents;

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current school year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending primary and secondary schools and are exempt from paying foreign course fees:

children.label: a
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is in New Zealand to study under an exchange programme approved by the New Zealand Government.

children.label: b
children.text: Children whose application for a residence class visa is under consideration and who are the dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand resident visa, or permanent resident visa.

children.label: c
children.text: Children whose application for New Zealand citizenship is under consideration and who are the dependent children of a New Zealand citizen.

children.label: d
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is onshore and the holder of a valid work visa other than those excluded under U8.20.

children.label: e
children.text: Students who have, or dependent children of any person who has, made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009.

children.label: f
children.text: Dependent children of a foreign student enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme in a New Zealand university.

children.label: g
children.text: Dependent children of any person who, during the current calendar year, last ceased to hold a special temporary visa (see H2).

children.label: h
children.text: Students who have entered New Zealand for the purposes of adoption and:

children.label: i
children.text: whose adoption application before the New Zealand Family Court (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student) is supported by the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services and who has a letter from the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services confirming this support; or

children.label: ii
children.text: who are the subject of an Interim Order of Adoption granted by the New Zealand Family Court under section 5 of the Adoption Act 1955 (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student).

children.label: i
children.text: People who are in the custody of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development pursuant to any of the following orders:

children.label: i
children.text: an order, pursuant to sections 78, 101 or 238(1)(d) of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, in favour of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 110 of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, appointing the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development as sole guardian; or

children.label: iii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 33 of the Care of Children Act 2004, whereby a child or young person is placed under the Guardianship of the Family Court or the High Court and the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development is appointed as agent of the court with power and discretion to place the child.

children.label: j
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand Aid Programme Scholarship.

children.label: k
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a visitor visa granted under V3.115.

children.label: l
children.text: Dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

children.label: m
children.text: Children granted a student visa under U10.5.

children.label: n
children.text: Students who are in New Zealand to study under an exchange scheme approved by the Ministry of Education (see E11.45).

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector (see U5.20) and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions or limited visa in order to undertake a course of study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue.

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents.

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents.

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current academic year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Despite (d) above, dependent children aged 21 and over of Diplomatic, Consular or Official staff, who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand, may not be eligible for domestic student status and may be required to pay foreign student fees (see H2.1(b)).

children.label: f
children.text: A person who has made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and who is the holder of a valid temporary entry class visa.

children.label: g
children.text: A person who has been recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and whose application for residence is being processed.

children.label: h
children.text: A person who is enrolled at a tertiary education provider for the purpose of participating in industry training funded under the Industry Training Act 1992.

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector and are exempt from paying foreign course fees for foreign students:

children.label: a
children.text: Students enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme, in any New Zealand university (see U5.20).

children.label: b
children.text: A person who is in New Zealand to study under a New Zealand Government approved exchange programme at a tertiary education provider.

pages.title: Students who wish to change their course of study and/or education provider
pages.page_title: U3.40 Students who wish to change their course of study and/or education provider (02/02/2011)

units.heading: Students who wish to change their course of study and/or education provider

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A further student visa or variation of conditions, for the purpose of changing course and/or education provider, will only be granted if an immigration officer is satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant meets the student requirements set out at U3.1; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant has not breached their visa conditions as set out at E3.20; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the original student visa would have been granted for the proposed course and/or education provider; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the applicant remains a bona fide applicant (see E5.1).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Factors that an immigration officer may take into consideration when determining (a)(iii) and (a)(iv) above include, but are not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: the time elapsed since the original visa was granted;

children.label: ii
children.text: whether the level and/or subject area of the proposed course are significantly different from the original course; and

children.label: iii
children.text: any relevant information held about the previous application(s) including advice from the original issuing branch (see E7.1.1).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have received New Zealand Aid Programme funding within the two years prior to their application to change course and/or education provider being made, must also provide evidence that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade supports the change of course or education provider and that any scholarship continues.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Applicants who wish to change their course and/or education provider may provide evidence of payment of course fees after the application has been approved in principle.

pages.title: Exchange students
pages.page_title: U4.15 Exchange students (26/11/2012)

units.heading: Exchange students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students studying under reciprocal exchange schemes approved by the Minister of Education are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending primary and secondary schools and are exempt from paying foreign course fees (see U3.35.5).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: There are two types of New Zealand student exchange schemes under which international students may be enrolled in New Zealand schools without paying international fees:

children.label: i
children.text: school-to-school student exchange schemes run by a school that is a signatory to the Ministry of Education's Code of Practice for the Pastoral Care of International Students (see E11.55.20); and

children.label: ii
children.text: student exchange schemes run by approved exchange programme organisations (see E11.55.20).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The general requirements for participants in approved student exchange schemes are set out at E11.55.

pages.page_title: U5.10 Primary and secondary schools (private) (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Primary and secondary schools (private)

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Private schools registered under section 35A of the Education Act 1989 may offer places to foreign students on a fee-paying basis and are not obliged to place other students first.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Where foreign students are enrolled in a course of study intended exclusively or mainly for foreign students that class, course or programme must be approved by the New Zealand Qualifications Authority (see section 35B Education Act 1989).

section_listing: U5.10 Primary and secondary schools (private) (02/12/2013)

pages.title: Private training establishments
pages.page_title: U5.15 Private training establishments (30/07/2012)

units.heading: Private training establishments

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Private training establishments may offer course places to foreign students provided the programme of study or training scheme meets the criteria for one in which a foreign student may be enrolled in accordance with the provisions of the Education Act 1989 (see section 232).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The definition of a foreign student is contained in section 159 of the Education Act 1989.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The primary requirements for satisfying section 232 and 233 of the Education Act 1989, in respect of programme of study or training schemes are that:

children.label: i
children.text: the private training establishment providing the programme of study or training scheme has been registered by the New Zealand Qualifications Authority, and

children.label: ii
children.text: the programme of study or training scheme is an approved programme of study or training scheme, and

children.label: iii
children.text: the private training establishment has been accredited to provide the programme of study. Note: These requirements apply to all programmes of study and training schemes with the exception of those programmes of study or training scheme that are exempt as provided for in section 232(2) of the Education Act 1989.

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Primary and secondary schools are accredited by the Ministry of Education for admitting fee-paying foreign students and may offer them places, within any limits imposed by that Ministry on levels and subjects, after all New Zealand domestic and New Zealand Aid Programme scholarship students have been placed.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Where foreign students are enrolled in a course of study intended exclusively or mainly for foreign students that class, course or programme must be approved by the New Zealand Qualifications Authority (see section 4E of the Education Act 1989).

pages.title: Fee-paying foreign students
pages.page_title: U4.10 Fee-paying foreign students (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Fee-paying foreign students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students must meet the full costs of their courses of study, whether by themselves or with the help of family members, friends, home governments, or others (such as the United Nations).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: This category includes students studying at private training establishments, such as those offering English language courses.

pages.title: Dependent children of holders of student visas
pages.page_title: U8.25 Dependent children of holders of student visas (07/11/2011)

units.heading: Dependent children of holders of student visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas if their parent is a student visa holder who is:

children.label: i
children.text: any person who is in New Zealand to study under an exchange programme approved by the New Zealand Government; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a foreign student enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme in a New Zealand university; or

children.label: iii
children.text: any person who is the holder of a New Zealand Aid Programme Scholarship.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of student visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (for the purpose of all course fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's student visa (see U3.35).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of student visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment (see E4.1).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and evidence of maintenance funds are required (see U3.20).

section_listing: U8.25 Dependent children of holders of student visas (02/12/2013)

pages.title: Status of education providers and programmes
pages.page_title: U5.1 Status of education providers and programmes (30/07/2012)

units.heading: Status of education providers and programmes

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All education providers must certify in their offers of places to foreign students (see U3.5) that the programme of study or training scheme offered complies with foreign student requirements for different kinds of education providers (see U5.5 - U5.20).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All education providers offering places to foreign students must be signatories to the Ministry of Education's Code of Practice for Pastoral Care of International Students.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Any queries on the status of programmes or training schemes offered by private training establishments should be referred to the Service Delivery Unit, Quality Assurance Division, New Zealand Qualifications Authority, PO Box 160, Wellington.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Immigration New Zealand (INZ) may suspend the processing of applications for student visas for study at an education provider where at least one of the following applies:

children.label: i
children.text: the offered programme of study or training scheme does not comply with foreign student requirements as set out in U5.5 to U5.20;

children.label: ii
children.text: the education provider is not complying with its obligations under the Immigration Act, immigration regulations, or immigration instructions;

children.label: iii
children.text: INZ has been informed by education agencies that the education provider is not complying with its obligations under the Education Act and education regulations.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Before a decision is made to suspend the processing of student visas, the following will be taken into account:

children.label: i
children.text: evidence of the non-compliance; and

children.label: ii
children.text: reasons for the non-compliance; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the duration, frequency, and severity of the non-compliance.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: INZ may resume the processing of student visas if it is satisfied that the education provider is complying with its obligations. Note: Despite (d), where an applicant fails to meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for health, character or bona fide applicants, the application may be declined.

pages.title: Work conditions for tertiary students
pages.page_title: U13.15 Work conditions for tertiary students (02/12/2013)

units.heading: Work conditions for tertiary students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For tertiary students, a student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work during the academic year, and during any scheduled vacations, including within the academic year.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Tertiary students aged 16 or 17 years of age must have written permission from their education provider and written parental consent to be granted conditions allowing work.

units.heading: Work conditions for up to twenty hours in any given week

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A tertiary student visa holder may be granted with conditions to work for up to 20 hours in any given week during the validity of the visa if the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1) of at least two academic years’ duration; or

children.label: b
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study, culminating in a New Zealand qualification that would qualify for points under the Skilled Migrant Category (see SM14); or

children.label: c
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study of at least one academic year's duration as part of an approved tertiary student exchange scheme (see E11.45); or

children.label: d
children.text: engaged in a full-time programme of study of at least six months’ duration; and

children.label: i
children.text: an immigration officer is satisfied that the primary purpose of the programme of study is to develop English language skills; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the student can provide a certificate (no more than 2 years old at the time the application is lodged) from the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) which shows an overall band score of at least 5.0 in the IELTS (General or Academic Module); or

children.label: e
children.text: undertaking a full-time English language programme of at least 14 weeks’ duration at an education provider that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the NZQA EER quality assurance system; or

children.label: f
children.text: undertaking a full-time foundation programme that commenced on or before 28 February 2014 and that programme of study is of at least one academic year’s duration at level four or higher on the New Zealand Qualification Framework at an education provider in Canterbury that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system; or

children.label: iii
children.text: is on a three-year audit cycle if no EER report is available for that provider.

units.heading: Full time work rights during Christmas-New Year vacation period

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation period provided that the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: studying full-time (see U6.1.1); and

children.label: b
children.text: enrolled in a programme of study that has a minimum duration of at least two semesters during a period of at least eight months.

units.heading: Full time work rights during scheduled vacations

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during all scheduled vacations, if the student is undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1) of at least one academic year’s duration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) where scheduled vacations are more than one third of the programme of study duration for programmes of study offered by tertiary providers other than universities, full-time work rights may not be granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: An academic year means a programme of study of a minimum of 120 credits during a period of at least eight months (minimum of two semesters)

units.heading: Work conditions for masters by research or doctoral students

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder unlimited work rights if the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: undertaking a Masters by Research or Doctoral degree, and

children.label: b
children.text: the qualification is awarded by a New Zealand tertiary institution.

units.heading: Offer of a place

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Applicants must have an offer of a place with a New Zealand education provider, which shows:

children.label: a
children.text: the name of the programme of study or training scheme and the minimum time required for completing it; and

children.label: b
children.text: evidence that the programme of study or training scheme and education provider meet foreign student requirements (see U5); and

children.label: c
children.text: confirmation that the education provider has assessed and is satisfied the prospective student meets the programme of study or training scheme competencies and enrolment provision (section 7.1) as set out in the Code of Practice for the Pastoral Care of International Students; and

children.label: d
children.text: the amount of the tuition fee, or, if the programme of study is longer than one year, the annual fee; and

children.label: e
children.text: whether or not the student has to pay programme of study or training scheme fees and whether the fees are domestic or foreign fees; and

children.label: f
children.text: whether the student is full-time (see U6.1.1) or part-time (see U7.20); and

children.label: g
children.text: the dates and duration of all scheduled vacations if the programme of study or training scheme is one academic year or more.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: ~For the information specified at U3.5(g), this can be provided in a separate document accompanying the Offer of Place or Confirmation of Enrolment. ~From January 2014, students seeking to enrol in a programme of study or training scheme offered at an education provider that holds a Category Four status under the NZQA’s External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system will not be granted a student visa.

pages.title: Dependent children of holders of work visas
pages.page_title: U8.20 Dependent children of holders of work visas (02/12/2013)

units.heading: Dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2); or

children.label: v
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: vi
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or.

children.label: vii
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.15 to A5.25.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Despite (a)(v) dependent children of Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) Job Search visa holders may be granted student visas if the related SMC application was under consideration on or before 24 July 2011.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$35,019 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$35,019 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Air New Zealand trainees

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Trainees from any airline that has made a special arrangement with Air New Zealand to accept its trainees may be granted a student visa for training for the requested period with Air New Zealand at an Air New Zealand Training Centre in New Zealand.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Applicants must provide a guarantee from Air New Zealand confirming placement, maintenance, accommodation and repatriation, for the length of the training, but they do not have to produce evidence that they have paid the tuition fee.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: A letter of support from Air New Zealand must accompany any application for a further student visa.

units.heading: Work conditions for tertiary students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For tertiary students, a student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work during the academic year, and during any scheduled vacations, including within the academic year.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Tertiary students aged 16 or 17 years of age must have written permission from their education provider and written parental consent to be granted conditions allowing work.

units.heading: Work conditions for up to twenty hours in any given week

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A tertiary student visa holder may be granted with conditions to work for up to 20 hours in any given week during the validity of the visa if the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1) of at least two academic years’ duration; or

children.label: b
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study, culminating in a New Zealand qualification that would qualify for points under the Skilled Migrant Category (see SM14); or

children.label: c
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study of at least one academic year's duration as part of an approved tertiary student exchange scheme (see E11.45); or

children.label: d
children.text: engaged in a full-time programme of study of at least six months’ duration; and

children.label: i
children.text: an immigration officer is satisfied that the primary purpose of the programme of study is to develop English language skills; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the student can provide a certificate (no more than 2 years old at the time the application is lodged) from the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) which shows an overall band score of at least 5.0 in the IELTS (General or Academic Module); or

children.label: e
children.text: undertaking full-time English language study of at least 14 consecutive weeks’ duration at an education provider that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the NZQA EER quality assurance system; or

children.label: f
children.text: undertaking a full-time foundation programme that commenced on or before 28 February 2014 and that programme of study is of at least one academic year’s duration at level four or higher on the New Zealand Qualification Framework at an education provider in Canterbury that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system; or

children.label: iii
children.text: is on a three-year audit cycle if no EER report is available for that provider.

units.heading: Full time work rights during Christmas-New Year vacation period

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation period provided that the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: studying full-time (see U6.1.1); and

children.label: b
children.text: enrolled in a programme of study that has a minimum duration of at least two semesters during a period of at least eight months.

units.heading: Full time work rights during scheduled vacations

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during all scheduled vacations, if the student is undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1) of at least one academic year’s duration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) where scheduled vacations are more than one third of the programme of study duration for programmes of study offered by tertiary providers other than universities, full-time work rights may not be granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: An academic year means a programme of study of a minimum of 120 credits during a period of at least eight months (minimum of two semesters)

blocks.label: p1

children.label: a

children.label: b

units.heading: Visas for the length of a programme of study

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Student visas may be granted for the length of a student's programme of study, regardless of the period for which they have paid their tuition fees, where:

children.label: i
children.text: the student has an offer of a place with an education provider with which INZ has a Memorandum of Understanding for the Students Online Initiative which allows for the grant of visas for the length of programme of study, and

children.label: ii
children.text: the education provider supports the grant of a length of programme of study visa.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of the education provider's support to grant a length of programme of study visa must be provided. Acceptable evidence may include written confirmation from the education provider, such as an offer of a place which indicates the education provider's support.

units.heading: Vocational trainees

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Only the following applicants may be granted a student visa as a vocational trainee:

children.label: i
children.text: Air New Zealand trainees that meet the requirements set out at U9.1;

children.label: ii
children.text: Nautical students that meet the requirements set out at U9.5;

children.label: iii
children.text: Religious trainees that meet the requirements set out at U9.10; and

children.label: iv
children.text: New Zealand Aid Programme Short-Term Training Award (STTA) trainees that meet the requirements set out at U9.15.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Applicants who intend to undertake industry training or a modern apprenticeship, not listed at U4.20(a) above, or U9, must apply for a work visa (see WK).

pages.title: Student visas and permission to study for refugee or protection status claimants
pages.page_title: U10.1 Student visas and permission to study for refugee or protection status claimants (02/12/2013)

units.heading: Student visas and permission to study for refugee or protection status claimants

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The only programme of study refugee or protection status claimants or their partner or dependent children may undertake without the need for a student visa is an English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL) programme of study at a New Zealand technical institute.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Permission to attend an ESOL programme of study may be given by special direction varying the conditions of the claimant's temporary entry class visa, and an immigration officer must inform the claimant of the special direction by letter.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Claimants not eligible for a student visa under these provisions may apply under the provisions for student visas at U3, but must meet all the requirements, including payment of the appropriate fee.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: For information on the eligibility of refugee or protection status claimants for other temporary visas see E8.10.

units.heading: Claimants' school-aged children

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Claimants' school-aged children wishing to study at primary or secondary school may be granted student visas.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Applications must be made in the prescribed manner (see E4.50); but an appropriately delegated immigration officer may waive:

children.label: i
children.text: the application fee; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the requirement to produce evidence of funds or sponsorship; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the requirement to produce evidence of travel tickets or onward travel arrangements.

pages.page_title: U13.10 Work conditions for secondary school students (02/12/2013)

units.heading: Work conditions for secondary school students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For secondary school students, a student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work, for up to 20 hours in any given week and full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation period where the student:

children.label: i
children.text: is a full-time student in Years 12 or 13; and

children.label: ii
children.text: has provided written permission from their school; and

children.label: iii
children.text: has written parental consent.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a)(ii) and (iii) above, secondary school students aged 18 years of age or older do not require parental consent or written permission to be granted conditions allowing full-time work during the Christmas-New Year vacation period.

pages.title: Dependent children of holders of work visas
pages.page_title: U8.20 Dependent children of holders of work visas (18/04/2014)

units.heading: Dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2); or

children.label: v
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: vi
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or.

children.label: vii
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.15 to A5.25.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Despite (a)(v) dependent children of Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) Job Search visa holders may be granted student visas if the related SMC application was under consideration on or before 24 July 2011.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$35,294.60 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$35,294.60 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation. Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

pages.title: Variations to work visas and visitor visas to allow study
pages.page_title: U6.20 Variations to work visas and visitor visas to allow study (02/12/2013)

units.heading: Variations to work visas and visitor visas to allow study

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless U2.5(a) applies, holders of work or visitor visas must apply for a variation of conditions to their current visa, if:

children.label: i
children.text: they wish to undertake a programme of study longer than 3 months (see also U7.20.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: it is inappropriate for some other reason to apply for a student visa.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Immigration officers with Schedule 3 delegations and above may give a special direction varying the conditions of the current visa to allow study, provided that they sight evidence that the applicant has:

children.label: i
children.text: an offer of a place at an education provider; and

children.label: ii
children.text: paid the tuition fees or is exempt from having to pay them.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Holders of visitor visas granted under the special category V3.100 may only be given a special direction varying conditions to allow part-time study.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If the variation of conditions is applied for at the same time as the work or visitor visa then a separate fee for the variation of conditions is not required.

pages.page_title: U9.10 Religious trainees (02/12/2013)

units.heading: Religious trainees

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Foreign students accepted for training in New Zealand to prepare them for entry to religious orders or the ministry are generally trained at one of the following institutions:

children.label: b1
children.text: College of St John the Evangelist (Anglican and Methodist)

children.label: b2
children.text: Knox College (Presbyterian)

children.label: b3
children.text: Holy Cross Seminary (Catholic).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Such students may be granted a student visa for the requested period.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: written confirmation of a place, and

children.label: ii
children.text: a guarantee of accommodation, maintenance and repatriation by the sponsoring church for the length of the programme of study, and

children.label: iii
children.text: if the student is undertaking university programme of study, evidence of an offer of a place from the university and evidence that the tuition fees have been paid.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Applications for further visas must meet the same requirements as in paragraph (c) above and be supported by both the religious organisation and the training provider.

pages.title: Immigration levy
pages.page_title: A6.11 Immigration levy

units.heading: Immigration levy
Objective

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The objective of the immigration levy is to fund:

children.label: i
children.text: the provision of programmes intended to assist the successful settlement of migrants or categories of migrants

children.label: ii
children.text: the carrying out of research into settlement issues and the impacts of immigration

children.label: iii
children.text: the infrastructure required for, and the operation of, the immigration system, including (without limitation) for the following purposes:

children.label: b1
children.text: establishing and verifying the identity of persons:

children.label: b2
children.text: managing risk to the integrity of the immigration system:

children.label: b3
children.text: managing immigration risk to the safety and security of New Zealand:

children.label: b4
children.text: managing compliance with the immigration system;

children.label: iv
children.text: activities aimed at attracting migrants to New Zealand; and

children.label: v
children.text: the Immigration Advisers Authority, to the extent that it is not otherwise funded.

units.heading: Who must pay the immigration levy

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Principal applicants applying for a visa outside of an immigration control area, for one of the following categories must pay an immigration levy, unless exempt:

children.label: i
children.text: temporary visas

children.label: b1
children.text: work visas; or

children.label: b2
children.text: student visas; or

children.label: b3
children.text: visitor visas, except group visitor visas; or

children.label: ii
children.text: limited visas; or

children.label: iii
children.text: resident visas, except second and subsequent resident visas under RV4.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All applicants applying for a group visitor visa must pay the immigration levy, unless exempt.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Applicants who made an application under the residence instructions made prior to 7 December 2015 must pay the migrant levy, as per R5.1 Applications determined by INZ officers.

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010, Reg 4B

units.heading: Immigration levy payable to INZ when making an application for a visa

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010 prescribe when an immigration levy is payable to INZ and the amounts payable.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: An immigration levy is payable at the time an application for a visa is made to INZ or its agents.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Different immigration levy rates are payable for applications based on the type of visa being applied for. Details of the immigration levy payable are available at www.immigration.govt.nz/fees.

units.heading: Exempt from immigration levy

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: a person to whom a visa waiver to travel to New Zealand applies (see E2.1); or

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: a diplomatic, consular and official staff and accompanying partners and dependent children (see A6.1.11); or

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: a person applying for a visa where there is a bilateral fee waiver for that visa (see A6.5); or

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: a citizen of Samoa applying for a residence class visa; or

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: a claimant, refugee, or protected person; or

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: a person applying for a residence class visa on the basis of the person’s relationship with a refugee or protected person; or

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: a person applying for a visa:

children.label: i
children.text: under the special instructions for Victims of People Trafficking; or

children.label: ii
children.text: under the special instructions for Victims of family Violence; or

children.label: iii
children.text: under the Skilled Migrant Category job search instructions; or

children.label: iv
children.text: under the Migrant Exploitation Protection work visa instructions; or

children.label: v
children.text: as the partner or dependent child of a person granted a visa under the Migrant Exploitation Protection work visa instructions.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: For the purposes of schedule 5(9) of the Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010, the category is also known as the Special Category for Victims of Family Violence.

see_also: See also Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010, Reg 4C

blocks.label: d

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Claimants' school-aged children wishing to study at primary or secondary school may be granted student visas.

children.label: i

children.label: ii
children.text: the requirement to produce evidence of funds or sponsorship; and
