pages.title: Work conditions for tertiary students
pages.page_title: U13.15 Work conditions for tertiary students (25/08/2014)

units.heading: Work conditions for tertiary students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For tertiary students, a student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work during the academic year, and during any scheduled vacations, including within the academic year.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Tertiary students aged 16 or 17 years of age must have written permission from their education provider and written parental consent to be granted conditions allowing work.

units.heading: Work conditions for up to twenty hours in any given week

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A tertiary student visa holder may be granted with conditions to work for up to 20 hours in any given week during the validity of the visa if the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1) of at least two academic years’ duration; or

children.label: b
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study, culminating in a New Zealand qualification that would qualify for points under the Skilled Migrant Category (see SM14); or

children.label: c
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study of at least one academic year's duration as part of an approved tertiary student exchange scheme (see E11.45); or

children.label: d
children.text: engaged in a full-time programme of study of at least six months’ duration; and

children.label: i
children.text: an immigration officer is satisfied that the primary purpose of the programme of study is to develop English language skills; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the student can provide a certificate (no more than 2 years old at the time the application is lodged) from the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) which shows an overall band score of at least 5.0 in the IELTS (General or Academic Module); or

children.label: e
children.text: undertaking full-time English language study of at least 14 consecutive weeks’ duration at an education provider that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the NZQA EER quality assurance system; or Note: When assessing eligibility for work rights under (e) for an applicant who holds a current student visa, all consecutive previous English language study undertaken on this and any previous student visa can be counted towards the 14 consecutive week period provided the programme of study the applicant is applying for: - follows directly from their current study and - is with the same provider as that on their current and any previous student visa.

children.label: f
children.text: undertaking a full-time foundation programme that commenced on or before 28 February 2014 and that programme of study is of at least one academic year’s duration at level four or higher on the New Zealand Qualification Framework at an education provider in Canterbury that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system.

units.heading: Full time work rights during Christmas-New Year vacation period

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation period provided that the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: studying full-time (see U6.1.1); and

children.label: b
children.text: enrolled in a programme of study that has a minimum duration of at least two semesters during a period of at least eight months.

units.heading: Full time work rights during scheduled vacations

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during all scheduled vacations, if the student is undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1) of at least one academic year’s duration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) where scheduled vacations are more than one third of the programme of study duration for programmes of study offered by tertiary providers other than universities, full-time work rights may not be granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: An academic year means a programme of study of a minimum of 120 credits during a period of at least eight months (minimum of two semesters)

units.heading: Work conditions for masters by research or doctoral students

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder unlimited work rights if:

children.label: a
children.text: the student is undertaking a Masters by Research or Doctoral degree, and

children.label: b
children.text: the qualification is awarded by a New Zealand tertiary institution.

pages.title: Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa
pages.page_title: U14.5 Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa

units.heading: Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To be granted a pathway student visa, an applicant must:

children.label: a
children.text: be offered an eligible study pathway from a qualifying provider(s) (U14.20); and

children.label: b
children.text: meet the general requirements to be granted a student visa as set out at U3.1; and

children.label: c
children.text: meet the additional evidential requirements for pathway student visa set out at U14.5.1.

units.heading: Evidence of meeting requirements

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: In addition to meeting the general requirements to be granted a student visa as set out at U3.1, when applying for a pathway student visa an applicant must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: where there is more than one education provider, a joint letter of support from pathway education providers; and

children.label: ii
children.text: an offer of place (or joint offer) for each programme of study that meets the requirements set out at U3.5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence that tuition fee requirements, as set out at U3.10, for either the first programme of study or first year of study (whichever is shorter) have been met and satisfy an immigration officer that they have the ability to fund any remaining balance of the first programme of study and subsequent programmes of study on the intended pathway; and

children.label: iv
children.text: evidence that the maintenance funds requirements set out in U3.20 for the first year of study on the intended pathway have been met and satisfy an immigration officer that they have the ability to fund any remaining balance of the first programme of study and subsequent programmes of study on the intended pathway.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a)(ii):

children.label: i
children.text: second and subsequent offers of place for a pathway can be conditional on meeting pre-requisite programme of study entry criteria; and

children.label: ii
children.text: year 12 and 13 students are not required to specify a particular tertiary discipline, but must provide the intended qualification type and level, as well as a participating tertiary provider.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Pathway student visa applicants from a country with a student visa decline rate of more than 20 per cent who intend a study pathway commencing with an English language programme of study and culminating in a qualification at Levels 1 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework must:

children.label: i
children.text: submit an International English Language Testing System test (IELTS) (or equivalent internationally recognised proficiency test) at the time of application; and

children.label: ii
children.text: demonstrate that they only require an improvement of 0.5 of an IELTS overall band score (or equivalent) to meet the English language prerequisite for entry into the intended level 1 to 8 programme of study.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The student visa decline rate for a country is based on statistics, generated over a calendar year (12 months), by Immigration New Zealand. The decline rate and the name of the country are published on the INZ website. For the purpose of this instruction, the internationally recognised English language tests and corresponding IELTS equivalent test scores set out on the INZ website are considered acceptable.

pages.page_title: U14.10 Currency and conditions of pathway student visas

units.heading: Currency and conditions of pathway student visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For the purposes of the pathway student visa pilot, a visa can be granted up to a maximum of five years.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A visa may be granted to expire no more than three months beyond completion of the final pathway programme of study within the maximum currency of five years.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Work conditions for the duration of the pathway student visa will only be granted where the first programme of study meets the requirements as set out at U13.1, U13.10 or U13.15.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If the second or subsequent programme of study meets the requirements set out at U13.1, U13.10 or U13.15, a variation of conditions is required in order to be granted work conditions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Where (d) applies, a Variation of Conditions or Variation of Travel Conditions (INZ 1020) application must be completed and submitted with the required fee.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: The holder must make satisfactory progress on the pathway by:

children.label: i
children.text: meeting the conditional pre-requisites for enrolment into a second or subsequent programme of study (E3.20(d)); and

children.label: ii
children.text: commencing the second or subsequent programme of study on a pathway within a 16 week period of completing their earlier programme of study.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Where a first time student has submitted an English language test result as set out at U14.5.1 (c) and been granted a pathway student visa to undertake an English language programme of study culminating in a qualification at Levels 1 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework, the English Language programme of study must be completed within a 30 week period.

pages.page_title: U14.15 Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions

units.heading: Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: If a pathway student visa holder wishes to move to a different education provider or to a lower level programme of study at the same provider than specified in their visa conditions, they must apply for a new student visa and meet the requirements set out at U3.40, unless the applicant can demonstrate that the proposed change is due to circumstances beyond the applicant's control (see E3.26.10).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A variation of conditions, for the purpose of changing a programme of study at the same education provider will only be granted if an immigration officer is satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant meets the student requirements set out at U3.1; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant has not breached their visa conditions as set out at E3.20; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the original student visa would have been granted for the proposed programme of study; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the applicant remains a bona fide applicant (see E5.1); and

children.label: v
children.text: the proposed programme of study is at the same or higher level on the New Zealand Qualifications and Credentials Framework as the original programme of study or the applicant can demonstrate that the proposed change is due to circumstances beyond the applicant’s control.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Factors that an immigration officer may take into consideration when determining (b)(iii) and (b)(iv) above include, but are not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: the time elapsed since the original visa was granted; and

children.label: ii
children.text: whether the level and/or subject area of the proposed programme of study are significantly different from the original programme of study; and

children.label: iii
children.text: any relevant information held about the previous application(s) including advice from the original issuing branch (see E7.1.1).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Students who have received New Zealand scholarship funding within the two years prior to their application to change programme of study must also provide evidence that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade supports the change of programme of study and that any scholarship continues.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: A pathway student visa holders whose visa does not specify a tertiary discipline or programme of study (see U14.5.1(b)(ii)) may be granted a variation of conditions to ensure their visa accurately specifies their course of study (see E3.26.10(d)).

units.heading: Breaching visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A pathway student visa holder will be considered to be in breach of visa conditions where:

children.label: i
children.text: they fail to meet conditional pre-requisites for enrolment into a second or subsequent programme of study (E3.20(d)); or

children.label: ii
children.text: the time between the completion of one programme of study and the start of a second or subsequent programme of study on a pathway exceeds 16 weeks; or

children.label: iii
children.text: they have submitted an English language test result as set out at U14.5.1(c) and their intended pathway is an English language programme of study culminating in a qualification at Levels 1 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework and the English Language programme of study is not completed within a 30 week period.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A breach of visa conditions is "sufficient reason" to make a temporary entry class visa holder liable for deportation, and may result in the issue of a Deportation Liability Notice (E3.60).

pages.title: Provider requirements
pages.page_title: U14.20 Provider requirements

units.heading: Provider requirements
Pathway pilot entry criteria

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To qualify for entry to the Pathway student visa pilot, an education provider must:

children.label: a
children.text: be invited by Immigration New Zealand to be a pilot participant; and

children.label: b
children.text: have signed the Pathway Student Visas - Pilot Participation Declaration agreeing to the requirements as set out at U14.20.10; and

children.label: c
children.text: be either a school, a university or hold a Category One or Two rating under New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation and Review framework; and

children.label: d
children.text: have a minimum 90% student visa application approval rate over the 2014/15 financial year or 2016 calendar year (12 month period); and

children.label: e
children.text: comply with the legislative requirements as set out under the Education and Training Act 2020 to offer programmes of study to foreign students (U5.5 to U5.20); and

children.label: f
children.text: be a signatory to the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021.

units.heading: Eligible pathways

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All pathways must demonstrate academic progression to the second or subsequent programme of study building on the previous study.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All consecutive programmes of study that demonstrate progression are eligible to be included in the pilot.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Breaks between consecutive programmes of study must not exceed 16 weeks.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: English language study or programmes must not exceed 30 weeks.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Only education providers who meet the requirements set out under U14.20.1 can offer a joint pathway in conjunction with one another.

units.heading: Formal agreement between qualifying education providers

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: To ensure a student’s pastoral care needs are met, qualifying education providers who intend offering an education pathway in conjunction with one another must enter into a formal agreement.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The formal agreement must include and set out the following processes and arrangements:

children.label: i
children.text: the application process; and

children.label: ii
children.text: pastoral care obligations; and

children.label: iii
children.text: handover arrangements in transition periods between programmes of study/education providers; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the process if a significant gap exists between completion of a programme of study and the start of a second or subsequent programme of study or in the event some papers are failed and cannot be repeated within a 16 week period; and

children.label: v
children.text: the process if conditional entry requirements for second or subsequent programmes of study are not met; and

children.label: vi
children.text: the process if the student fails to attend and/or make satisfactory progress (E3.20(d)); and

children.label: vii
children.text: the process if the student wishes to leave intended pathway; and

children.label: viii
children.text: the obligation to notify INZ where a pathway student:

children.label: b1
children.text: requires additional time to complete a programme of study and time required is likely to exceed 16 weeks; or

children.label: b2
children.text: fails to meet the conditional entry requirements for a second or subsequent programme of study; or

children.label: b3
children.text: fails to enrol for a subsequent programme of study; or

children.label: b4
children.text: fails to attend and/or make satisfactory progress; or

children.label: b5
children.text: has their enrolment in a programme of study terminated.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The signed formal agreement does not have to be submitted with a pathway student visa application, however it must be made available to INZ if requested.

units.heading: Non-compliance with formal agreement requirements or when under active investigation by Immigration New Zealand

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Where non-compliance, other than of a minor nature, with any of the matters agreed to in the Pathway Student Visas - Pilot Participation Declaration, or where the pathway education provider is under active investigation by INZ for offences committed under part 10 of the Immigration Act 2009 the following process may occur:

children.label: a
children.text: INZ will suspend the processing of any student visa applications related to an existing pathway agreement immediately.

children.label: b
children.text: The non-compliant pathway education provider(s) will be advised in writing of the suspension and will be sent a report detailing the non-compliance, and will be given 30 days to remedy the non-compliance.

children.label: c
children.text: Resolution (or satisfactory progress towards resolution) of the non-compliance to the satisfaction of INZ within the 30 day period will see the suspension lifted and processing of related pathway student visa applications will resume.

children.label: d
children.text: Where a resolution is reached, the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment or the New Zealand Qualifications Authority may conduct an investigation three to six months later to assess the effectiveness of the remediation undertaken. If the remediation is deemed inadequate or ineffective, the suspension can be re-imposed or the provider may be removed from the pathways pilot and current pathway student visa holders may become liable for deportation.

children.label: e
children.text: If INZ is not satisfied that the non-compliance has been addressed or satisfactory progress has been made towards resolution within the 30 day period, the suspension of related student visa processing will continue (until resolution occurs).

children.label: f
children.text: Failure to address or make satisfactory progress towards resolving the non-compliance may result in removal from the pathways pilot, and current student visa holders becoming liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: INZ may rely on the advice of the Ministry of Education and/or the New Zealand Qualifications Authority in determining whether resolution has been reached or satisfactory progress has been made towards resolution.

pages.title: Multiple short-term English language programmes of study
pages.page_title: U15 Multiple short-term English language programmes of study

units.heading: Multiple short-term English language programmes of study

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants may be granted a student visa to undertake multiple short–term English language programmes of study for a maximum period of six months if they:

children.label: i
children.text: submit a joint covering letter from eligible pathway education providers (U14.20.1) setting out the English language programmes of study and start and end dates of each programme of study showing at least 14 weeks of English language study in total;

children.label: ii
children.text: submit an offer of place (or joint offer) for each programme of study that meets the requirements set out at U3.5;

children.label: iii
children.text: meet the general requirements to be granted a student visa as set out at U3.1;

children.label: iv
children.text: can demonstrate they have sufficient funds for maintenance for the duration of their stay in New Zealand (U3.20);

children.label: v
children.text: have not previously been granted a visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Work conditions will not be granted unless the part –time work requirements set out at U13.15.1 (e) are met.

pages.title: Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa
pages.page_title: U14.5 Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa (07/12/2015)

units.heading: Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To be granted a pathway student visa, an applicant must:

children.label: a
children.text: be offered an eligible study pathway from a qualifying provider (U14.20);

children.label: b
children.text: meet the general requirements to be granted a student visa as set out at U3.1;

children.label: c
children.text: meet the additional evidential requirements for pathway student visa set out at U14.5.1;

children.label: d
children.text: make an application for a student visa before 7 June 2017.

units.heading: Evidence of meeting requirements

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: In addition to meeting the general requirements to be granted a student visa as set out at U3.1, when applying for a pathway student visa an applicant must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: A joint covering letter from pathway education providers setting out the pathway programmes of study and start and end dates of each programme of study;

children.label: ii
children.text: An offer of place (or joint offer) for each programme of study that meets the requirements set out at U3.5;

children.label: iii
children.text: Evidence that tuition fee requirements, as set out at U3.10, for either the first programme of study or first year of study (whichever is shorter) have been met and satisfy an immigration officer that they have the ability to fund the remaining balance of the first programme of study and subsequent programmes of study on the intended pathway; and

children.label: iv
children.text: Evidence that the maintenance funds requirements set out in U3.20 for the first year of study on the intended pathway have been met and satisfy an immigration officer that they have the ability to fund the remaining balance of the first programme of study and subsequent programmes of study on the intended pathway.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a)(ii), second and subsequent offers of place for a pathway can be conditional on meeting pre-requisite programme of study entry criteria.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where the intended pathway is a English language programme of study culminating in a qualification at Levels 5 to 7 on the NZQF, applicants must submit an International English language Testing System (IELTS) test (or equivalent internationally recognised test) at the time of application demonstrating that they only require 0.5 of an IELTS overall band score (or equivalent) to meet the English language prerequisite for entry into the intended level 5 to 7 programme of study.

units.heading: Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: If a student holding a pathway student visa wishes to move to a different education provider or lower level programme of study than those specified in their visa conditions, they must apply for a new student visa and meet the requirements set out at U3.40.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A variation of conditions, for the purpose of changing a programme of study at the same education provider will only be granted if an immigration officer is satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant meets the student requirements set out at U3.1; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant has not breached their visa conditions as set out at E3.20; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the original student visa would have been granted for the proposed programme of study; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the proposed programme of study is at the same or higher level on the New Zealand Qualification Framework as the original programme of study; and

children.label: v
children.text: the applicant remains a bona fide applicant (see E5.1).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Factors that an immigration officer may take into consideration when determining (b)(iii) and (b)(iv) above include, but are not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: the time elapsed since the original visa was granted;

children.label: ii
children.text: whether the level and/or subject area of the proposed programme of study are significantly different from the original programme of study; and

children.label: iii
children.text: any relevant information held about the previous application(s) including advice from the original issuing branch (see E7.1.1).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Students who have received New Zealand Aid Programme funding within the two years prior to their application to change programme of study must also provide evidence that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade supports the change of programme of study and that any scholarship continues.

units.heading: Breaching visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student on an pathway student visa will be considered to be in breach of visa conditions where:

children.label: i
children.text: they fail to meet conditional pre-requisites for enrolment into a second or subsequent programme of study (E3.20(d); or

children.label: ii
children.text: the time between the completion of one programme of study and the start of a second or subsequent programme of study on a pathway exceeds 16 weeks; or

children.label: iii
children.text: the intended pathway is an English language programme of study culminating in a qualification at Levels 5 to 7 on the New Zealand Qualification Framework and the English Language programme of study is not completed within a 16 week period.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A breach of visa conditions may result in the issue of a Deportation Liability Notice (E3.60).

pages.title: Dependent children of holders of work visas
pages.page_title: U8.20 Dependent children of holders of work visas (30/03/2015)

units.heading: Dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2); or

children.label: v
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: vi
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or.

children.label: vii
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.15 to A5.25.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Despite (a)(v) dependent children of Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) Job Search visa holders may be granted student visas if the related SMC application was under consideration on or before 24 July 2011.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$35,397.56 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$35,397.56 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

pages.title: Definition of 'domestic student'
pages.page_title: U3.35 Definition of 'domestic student' (02/12/2013)

units.heading: Definition of 'domestic student'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of student instructions a 'domestic student' means a domestic student as defined in section 2 of the Education Act 1989. The Ministry of Education holds a complete list of who is considered to be a domestic student for the purpose of fee payment and enrolment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary schooling domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending primary and secondary schools and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue;

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents;

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents;

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current school year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: f
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: g
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending primary and secondary schools and are exempt from paying foreign tuition fees:

children.label: a
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is in New Zealand to study under an exchange programme approved by the New Zealand Government.

children.label: b
children.text: Children whose application for a residence class visa is under consideration and who are the dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand resident visa, or permanent resident visa.

children.label: c
children.text: Children whose application for New Zealand citizenship is under consideration and who are the dependent children of a New Zealand citizen.

children.label: d
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is onshore and the holder of a valid work visa other than those excluded under U8.20.

children.label: e
children.text: Students who have, or dependent children of any person who has, made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009.

children.label: f
children.text: Dependent children of a foreign student enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme in a New Zealand university.

children.label: g
children.text: Dependent children of any person who, during the current calendar year, last ceased to hold a special temporary visa (see H2).

children.label: h
children.text: Students who have entered New Zealand for the purposes of adoption and:

children.label: i
children.text: whose adoption application before the New Zealand Family Court (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student) is supported by the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services and who has a letter from the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services confirming this support; or

children.label: ii
children.text: who are the subject of an Interim Order of Adoption granted by the New Zealand Family Court under section 5 of the Adoption Act 1955 (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student).

children.label: i
children.text: People who are in the custody of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development pursuant to any of the following orders:

children.label: i
children.text: an order, pursuant to sections 78, 101 or 238(1)(d) of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, in favour of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 110 of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, appointing the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development as sole guardian; or

children.label: iii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 33 of the Care of Children Act 2004, whereby a child or young person is placed under the Guardianship of the Family Court or the High Court and the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development is appointed as agent of the court with power and discretion to place the child.

children.label: j
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand Aid Programme Scholarship.

children.label: k
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a visitor visa granted under V3.115.

children.label: l
children.text: Dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

children.label: m
children.text: Children granted a student visa under U10.5.

children.label: n
children.text: Students who are in New Zealand to study under an exchange scheme approved by the Ministry of Education (see E11.45).

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector (see U5.20) and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions or limited visa in order to undertake a programme of study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue.

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents.

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents.

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current academic year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Despite (d) above, dependent children aged 21 and over of Diplomatic, Consular or Official staff, who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand, may not be eligible for domestic student status and may be required to pay foreign student fees (see H2.1(b)).

children.label: f
children.text: A person who has made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and who is the holder of a valid temporary entry class visa.

children.label: g
children.text: A person who has been recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and whose application for residence is being processed.

children.label: h
children.text: A person who is enrolled at a tertiary education provider for the purpose of participating in industry training funded under the Industry Training Act 1992.

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector and are exempt from paying foreign tuition fees for foreign students:

children.label: a
children.text: Students enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme, in any New Zealand university (see U5.20).

children.label: b
children.text: A person who is in New Zealand to study under a New Zealand Government approved exchange programme at a tertiary education provider.

pages.title: Varying the conditions of temporary entry class visas
pages.page_title: E3.26 Varying the conditions of temporary entry class visas

units.heading: Varying the conditions of temporary entry class visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of temporary entry class visas should apply for a variation of the conditions of their visa, or a Job Change if they hold an Accredited Employer Work Visa, if:

children.label: i
children.text: they wish to work and do not have a visa that allows work in New Zealand; or

children.label: ii
children.text: they hold a work or visitor visa and wish to undertake a programme of study in New Zealand for longer than 3 months (unless U2.5 applies); or

children.label: iii
children.text: they hold a work visa limited by conditions and wish to change employers, and/or occupation and/or the location of employment; or

children.label: iv
children.text: they hold a work visa as a partner of an Accredited Employer or Essential Skills work visa holder which is limited by conditions and wish to remove these conditions.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Immigration officers may grant a variation of conditions for cases (a) (i)–(iii) above provided that the applicant completes the relevant application for Variation of Conditions or Job Change and produces:

children.label: i
children.text: the appropriate fee;

children.label: ii
children.text: a valid passport (or a certified copy) or travel document (or a certified copy), if not previously provided;

children.label: iii
children.text: documents which support the requested variation, such as:

children.label: b1
children.text: an offer of employment that meets W2.10.10, or WA4.10.1; or

children.label: b2
children.text: an offer of place at a suitable education provider that meets U3.5, and evidence of tuition fee payment or exemption that meets U3.10; and

children.label: b3
children.text: any other documents or information requested by the immigration officer.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: A variation of conditions will only be granted where the varied conditions still meet the objectives of the instructions which the visa was granted under.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: A variation of conditions to work for a specific employer (including any person associated with the employer who is able to influence the recruitment, employment or supervision of workers of that employer) will only be granted where the employer meets requirements at W2.10.5, W2.10.15 and W2.10.20 except where E3.26.1.20 applies.

units.heading: Varying the conditions of work visas
Varying Essential Skills work visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Essential skills work visa holders may be granted a variation of conditions to change the conditions of their visa relating to their employer, occupation, location of employment or a combination of these.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Essential skills work visa holders seeking to change their occupation or location of employment will need to meet a labour market test unless:

children.label: i
children.text: their new occupation is listed on an Essential Skills in Demand list and they meet the requirements of the list; or

children.label: ii
children.text: their new occupation is listed on the Green List (Appendix 13) and they meet the requirements of the list; or

children.label: iii
children.text: they are being paid at least twice the median wage ($70.00) (WA3.20(a)(i)).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The labour market test is met if:

children.label: i
children.text: the employer has advertised the position; and

children.label: ii
children.text: they did not find any suitable and available New Zealand workers for the job.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Essential skills work visa holders seeking to change their occupation need to be suitably qualified by qualification and/or experience for the employment on offer as required by the occupation in the ANZSCO which substantially matches the applicant’s proposed employment.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence of their job offer.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Despite the normal requirement that applications must be determined in accordance with the instructions in force at the date an application is made (E7.10(a)(ii)), applications made before these instructions came into effect that had not yet been decided, may be granted under these instructions, even if the instructions on the date they applied specified different requirements.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The ‘twice median wage rate’ for Variations of Conditions of Essential Skills work visas is $70.00 and reflects the June 2025 quarter publication of median wage data by Statistics New Zealand.

units.heading: Varying Specific Purpose or Event visa conditions

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Holders of a work visa granted under WS2 as players or professional sports coaches may apply for a variation of conditions of their work visa to undertake additional employment. A variation of conditions may be granted if:

children.label: a
children.text: the terms of the existing employment have been met, and will continue to be met; and either

children.label: b
children.text: the secondary employment is offered by the sports club or a company involved in the sport and the position is offered solely to this particular player or coach; or

children.label: c
children.text: the secondary employment is offered by an employer other than the sports club or a company involved in the sport and an immigration officer is satisfied that there are no New Zealand citizens or residence class visa holders available to be employed in the position (see WK3.10).

units.heading: Varying Talent (Accredited Employers) work visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of a work visa granted under WR1 (Talent (Accredited Employers) Work Instructions) may apply for a variation of conditions of their work visa to change employers. Variation of conditions may be granted:

children.label: i
children.text: to undertake employment for another employer who is accredited under WR1 (Talent (Accredited Employers) Work Instructions); or

children.label: ii
children.text: to undertake employment for another employer who is not accredited under WR1 (Talent (Accredited Employers) Work Instructions), if their employment is no longer available due to reasons beyond the visa holder’s control. When assessing such applications for a variation of conditions, immigration officers will consider all the circumstances of the applicant and the reasons for which the former accredited employer did not continue employment or the former employer’s accreditation was not renewed or rescinded; or

children.label: iii
children.text: to undertake employment for another employer who held accreditation (as defined by WR1.20) under Talent (Accredited Employer) Work Instructions after 31 March 2021 and accreditation has since expired.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: In order to be granted a variation of conditions under (a) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the base salary offered must be no less than the base salary that was required at the time the initial work visa application was made; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the offer of employment must meet the requirements of WR1.10, except WR1.10(a) and

children.label: iii
children.text: employers (including any person associated with the employer who is able to influence the recruitment, employment or supervision of workers of that employer) must meet the requirements under W2.10.5, W2.10.10, W2.10.15, W2.10.20 and W2.10.25.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite E7.10(a)(ii), immigration officers may apply E3.26.1.10(a)(iii) to an application to vary employer conditions of a Talent (Accredited Employer) work visa that has not been decided and was submitted before the effective date of these instructions.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Notes: - Where a person fails to continue employment in the circumstances described in (a) and (b) above, they will not be eligible for residence under the Residence Instructions for holders of work visas granted under the Talent (Accredited Employers) Work Instructions. - For the avoidance of doubt, the base salary in (b) above excludes employment-related allowances (for example overtime, tool or uniform allowances). The base salary is calculated on the basis of 40 hours work per week.

units.heading: Varying South Island Contribution work visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Despite WR7.15(b), holders of a work visa granted under WR7 (South Island Contribution work instructions) may apply for a variation of conditions of their work visa to change industries and/or regions.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A variation of conditions may be granted:

children.label: i
children.text: to undertake employment in another industry in the same region; or

children.label: ii
children.text: to undertake employment in the same industry in another South Island region.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: In order to be granted a variation of conditions under (a) above the applicant must:

children.label: i
children.text: provide evidence to show they meet the requirements of WR7.10(b)-WR7.10(f); and

children.label: ii
children.text: demonstrate that their employment is no longer available due to reasons beyond their control.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: When assessing such applications for a variation of conditions, immigration officers will consider all the circumstances of the applicant and the reasons for which the former employer did not continue employment.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: A variation may only be granted once under these instructions.

units.heading: Job Change for Accredited Employer work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Accredited Employer work visa holders who apply for a Job Change may be granted a variation of the conditions of their visa relating to their employer, occupation, location of employment or a combination of these.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A variation will only be granted where the employer holds accreditation under Accredited Employer Work instructions (WA2) and the AEWV holder has a valid job token.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: A variation will only be granted where the employment offered meets the usual requirements for employment as set out at WA4.10.1, including WA4.10.1.(e) which states that the employment must continue to meet the remuneration thresholds in effect at the time the Accredited Employer work visa application is made, or in this case, the Job Change application.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: A variation of visa conditions relating to occupation will only be granted where the applicant is suitably qualified by training and experience to do the job they have been offered (see WA4.10.5).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Accredited Employer work visa holders who apply for a Job Change will only be granted a variation of the conditions if the job token used to apply for the Job Change was approved under the same Accredited Employer work visa pathway (see WA1.10(a)).

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: A variation of conditions relating to occupation will only be granted where the applicant meets the minimum skills threshold (see WA4.10.6) and where the job token used to apply for a Job Change is a Global Workforce Seasonal Visa job token or a Peak Seasonal Visa job token.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: An application for a Job Change of an AEWV must be made using the approved online form provided by INZ for this purpose.

blocks.label: h
blocks.text: Accredited employer work visa holders whose visa is based on a type of employment that allows a five-year maximum continuous stay (see WA4.11.1) may not be granted a variation of conditions to work in a role allowing a three-year maximum continuous stay (see also WA4.11.1), unless they:

children.label: i
children.text: were paid at or above $29.66 and their application for an Accredited Employer work visa was submitted on or before 6 April 2024; and

children.label: ii
children.text: are in an ANZSCO skill level 4-5 occupation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The requirement to meet the minimum skills threshold (see WA4.10.6) does not apply to Job Change applications where the job token used to apply for a Job Change is a regular AEWV job token. The requirement to meet the minimum standard of English language (see WA4.12) does not apply to Job Change applications regardless of the pathway the job token was approved under.

units.heading: Job Change to vary employer following a business sale or restructure

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A Job Change to vary employer may be granted if an Accredited Employer work visa holder’s employment moves to another employer as a direct result of a business sale or restructure if:

children.label: i
children.text: the new employer holds or has applied for accreditation under WA2; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the employer has confirmed that they are transferring the existing work visa holder to the new entity; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the rate of pay, or salary, offered is the same as, or higher than, that currently received for performing the role; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the work visa holder is remaining in the same role and location.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: An immigration officer may postpone making a decision on the application if there is information that indicates the employer will likely no longer (in cases where the employer holds accreditation), or will likely not (in cases where an employer who currently holds, or has an accreditation application in progress), meet the requirements of their accreditation, until the employer is determined to meet the requirements.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If the employer’s accreditation is subsequently declined or revoked while a decision has been postponed under (b), the Job Change application must be declined, and the application will not be further postponed to await the outcome of any new accreditation application submitted by the employer.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: For the purposes of an immigration officer’s discretion in (b) above, the officer may consider postponing a decision if:

children.label: i
children.text: the accreditation of the employer — or, in the case of a restructure, the employer named on the applicant’s current visa — was revoked within the 12 months prior to the date the Job Change application was submitted (provided that E.26.1.21(a)(ii) does not apply); or

children.label: ii
children.text: there is information on INZ’s systems that the employer or any of its key persons fails to meet requirements related to compliance with specific employment, immigration and business standards as set out at WA2.10.10(a), (b), (g), (h), or (j); or

children.label: iii
children.text: the employer or, in the case of restructure, the employer named on the applicant’s current visa is being prosecuted for non-compliance (see WA2.10.10(l)).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: With regard to other instances of potential employer non-compliance (including but not limited to WA2.10.10(c) to (f), (m), (n) and (p)) an immigration officer’s discretion to postpone making a decision under (b) above may depend on factors such as:

children.label: i
children.text: the nature and seriousness of the alleged or proven non-compliance; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the number of instances of alleged or proven non-compliance; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the extent of certainty that these instances took place; and

children.label: iv
children.text: how long ago these instances occurred; and

children.label: v
children.text: whether any mitigation of proven instances has taken place (see for example WA2.10.10(e) and (i)).

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: An application under these instructions must be made using the approved online form provided by INZ for this purpose.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Any Accredited Employer work visa holders whose visas are varied in line with these instructions are considered to have jobs associated with the new employer and will therefore count towards the quota for standard accreditation as set out in WA2.15 (if applicable).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Notes: A Job Check is still required for any new position that a migrant is being hired into, or for any position that a migrant is being moved into, or any other situation that does not meet these instructions. In these situations, the applicant must apply for a Job Change under E3.26.1.20 above or submit a new AEWV application. The requirement to meet the minimum standard of English language (see WA4.12) does not apply to Job Change applications regardless of the pathway the job token was approved under.

units.heading: Varying work visa conditions for partners of Accredited Employer and Essential Skills work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of a work visa granted under WF3.1.5 (Partners of Accredited Employer and Essential Skills work visa holders) may apply for a variation of conditions to remove conditions on their work visa which state that they must:

children.label: i
children.text: work for an employer accredited under the AEWV scheme; and

children.label: b1
children.text: in a role paid at or above the median wage; or

children.label: b2
children.text: in a role earning the relevant wage threshold if a sector agreement is in place for that role; and

children.label: ii
children.text: not work in a role covered by a capped sector agreement

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Variation of conditions may be granted to allow the holder to undertake any work, in any occupation and location in New Zealand.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Self-employment is permitted however holders of visas granted under these instructions are restricted from employing others, whether directly, or indirectly via a business they operate as an owner.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: In order to be granted a variation of conditions under (a) above, the applicant’s supporting partner must earn at least $28.00 per hour (80 percent of the median wage).

units.heading: Varying the conditions of visitor visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of visitor visas granted under V3.100 Guardians accompanying students to New Zealand may only be granted a variation of conditions for part time work or part time study between the hours 9:30am and 2:30pm Monday to Friday (inclusive) (see V3.100.35).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Holders of visitor visas may be granted a variation of conditions for a duration of six weeks to undertake seasonal work (planting, maintaining, harvesting and packing crops) in any region where the Ministry of Social Development has identified a shortage of seasonal labour and for any employer in the horticulture or viticulture industries, provided the applicant has not been granted a variation of conditions for this purpose since their most recent entry to New Zealand.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Holders of visitor visas who are aged 18 or older, have left secondary school, and are included as a dependent child in an application for a 2021 Resident Visa may be granted a variation of conditions to allow them to work for up to 25 hours per week.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Holders of visitor visas may be granted a variation of conditions to allow them to work for up to 20 hours in any given week and full-time during the summer holiday period (1 December-31 January inclusive annually) where they:

children.label: i
children.text: Hold one of the following visitor visas:

children.label: b1
children.text: Child of a New Zealander Visitor Visa (V3.20); or

children.label: b2
children.text: Child of a Worker Visitor Visa (V3.10); or

children.label: b3
children.text: A general visitor visa (V2), provided they previously held a visitor or student visa as a dependent child (U8, V3.10 or V3.20) as the child of a New Zealand citizen or resident, or the primary applicant of a residence application listed below at (v); and

children.label: ii
children.text: meet age requirements as a result of being between 17 and 24 years old (inclusive) when they make their application; and

children.label: iii
children.text: have provided evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that they have successfully completed year 13 of secondary school (or the overseas equivalent) if they are aged 17 years old when they make their application; and

children.label: iv
children.text: have applied for residence under the Dependent Child Resident Visa (F5) category; or

children.label: v
children.text: are included as a dependent child in an application for residence under one of the below categories:

children.label: b1
children.text: Partnership Category (F2); or

children.label: b2
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa (SM); or

children.label: b3
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Visa (SR3); or

children.label: b4
children.text: Green List: Straight to Residence (SR4; or

children.label: b5
children.text: Green List: Work to Residence (SR5); or

children.label: b6
children.text: Care Workforce: Work to Residence (SR6); or

children.label: b7
children.text: Transport Sector: Work to Residence (SR7).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Notes: - The summer holiday period is defined as running from 1 December to 31 January (inclusive) annually for visitor visa holders with work conditions granted under E3.26.5, V3.10.20 or V3.20.5), which specify that they may undertake full-time work during the summer holiday period. This definition does not apply under student visa instructions, where the summer holiday period is determined by the associated education provider. - Evidence that a 17-year-old applicant has completed year 13 of secondary school (or the overseas equivalent) may include but is not limited to: a letter from their secondary school, a final school report or a graduation certificate. - As per R2.1.30(f) where immigration officers are required to assess the financial dependence of children included in a resident application, any part-time work undertaken in accordance with these conditions will not affect that assessment.

units.heading: Varying the conditions of student visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of student visas may be granted a variation of conditions to allow them to work in line with the requirements at U13.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Student visa holders with conditions specifying they may work for 20 hours a week who want to increase their work entitlement to 25 hours per week must apply using the online form for this purpose.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Holders of student visas may be granted a variation of conditions (see U3.40) to allow them to change their programme of study to a programme of study of the same or higher level provided the proposed programme of study is being undertaken at the same education provider specified on their visa.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: A pathway student visa holders whose visa does not specify a tertiary discipline or programme of study may be granted a variation of conditions to ensure their visa accurately specifies their course of study.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Variations of conditions will not be granted to allow a student visa holder enrol in a lower-level programme of study or to enrol with a different education provider.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Despite (e) above, a variation of conditions may be granted to allow a student visa holder to enrol with a different education provider if the student visa holder can demonstrate that the change to the new provider is for reasons beyond the student visa holder’s control (for example, but not limited to, circumstances where the education provider has closed or is going to close or circumstances arising from compliance action undertaken by NZQA).

units.heading: Varying the conditions of Skilled Migrant Category interim visas

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of meeting E3.26.15 instructions, ‘Skilled Migrant Category’ (SMC) is defined as those set out in SR3 instructions. SMC interim visa conditions may only be varied in accordance with these (E3.26.15) instructions.

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Holders of SMC interim visas with employer-specific work conditions may be granted a variation of conditions to change employer, occupation, location of employment, or a combination of these. A variation of conditions may be granted if:

children.label: i
children.text: the SMC interim visa holder meets the requirements set out in E3.26.1.20; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the employment is paid at or above the median wage ($35.00).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Holders of SMC interim visas with student conditions may be granted a variation of conditions to allow them to work for up to 25 hours in any given week and full-time in specified vacation periods (see U13.10 and U13.15) if the interim visa holder:

children.label: i
children.text: meets the applicable requirements at U13; and

children.label: ii
children.text: is aged 16 or older; and

children.label: iii
children.text: has written permission from their parents and education provider (if they are enrolled with an education provider) if they are aged 16 or 17 years old; and

children.label: iv
children.text: is included in an SMC resident visa application as a dependent child, if they held a visitor visa directly before being granted an SMC interim visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Holders of SMC interim visas with visitor conditions may be granted a variation of conditions to allow them to hold open study conditions and/or work for up to 25 hours in any given week and full-time during specified vacation periods (see U13.15) if they are:

children.label: i
children.text: aged 18 or older; and

children.label: ii
children.text: included as a dependent child in an application for a Skilled Migrant Category resident visa.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Notes: - The median wage rate for Variations of Conditions of Skilled Migrant Category interim visa holders is $35.00 and reflects the June 2025 quarter publication of median wage data by Statistics New Zealand. - Where the SMC application includes the requirement to have a job or job offer which meets the definition of skilled employment, applicants seeking a variation of conditions will be responsible for ensuring that the planned new employment still meets the SMC application criteria.

pages.title: Summary

units.heading: Summary

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless otherwise specified, to be granted a student visa to attend a programme of study of more than three months, applicants must:

children.label: i
children.text: have an offer of a place or, if returning to continue a programme of study, a confirmation of enrolment in an approved programme of study with an education provider in New Zealand that meets student visa requirements (see U3.5, U3.10, and U5.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: be exempted from or have paid tuition fees; and

children.label: iii
children.text: if aged under 18, meet accommodation requirements (see U3.15); and

children.label: iv
children.text: have fulfilled the purpose and met the conditions for any previous or current temporary visas held as set out in E3.15 and E3.20; and

children.label: v
children.text: meet the conditions set out in E3.20; and

children.label: vi
children.text: not be the holder of a current visitor visa granted under Guardians accompanying students to New Zealand instructions (see V3.100).); and

children.label: vii
children.text: hold acceptable insurance (see U3.45), unless they are a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) student or a New Zealand Aid Programme-supported student.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All applicants must meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for:

children.label: i
children.text: lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa as set out at E4; and

children.label: ii
children.text: bona fide applicants as set out at E5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: health and character as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have not completed, or will not be completing the programme of study endorsed on their student visa and who wish to change their programme of study and/or education provider must:

children.label: i
children.text: meet requirements (a) and (b) above; and

children.label: ii
children.text: meet the requirements set out at U3.40. Note: Applicants who are progressing to further study, for example a student in Year 13 who is progressing to tertiary studies, will not need to meet U3.40.

pages.title: Offer of a place
pages.page_title: U3.5 Offer of a place (24/03/2014)

units.heading: Offer of a place

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Applicants must have an offer of a place with a New Zealand education provider, which shows:

children.label: a
children.text: the name of the programme of study or training scheme and the minimum time required for completing it; and

children.label: b
children.text: evidence that the programme of study or training scheme and education provider meet foreign student requirements (see U5); and

children.label: c
children.text: confirmation that the education provider has assessed and is satisfied the prospective student meets the programme of study or training scheme competencies and enrolment provision (section 7.1) as set out in the Code of Practice for the Pastoral Care of International Students; and

children.label: d
children.text: the amount of the tuition fee, or, if the programme of study is longer than one year, the annual fee; and

children.label: e
children.text: whether or not the student has to pay programme of study or training scheme fees and whether the fees are domestic or foreign fees; and

children.label: f
children.text: whether the student is full-time (see U6.1.1) or part-time (see U7.20); and

children.label: g
children.text: the dates and duration of all scheduled vacations if the programme of study or training scheme is one academic year or more.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: ~For the information specified at U3.5(g), this can be provided in a separate document accompanying the Offer of Place or Confirmation of Enrolment. ~ An academic year means a programme of study of a minimum of 120 credits during a period of at least eight months (minimum of two semesters). ~From January 2014, students seeking to enrol in a programme of study or training scheme offered at an education provider that holds a Category Four status under the NZQA’s External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system will not be granted a student visa.

pages.title: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand
pages.page_title: U3.20 Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand (02/12/2013)

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that they have sufficient funds available to maintain themselves throughout the period of their stay in New Zealand.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence may include but is not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: a notice of the award of a full scholarship; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a completed Sponsorship for Temporary Entry (INZ 1025) form (see U3.20.5); or

children.label: iii
children.text: a completed Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form, which covers a stay in New Zealand for the length of the visa (see U3.20.10); or

children.label: iv
children.text: funds held by or on behalf of the student (see U3.20.20).

units.heading: Sponsorship

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A sponsor for a student visa application must be an acceptable sponsor (see E6.5) and be either:

children.label: i
children.text: a natural person who is a relative or a friend of the applicant; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an organisation or government agency (an individual must be nominated as the authorised contact).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Sponsors must satisfy an immigration officer that they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet sponsorship obligations); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are sponsoring.

units.heading: Financial Undertaking

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Before the student’s arrival in New Zealand, a financial undertaking may be provided by a third party.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the third party is a person, they must be a relative or a friend of the applicant.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If the third party is not a person, they must nominate an individual as an authorised contact.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The third party providing the financial undertaking must satisfy an immigration officer they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet their financial obligations as set out on the Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are supporting.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Where a third party wishes to continue providing a financial undertaking for the student’s subsequent onshore student visa applications, they may do so if they continue to meet (d).

units.heading: Determining whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To determine whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide, immigration officers may consider:

children.label: a
children.text: the relationship between the applicant and the sponsor or third party;

children.label: b
children.text: any previous breaches of financial obligations set out in undertakings;

children.label: c
children.text: the number of student visa applications they are currently supporting;

children.label: d
children.text: the period of time for which funds have been held by the sponsor or third party; and

children.label: e
children.text: the student’s ability to access funds from the sponsor or third party while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds held by or on behalf of the student

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Where funds are held by or on behalf of the student, immigration officers must be satisfied that the funds are from a genuine source and are genuinely available for the purposes of the applicant’s maintenance requirements.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: When determining whether a student has sufficient funds to maintain themselves throughout their stay in New Zealand, immigration officers may consider the period of time for which funds have been held by the student and the student’s ability to access funds while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking programmes of study lasting less than 36 weeks

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students taking programmes of study lasting less than 36 weeks must provide evidence they have funds of at least NZ$1,250 per month of study available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: This evidence may be sighted after the application has been approved in principle.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking programmes of study lasting 36 weeks or longer

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students taking programmes of study lasting 36 weeks or longer must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that:

children.label: a
children.text: they have NZ$15,000.00 per year available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses); or

children.label: b
children.text: if they are citizens of Samoa and Tonga a written guarantee of maintenance from a relative in New Zealand who is either a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder.

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maternity health services

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Pregnant applicants for a student visa who are due to give birth while in New Zealand must provide evidence that they:

children.label: a
children.text: have funds of at least NZ$9,000 available to pay for maternity health services; or

children.label: b
children.text: have sponsorship by a person, an organisation or a Government agency which meets generic sponsorship requirements set out at E6.5, to cover maternity health services; or

children.label: c
children.text: have a guarantee of financial undertaking by a third party which covers maternity health services (see U3.20.10); or

children.label: d
children.text: are eligible for publicly-funded maternity health services.
