pages.title: Students aged 13 and under and students enrolled in Years 1 to 8
pages.page_title: U3.30 Students aged 13 and under and students enrolled in Years 1 to 8 (08/04/2013)

units.heading: Students aged 13 and under and students enrolled in Years 1 to 8

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Student visas will only be granted to students enrolled in school years 1 to 8 and students aged 13 and under who are enrolled in any other provider (see U3.30.5 below) if they will be living in New Zealand with their legal guardian (see U3.30.1) unless:

children.label: i
children.text: they are domestic students (see U3.35); or

children.label: ii
children.text: they are enrolled in a school hostel (see U3.30.10 below) approved by the Code Administrator; or

children.label: iii
children.text: they are enrolled in Years 7 or 8 of a school, or are aged 11 to 13 years and enrolled in any other provider (see U3.30.5), which has prior programme approval from the Code Administrator.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All visas granted under these instructions are subject to the condition that the holder live with their legal guardian (see U3.30.1) in New Zealand, unless the student visa holder has been granted a variation of conditions under U7.25 or one of the exceptions listed in U3.30(a) i-iii applies.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The Code Administrator is the Ministry of Education.

units.heading: Definition of 'legal guardian'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of these instructions a 'legal guardian' is the person with the legal right and responsibility to provide for the care (including education and health) of an international student, and provides for the care of the student in the student's home country. This definition includes the student's biological or adoptive parents, testamentary guardian, or court-appointed guardian.

units.heading: Definition of 'other provider'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of these instructions 'other provider' is a private training establishment.

units.heading: Definition of 'school hostel'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of these instructions 'school hostel' means a hostel as defined in section 2 of the Education Act 1989, and:

children.label: a
children.text: licensed under regulations made under section 144C of the Education Act 1989 (if any); or

children.label: b
children.text: approved and monitored by the Code Administrator, for international students enrolled in Years 1 to 6 of a school, or aged 10 and under and enrolled in any other provider.

pages.title: Insurance requirements for fee-paying foreign students
pages.page_title: U3.45 Insurance requirements for fee-paying foreign students (30/07/2012)

units.heading: Insurance requirements for fee-paying foreign students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Fee-paying foreign students must hold acceptable insurance as a condition of their visa (see E3.20(f)) unless (e) below applies.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A fee-paying foreign student must declare that they will arrange and hold acceptable insurance from the period of their enrolment until the expiry of their student visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: An acceptable insurance policy is one which complies with the insurance requirements of the Code of Practice for the Pastoral Care of International Students and is acceptable to the applicant’s education provider.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: A student may be required to provide evidence that they held insurance from the time of their enrolment until the expiry of their student visa with any further visa application made.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: The requirement to hold acceptable insurance does not apply to Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) students or New Zealand Aid Programme-supported students.

units.heading: Exchange students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students studying under reciprocal exchange schemes approved by the Minister of Education are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending primary and secondary schools and are exempt from paying foreign tuition fees (see U3.35.5).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: There are two types of New Zealand student exchange schemes under which international students may be enrolled in New Zealand schools without paying international fees: Note: The general requirements for participants in approved student exchange schemes are set out at E11.55.

children.label: i
children.text: school-to-school student exchange schemes run by a school that is a signatory to the Ministry of Education's Code of Practice for the Pastoral Care of International Students (see E11.55.20); and

children.label: ii
children.text: student exchange schemes run by approved exchange programme organisations (see E11.55.20).

pages.title: Status of education providers and programmes
pages.page_title: U5.1 Status of education providers and programmes (13/01/2014)

units.heading: Status of education providers and programmes

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All education providers must certify in their offers of places to foreign students (see U3.5) that the programme of study or training scheme offered complies with foreign student requirements for different kinds of education providers (see U5.5- U5.20).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All education providers offering places to foreign students must be signatories to the Ministry of Education's Code of Practice for Pastoral Care of International Students.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Any queries on the status of programmes or training schemes offered by private training establishments should be referred to the Service Delivery Unit, Quality Assurance Division, New Zealand Qualifications Authority (NZQA), PO Box 160, Wellington.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Students seeking to enrol in a programme of study or training scheme offered at an education provider that holds a Category Four status under the NZQA’s External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system will not be granted a student visa.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Immigration New Zealand (INZ) may suspend the processing of applications for student visas for study at an education provider where at least one of the following applies:

children.label: i
children.text: the offered programme of study or training scheme does not comply with foreign student requirements as set out in U5.5 to U5.20;

children.label: ii
children.text: the education provider is not complying with its obligations under the Immigration Act, immigration regulations, or immigration instructions;

children.label: iii
children.text: INZ has been informed by education agencies that the education provider is not complying with its obligations under the Education Act and education regulations.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Before a decision is made to suspend the processing of student visas, the following will be taken into account:

children.label: i
children.text: evidence of the non-compliance; and

children.label: ii
children.text: reasons for the non-compliance; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the duration, frequency, and severity of the non-compliance.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: INZ may resume the processing of student visas if it is satisfied that the education provider is complying with its obligations.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Despite (d), where an applicant fails to meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for health, character or bona fide applicants, the application may be declined.

pages.title: Visas for the length of a programme of study
pages.page_title: U6.35 Visas for the length of a programme of study (25/08/2014)

units.heading: Visas for the length of a programme of study

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students may be granted a student visa for the length of their programme of study, regardless of the period for which they have paid their tuition fees, as specified in:

children.label: a
children.text: Students Online Initiative (see U6.35.1); or

children.label: b
children.text: Aviation students instructions (U6.35.5).

units.heading: Students Online Initiative

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students may be granted a student visa for the length of their programme of study if the:

children.label: i
children.text: student has an offer of a place with an education provider with which INZ has a Memorandum of Understanding for the Students Online Initiative which allows for the grant of visas for the length of programme of study; and

children.label: ii
children.text: education provider supports the grant of a length of programme of study visa.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of the education provider support to grant a length of a programme of study visa must be provided.

units.heading: Aviation students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Aviation students may be granted a student visa for the length of their programme of study if:

children.label: i
children.text: the student has an offer of place from an aviation training provider that is:

children.label: b1
children.text: certified by the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand; and

children.label: b2
children.text: a signatory to the Ministry of Education’s Code of Practice for the Pastoral Care of International Students (see U3.5 and U5.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: the aviation training provider supports the grant of a length of programme of study visa; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the full first term of tuition fees have been paid.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of the aviation training provider’s support to grant a length of a programme of study visa must be provided.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a)(iii), evidence of tuition fee payment is not required where the aviation student is an Air New Zealand trainee and provides a guarantee from Air New Zealand.

pages.page_title: U7.10 Student visa holders liable for deportation (02/12/2013)

units.heading: Student visa holders liable for deportation

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa holder who breaches any of the conditions of their visa (in particular those relating to attendance, employment, holding acceptable insurance and living with their legal guardian) may become liable for deportation (see E3.60 and U13.1c).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Where the student is required to live with a legal guardian (see U3.30) and that legal guardian becomes liable for deportation, the student will also become liable for deportation (see E3.60).

pages.title: Temporary exemption from the requirement to live with a legal guardian in New Zealand
pages.page_title: U7.25 Temporary exemption from the requirement to live with a legal guardian in New Zealand (29/11/2010)

units.heading: Temporary exemption from the requirement to live with a legal guardian in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students enrolled in school years 1 to 8, and students aged 13 and under who are enrolled in any other provider (see U3.30.5), may apply for a variation of conditions to their student visa to temporarily exempt them from the requirement to live with their legal guardian in New Zealand as set out at U3.30(b).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A variation of conditions will only be granted where an immigration officer is satisfied that an emergency exists that requires the legal guardian to temporarily return to their home country.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The applicant must provide evidence that:

children.label: i
children.text: an emergency exists that requires the legal guardian to temporarily return to their home country; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the education provider has approved the alternative caregiving arrangements, consistent with its obligations under the Code of Practice for the Pastoral Care of International Students; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the legal guardian has purchased a return travel ticket.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The variation of conditions may be granted for the period of time required, up to a maximum of four weeks.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Any failure of the legal guardian to return to New Zealand within the approved period may result in the student visa holder becoming liable for deportation (see U7.10).

pages.title: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment
pages.page_title: U13.15 Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment (07/12/2015)

units.heading: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment, a student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work during the academic year, and during any scheduled vacations, including within the academic year.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Students aged 16 or 17 years of age enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment must have written permission from their education provider and written parental consent to be granted conditions allowing work.

units.heading: Work conditions for up to twenty hours in any given week

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa holder may be granted with conditions to work for up to 20 hours in any given week during the validity of the visa if the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1) of at least two academic years’ duration; or

children.label: b
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study, culminating in a New Zealand qualification that would qualify for points under the Skilled Migrant Category (see SM14); or

children.label: c
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study of at least one academic year's duration as part of an approved tertiary student exchange scheme (see E11.45); or

children.label: d
children.text: engaged in a full-time programme of study of at least six months’ duration; and

children.label: i
children.text: an immigration officer is satisfied that the primary purpose of the programme of study is to develop English language skills; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the student can provide a certificate (no more than 2 years old at the time the application is lodged) from the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) which shows an overall band score of at least 5.0 in the IELTS (General or Academic Module); or

children.label: e
children.text: undertaking full-time English language study of at least 14 consecutive weeks’ duration at an education provider that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the NZQA EER quality assurance system; or Note: When assessing eligibility for work rights under (e) for an applicant who holds a current student visa, all consecutive previous English language study undertaken on this and any previous student visa can be counted towards the 14 consecutive week period provided the programme of study the applicant is applying for: - follows directly from their current study and - is with the same provider as that on their current and any previous student visa.

children.label: f
children.text: undertaking a full-time foundation programme that commenced on or before 28 February 2014 and that programme of study is of at least one academic year’s duration at level four or higher on the New Zealand Qualification Framework at an education provider in Canterbury that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system.

units.heading: Full time work rights during Christmas-New Year vacation period

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation period provided that the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: studying full-time (see UU6.1.1); and

children.label: b
children.text: enrolled in a programme of study that has a minimum duration of at least two semesters during a period of at least eight months.

units.heading: Full time work rights during scheduled vacations

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during all scheduled vacations, if the student is undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1); and of at least one academic year’s duration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) where scheduled vacations are more than one third of the programme of study duration for programmes of study offered by tertiary providers other than universities, full-time work rights may not be granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: An academic year means a programme of study of a minimum of 120 credits during a period of at least eight months (minimum of two semesters)

units.heading: Work conditions for masters by research or doctoral students

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder unlimited work rights if:

children.label: a
children.text: the student is undertaking a Masters by Research or Doctoral degree, and

children.label: b
children.text: the qualification is awarded by a New Zealand tertiary institution.

pages.title: Provider requirements
pages.page_title: U14.20 Provider requirements (07/12/2015)

units.heading: Provider requirements
Pathway pilot entry criteria

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: To qualify for entry to the Pathway student visa pilot, an education provider must:

children.label: i
children.text: be invited by Immigration New Zealand to be a pilot participant; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have signed the Pathway Student Visas - Pilot Participation Declaration agreeing to the requirements as set out at U14.20.10; and

children.label: iii
children.text: be either a school, a university or hold a Category One or Two rating under New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation and Review framework; and

children.label: iv
children.text: have a minimum 90% student visa application approval rate over the 2014/15 financial year (12 month period); and

children.label: v
children.text: comply with the legislative requirements as set out under the Education Act 1989 to offer programmes of study to foreign students (U5.5 to U5.20); and

children.label: vi
children.text: be a signatory to the Ministry of Education's Code of Practice for Pastoral Care of International Students.

units.heading: Eligible pathways

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All pathways must demonstrate academic progression to the second or subsequent programme of study building on the previous study.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All consecutive programmes of study that demonstrate progression are eligible to be included in the pilot with the exception of the following pathways:

children.label: i
children.text: Any English language programme of study to any Level 1-4 Certificate on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework (NZQF);

children.label: ii
children.text: All pathways within and between NZQF Levels 1-4 Certificates, and

children.label: iii
children.text: Secondary school to any NZQF Levels 1–4 Certificates.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Breaks between consecutive programmes of study must not exceed 16 weeks

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Only education providers who meet the requirements set out under U14.20.1 can offer a joint pathway in conjunction with one another.

units.heading: Formal agreement between qualifying education providers

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: To ensure a student’s pastoral care needs are met, qualifying education providers who intend offering an education pathway in conjunction with one another must enter into a formal agreement.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The formal agreement must include and set out the following processes and arrangements:

children.label: i
children.text: The application process (joint covering letter with two/three offers of place)

children.label: ii
children.text: Pastoral care obligations

children.label: iii
children.text: Handover arrangements in transition periods between programmes of study/education providers

children.label: iv
children.text: The process if a significant gap exists between completion of a programme of study and the start of a second or subsequent programme of study or in the event some papers are failed and cannot be repeated within a 16 week period.

children.label: v
children.text: The process if conditional entry requirements for second or subsequent programmes of study are not met

children.label: vi
children.text: The process if the student fails to attend and/or make satisfactory progress (E3.20(d))

children.label: vii
children.text: The process if the student wishes to leave intended pathway

children.label: viii
children.text: The obligation to notify INZ where a pathway student:

children.label: b1
children.text: requires additional time to complete a programme of study and time required is likely to exceed 16 weeks; or

children.label: b2
children.text: fails to meet the conditional entry requirements for a second or subsequent programme of study; or

children.label: b3
children.text: fails to enrol for a subsequent programme of study; or

children.label: b4
children.text: fails to attend and/or make satisfactory progress; and

children.label: b5
children.text: has their enrolment in a programme of study terminated.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where an education pathway is offered by a single qualifying education provider, the formal agreement processes set out at (b) must be met.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The signed formal agreement does not have to be submitted with a pathway student visa application, however it must be made available to INZ if requested.

units.heading: Non-compliance with formal agreement requirements or when under active investigation by Immigration New Zealand

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Where non-compliance, other than of a minor nature, with any of the matters agreed to in the Pathway Student Visas - Pilot Participation Declaration, or where the pathway education provider is under active investigation by INZ for offences committed under part 10 of the Immigration Act 2009 the following process may occur:

children.label: a
children.text: INZ will suspend the processing of any student visa applications related to an existing pathway agreement immediately.

children.label: b
children.text: The non-compliant pathway education providers will be advised in writing of the suspension and will be sent a report detailing the non-compliance, and will be given 30 days to remedy the non-compliance.

children.label: c
children.text: Resolution (or satisfactory progress towards resolution) of the non-compliance to the satisfaction of INZ within the 30 day period will see the suspension lifted and processing of related pathway student visa applications will resume.

children.label: d
children.text: The Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment or the New Zealand Qualifications Authority may conduct an investigation three to six months later to assess the effectiveness of the remediation undertaken. If the remediation is deemed inadequate or ineffective, the suspension can be re-imposed or the provider may be removed from the pathways pilot and current pathway student visa holders become liable for deportation.

children.label: e
children.text: If INZ is not satisfied that the non-compliance has been addressed or satisfactory progress has been made towards resolution within the 30 day period, the suspension of related student visa processing will continue (until resolution occurs).

children.label: f
children.text: Failure to address or make satisfactory progress towards resolving the non-compliance may result in removal from the pathways pilot, and current student visa holders becoming liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: INZ may rely on the advice of the Ministry of Education and/or the New Zealand Qualifications Authority in determining whether resolution has been reached or satisfactory progress has been made towards resolution.

pages.page_title: U3.5 Offer of a place (22/08/2016)

units.heading: Offer of a place

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Applicants must have an offer of a place with a New Zealand education provider, which shows:

children.label: a
children.text: the name of the programme of study or training scheme and the minimum time required for completing it; and

children.label: b
children.text: evidence that the programme of study or training scheme and education provider meet foreign student requirements (see U5); and

children.label: c
children.text: confirmation that the education provider has assessed and is satisfied the prospective student meets the programme of study or training scheme competencies and enrolment provision (section 7.1) as set out in the Education (Pastoral Care of International Students) Code of Practice 2016; and

children.label: d
children.text: the amount of the tuition fee, or, if the programme of study is longer than one year, the annual fee; and

children.label: e
children.text: whether or not the student has to pay programme of study or training scheme fees and whether the fees are domestic or foreign fees; and

children.label: f
children.text: whether the student is full-time (see U6.1.1) or part-time (see U7.20); and

children.label: g
children.text: the dates and duration of all scheduled vacations if the programme of study or training scheme is one academic year or more.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: ~For the information specified at U3.5(g), this can be provided in a separate document accompanying the Offer of Place or Confirmation of Enrolment. ~ An academic year means a programme of study of a minimum of 120 credits during a period of at least eight months (minimum of two semesters). ~From January 2014, students seeking to enrol in a programme of study or training scheme offered at an education provider that holds a Category Four status under the NZQA’s External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system will not be granted a student visa.

pages.title: Insurance requirements for fee-paying foreign students
pages.page_title: U3.45 Insurance requirements for fee-paying foreign students (22/08/2016)

units.heading: Insurance requirements for fee-paying foreign students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Fee-paying foreign students must hold insurance as a condition of their visa (see E3.20(f)) unless (e) below applies.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A fee-paying foreign student must declare that they will arrange and hold insurance, which complies with the insurance requirements of the Education (Pastoral Care of International Students) Code of Practice 2016 and is acceptable to the student’s education provider, from the period of their enrolment until the expiry of their student visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: A student may be required to provide evidence that they held insurance from the time of their enrolment until the expiry of their student visa with any further visa application made.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The requirement to hold insurance does not apply to Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) students or New Zealand Aid Programme-supported students.

pages.title: Currency and conditions of pathway student visas
pages.page_title: U14.10 Currency and conditions of pathway student visas (04/02/2016)

units.heading: Currency and conditions of pathway student visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For the purposes of the pathway student visa pilot, a visa can be granted up to a maximum of five years;

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A visa may be granted to expire no more than three months beyond completion of the final pathway programme of study within the maximum currency of five years;

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Work conditions for the duration of the pathway student visa will only be granted where the first programme of study meets the requirements as set out at U13.1, U13.10 or U13.15;

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If the second or subsequent programme of study meets the requirements set out at U13.1, U13.10 or U13.15, a variation of conditions is required in order to be granted work conditions;

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Where (d) applies, a Variation of Conditions or Variation of Travel Conditions (INZ 1020) application form must be completed and submitted with the required fee.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: The holder must make satisfactory progress on the pathway by:

children.label: i
children.text: meeting the conditional pre-requisites for enrolment into a second or subsequent programme of study (E3.20(d); and

children.label: ii
children.text: commencing the second or subsequent programme of study on a pathway within a 16 week period of completing an earlier programme of study.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Where a first time student has submitted an IELTS test (or equivalent) as set out at U14.5.1 (c) and been granted a pathway student visa to undertake an English language programme of study culminating in a qualification at Levels 5 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework, the English Language programme of study must be completed within a 16 week period.

pages.title: Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions
pages.page_title: U14.15 Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions (04/02/2016)

units.heading: Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: If a student holding a pathway student visa wishes to move to a different education provider or lower level programme of study than those specified in their visa conditions, they must apply for a new student visa and meet the requirements set out at U3.40.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A variation of conditions, for the purpose of changing a programme of study at the same education provider will only be granted if an immigration officer is satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant meets the student requirements set out at U3.1; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant has not breached their visa conditions as set out at E3.20; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the original student visa would have been granted for the proposed programme of study; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the proposed programme of study is at the same or higher level on the New Zealand Qualification Framework as the original programme of study; and

children.label: v
children.text: the applicant remains a bona fide applicant (see E5.1).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Factors that an immigration officer may take into consideration when determining (b)(iii) and (b)(iv) above include, but are not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: the time elapsed since the original visa was granted;

children.label: ii
children.text: whether the level and/or subject area of the proposed programme of study are significantly different from the original programme of study; and

children.label: iii
children.text: any relevant information held about the previous application(s) including advice from the original issuing branch (see E7.1.1).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Students who have received New Zealand Aid Programme funding within the two years prior to their application to change programme of study must also provide evidence that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade supports the change of programme of study and that any scholarship continues.

units.heading: Breaching visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student on an pathway student visa will be considered to be in breach of visa conditions where:

children.label: i
children.text: they fail to meet conditional pre-requisites for enrolment into a second or subsequent programme of study (E3.20(d); or

children.label: ii
children.text: the time between the completion of one programme of study and the start of a second or subsequent programme of study on a pathway exceeds 16 weeks; or

children.label: iii
children.text: they have submitted an IELTS test (or equivalent) as set out at U14.5.1 (c) and their intended pathway is an English language programme of study culminating in a qualification at Levels 5 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework and the English Language programme of study is not completed within a 16 week period.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A breach of visa conditions may result in the issue of a Deportation Liability Notice (E3.60).

pages.title: Students affected by New Zealand Qualifications Authority Compliance notification
pages.page_title: U16 Students affected by New Zealand Qualifications Authority Compliance notification

units.heading: Students affected by New Zealand Qualifications Authority Compliance notification

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The intent of these instructions is to allow people whose education provider is subject to statutory intervention by the New Zealand Qualifications Authority (NZQA) to maintain their status as student visa holders while awaiting a determination of whether their qualification can be awarded.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Student visas may be granted under these instructions where the applicant:

children.label: i
children.text: has submitted all required material for the assessment of their qualification;

children.label: ii
children.text: is or has been enrolled at an education provider that is subject to statutory intervention by NZQA which prevents the awarding of their qualification;

children.label: iii
children.text: is awaiting NZQA’s confirmation that their qualification can be awarded; and

children.label: iv
children.text: meets health and character requirements as set out at A4 and A5.

pages.title: Application and evidence
pages.page_title: U16.1 Application and evidence

units.heading: Application and evidence

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: a completed student visa application form and fee; and

children.label: ii
children.text: that they have the required funds available to maintain themselves during their intended stay in New Zealand as per U3.20.25(a); and

children.label: iii
children.text: confirmation from their education provider that they have submitted all required material for the assessment of their qualification.

blocks.label: b

pages.title: Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa
pages.page_title: U14.5 Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa (04/02/2016)

units.heading: Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To be granted a pathway student visa, an applicant must:

children.label: a
children.text: be offered an eligible study pathway from a qualifying provider (U14.20);

children.label: b
children.text: meet the general requirements to be granted a student visa as set out at U3.1;

children.label: c
children.text: meet the additional evidential requirements for pathway student visa set out at U14.5.1;

children.label: d
children.text: make an application for a student visa before 7 June 2017.

units.heading: Evidence of meeting requirements

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: In addition to meeting the general requirements to be granted a student visa as set out at U3.1, when applying for a pathway student visa an applicant must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: Where there is more than one education provider, A joint covering letter from pathway education providers setting out the pathway programmes of study and start and end dates of each programme of study;

children.label: ii
children.text: An offer of place (or joint offer) for each programme of study that meets the requirements set out at U3.5;

children.label: iii
children.text: Evidence that tuition fee requirements, as set out at U3.10, for either the first programme of study or first year of study (whichever is shorter) have been met and satisfy an immigration officer that they have the ability to fund any remaining balance of the first programme of study and subsequent programmes of study on the intended pathway; and

children.label: iv
children.text: Evidence that the maintenance funds requirements set out in U3.20 for the first year of study on the intended pathway have been met and satisfy an immigration officer that they have the ability to fund any remaining balance of the first programme of study and subsequent programmes of study on the intended pathway.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a)(ii), second and subsequent offers of place for a pathway can be conditional on meeting pre-requisite programme of study entry criteria.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: First time pathway student visa applicants from a country with a student visa decline rate of more than 20 per cent who intend a study pathway commencing with an English language programme of study and culminating in a qualification at Levels 5 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework must:

children.label: i
children.text: submit an International English Language Testing System test (IELTS) (or equivalent internationally recognised test) at the time of application; and

children.label: ii
children.text: demonstrate that they only require an improvement of 0.5 of an IELTS overall band score (or equivalent) to meet the English language prerequisite for entry into the intended level 5 to 8 programme of study.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The student visa decline rate for a country is based on statistics, generated over a calendar year (12 months), by Immigration New Zealand. The decline rate and the name of the country are published on the INZ website. For the purpose of this instruction, the internationally recognised English language tests and corresponding IELTS equivalent test scores set out on the INZ website are considered acceptable.

units.heading: Provider requirements
Pathway pilot entry criteria

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: To qualify for entry to the Pathway student visa pilot, an education provider must:

children.label: i
children.text: be invited by Immigration New Zealand to be a pilot participant; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have signed the Pathway Student Visas - Pilot Participation Declaration agreeing to the requirements as set out at U14.20.10; and

children.label: iii
children.text: be either a school, a university or hold a Category One or Two rating under New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation and Review framework; and

children.label: iv
children.text: have a minimum 90% student visa application approval rate over the 2014/15 financial year (12 month period); and

children.label: v
children.text: comply with the legislative requirements as set out under the Education Act 1989 to offer programmes of study to foreign students (U5.5 to U5.20); and

children.label: vi
children.text: be a signatory to the Ministry of Education's Education (Pastoral Care of International Students) Code of Practice 2016.

units.heading: Eligible pathways

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All pathways must demonstrate academic progression to the second or subsequent programme of study building on the previous study.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All consecutive programmes of study that demonstrate progression are eligible to be included in the pilot with the exception of the following pathways:

children.label: i
children.text: Any English language programme of study to any Level 1-4 Certificate on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework (NZQF);

children.label: ii
children.text: All pathways within and between NZQF Levels 1-4 Certificates, and

children.label: iii
children.text: Secondary school to any NZQF Levels 1–4 Certificates.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Breaks between consecutive programmes of study must not exceed 16 weeks

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Only education providers who meet the requirements set out under U14.20.1 can offer a joint pathway in conjunction with one another.

units.heading: Formal agreement between qualifying education providers

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: To ensure a student’s pastoral care needs are met, qualifying education providers who intend offering an education pathway in conjunction with one another must enter into a formal agreement.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The formal agreement must include and set out the following processes and arrangements:

children.label: i
children.text: The application process (joint covering letter with two/three offers of place)

children.label: ii
children.text: Pastoral care obligations

children.label: iii
children.text: Handover arrangements in transition periods between programmes of study/education providers

children.label: iv
children.text: The process if a significant gap exists between completion of a programme of study and the start of a second or subsequent programme of study or in the event some papers are failed and cannot be repeated within a 16 week period.

children.label: v
children.text: The process if conditional entry requirements for second or subsequent programmes of study are not met

children.label: vi
children.text: The process if the student fails to attend and/or make satisfactory progress (E3.20(d))

children.label: vii
children.text: The process if the student wishes to leave intended pathway

children.label: viii
children.text: The obligation to notify INZ where a pathway student:

children.label: b1
children.text: requires additional time to complete a programme of study and time required is likely to exceed 16 weeks; or

children.label: b2
children.text: fails to meet the conditional entry requirements for a second or subsequent programme of study; or

children.label: b3
children.text: fails to enrol for a subsequent programme of study; or

children.label: b4
children.text: fails to attend and/or make satisfactory progress; and

children.label: b5
children.text: has their enrolment in a programme of study terminated.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where an education pathway is offered by a single qualifying education provider, the formal agreement processes set out at (b) must be met.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The signed formal agreement does not have to be submitted with a pathway student visa application, however it must be made available to INZ if requested.

units.heading: Non-compliance with formal agreement requirements or when under active investigation by Immigration New Zealand

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Where non-compliance, other than of a minor nature, with any of the matters agreed to in the Pathway Student Visas - Pilot Participation Declaration, or where the pathway education provider is under active investigation by INZ for offences committed under part 10 of the Immigration Act 2009 the following process may occur:

children.label: a
children.text: INZ will suspend the processing of any student visa applications related to an existing pathway agreement immediately.

children.label: b
children.text: The non-compliant pathway education providers will be advised in writing of the suspension and will be sent a report detailing the non-compliance, and will be given 30 days to remedy the non-compliance.

children.label: c
children.text: Resolution (or satisfactory progress towards resolution) of the non-compliance to the satisfaction of INZ within the 30 day period will see the suspension lifted and processing of related pathway student visa applications will resume.

children.label: d
children.text: The Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment or the New Zealand Qualifications Authority may conduct an investigation three to six months later to assess the effectiveness of the remediation undertaken. If the remediation is deemed inadequate or ineffective, the suspension can be re-imposed or the provider may be removed from the pathways pilot and current pathway student visa holders become liable for deportation.

children.label: e
children.text: If INZ is not satisfied that the non-compliance has been addressed or satisfactory progress has been made towards resolution within the 30 day period, the suspension of related student visa processing will continue (until resolution occurs).

children.label: f
children.text: Failure to address or make satisfactory progress towards resolving the non-compliance may result in removal from the pathways pilot, and current student visa holders becoming liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: INZ may rely on the advice of the Ministry of Education and/or the New Zealand Qualifications Authority in determining whether resolution has been reached or satisfactory progress has been made towards resolution.

units.heading: Dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2); or

children.label: v
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: vi
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or.

children.label: vii
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.15 to A5.25.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Despite (a)(v) dependent children of Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) Job Search visa holders may be granted student visas if the related SMC application was under consideration on or before 24 July 2011.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$36,850.44 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$36,850.44 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

pages.page_title: U5.1 Status of education providers and programmes (22/08/2016)

units.heading: Status of education providers and programmes

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All education providers must certify in their offers of places to foreign students (see U3.5) that the programme of study or training scheme offered complies with foreign student requirements for different kinds of education providers (see U5.5- U5.20).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All education providers offering places to foreign students must be signatories to the Ministry of Education's Education (Pastoral Care of International Students) Code of Practice 2016.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Any queries on the status of programmes or training schemes offered by private training establishments should be referred to the Service Delivery Unit, Quality Assurance Division, New Zealand Qualifications Authority (NZQA), PO Box 160, Wellington.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Students seeking to enrol in a programme of study or training scheme offered at an education provider that holds a Category Four status under the NZQA’s External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system will not be granted a student visa.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Immigration New Zealand (INZ) may suspend the processing of applications for student visas for study at an education provider where at least one of the following applies:

children.label: i
children.text: the offered programme of study or training scheme does not comply with foreign student requirements as set out in U5.5 to U5.20;

children.label: ii
children.text: the education provider is not complying with its obligations under the Immigration Act, immigration regulations, or immigration instructions;

children.label: iii
children.text: INZ has been informed by education agencies that the education provider is not complying with its obligations under the Education Act and education regulations.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Before a decision is made to suspend the processing of student visas, the following will be taken into account:

children.label: i
children.text: evidence of the non-compliance; and

children.label: ii
children.text: reasons for the non-compliance; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the duration, frequency, and severity of the non-compliance.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: INZ may resume the processing of student visas if it is satisfied that the education provider is complying with its obligations.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Despite (d), where an applicant fails to meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for health, character or bona fide applicants, the application may be declined.

units.heading: Pathway student visas pilot

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For the purposes of these instructions, a pathway is defined as a progression of up to three consecutive programmes of study, offered by qualifying education providers, either within their institution or in conjunction with other qualifying education providers.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Pathway study can be undertaken on a single student visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: A pathway student visa cannot be granted after 7 June 2018, and any application for a pathway student visa made after this date must be declined.

pages.title: Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions
pages.page_title: U14.15 Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions (21/11/2016)

units.heading: Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: If a student holding a pathway student visa wishes to move to a different education provider or lower level programme of study than those specified in their visa conditions, they must apply for a new student visa and meet the requirements set out at U3.40.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A variation of conditions, for the purpose of changing a programme of study at the same education provider will only be granted if an immigration officer is satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant meets the student requirements set out at U3.1; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant has not breached their visa conditions as set out at E3.20; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the original student visa would have been granted for the proposed programme of study; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the proposed programme of study is at the same or higher level on the New Zealand Qualification Framework as the original programme of study; and

children.label: v
children.text: the applicant remains a bona fide applicant (see E5.1).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Factors that an immigration officer may take into consideration when determining (b)(iii) and (b)(iv) above include, but are not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: the time elapsed since the original visa was granted;

children.label: ii
children.text: whether the level and/or subject area of the proposed programme of study are significantly different from the original programme of study; and

children.label: iii
children.text: any relevant information held about the previous application(s) including advice from the original issuing branch (see E7.1.1).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Students who have received New Zealand Aid Programme funding within the two years prior to their application to change programme of study must also provide evidence that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade supports the change of programme of study and that any scholarship continues.

units.heading: Breaching visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student on an pathway student visa will be considered to be in breach of visa conditions where:

children.label: i
children.text: they fail to meet conditional pre-requisites for enrolment into a second or subsequent programme of study (E3.20(d); or

children.label: ii
children.text: the time between the completion of one programme of study and the start of a second or subsequent programme of study on a pathway exceeds 16 weeks; or

children.label: iii
children.text: they have submitted an English language test result as set out at U14.5.1 (c) and their intended pathway is an English language programme of study culminating in a qualification at Levels 5 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework and the English Language programme of study is not completed within a 16 week period.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A breach of visa conditions may result in the issue of a Deportation Liability Notice (E3.60).

pages.title: Provider requirements
pages.page_title: U14.20 Provider requirements (14/02/2017)

units.heading: Provider requirements
Pathway pilot entry criteria

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: To qualify for entry to the Pathway student visa pilot, an education provider must:

children.label: i
children.text: be invited by Immigration New Zealand to be a pilot participant; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have signed the Pathway Student Visas - Pilot Participation Declaration agreeing to the requirements as set out at U14.20.10; and

children.label: iii
children.text: be either a school, a university or hold a Category One or Two rating under New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation and Review framework; and

children.label: iv
children.text: have a minimum 90% student visa application approval rate over the 2014/15 financial year or 2016 calendar year (12 month period); and

children.label: v
children.text: comply with the legislative requirements as set out under the Education Act 1989 to offer programmes of study to foreign students (U5.5 to U5.20); and

children.label: vi
children.text: be a signatory to the Ministry of Education's Education (Pastoral Care of International Students) Code of Practice 2016.

units.heading: Eligible pathways

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All pathways must demonstrate academic progression to the second or subsequent programme of study building on the previous study.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All consecutive programmes of study that demonstrate progression are eligible to be included in the pilot with the exception of the following pathways:

children.label: i
children.text: Any English language programme of study to any Level 1-4 Certificate on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework (NZQF);

children.label: ii
children.text: All pathways within and between NZQF Levels 1-4 Certificates, and

children.label: iii
children.text: Secondary school to any NZQF Levels 1–4 Certificates.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Breaks between consecutive programmes of study must not exceed 16 weeks

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Only education providers who meet the requirements set out under U14.20.1 can offer a joint pathway in conjunction with one another.

units.heading: Formal agreement between qualifying education providers

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: To ensure a student’s pastoral care needs are met, qualifying education providers who intend offering an education pathway in conjunction with one another must enter into a formal agreement.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The formal agreement must include and set out the following processes and arrangements:

children.label: i
children.text: The application process (joint covering letter with two/three offers of place)

children.label: ii
children.text: Pastoral care obligations

children.label: iii
children.text: Handover arrangements in transition periods between programmes of study/education providers

children.label: iv
children.text: The process if a significant gap exists between completion of a programme of study and the start of a second or subsequent programme of study or in the event some papers are failed and cannot be repeated within a 16 week period.

children.label: v
children.text: The process if conditional entry requirements for second or subsequent programmes of study are not met

children.label: vi
children.text: The process if the student fails to attend and/or make satisfactory progress (E3.20(d))

children.label: vii
children.text: The process if the student wishes to leave intended pathway

children.label: viii
children.text: The obligation to notify INZ where a pathway student:

children.label: b1
children.text: requires additional time to complete a programme of study and time required is likely to exceed 16 weeks; or

children.label: b2
children.text: fails to meet the conditional entry requirements for a second or subsequent programme of study; or

children.label: b3
children.text: fails to enrol for a subsequent programme of study; or

children.label: b4
children.text: fails to attend and/or make satisfactory progress; and

children.label: b5
children.text: has their enrolment in a programme of study terminated.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where an education pathway is offered by a single qualifying education provider, the formal agreement processes set out at (b) must be met.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The signed formal agreement does not have to be submitted with a pathway student visa application, however it must be made available to INZ if requested.

units.heading: Non-compliance with formal agreement requirements or when under active investigation by Immigration New Zealand

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Where non-compliance, other than of a minor nature, with any of the matters agreed to in the Pathway Student Visas - Pilot Participation Declaration, or where the pathway education provider is under active investigation by INZ for offences committed under part 10 of the Immigration Act 2009 the following process may occur:

children.label: a
children.text: INZ will suspend the processing of any student visa applications related to an existing pathway agreement immediately.

children.label: b
children.text: The non-compliant pathway education providers will be advised in writing of the suspension and will be sent a report detailing the non-compliance, and will be given 30 days to remedy the non-compliance.

children.label: c
children.text: Resolution (or satisfactory progress towards resolution) of the non-compliance to the satisfaction of INZ within the 30 day period will see the suspension lifted and processing of related pathway student visa applications will resume.

children.label: d
children.text: The Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment or the New Zealand Qualifications Authority may conduct an investigation three to six months later to assess the effectiveness of the remediation undertaken. If the remediation is deemed inadequate or ineffective, the suspension can be re-imposed or the provider may be removed from the pathways pilot and current pathway student visa holders become liable for deportation.

children.label: e
children.text: If INZ is not satisfied that the non-compliance has been addressed or satisfactory progress has been made towards resolution within the 30 day period, the suspension of related student visa processing will continue (until resolution occurs).

children.label: f
children.text: Failure to address or make satisfactory progress towards resolving the non-compliance may result in removal from the pathways pilot, and current student visa holders becoming liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: INZ may rely on the advice of the Ministry of Education and/or the New Zealand Qualifications Authority in determining whether resolution has been reached or satisfactory progress has been made towards resolution.

pages.title: Tuition fees
pages.page_title: U3.10 Tuition fees (02/12/2013)

units.heading: Tuition fees

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence of:

children.label: i
children.text: exemption from tuition fees, or

children.label: ii
children.text: payment of tuition fees, or

children.label: iii
children.text: a notice of the award of a full New Zealand Aid Programme scholarship. Note: For applications processed outside New Zealand, evidence of payment is not required until after the application has been approved in principle.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, evidence of payment of tuition fees need not be provided if an immigration officer is satisfied that the student is awaiting home country government loan approval to pay their tuition fees once the student enrols in person at the New Zealand Tertiary Education Institution (TEI). The student must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: evidence the loan has been applied for, and

children.label: ii
children.text: confirmation from the enrolling New Zealand TEI that they expect to receive the fee directly once the student is onshore and has completed enrolment at that TEI.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The exception set out in (b) above also applies to students who are undertaking a bachelor degree programme or higher at a private training establishment (PTE) if an immigration officer is satisfied that the student is awaiting home country government loan approval to pay their tuition fees once the student enrols in person at the PTE. The student must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: evidence the loan has been applied for,

children.label: ii
children.text: confirmation from the enrolling New Zealand PTE that they expect to receive the fee directly once the student is onshore and has completed enrolment at that PTE, and

children.label: iii
children.text: confirmation from the PTE that the programme of study the student is enrolling in is a bachelor degree programme or higher. Note: Where the programme of study is offered by a PTE, the applicant must ensure that the primary requirements for satisfying sections 232 and 233 of the Education Act 1989, in respect of programmes of study, are met (see U5.15).

pages.page_title: U3.40 Students who wish to change their programme of study and/or education provider (02/12/2013)

units.heading: Students who wish to change their programme of study and/or education provider

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A further student visa or variation of conditions, for the purpose of changing programme of study and/or education provider, will only be granted if an immigration officer is satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant meets the student requirements set out at U3.1; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant has not breached their visa conditions as set out at E3.20; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the original student visa would have been granted for the proposed programme of study and/or education provider; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the applicant remains a bona fide applicant (see E5.1).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Factors that an immigration officer may take into consideration when determining (a)(iii) and (a)(iv) above include, but are not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: the time elapsed since the original visa was granted;

children.label: ii
children.text: whether the level and/or subject area of the proposed programme of study are significantly different from the original programme of study; and

children.label: iii
children.text: any relevant information held about the previous application(s) including advice from the original issuing branch (see E7.1.1).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have received New Zealand Aid Programme funding within the two years prior to their application to change programme of study and/or education provider being made, must also provide evidence that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade supports the change of programme of study or education provider and that any scholarship continues.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Applicants who wish to change their programme of study and/or education provider may provide evidence of payment of tuition fees after the application has been approved in principle.

units.heading: Exchange students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students studying under reciprocal exchange schemes approved by the Minister of Education are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending primary and secondary schools and are exempt from paying foreign tuition fees (see U3.35.5).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: There are two types of New Zealand student exchange schemes under which international students may be enrolled in New Zealand schools without paying international fees: Note: The general requirements for participants in approved student exchange schemes are set out at E11.55.

children.label: i
children.text: school-to-school student exchange schemes run by a school that is a signatory to the Ministry of Education's Education (Pastoral Care of International Students) Code of Practice 2016 (see E11.55.20); and

children.label: ii
children.text: student exchange schemes run by approved exchange programme organisations (see E11.55.20).

units.heading: Status of education providers and programmes

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All education providers must certify in their offers of places to foreign students (s ee U 3.5) that the programme of study or training scheme offered complies with foreign student requirements for different kinds of education providers (see U5.5- U5.20).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All education providers offering places to foreign students must be signatories to the Ministry of Education's Education (Pastoral Care of International Students) Code of Practice 2016.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Any queries on the status of programmes or training schemes offered by private training establishments should be referred to the Service Delivery Unit, Quality Assurance Division, New Zealand Qualifications Authority (NZQA), PO Box 160, Wellington.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Students will not be granted a student visa to undertake a programme of study or training scheme offered at an education provider that holds a Category Four status under the NZQA’s External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Immigration New Zealand (INZ) may suspend the processing of applications for student visas for study at an education provider where at least one of the following applies:

children.label: i
children.text: the offered programme of study or training scheme does not comply with foreign student requirements as set out in U5.5 to U5.20;

children.label: ii
children.text: the education provider is not complying with its obligations under the Immigration Act, immigration regulations, or immigration instructions;

children.label: iii
children.text: INZ has been informed by education agencies that the education provider is not complying with its obligations under the Education Act and education regulations.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Before a decision is made to suspend the processing of student visas, the following will be taken into account:

children.label: i
children.text: evidence of the non-compliance; and

children.label: ii
children.text: reasons for the non-compliance; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the duration, frequency, and severity of the non-compliance.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: INZ may resume the processing of student visas if it is satisfied that the education provider is complying with its obligations.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Despite (d), where an applicant fails to meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for health, character or bona fide applicants, the application may be declined.

pages.title: Visas for the length of a programme of study
pages.page_title: U6.35 Visas for the length of a programme of study (22/08/2016)

units.heading: Visas for the length of a programme of study

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students may be granted a student visa for the length of their programme of study, regardless of the period for which they have paid their tuition fees, as specified in:

children.label: a
children.text: Students Online Initiative (see U6.35.1); or

children.label: b
children.text: Aviation students instructions (U6.35.5).

units.heading: Students Online Initiative

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students may be granted a student visa for the length of their programme of study if the:

children.label: i
children.text: student has an offer of a place with an education provider with which INZ has a Memorandum of Understanding for the Students Online Initiative which allows for the grant of visas for the length of programme of study; and

children.label: ii
children.text: education provider supports the grant of a length of programme of study visa.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of the education provider support to grant a length of a programme of study visa must be provided.

units.heading: Aviation students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Aviation students may be granted a student visa for the length of their programme of study if:

children.label: i
children.text: the student has an offer of place from an aviation training provider that is:

children.label: b1
children.text: certified by the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand; and

children.label: b2
children.text: a signatory to the Ministry of Education’s Education (Pastoral Care of International Students) Code of Practice 2016 (see U3.5 and U5.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: the aviation training provider supports the grant of a length of programme of study visa; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the full first term of tuition fees have been paid.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of the aviation training provider’s support to grant a length of a programme of study visa must be provided.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a)(iii), evidence of tuition fee payment is not required where the aviation student is an Air New Zealand trainee and provides a guarantee from Air New Zealand.

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The STTA scheme is part of the New Zealand Aid Programme and provides partner governments with the opportunities to develop new competencies in identified areas of need as well as to upskill their work force. Training may involve placement with a New Zealand government department, a private training establishment, or at a tertiary institution. Trainees are provided with entitlements for accommodation and maintenance whilst on this scheme.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Applicants providing evidence of an award under the STTA scheme may be granted a student visa for the period of their award up to a maximum period of 12 months.

units.heading: New Zealand Aid Programme-supported students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A New Zealand Aid Programme-supported student receives funding from the New Zealand Government under the following schemes:

children.label: i
children.text: New Zealand Development Scholarships;

children.label: ii
children.text: Short-Term Training Awards;

children.label: iii
children.text: Commonwealth Scholarships;

children.label: iv
children.text: New Zealand Regional Development Scholarships;

children.label: v

children.label: vi

children.label: vii

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The objective of the scholarships and awards is for candidates to gain knowledge and skills in specific subject areas that will assist in the development of their home country. Awardees are required to return to their home country for at least two years after the completion of their scholarship/award to apply these new skills and knowledge in government, civil society or private business organisations.

pages.page_title: U11.1 New Zealand Aid Programme (NZAP)-supported students undertaking employment (02/12/2013)

units.heading: New Zealand Aid Programme (NZAP)-supported students undertaking employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: New Zealand Aid Programme (NZAP)-supported students may be granted conditions on their student visa to allow them to work during the academic year for up to 20 hours per week, during any holidays within the academic year for up to 20 hours per week, and full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period unless they are studying under the following schemes:

children.label: i
children.text: Short-Term Training Awards; or

children.label: ii
children.text: New Zealand Regional Development Scholarships; or

children.label: iii
children.text: English Language Training for Officials. Note: NZAP-supported students may also be eligible for full-time work rights during scheduled vacation periods. See U13.15.10

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: With the exception of the schemes listed under (a), NZAP scholars may be granted work visas at the completion of their programmes of study for qualification-related work experience for the minimum time needed to complete practical work requirements. Note: NZAP-supported senior medical and pharmacy students may be granted a work visa for their internship/registration year.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: NZAP-supported students are not permitted to:

children.label: i
children.text: work in self-employment; or

children.label: ii
children.text: provide commercial sexual services; or

children.label: iii
children.text: act as an operator of a New Zealand business of prostitution; or

children.label: iv
children.text: invest in a business of prostitution (see E7.40).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Any NZAP-supported student, or their partner or dependent children may only be granted a visa for New Zealand in the two-year period following completion of the NZAP student's scholarship, with written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (with the exception of a work visa to complete programme of study requirements or, if the applicant is outside New Zealand, a short-term visitor visa). Note: See WF4.5 for work instructions for partners of holders of student visas who are NZAP-supported.
