pages.title: Provider requirements
pages.page_title: U14.20 Provider requirements (08/05/2017)

units.heading: Provider requirements
Pathway pilot entry criteria

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: To qualify for entry to the Pathway student visa pilot, an education provider must:

children.label: i
children.text: be invited by Immigration New Zealand to be a pilot participant; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have signed the Pathway Student Visas - Pilot Participation Declaration agreeing to the requirements as set out at U14.20.10; and

children.label: iii
children.text: be either a school, a university or hold a Category One or Two rating under New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation and Review framework; and

children.label: iv
children.text: have a minimum 90% student visa application approval rate over the 2014/15 financial year or 2016 calendar year (12 month period); and

children.label: v
children.text: comply with the legislative requirements as set out under the Education Act 1989 to offer programmes of study to foreign students (U5.5 to U5.20); and

children.label: vi
children.text: be a signatory to the Ministry of Education's Education (Pastoral Care of International Students) Code of Practice 2016.

units.heading: Eligible pathways

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All pathways must demonstrate academic progression to the second or subsequent programme of study building on the previous study.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All consecutive programmes of study that demonstrate progression are eligible to be included in the pilot with the exception of the following pathways:

children.label: i
children.text: Any English language programme of study to any tertiary sector Level 1–4 Certificate on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework (NZQF); and

children.label: ii
children.text: All pathways within and between tertiary sector NZQF Levels 1–4 Certificates; and

children.label: iii
children.text: Secondary school to any tertiary sector NZQF Levels 1–4 Certificates.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Breaks between consecutive programmes of study must not exceed 16 weeks

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Only education providers who meet the requirements set out under U14.20.1 can offer a joint pathway in conjunction with one another.

units.heading: Formal agreement between qualifying education providers

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: To ensure a student’s pastoral care needs are met, qualifying education providers who intend offering an education pathway in conjunction with one another must enter into a formal agreement.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The formal agreement must include and set out the following processes and arrangements:

children.label: i
children.text: The application process (joint covering letter with two/three offers of place)

children.label: ii
children.text: Pastoral care obligations

children.label: iii
children.text: Handover arrangements in transition periods between programmes of study/education providers

children.label: iv
children.text: The process if a significant gap exists between completion of a programme of study and the start of a second or subsequent programme of study or in the event some papers are failed and cannot be repeated within a 16 week period.

children.label: v
children.text: The process if conditional entry requirements for second or subsequent programmes of study are not met

children.label: vi
children.text: The process if the student fails to attend and/or make satisfactory progress (E3.20(d))

children.label: vii
children.text: The process if the student wishes to leave intended pathway

children.label: viii
children.text: The obligation to notify INZ where a pathway student:

children.label: b1
children.text: requires additional time to complete a programme of study and time required is likely to exceed 16 weeks; or

children.label: b2
children.text: fails to meet the conditional entry requirements for a second or subsequent programme of study; or

children.label: b3
children.text: fails to enrol for a subsequent programme of study; or

children.label: b4
children.text: fails to attend and/or make satisfactory progress; and

children.label: b5
children.text: has their enrolment in a programme of study terminated.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where an education pathway is offered by a single qualifying education provider, the formal agreement processes set out at (b) must be met.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The signed formal agreement does not have to be submitted with a pathway student visa application, however it must be made available to INZ if requested.

units.heading: Non-compliance with formal agreement requirements or when under active investigation by Immigration New Zealand

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Where non-compliance, other than of a minor nature, with any of the matters agreed to in the Pathway Student Visas - Pilot Participation Declaration, or where the pathway education provider is under active investigation by INZ for offences committed under part 10 of the Immigration Act 2009 the following process may occur:

children.label: a
children.text: INZ will suspend the processing of any student visa applications related to an existing pathway agreement immediately.

children.label: b
children.text: The non-compliant pathway education providers will be advised in writing of the suspension and will be sent a report detailing the non-compliance, and will be given 30 days to remedy the non-compliance.

children.label: c
children.text: Resolution (or satisfactory progress towards resolution) of the non-compliance to the satisfaction of INZ within the 30 day period will see the suspension lifted and processing of related pathway student visa applications will resume.

children.label: d
children.text: The Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment or the New Zealand Qualifications Authority may conduct an investigation three to six months later to assess the effectiveness of the remediation undertaken. If the remediation is deemed inadequate or ineffective, the suspension can be re-imposed or the provider may be removed from the pathways pilot and current pathway student visa holders become liable for deportation.

children.label: e
children.text: If INZ is not satisfied that the non-compliance has been addressed or satisfactory progress has been made towards resolution within the 30 day period, the suspension of related student visa processing will continue (until resolution occurs).

children.label: f
children.text: Failure to address or make satisfactory progress towards resolving the non-compliance may result in removal from the pathways pilot, and current student visa holders becoming liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: INZ may rely on the advice of the Ministry of Education and/or the New Zealand Qualifications Authority in determining whether resolution has been reached or satisfactory progress has been made towards resolution.

pages.title: Definition of 'domestic student'
pages.page_title: U3.35 Definition of 'domestic student' (11/04/2016)

units.heading: Definition of 'domestic student'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of student instructions a 'domestic student' means a domestic student as defined in section 2 of the Education Act 1989. The Ministry of Education holds a complete list of who is considered to be a domestic student for the purpose of fee payment and enrolment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary schooling domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending primary and secondary schools and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue;

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents;

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents;

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current school year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: f
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: g
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending primary and secondary schools and are exempt from paying foreign tuition fees:

children.label: a
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is in New Zealand to study under an exchange programme approved by the New Zealand Government.

children.label: b
children.text: Children whose application for a residence class visa is under consideration and who are the dependent children of any person who is a New Zealand citizen or the holder of a residence class visa.

children.label: c
children.text: Children whose application for New Zealand citizenship is under consideration and who are the dependent children of a New Zealand citizen.

children.label: d
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is onshore and the holder of a valid work visa other than those excluded under U8.20.

children.label: e
children.text: Students who have, or dependent children of any person who has, made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009.

children.label: f
children.text: Dependent children of a foreign student enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme in a New Zealand university.

children.label: g
children.text: Dependent children of any person who, during the current calendar year, last ceased to hold a special temporary visa (see H2).

children.label: h
children.text: Students who have entered New Zealand for the purposes of adoption and:

children.label: i
children.text: whose adoption application before the New Zealand Family Court (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student) is supported by the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services and who has a letter from the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services confirming this support; or

children.label: ii
children.text: who are the subject of an Interim Order of Adoption granted by the New Zealand Family Court under section 5 of the Adoption Act 1955 (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student).

children.label: i
children.text: People who are in the custody of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development pursuant to any of the following orders:

children.label: i
children.text: an order, pursuant to sections 78, 101 or 238(1)(d) of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, in favour of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 110 of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, appointing the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development as sole guardian; or

children.label: iii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 33 of the Care of Children Act 2004, whereby a child or young person is placed under the Guardianship of the Family Court or the High Court and the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development is appointed as agent of the court with power and discretion to place the child.

children.label: j
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand Aid Programme Scholarship.

children.label: k
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a visitor visa granted under V3.115.

children.label: l
children.text: Dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

children.label: m
children.text: Children granted a student visa under U10.5.

children.label: n
children.text: Students who are in New Zealand to study under an exchange scheme approved by the Ministry of Education (see E11.45).

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector (see U5.20) and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions or limited visa in order to undertake a programme of study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue.

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents.

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents.

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current academic year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Despite (d) above, dependent children aged 21 and over of Diplomatic, Consular or Official staff, who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand, may not be eligible for domestic student status and may be required to pay foreign student fees (see H2.1(b)).

children.label: f
children.text: A person who has made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and who is the holder of a valid temporary entry class visa.

children.label: g
children.text: A person who has been recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and whose application for residence is being processed.

children.label: h
children.text: A person who is enrolled at a tertiary education provider for the purpose of participating in industry training funded under the Industry Training Act 1992.

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector and are exempt from paying foreign tuition fees for foreign students:

children.label: a
children.text: Students enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme, in any New Zealand university (see U5.20).

children.label: b
children.text: A person who is in New Zealand to study under a New Zealand Government approved exchange programme at a tertiary education provider.

pages.title: Dependent children of holders of work visas
pages.page_title: U8.20 Dependent children of holders of work visas (08/05/2017)

units.heading: Dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2); or

children.label: v
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: vi
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or.

children.label: vii
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.15 to A5.25.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Despite (a)(v) dependent children of Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) Job Search visa holders may be granted student visas if the related SMC application was under consideration on or before 24 July 2011.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$37,090.68 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$37,090.68 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

pages.title: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment
pages.page_title: U13.15 Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment (21/11/2016)

units.heading: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment, a student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work during the academic year, and during any scheduled vacations, including within the academic year.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Students aged 16 or 17 years of age enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment must have written permission from their education provider and written parental consent to be granted conditions allowing work.

units.heading: Work conditions for up to twenty hours in any given week

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa holder may be granted with conditions to work for up to 20 hours in any given week during the validity of the visa if the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1) of at least two academic years’ duration; or

children.label: b
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study, culminating in a New Zealand qualification that would qualify for points under the Skilled Migrant Category (see SM14); or

children.label: c
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study of at least one academic year's duration as part of an approved tertiary student exchange scheme (see E11.45); or

children.label: d
children.text: engaged in a full-time programme of study of at least six months’ duration; and

children.label: i
children.text: an immigration officer is satisfied that the primary purpose of the programme of study is to develop English language skills; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the student can provide acceptable English language test results, as set out at U13.15.20 (no more than 2 years old at the time the application is lodged); or

children.label: e
children.text: undertaking full-time English language study of at least 14 consecutive weeks’ duration at an education provider that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the NZQA EER quality assurance system; or Note: When assessing eligibility for work rights under (e) for an applicant who holds a current student visa, all consecutive previous English language study undertaken on this and any previous student visa can be counted towards the 14 consecutive week period provided the programme of study the applicant is applying for: - follows directly from their current study and - is with the same provider as that on their current and any previous student visa.

children.label: f
children.text: undertaking a full-time foundation programme that commenced on or before 28 February 2014 and that programme of study is of at least one academic year’s duration at level four or higher on the New Zealand Qualification Framework at an education provider in Canterbury that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system.

units.heading: Full time work rights during Christmas-New Year vacation period

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation (summer vacation) period provided that the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: studying full-time (see UU6.1.1); and

children.label: b
children.text: enrolled in a programme of study that has a minimum duration of at least two semesters during a period of at least eight months.

units.heading: Full time work rights during scheduled vacations

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during all scheduled vacations, if the student is undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1); and of at least one academic year’s duration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) where scheduled vacations are more than one third of the programme of study duration for programmes of study offered by tertiary providers other than universities, full-time work rights may not be granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: An academic year means a programme of study of a minimum of 120 credits during a period of at least eight months (minimum of two semesters)

units.heading: Work conditions for masters by research or doctoral students

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder unlimited work rights if:

children.label: a
children.text: the student is undertaking a Masters by Research or Doctoral degree, and

children.label: b
children.text: the qualification is awarded by a New Zealand tertiary institution.

units.heading: Acceptable English language test results

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following English language test results are acceptable:

blocks.label: table1
blocks.text: Test | Minimum score required ; International English Language Testing System (IELTS) - General or Academic Module | Overall score of 5.0 or more ; Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-based Test (TOEFL iBT) | Overall score of 35 or more ; Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic) | Overall score of 36 or more ; Cambridge English: First (FCE) or Cambridge English: First (FCE) for Schools | Overall score of 154 or more ; Occupational English Test (OET) | Grade C or higher in all four skills (Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking)*

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: * A score of Grade C or higher in all four skills is required for the OET as there is no overall grade for this test.

pages.title: Visas for the length of a programme of study
pages.page_title: U6.35 Visas for the length of a programme of study (28/08/2017)

units.heading: Visas for the length of a programme of study

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students may be granted a student visa for the length of their programme of study, regardless of the period for which they have paid their tuition fees, as specified in:

children.label: a
children.text: Students Online Initiative (see U6.35.1); or

children.label: b
children.text: Aviation students instructions (U6.35.5).

units.heading: Students Online Initiative

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students may be granted a student visa for the length of their programme of study if the:

children.label: i
children.text: student has an offer of a place with an education provider with which INZ has a Memorandum of Understanding for the Students Online Initiative which allows for the grant of visas for the length of programme of study; and

children.label: ii
children.text: education provider supports the grant of a length of programme of study visa.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of the education provider support to grant a length of a programme of study visa must be provided.

units.heading: Aviation students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Aviation students may be granted a student visa for the length of their programme of study if:

children.label: i
children.text: the student has an offer of place from an aviation training provider that is:

children.label: b1
children.text: certified by the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand; and

children.label: b2
children.text: signatory to the Education (Pastoral Care of International Students) Code of Practice 2016 (see U3.5 and U5.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: the aviation training provider supports the grant of a length of programme of study visa; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the full first term of tuition fees have been paid.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of the aviation training provider’s support to grant a length of a programme of study visa must be provided.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a)(iii), evidence of tuition fee payment is not required where the aviation student is an Air New Zealand trainee and provides a guarantee from Air New Zealand.

pages.title: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment
pages.page_title: U13.15 Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment (28/08/2017)

units.heading: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment, a student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work during the academic year, and during any scheduled vacations, including within the academic year.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Students aged 16 or 17 years of age enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment must have written permission from their education provider and written parental consent to be granted conditions allowing work.

units.heading: Work conditions for up to twenty hours in any given week

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa holder may be granted with conditions to work for up to 20 hours in any given week during the validity of the visa if the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1) of at least two academic years’ duration; or

children.label: b
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study, culminating in a New Zealand qualification that would qualify for points under the Skilled Migrant Category (see SM8); or

children.label: c
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study of at least one academic year's duration as part of an approved tertiary student exchange scheme (see E11.45); or

children.label: d
children.text: engaged in a full-time programme of study of at least six months’ duration; and

children.label: i
children.text: an immigration officer is satisfied that the primary purpose of the programme of study is to develop English language skills; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the student can provide acceptable English language test results, as set out at U13.15.20 (no more than 2 years old at the time the application is lodged); or

children.label: e
children.text: undertaking full-time English language study of at least 14 consecutive weeks’ duration at an education provider that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the NZQA EER quality assurance system; or Note: When assessing eligibility for work rights under (e) for an applicant who holds a current student visa, all consecutive previous English language study undertaken on this and any previous student visa can be counted towards the 14 consecutive week period provided the programme of study the applicant is applying for: - follows directly from their current study and - is with the same provider as that on their current and any previous student visa.

children.label: f
children.text: undertaking a full-time foundation programme that commenced on or before 28 February 2014 and that programme of study is of at least one academic year’s duration at level four or higher on the New Zealand Qualification Framework at an education provider in Canterbury that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system.

units.heading: Full time work rights during Christmas-New Year vacation period

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation (summer vacation) period provided that the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: studying full-time (see U6.1.1); and

children.label: b
children.text: enrolled in a programme of study that has a minimum duration of at least two semesters during a period of at least eight months.

units.heading: Full time work rights during scheduled vacations

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during all scheduled vacations, if the student is undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1); and of at least one academic year’s duration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) where scheduled vacations are more than one third of the programme of study duration for programmes of study offered by tertiary providers other than universities, full-time work rights may not be granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: An academic year means a programme of study of a minimum of 120 credits during a period of at least eight months (minimum of two semesters)

units.heading: Work conditions for masters by research or doctoral students

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder unlimited work rights if:

children.label: a
children.text: the student is undertaking a Masters by Research or Doctoral degree, and

children.label: b
children.text: the qualification is awarded by a New Zealand tertiary institution.

units.heading: Acceptable English language test results

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following English language test results are acceptable:

blocks.label: table1
blocks.text: Test | Minimum score required ; International English Language Testing System (IELTS) - General or Academic Module | Overall score of 5.0 or more ; Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-based Test (TOEFL iBT) | Overall score of 35 or more ; Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic) | Overall score of 36 or more ; Cambridge English: First (FCE) or Cambridge English: First (FCE) for Schools | Overall score of 154 or more ; Occupational English Test (OET) | Grade C or higher in all four skills (Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking)*

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: * A score of Grade C or higher in all four skills is required for the OET as there is no overall grade for this test.

pages.page_title: U14.5 Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa (14/02/2017)

units.heading: Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To be granted a pathway student visa, an applicant must:

children.label: a
children.text: be offered an eligible study pathway from a qualifying provider (U14.20);

children.label: b
children.text: meet the general requirements to be granted a student visa as set out at U3.1;

children.label: c
children.text: meet the additional evidential requirements for pathway student visa set out at U14.5.1;

children.label: d
children.text: make an application for a student visa before 7 June 2018.

units.heading: Evidence of meeting requirements

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: In addition to meeting the general requirements to be granted a student visa as set out at U3.1, when applying for a pathway student visa an applicant must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: Where there is more than one education provider, A joint covering letter from pathway education providers setting out the pathway programmes of study and start and end dates of each programme of study;

children.label: ii
children.text: An offer of place (or joint offer) for each programme of study that meets the requirements set out at U3.5;

children.label: iii
children.text: Evidence that tuition fee requirements, as set out at U3.10, for either the first programme of study or first year of study (whichever is shorter) have been met and satisfy an immigration officer that they have the ability to fund any remaining balance of the first programme of study and subsequent programmes of study on the intended pathway; and

children.label: iv
children.text: Evidence that the maintenance funds requirements set out in U3.20 for the first year of study on the intended pathway have been met and satisfy an immigration officer that they have the ability to fund any remaining balance of the first programme of study and subsequent programmes of study on the intended pathway.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a)(ii), second and subsequent offers of place for a pathway can be conditional on meeting pre-requisite programme of study entry criteria.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: First time pathway student visa applicants from a country with a student visa decline rate of more than 20 per cent who intend a study pathway commencing with an English language programme of study and culminating in a qualification at Levels 5 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework must:

children.label: i
children.text: submit an International English Language Testing System test (IELTS) (or equivalent internationally recognised test) at the time of application; and

children.label: ii
children.text: demonstrate that they only require an improvement of 0.5 of an IELTS overall band score (or equivalent) to meet the English language prerequisite for entry into the intended level 5 to 8 programme of study.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The student visa decline rate for a country is based on statistics, generated over a calendar year (12 months), by Immigration New Zealand. The decline rate and the name of the country are published on the INZ website. For the purpose of this instruction, the internationally recognised English language tests and corresponding IELTS equivalent test scores set out on the INZ website are considered acceptable.

pages.title: Dependent children of holders of work visas
pages.page_title: U8.20 Dependent children of holders of work visas (28/08/2017)

units.heading: Dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Essential Skills work visa where the employment has been assessed as lower-skilled (WK3.5.1), unless U8.20.1 below applies; or

children.label: ii
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: v
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2); or

children.label: vi
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: vii
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or.

children.label: viii
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.15 to A5.25.

units.heading: Holders of Essential Skills work visas for lower-skilled employment who are able to support student visas for their dependent children

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The applicant (who is the dependent child of an Essential Skills work visa holder whose employment has been assessed as lower-skilled) may be granted a student visa under these instructions if:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant held a visa on the basis of being a dependent child of the Essential Skills work visa holder on 28 August 2017; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the Essential Skills work visa holder has not been subject to a stand-down period (see WK3.20.5).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The applicant (who is the dependent child of an Essential Skills work visa holder whose employment has been assessed as lower-skilled) may be granted a student visa under these instructions if:

children.label: i
children.text: the Essential Skills work visa holder parent previously held a student visa that made them eligible to support a child for a student visa (U8.25); and

children.label: ii
children.text: subsequently held a post-study work visa (WD) based on that student visa; and

children.label: iii
children.text: supported the applicant for a visa based on their relationship while holding a post-study work visa.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$37,090.68 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$37,090.68 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

pages.title: Part-time study
pages.page_title: U7.20 Part-time study (02/12/2013)

units.heading: Part-time study

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: People who are not considered to be full-time students (see U6.1.1) may apply for a visitor visa with a variation of conditions to allow study on a part-time basis.

units.heading: Programmes of study lasting up to 9 months

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: People outside New Zealand may apply for and be granted a variation of conditions to allow study on a part-time basis for a maximum of 9 months from the date of their arrival in New Zealand, provided that they are enrolled in a part-time programme of study certified as one that complies with foreign student requirements (see U3.1) and lasts no more than 9 months, and comply with visitor requirements (see V2.1).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: People already in New Zealand may apply for and be granted a visitor visa with a variation of conditions to allow study on a part-time basis for the balance of their stay up to a maximum of 9 months from the date of their arrival.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If study is the main reason for the applicant being in New Zealand, immigration officers must decline any application to undertake part-time programmes of study lasting longer than 9 months, unless the officers are satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the application has special merit that warrants the application being approved, and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant will comply with the conditions of their visa.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Immigration officers must be satisfied that applicants who wish to undertake part-time programmes of study lasting up to 9 months after their date of arrival:

children.label: i
children.text: are enrolled in and have paid the fees for such a programme of study; and

children.label: ii
children.text: are able to satisfy the standard visitor requirements (see V2.1).

units.heading: Students completing their programme of study

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Despite U7.20 above and U6.1.1, a person who is: may be considered to be a full-time student and may be granted a student visa for the remaining duration of their programme of study if they can meet student requirements (see U3.1).

children.label: i
children.text: in their final semester of a programme of study in New Zealand, that is of at least 2 academic years’ duration; or

children.label: ii
children.text: in their final semester of a programme of study in New Zealand, culminating in a New Zealand qualification that would qualify for points under the Skilled Migrant Category (see SM14)

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: To be eligible for a student visa under these instructions, applicants must not previously have been granted a visa under these instructions.

pages.title: Currency and conditions of pathway student visas
pages.page_title: U14.10 Currency and conditions of pathway student visas (21/11/2016)

units.heading: Currency and conditions of pathway student visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For the purposes of the pathway student visa pilot, a visa can be granted up to a maximum of five years;

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A visa may be granted to expire no more than three months beyond completion of the final pathway programme of study within the maximum currency of five years;

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Work conditions for the duration of the pathway student visa will only be granted where the first programme of study meets the requirements as set out at U13.1, U13.10 or U13.15;

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If the second or subsequent programme of study meets the requirements set out at U13.1, U13.10 or U13.15, a variation of conditions is required in order to be granted work conditions;

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Where (d) applies, a Variation of Conditions or Variation of Travel Conditions (INZ 1020) application form must be completed and submitted with the required fee.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: The holder must make satisfactory progress on the pathway by:

children.label: i
children.text: meeting the conditional pre-requisites for enrolment into a second or subsequent programme of study (E3.20(d); and

children.label: ii
children.text: commencing the second or subsequent programme of study on a pathway within a 16 week period of completing an earlier programme of study.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Where a first time student has submitted an English language test result as set out at U14.5.1 (c) and been granted a pathway student visa to undertake an English language programme of study culminating in a qualification at Levels 5 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework, the English Language programme of study must be completed within a 20 week period.

pages.title: Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions
pages.page_title: U14.15 Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions (08/05/2017)

units.heading: Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: If a student holding a pathway student visa wishes to move to a different education provider or lower level programme of study than those specified in their visa conditions, they must apply for a new student visa and meet the requirements set out at U3.40.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A variation of conditions, for the purpose of changing a programme of study at the same education provider will only be granted if an immigration officer is satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant meets the student requirements set out at U3.1; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant has not breached their visa conditions as set out at E3.20; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the original student visa would have been granted for the proposed programme of study; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the proposed programme of study is at the same or higher level on the New Zealand Qualification Framework as the original programme of study; and

children.label: v
children.text: the applicant remains a bona fide applicant (see E5.1).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Factors that an immigration officer may take into consideration when determining (b)(iii) and (b)(iv) above include, but are not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: the time elapsed since the original visa was granted;

children.label: ii
children.text: whether the level and/or subject area of the proposed programme of study are significantly different from the original programme of study; and

children.label: iii
children.text: any relevant information held about the previous application(s) including advice from the original issuing branch (see E7.1.1).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Students who have received New Zealand Aid Programme funding within the two years prior to their application to change programme of study must also provide evidence that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade supports the change of programme of study and that any scholarship continues.

units.heading: Breaching visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student on a pathway student visa will be considered to be in breach of visa conditions where:

children.label: i
children.text: they fail to meet conditional pre-requisites for enrolment into a second or subsequent programme of study (E3.20(d)); or

children.label: ii
children.text: the time between the completion of one programme of study and the start of a second or subsequent programme of study on a pathway exceeds 16 weeks; or

children.label: iii
children.text: they have submitted an English language test result as set out at U14.5.1(c) and their intended pathway is an English language programme of study culminating in a qualification at Levels 5 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework and the English Language programme of study is not completed within a 20 week period.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A breach of visa conditions is “sufficient reason” to make a temporary entry class visa holder liable for deportation, and may result in the issue of a Deportation Liability Notice (E3.60).

pages.title: Provider requirements
pages.page_title: U14.20 Provider requirements (28/08/2017)

units.heading: Provider requirements
Pathway pilot entry criteria

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: To qualify for entry to the Pathway student visa pilot, an education provider must:

children.label: i
children.text: be invited by Immigration New Zealand to be a pilot participant; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have signed the Pathway Student Visas - Pilot Participation Declaration agreeing to the requirements as set out at U14.20.10; and

children.label: iii
children.text: be either a school, a university or hold a Category One or Two rating under New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation and Review framework; and

children.label: iv
children.text: have a minimum 90% student visa application approval rate over the 2014/15 financial year or 2016 calendar year (12 month period); and

children.label: v
children.text: comply with the legislative requirements as set out under the Education Act 1989 to offer programmes of study to foreign students (U5.5 to U5.20); and

children.label: vi
children.text: be a signatory to the Education (Pastoral Care of International Students) Code of Practice 2016.

units.heading: Eligible pathways

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All pathways must demonstrate academic progression to the second or subsequent programme of study building on the previous study.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All consecutive programmes of study that demonstrate progression are eligible to be included in the pilot with the exception of the following pathways:

children.label: i
children.text: Any English language programme of study to any tertiary sector Level 1–4 Certificate on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework (NZQF); and

children.label: ii
children.text: All pathways within and between tertiary sector NZQF Levels 1–4 Certificates; and

children.label: iii
children.text: Secondary school to any tertiary sector NZQF Levels 1–4 Certificates.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Breaks between consecutive programmes of study must not exceed 16 weeks

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Only education providers who meet the requirements set out under U14.20.1 can offer a joint pathway in conjunction with one another.

units.heading: Formal agreement between qualifying education providers

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: To ensure a student’s pastoral care needs are met, qualifying education providers who intend offering an education pathway in conjunction with one another must enter into a formal agreement.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The formal agreement must include and set out the following processes and arrangements:

children.label: i
children.text: The application process (joint covering letter with two/three offers of place)

children.label: ii
children.text: Pastoral care obligations

children.label: iii
children.text: Handover arrangements in transition periods between programmes of study/education providers

children.label: iv
children.text: The process if a significant gap exists between completion of a programme of study and the start of a second or subsequent programme of study or in the event some papers are failed and cannot be repeated within a 16 week period.

children.label: v
children.text: The process if conditional entry requirements for second or subsequent programmes of study are not met

children.label: vi
children.text: The process if the student fails to attend and/or make satisfactory progress (E3.20(d))

children.label: vii
children.text: The process if the student wishes to leave intended pathway

children.label: viii
children.text: The obligation to notify INZ where a pathway student:

children.label: b1
children.text: requires additional time to complete a programme of study and time required is likely to exceed 16 weeks; or

children.label: b2
children.text: fails to meet the conditional entry requirements for a second or subsequent programme of study; or

children.label: b3
children.text: fails to enrol for a subsequent programme of study; or

children.label: b4
children.text: fails to attend and/or make satisfactory progress; and

children.label: b5
children.text: has their enrolment in a programme of study terminated.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where an education pathway is offered by a single qualifying education provider, the formal agreement processes set out at (b) must be met.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The signed formal agreement does not have to be submitted with a pathway student visa application, however it must be made available to INZ if requested.

units.heading: Non-compliance with formal agreement requirements or when under active investigation by Immigration New Zealand

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Where non-compliance, other than of a minor nature, with any of the matters agreed to in the Pathway Student Visas - Pilot Participation Declaration, or where the pathway education provider is under active investigation by INZ for offences committed under part 10 of the Immigration Act 2009 the following process may occur:

children.label: a
children.text: INZ will suspend the processing of any student visa applications related to an existing pathway agreement immediately.

children.label: b
children.text: The non-compliant pathway education providers will be advised in writing of the suspension and will be sent a report detailing the non-compliance, and will be given 30 days to remedy the non-compliance.

children.label: c
children.text: Resolution (or satisfactory progress towards resolution) of the non-compliance to the satisfaction of INZ within the 30 day period will see the suspension lifted and processing of related pathway student visa applications will resume.

children.label: d
children.text: The Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment or the New Zealand Qualifications Authority may conduct an investigation three to six months later to assess the effectiveness of the remediation undertaken. If the remediation is deemed inadequate or ineffective, the suspension can be re-imposed or the provider may be removed from the pathways pilot and current pathway student visa holders become liable for deportation.

children.label: e
children.text: If INZ is not satisfied that the non-compliance has been addressed or satisfactory progress has been made towards resolution within the 30 day period, the suspension of related student visa processing will continue (until resolution occurs).

children.label: f
children.text: Failure to address or make satisfactory progress towards resolving the non-compliance may result in removal from the pathways pilot, and current student visa holders becoming liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: INZ may rely on the advice of the Ministry of Education and/or the New Zealand Qualifications Authority in determining whether resolution has been reached or satisfactory progress has been made towards resolution.

pages.title: Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa
pages.page_title: U14.5 Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa (26/11/2018)

units.heading: Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To be granted a pathway student visa, an applicant must:

children.label: a
children.text: be offered an eligible study pathway from a qualifying provider(s) (U14.20); and

children.label: b
children.text: meet the general requirements to be granted a student visa as set out at U3.1; and

children.label: c
children.text: meet the additional evidential requirements for pathway student visa set out at U14.5.1; and

children.label: d
children.text: make an application for a student visa before 30 April 2019.

units.heading: Evidence of meeting requirements

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: In addition to meeting the general requirements to be granted a student visa as set out at U3.1, when applying for a pathway student visa an applicant must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: where there is more than one education provider, a joint letter of support from pathway education providers; and

children.label: ii
children.text: an offer of place (or joint offer) for each programme of study that meets the requirements set out at U3.5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence that tuition fee requirements, as set out at U3.10, for either the first programme of study or first year of study (whichever is shorter) have been met and satisfy an immigration officer that they have the ability to fund any remaining balance of the first programme of study and subsequent programmes of study on the intended pathway; and

children.label: iv
children.text: evidence that the maintenance funds requirements set out in U3.20 for the first year of study on the intended pathway have been met and satisfy an immigration officer that they have the ability to fund any remaining balance of the first programme of study and subsequent programmes of study on the intended pathway.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a)(ii), second and subsequent offers of place for a pathway can be conditional on meeting pre-requisite programme of study entry criteria.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Pathway student visa applicants from a country with a student visa decline rate of more than 20 per cent who intend a study pathway commencing with an English language programme of study and culminating in a qualification at Levels 5 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework must:

children.label: i
children.text: submit an International English Language Testing System test (IELTS) (or equivalent internationally recognised proficiency test) at the time of application; and

children.label: ii
children.text: demonstrate that they only require an improvement of 0.5 of an IELTS overall band score (or equivalent) to meet the English language prerequisite for entry into the intended level 5 to 8 programme of study.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The student visa decline rate for a country is based on statistics, generated over a calendar year (12 months), by Immigration New Zealand. The decline rate and the name of the country are published on the INZ website. For the purpose of this instruction, the internationally recognised English language tests and corresponding IELTS equivalent test scores set out on the INZ website are considered acceptable.

pages.title: Summary

units.heading: Summary

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless otherwise specified, to be granted a student visa to attend a programme of study of more than three months, applicants must:

children.label: i
children.text: have an offer of a place or, if returning to continue a programme of study, a confirmation of enrolment in an approved programme of study with an education provider in New Zealand that meets student visa requirements (see U3.5, U3.10, and U5.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: be exempted from or have paid tuition fees; and

children.label: iii
children.text: if aged under 18, meet accommodation requirements (see U3.15); and

children.label: iv
children.text: have fulfilled the purpose and met the conditions for any previous or current temporary visas held as set out in E3.15 and E3.20; and

children.label: v
children.text: meet the conditions set out in E3.20; and

children.label: vi
children.text: not be the holder of a current visitor visa granted under Guardians accompanying students to New Zealand instructions (see V3.100).); and

children.label: vii
children.text: hold insurance (see U3.45), unless they are a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) student or a New Zealand Aid Programme-supported student.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All applicants must meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for:

children.label: i
children.text: lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa as set out at E4; and

children.label: ii
children.text: bona fide applicants as set out at E5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: health and character as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have not completed, or will not be completing the programme of study endorsed on their student visa and who wish to change their programme of study and/or education provider must:

children.label: i
children.text: meet requirements (a) and (b) above; and

children.label: ii
children.text: meet the requirements set out at U3.40. Note: Applicants who are progressing to further study, for example a student in Year 13 who is progressing to tertiary studies, will not need to meet U3.40.

pages.title: Tuition fees
pages.page_title: U3.10 Tuition fees (28/08/2017)

units.heading: Tuition fees

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence of payment of tuition fees.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: For applicants living outside New Zealand, evidence of payment is not required until after the application has been approved in principle.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a), the following students are not required to provide evidence of tuition fee payment if they can meet the required exemption and provide evidence as below: Exemption Evidence required i Exempt from tuition fees Confirmation that the programme of study is exempt from fees or that the student is exempt from paying any fees ii Students participating in a Study Abroad or Non-award scheme under a study abroad partner agreement with a New Zealand Tertiary education institution Confirmation from the New Zealand tertiary institution that tuition fees are being paid directly to them from a foreign tertiary institution or authorised third party provider on behalf of the foreign tertiary institution. iii New Zealand Aid Programme scholarship Notice of the award of a full New Zealand Aid Programme scholarship. iv Home country government loan approval at a tertiary institution Evidence that the loan has been applied for and confirmation from the tertiary institution that the fees will be paid directly to them. v Home country government loan approval at a private training establishment (PTE) for study at Bachelor’s Degree and above Evidence that the loan has been applied for and confirmation from the PTE that the fees will be paid directly to them. vi Foreign government-supported student Meet the all requirements as applicable under U12.

pages.title: Definition of 'domestic student'
pages.page_title: U3.35 Definition of 'domestic student' (28/08/2017)

units.heading: Definition of 'domestic student'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of student instructions a 'domestic student' means a domestic student as defined in section 2 of the Education Act 1989. The Ministry of Education holds a complete list of who is considered to be a domestic student for the purpose of fee payment and enrolment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary schooling domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending primary and secondary schools and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue;

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents;

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents;

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current school year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending primary and secondary schools and are exempt from paying foreign tuition fees:

children.label: a
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is in New Zealand to study under an exchange programme approved by the New Zealand Government.

children.label: b
children.text: Children whose application for a residence class visa is under consideration and who are the dependent children of any person who is a New Zealand citizen or the holder of a residence class visa.

children.label: c
children.text: Children whose application for New Zealand citizenship is under consideration and who are the dependent children of a New Zealand citizen.

children.label: d
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is onshore and the holder of a valid work visa other than those excluded under U8.20.

children.label: e
children.text: Students who have, or dependent children of any person who has, made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009.

children.label: f
children.text: Dependent children of a foreign student enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme in a New Zealand university.

children.label: g
children.text: Dependent children of any person who, during the current calendar year, last ceased to hold a special temporary visa (see H2).

children.label: h
children.text: Students who have entered New Zealand for the purposes of adoption and:

children.label: i
children.text: whose adoption application before the New Zealand Family Court (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student) is supported by the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services and who has a letter from the Department of Child, Youth and Family Services confirming this support; or

children.label: ii
children.text: who are the subject of an Interim Order of Adoption granted by the New Zealand Family Court under section 5 of the Adoption Act 1955 (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student).

children.label: i
children.text: People who are in the custody of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development pursuant to any of the following orders:

children.label: i
children.text: an order, pursuant to sections 78, 101 or 238(1)(d) of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, in favour of the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 110 of the Children, Young Persons and their Families Act 1989, appointing the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development as sole guardian; or

children.label: iii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 33 of the Care of Children Act 2004, whereby a child or young person is placed under the Guardianship of the Family Court or the High Court and the Chief Executive of the Ministry of Social Development is appointed as agent of the court with power and discretion to place the child.

children.label: j
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand Aid Programme Scholarship.

children.label: k
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a visitor visa granted under V3.115.

children.label: l
children.text: Dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

children.label: m
children.text: Children granted a student visa under U10.5.

children.label: n
children.text: Students who are in New Zealand to study under an exchange scheme approved by the Ministry of Education (see E11.45).

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector (see U5.20) and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions or limited visa in order to undertake a programme of study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue.

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents.

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents.

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current academic year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Despite (d) above, dependent children aged 21 and over of Diplomatic, Consular or Official staff, who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand, may not be eligible for domestic student status and may be required to pay foreign student fees (see H2.1(b)).

children.label: f
children.text: A person who has made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and who is the holder of a valid temporary entry class visa.

children.label: g
children.text: A person who has been recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and whose application for residence is being processed.

children.label: h
children.text: A person who is enrolled at a tertiary education provider for the purpose of participating in industry training funded under the Industry Training Act 1992.

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector and are exempt from paying foreign tuition fees for foreign students:

children.label: a
children.text: Students enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme, in any New Zealand university (see U5.20).

children.label: b
children.text: A person who is in New Zealand to study under a New Zealand Government approved exchange programme at a tertiary education provider.

units.heading: Students who wish to change their study conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A further student visa or variation of conditions, for the purpose of changing programme of study, education provider and/or study location, will only be granted if an immigration officer is satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant meets the student requirements set out at U3.1; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant has not breached their visa conditions as set out at E3.20; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the original student visa would have been granted for the proposed programme of study, education provider, and/or study location; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the applicant remains a bona fide applicant (see E5.1).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Factors that an immigration officer may take into consideration when determining (a)(iii) and (a)(iv) above include, but are not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: the time elapsed since the original visa was granted;

children.label: ii
children.text: whether the level and/or subject area of the proposed programme of study are significantly different from the original programme of study; and

children.label: iii
children.text: any relevant information held about the previous application(s) including advice from the original issuing branch (see E7.1.1).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have received New Zealand Aid Programme funding within the two years prior to their application to change programme of study and/or education provider being made, must also provide evidence that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade supports the change of programme of study or education provider and that any scholarship continues.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Applicants who wish to change their programme of study and/or education provider may provide evidence of payment of tuition fees after the application has been approved in principle.
