pages.title: Insurance requirements for fee-paying foreign students
pages.page_title: U3.45 Insurance requirements for fee-paying foreign students (21/11/2016)

units.heading: Insurance requirements for fee-paying foreign students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Fee-paying foreign students must hold insurance as a condition of their visa (see E3.20 (f)) unless (d) below applies.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A fee-paying foreign student must declare that they will arrange and hold insurance, which complies with the insurance requirements of the Education (Pastoral Care of International Students) Code of Practice 2016 and is acceptable to the student’s education provider, from the period of their enrolment until the expiry of their student visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: A student may be required to provide evidence that they held insurance from the time of their enrolment until the expiry of their student visa with any further visa application made.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The requirement to hold insurance does not apply to Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) students or New Zealand Aid Programme-supported students.

units.heading: Tertiary institutions (Universities, Polytechnics, Colleges of Education, Wananga)

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Tertiary institutions may offer programmes of study or training scheme places to foreign students provided the programme of study or training scheme meets the criteria for one in which a foreign student may be enrolled in accordance with the provisions of the Education Act 1989 (see section 224(7)–(12)).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The definition of a foreign student is contained in section 159 of the Education Act 1989.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The primary requirements for section 224(7)–(12) of the Education Act 1989 in respect of programmes of study or training schemes that are or are likely to be longer than 3 months are that:

children.label: i
children.text: the programme or training scheme is an approved programme or training scheme, and

children.label: ii
children.text: the institution is accredited to provide the programme or training scheme, and

children.label: iii
children.text: the effect of the enrolment is not to deprive a domestic or exempt student of a place at the institution or on the programme of study or training scheme unless:

children.label: b1
children.text: the student is an New Zealand Aid Programme scholarship student; or

children.label: b2
children.text: the place has been established by the Council of the institution for a foreign student and its continued availability is dependent on the fees payable by the foreign student enrolled in it. Note: ~ Polytechnics also include institutes of technology, technical institutes or community colleges established before 1 January 1991. ~ These requirements apply to all programmes of study and training schemes with the exception of those programmes of study or training schemes that are exempt as provided for in section 232(2) of the Education Act 1989.

pages.page_title: U8.20 Dependent children of holders of work visas (01/07/2018)

units.heading: Dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Essential Skills work visa where the employment has been assessed as lower-skilled (WK3.5.1), unless U8.20.1 below applies; or

children.label: ii
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: v
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2); or

children.label: vi
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: vii
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or.

children.label: viii
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.15 to A5.25.

units.heading: Holders of Essential Skills work visas for lower-skilled employment who are able to support student visas for their dependent children

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The applicant (who is the dependent child of an Essential Skills work visa holder whose employment has been assessed as lower-skilled) may be granted a student visa under these instructions if:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant held a visa on the basis of being a dependent child of the Essential Skills work visa holder on 28 August 2017; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the Essential Skills work visa holder has not been subject to a stand-down period (see WK3.20.5).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The applicant (who is the dependent child of an Essential Skills work visa holder whose employment has been assessed as lower-skilled) may be granted a student visa under these instructions if:

children.label: i
children.text: the Essential Skills work visa holder parent previously held a student visa that made them eligible to support a child for a student visa (U8.25); and

children.label: ii
children.text: subsequently held a post-study work visa (WD) based on that student visa; and

children.label: iii
children.text: supported the applicant for a visa based on their relationship while holding a post-study work visa.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$42,944.20 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$42,944.20 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The STTS scheme is part of the New Zealand Aid Programme and provides partner governments with the opportunities to develop new competencies in identified areas of need as well as to upskill their work force. Training may involve placement with a New Zealand government department, a private training establishment, or at a tertiary institution. Trainees are provided with entitlements for accommodation and maintenance whilst on this scheme.

blocks.label: b

units.heading: New Zealand Aid Programme-supported students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A New Zealand Aid Programme-supported student receives funding from the New Zealand Government under the following schemes:

children.label: i
children.text: New Zealand Development Scholarships;

children.label: ii
children.text: Short-Term Training Scholarships;

children.label: iii

children.label: iv

children.label: v
children.text: English Language Training for Officials;

children.label: vi

children.label: vii
children.text: New Zealand Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) Scholars Award.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The objective of the scholarships is for candidates to gain knowledge and skills in specific subject areas that will assist in the development of their home country.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Recipients are required to return to their home country for at least two years after the completion of their scholarship to apply these new skills and knowledge in government, civil society or private business organisations.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (c) above, NZAP-supported students who have completed Short-Term Training Scholarships or English Language Training for Officials of less than six months in duration are required to return to their home country for at least one year after the completion of their scholarship.

units.heading: New Zealand Aid Programme (NZAP)-supported students undertaking employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: New Zealand Aid Programme (NZAP)-supported students may be granted conditions on their student visa to allow them to work during the academic year for up to 20 hours per week, during any holidays within the academic year for up to 20 hours per week, and full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period unless they are studying under the following schemes:

children.label: i
children.text: Short-Term Training Scholarships; or

children.label: ii
children.text: New Zealand Regional Development Scholarships; or

children.label: iii
children.text: English Language Training for Officials. Note: NZAP-supported students may also be eligible for full-time work rights during scheduled vacation periods. See U13.15.10

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: With the exception of the schemes listed under (a), NZAP scholars may be granted work visas at the completion of their programmes of study for qualification-related work experience for the minimum time needed to complete practical work requirements. Note: NZAP-supported senior medical and pharmacy students may be granted a work visa for their internship/registration year.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: NZAP-supported students are not permitted to:

children.label: i
children.text: work in self-employment; or

children.label: ii
children.text: provide commercial sexual services; or

children.label: iii
children.text: act as an operator of a New Zealand business of prostitution; or

children.label: iv
children.text: invest in a business of prostitution (see E7.40).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Any NZAP-supported student, or their partner or dependent children, may only be granted a visa for New Zealand in the two-year period following completion of the NZAP-supported student's scholarship, with written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (with the exception of a work visa to complete programme of study requirements or, if the applicant is outside New Zealand, a short-term visitor visa).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Despite (d) above, where a NZAP-supported student has completed a Short-Term Training Scholarships or English Language Training for Officials of less than six months in duration, the NZAP-supported student, their partner or dependent children may only be granted a visa for New Zealand in the one year period following completion of their scholarship or training, with the written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (with the exception of a work visa to complete programme of study requirements or, if the applicant is outside New Zealand, a short-term visitor visa). Note: See WF4.5 for work instructions for partners of holders of student visas who are NZAP-supported.

pages.title: Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions
pages.page_title: U14.15 Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions (26/11/2018)

units.heading: Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: If a pathway student visa holder wishes to move to a different education provider or lower level programme of study than those specified in their visa conditions, they must apply for a new student visa and meet the requirements set out at U3.40.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A variation of conditions, for the purpose of changing a programme of study at the same education provider will only be granted if an immigration officer is satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant meets the student requirements set out at U3.1; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant has not breached their visa conditions as set out at E3.20; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the original student visa would have been granted for the proposed programme of study; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the proposed programme of study is at the same or higher level on the New Zealand Qualification Framework as the original programme of study; and

children.label: v
children.text: the applicant remains a bona fide applicant (see E5.1).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Factors that an immigration officer may take into consideration when determining (b)(iii) and (b)(iv) above include, but are not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: the time elapsed since the original visa was granted; and

children.label: ii
children.text: whether the level and/or subject area of the proposed programme of study are significantly different from the original programme of study; and

children.label: iii
children.text: any relevant information held about the previous application(s) including advice from the original issuing branch (see E7.1.1).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Students who have received New Zealand Aid Programme funding within the two years prior to their application to change programme of study must also provide evidence that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade supports the change of programme of study and that any scholarship continues.

units.heading: Breaching visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A pathway student visa holder will be considered to be in breach of visa conditions where:

children.label: i
children.text: they fail to meet conditional pre-requisites for enrolment into a second or subsequent programme of study (E3.20(d)); or

children.label: ii
children.text: the time between the completion of one programme of study and the start of a second or subsequent programme of study on a pathway exceeds 16 weeks; or

children.label: iii
children.text: they have submitted an English language test result as set out at U14.5.1(c) and their intended pathway is an English language programme of study culminating in a qualification at Levels 5 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework and the English Language programme of study is not completed within a 20 week period.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A breach of visa conditions is "sufficient reason" to make a temporary entry class visa holder liable for deportation, and may result in the issue of a Deportation Liability Notice (E3.60).

pages.title: Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa
pages.page_title: U14.5 Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa (01/05/2019)

units.heading: Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To be granted a pathway student visa, an applicant must:

children.label: a
children.text: be offered an eligible study pathway from a qualifying provider(s) (U14.20); and

children.label: b
children.text: meet the general requirements to be granted a student visa as set out at U3.1; and

children.label: c
children.text: meet the additional evidential requirements for pathway student visa set out at U14.5.1; and

children.label: d
children.text: make an application for a student visa before 24 November 2019.

units.heading: Evidence of meeting requirements

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: In addition to meeting the general requirements to be granted a student visa as set out at U3.1, when applying for a pathway student visa an applicant must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: where there is more than one education provider, a joint letter of support from pathway education providers; and

children.label: ii
children.text: an offer of place (or joint offer) for each programme of study that meets the requirements set out at U3.5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence that tuition fee requirements, as set out at U3.10, for either the first programme of study or first year of study (whichever is shorter) have been met and satisfy an immigration officer that they have the ability to fund any remaining balance of the first programme of study and subsequent programmes of study on the intended pathway; and

children.label: iv
children.text: evidence that the maintenance funds requirements set out in U3.20 for the first year of study on the intended pathway have been met and satisfy an immigration officer that they have the ability to fund any remaining balance of the first programme of study and subsequent programmes of study on the intended pathway.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a)(ii), second and subsequent offers of place for a pathway can be conditional on meeting pre-requisite programme of study entry criteria.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Pathway student visa applicants from a country with a student visa decline rate of more than 20 per cent who intend a study pathway commencing with an English language programme of study and culminating in a qualification at Levels 5 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework must:

children.label: i
children.text: submit an International English Language Testing System test (IELTS) (or equivalent internationally recognised proficiency test) at the time of application; and

children.label: ii
children.text: demonstrate that they only require an improvement of 0.5 of an IELTS overall band score (or equivalent) to meet the English language prerequisite for entry into the intended level 5 to 8 programme of study.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The student visa decline rate for a country is based on statistics, generated over a calendar year (12 months), by Immigration New Zealand. The decline rate and the name of the country are published on the INZ website. For the purpose of this instruction, the internationally recognised English language tests and corresponding IELTS equivalent test scores set out on the INZ website are considered acceptable.

pages.page_title: H5.25 Determining an application for a visa or variation of conditions (to 29/07/2024)

units.heading: Determining an application for a visa or variation of conditions
Determining an application for a Critical Purpose visitor visa

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A Critical Purpose visitor visa may be granted if an immigration officer is satisfied that all applicants included in the application:

children.label: i
children.text: meet health and character requirements for temporary entry (A4 and A5); and

children.label: ii
children.text: are bona fide (E5) applicants for a temporary entry class visa; and

children.label: iii
children.text: meet funds or sponsorship requirements for visitors (V2.20); and

children.label: iv
children.text: meet onward travel requirements for visitors (V2.25); and

children.label: v
children.text: have a critical purpose for travel to New Zealand as described in H5.25.15; and

children.label: vi
children.text: if they are a ‘critical health worker’ (H5.30.1) or an ‘other critical worker’ (H5.30.5), they have provided sufficient evidence to demonstrate that they meet the requirements of W2.10.1(b) as applicable.

units.heading: Determining an application for another visa (appropriate to the applicant’s circumstances)

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: An immigration officer may grant a visa appropriate to the applicant’s circumstances if they are satisfied that the applicant:

children.label: a
children.text: meets all relevant immigration instructions required for the grant of that visa; and

children.label: b
children.text: has a critical purpose for travel to New Zealand as described in H5.25.15.

units.heading: Determining an application for a variation of conditions (for holders of a valid temporary entry class visa)

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A variation of conditions can be granted where an immigration officer is satisfied:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant has a critical purpose for travelling to and being in New Zealand as described at H5.25.15; and

children.label: ii
children.text: all the other requirements of the visa the person currently holds continue to be met.

units.heading: List of critical purpose for travelling to New Zealand

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are defined as having a critical purpose for travelling to New Zealand under these instructions.

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Critical health workers and their partners and dependent children (H5.30.1).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Other critical workers, and their partners and dependent children (except where H5.30.20 states that partners and dependent children are not eligible to be included) (H5.30.5).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: People belonging to a class exception agreed to by Cabinet or the Minister of Immigration, consisting of either:

children.label: i
children.text: class of workers, that meets the requirements set out at H5.30.20; or

children.label: ii
children.text: ia class of individuals, that meets the requirements set out at H5.30.21.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Citizens of Samoa and Tonga, and Vanuatu government representatives, making essential travel to New Zealand where this travel has been officially requested by the Government of Samoa, Vanuatu or Tonga, and this request has been formally approved by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: People who meet compassionate entry requirements, or who hold a valid invitation to apply based on previous humanitarian requirements (H5.30.25).

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: The partner, dependent child or legal guardian of a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder (with the exception of the holder of a resident visa granted outside New Zealand who has not entered New Zealand as the holder of the visa), who is either:

children.label: i
children.text: travelling with that New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder; or

children.label: ii
children.text: ordinarily resident in New Zealand; or

children.label: iii
children.text: has a visa based on their relationship to the New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: People who hold a visitor, work or student visa and:

children.label: i
children.text: are ordinarily resident in New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: are the partner or dependent child (see E4.1) of a work or student visa holder who is in New Zealand.

blocks.label: h
blocks.text: Replacement commercial ship crew travelling to New Zealand by air (H5.30.30).

blocks.label: i
blocks.text: People who held a visitor, work or student visa on 19 March 2020 that was granted on the basis of their relationship to a work or student visa holder and, on the date they express interest:

children.label: i
children.text: the work or student visa holder is in New Zealand; and either

children.label: ii
children.text: that relationship-based visa is still current; or

children.label: iii
children.text: that relationship-based visa had a "first entry" condition and, had they entered New Zealand on the last date allowed for by the first entry condition, their visa would still be current (H5.30.40).

blocks.label: j
blocks.text: The partner or dependent child of a work visa or a Critical Purpose visa holder who is in New Zealand when the expression of interest is made and that visa-holder’s visa either:

children.label: i
children.text: is employed in an occupation in critical health services (H5.30.45); or

children.label: ii
children.text: was granted on the basis of current employment that meets the specified salary, and is highly-skilled, as defined in H5.30.50; or

children.label: iii
children.text: is employed as a full-time teacher in either Early Childhood Education or at a primary or secondary school.

units.heading: Family relationships

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A person will be considered to be the partner of a New Zealand citizen, or permanent resident visa holder, or resident visa holder, or Australian citizen or permanent resident who is ordinarily resident in New Zealand, if they meet the requirements for partners specified in E4.1.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A person will be considered to be a dependent child of a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident visa holder, or resident visa holder, or Australian citizen or permanent resident who is ordinarily resident in New Zealand, if they meet the requirements for dependent children specified in E4.1.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: A person will be considered to be a partner of a visitor, work or student visa holder who is in New Zealand, if they meet the requirements for partners specified in E4.1.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: A person will be considered to be a dependent child of a visitor, work or student visa holder who is in New Zealand, if they meet the requirements for dependent children specified in E4.1.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: An immigration officer must be satisfied that a person is a partner or dependent child of a New Zealand citizen or visa holder, or Australian citizen or permanent resident who is ordinarily resident in New Zealand, before a visa can be granted to a person for a critical purpose based on that relationship.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: For the avoidance of doubt and the purposes of (a) (c) and (e) above, a person will only be considered to have met the requirements of partnership if they also have lived together.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Any New Zealand citizen or resident visa holder partner who is supporting an application for a relationship based visitor visa made by a person described in H5.25.20(a), must meet the character requirements for partners supporting ‘partnership-based temporary entry applications’ (E7.45).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where a person is applying as the partner or dependent child of a New Zealand citizen or visa holder, or Australian citizen or permanent resident who is ordinarily resident in New Zealand, evidence of the relationship must be provided if Immigration New Zealand has not established the relationship in a previous visa application.

pages.page_title: H5.30 Definitions (to 29/07/2024)

units.heading: Definitions
Critical health workers

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A critical health worker is a person who will work in an occupation needed to deliver critical health services in New Zealand (see H5.30.1(b)) for an employer listed at H5.30.1(c).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Occupations needed to deliver critical health services in New Zealand are:

children.label: i
children.text: registered health practitioners as set out in the Health Practitioners Competence Assurance Act 2003; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a worker who installs, operates or maintains medical equipment; or

children.label: iii
children.text: paramedics and ambulance workers (including air and road); or

children.label: iv
children.text: physician associates; or

children.label: v
children.text: technical and support staff working in:

children.label: b1
children.text: theatre

children.label: b2
children.text: laboratory

children.label: b3
children.text: radiology

children.label: b4
children.text: pharmacy services

children.label: b5
children.text: cardiology blood service

children.label: b6
children.text: nuclear medicine

children.label: b7
children.text: oncology

children.label: b8
children.text: haematology

children.label: b9
children.text: pathology

children.label: b10
children.text: hyperbaric medicine

children.label: b11
children.text: mortuary

children.label: b12
children.text: research staff; or

children.label: vi
children.text: workers delivering mental health and addictions services, aged care, respite, home care and support, child health, palliative and hospice care, forensic health, and disability support.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Critical health workers may work in one or more of the following:

children.label: i
children.text: ia District Health Board;

children.label: ii
children.text: the New Zealand Blood Service;

children.label: iii
children.text: a hospice or palliative care provider;

children.label: iv
children.text: a primary care practice such as urgent care or a medical or healthcare centre;

children.label: v
children.text: an aged residential care, respite or continuing care facility, including care in a person’s home or community facility;

children.label: vi
children.text: a government or Non-Government Organisation delivering health and disability services;

children.label: vii
children.text: organisations that provide, operate and maintain medical equipment;

children.label: viii
children.text: private employers delivering health and disability services.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Workers in an occupation that is indirectly related to the provision of health services, or corporate functions such as (but not limited to) human resources, office administration or property maintenance are not considered critical health workers.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: For the purposes of these instructions, internationally qualified nurses are also considered to be critical health workers where they:

children.label: i
children.text: are invited to come to New Zealand by the Nursing Council of New Zealand, and

children.label: ii
children.text: are enrolled in a Competence Assessment Programme.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Any partners or dependent children (see E4.1) of critical health workers who have been granted a visa or a variation of conditions on the basis of this critical purpose, may be granted a visa to travel to New Zealand together with, or separately from, the critical health worker.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: When considering whether a person is a critical health worker, an immigration officer may request evidence of the person’s qualifications or registration.

blocks.label: h
blocks.text: An immigration officer may request the critical health worker to provide evidence of an offer of employment (see W2.10.10).

units.heading: Other critical workers

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A person may be considered an ‘other critical worker’ and granted a visa or variation of conditions for up to six months if they are required to come to New Zealand for up to six months and they:

children.label: i
children.text: have unique experience and technical or specialist skills that are not readily obtainable in New Zealand; or

children.label: ii
children.text: are undertaking a time-critical role:

children.label: b1
children.text: for a government approved event or a major government-approved programme (as defined in H5.30.15); or

children.label: b2
children.text: in support of an approved government-to-government agreement (as defined in H5.30.15); or

children.label: b3
children.text: for work which brings significant wider benefit to the national or regional economy; or

children.label: iii
children.text: meets the requirements of an approved class of worker listed at H5.30.20.; or

children.label: iv
children.text: have a role in which they earn at least the median salary (currently $27 per hour) for the delivery or execution of an approved major infrastructure project (as defined in H5.30.10).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: However, a person may be considered an ‘other critical worker’ and granted a visa or variation of conditions for more than six months (up to a maximum of 12 months), if they are required to stay in New Zealand for more than six months to achieve their critical purpose, and they have:

children.label: i
children.text: a role in which they earn at least 1.5 times the median salary (currently $84,240 per annum); or

children.label: ii
children.text: a role that is essential for the completion or continuation of a science programme under a government funded or partially government-funded contract, including research and development exchanges and partnerships, and has the support of MBIE Science, Innovation and International Branch to travel to New Zealand to carry out their work; or

children.label: iii
children.text: an essential role for a government approved event or a major government-approved programme (as defined in H5.30.15); or

children.label: iv
children.text: have a role in which they earn at least the median salary (currently $27 per hour) for the delivery or execution of an approved major infrastructure project (as defined in H5.30.10).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite, (a) above, a person considered an ‘other critical worker’ approved on the basis of being part of a class of workers, may be granted a visa or variation of conditions for up to six months unless a maximum duration is specified at H5.30.20.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: When considering H5.30.5 (b)(i) and (iv), an immigration officer must be satisfied that the offer of employment meets the requirements set out at W2.10.5 and W2.10.10.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Factors an immigration officer may take into account when determining whether a person is an ‘other critical worker’ as defined in H5.30.5 (a) and (b), include:

children.label: i
children.text: why that person is needed to ensure the delivery, continuity or execution of the work or service, and the effect on the work or service if the person was unable to come; and

children.label: ii
children.text: why it is not possible to re-deploy workers already in New Zealand (this could include time constraints or the specific nature of the work or service to be done); and

children.label: iii
children.text: the situation of the staff (if any) currently performing the role(s), and whether they can remain or not in the roles; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the length of the visa required and the reason for that length of visa.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Any partners or dependent children (see E4.1) of an ‘other critical worker’ who has been granted a visa or a variation of conditions on the basis of this critical purpose, may be granted a visa to travel to New Zealand together with, or separately from, the ‘other critical worker’ (except where H5.30.20) states that partners and dependent children are not eligible to be included).

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: When considering H5.30.5 (a)(i), the factors that an immigration officer may take into consideration when assessing:

children.label: i
children.text: "unique experience and technical or specialist skills" include, but are not limited to, whether these skills or experience:

children.label: b1
children.text: have been gained in a specialist training institution or by working in a highly-specialist firm

children.label: b2
children.text: can be demonstrated through global experience

children.label: b3
children.text: are inherent to a person

children.label: ii
children.text: "not readily obtainable" include, but are not limited to, whether:

children.label: b1
children.text: there are no workers in the country who could perform the role, or

children.label: b2
children.text: there is a very limited pool of available workers who could perform the role and they are not available to the employer.

blocks.label: h
blocks.text: When considering H5.30.5 (a)(i), applications for seasonal workers will generally not be approved under these instructions. The only exceptions will be if the nature of the work is highly skilled or uniquely specialised.

blocks.label: i
blocks.text: "Time critical" in H5.30.5 (a)(ii) includes if the person does not come to New Zealand, the project, work or event will cease or be severely compromised, or significant costs will be incurred.

blocks.label: j
blocks.text: When considering H5.30.5 (a)(iv) and (b)(iv), workers in an occupation that is indirectly related to the delivery or execution of an approved major infrastructure project, such as (but not limited to) human resources, office administration or property maintenance are not considered other critical workers.

blocks.label: k
blocks.text: A person enrolled in, or with an offer to study, a Doctoral Degree at a New Zealand university, may be determined to be an ‘other critical worker’, if the person:

children.label: i
children.text: has a role that is essential for the completion or continuation of a science programme under a government funded or partially government-funded contract, including research and development exchanges and partnerships, and has the support of MBIE Science, Innovation and International Branch to travel to New Zealand to carry out their work, or

children.label: ii
children.text: has unique experience and technical or specialist skills that are not readily obtainable in New Zealand or

children.label: iii
children.text: is undertaking a time-critical role:

children.label: b1
children.text: for the delivery of an approved major infrastructure project (as defined in H5.30.10); or a government approved event or a major government-approved programme (as defined in H5.30.15); or

children.label: b2
children.text: in support of an approved government-to-government agreement (as defined in H5.30.15); or

children.label: b3
children.text: for work which brings significant wider benefit to the national or regional economy.

blocks.label: l
blocks.text: A student who is assessed as meeting the criteria in (k) can be invited to apply for a:

children.label: i
children.text: student visa, and if their visa application is approved, may be granted a student visa for more than six months (up to a maximum of 12 months); or

children.label: ii
children.text: variation of conditions, if they already hold a student visa for their study for a Doctoral Degree.

blocks.label: m
blocks.text: For the purpose of the H5 instructions, the median wage is $27 per hour.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Notes: - Examples of workers meeting this standard may include: some highly specialist veterinarians, vendor-appointed engineers required to install major equipment, or an actor in a key film role. - For the absence of doubt, co-owners of America’s Cup syndicates may be considered other critical workers under H5.30.5(a)(ii). - For the avoidance of doubt, a person outside of New Zealand who is required for more than six months must meet the relevant criteria at H5.30.5(b) if they are an ‘other critical worker’ as defined at H5.30.5(a)(i) or (ii).

units.heading: Approved major infrastructure projects

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: those projects with a cost of $50 million or more, as listed on the infrastructure pipeline on a website maintained by the Infrastructure Commission (except those listed as "project complete"); or

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: the Marsden Point decommissioning project.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Notes: The infrastructure pipeline can be viewed at www.infracom.govt.nz/projects/pipeline/

units.heading: Compassionate entry exception

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A person meets the compassionate entry requirements if there are exceptional circumstances of a familial (see H5.30.25.1) or medical (see H5.30.25.5) nature which make it critical for that person to urgently travel to and enter New Zealand specifically, over and above any other country.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: When determining whether an applicant meets the compassionate entry requirements, factors that are not considered relevant include whether:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant has been affected by a humanitarian crisis occurring outside of New Zealand

children.label: ii
children.text: an application, sponsorship registration, or Expression of Interest for a New Zealand visa has been made.

units.heading: Compassionate entry exception for familial reasons

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Familial reasons are extraordinary family circumstances resulting in the need for a person to travel to New Zealand to lend support in order to prevent significant harm.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Relevant factors when considering if there are familial reasons that support entry on compassionate grounds under these instructions include:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant’s familial or otherwise demonstrably close personal connection to someone in New Zealand

children.label: ii
children.text: whether the situation involves extraordinary family trauma, or provision of support for a minor

children.label: iii
children.text: whether the applicant’s close personal connection in New Zealand has any alternative supporting options

children.label: iv
children.text: whether New Zealand is their primary place of residence, and their period of absence from New Zealand.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: - For the avoidance of doubt, separation from close family members as a result of COVID-19 does not in and of itself meet the compassionate entry threshold. The government has created alternate border exceptions to enable entry to these groups, such as the family relationships category (see H5.25.15(m)). - An example of a situation that would meet the compassionate entry threshold is allowing the closest relative of an orphaned child to travel to New Zealand to support the child temporarily, due to a lack of New Zealand-based alternatives.

units.heading: Compassionate entry exception for medical treatment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Where a person is applying on compassionate entry grounds because they require medical treatment in New Zealand, that person must have the support of the Ministry of Health or a District Health Board.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Where the applicant can reasonably delay, or otherwise obtain treatment outside of New Zealand, an exception will not be granted.

units.heading: Replacement commercial ship crew

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A replacement commercial ship crew member is a person travelling to New Zealand as a passenger on a commercial aircraft for the purpose of leaving New Zealand as crew on a commercial ship.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: After arriving in New Zealand, replacement commercial ship crew must transfer as soon as reasonably practicable to a commercial ship to depart New Zealand.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Commercial crew include any crew on ships that are in New Zealand, excluding crew who:

children.label: i
children.text: intend to work in New Zealand rather than immediately departing; or

children.label: ii
children.text: are on ships that are pleasure craft; or

children.label: iii
children.text: are on ships that are powered solely manually or by sail.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Notes: For the avoidance of doubt, crew subject to regulation 25 of the Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations 2010 are not subject to this instruction (namely cargo crew on a ship when arriving by sea in New Zealand). "Pleasure craft" as outlined in (c)(ii) above means the same as defined under the Maritime Transport Act 1994.

units.heading: Partner or dependent child with a visa based on their relationship to a temporary visa holder in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A person will be considered to have a critical purpose for travel to New Zealand (H5.25.15(l)) if they meet the following requirements:

children.label: i
children.text: the person is currently outside of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: on 19 March 2020 the person held a temporary visa granted on the basis on their relationship with a work or student visa holder; and

children.label: iii
children.text: at the time the person expresses interest in travelling to New Zealand under these instructions (see H5.10), the visa that they held on 19 March 2020 either:

children.label: b1
children.text: is still current; or

children.label: b2
children.text: had a "first entry" condition and, had the holder entered New Zealand on the last date allowed for by the first entry condition, would be current; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the visa the person holds or held is based on their relationship to their partner or parent who:

children.label: b1
children.text: is in New Zealand when the expression of interest is made; and

children.label: b2
children.text: holds a work or student visa that is valid for at least a further 12 months, on the date that the person expresses interest in travelling to New Zealand under H5.25.15(l).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A person who is considered to have a critical purpose for travel to New Zealand under (a) may be invited to apply under these instructions (see H5.10) for either:

children.label: i
children.text: a visa appropriate to their circumstances, which will be a visa based on their relationship to their partner or parent who is the work or student visa holder referred to in (a)(iii); or

children.label: ii
children.text: a variation of conditions for the visa they hold.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If the person otherwise meets the criteria in (a) but does not hold a visa because they are a dependent child who meets the criteria in H5.10(c)(iv), then they must be considered as meeting the requirements in (a)(ii) and (iii).

units.heading: Partner or dependent child of a worker in critical health services

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A person will be considered to have a critical purpose for travel to New Zealand (H5.25.15(m)(i)) if they meet the following requirements:

children.label: i
children.text: the person is currently outside of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the person is the partner or dependent child of a temporary visa holder who is in New Zealand when the expression of interest is made and is employed in an occupation needed to deliver critical health services in New Zealand (as defined in H5.30.1(b)).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A person who is considered to have a critical purpose for travel to New Zealand under (a) may be invited to apply under these instructions (see H5.10) for either:

children.label: i
children.text: a visa appropriate to their circumstances, which will be a visa based on their relationship to their partner or parent who is the health worker referred to in (a)(ii); or

children.label: ii
children.text: a variation of conditions for the visa they hold.

units.heading: Partner or dependent child of a highly-skilled worker in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A person will be considered to have a critical purpose for travel to New Zealand (H5.25.15(m)(ii)) if they meet the requirements in (b) and (c) below.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The person is currently outside of New Zealand.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The person is the partner or dependent child of a temporary visa holder who:

children.label: i
children.text: is in New Zealand when the expression of interest is made; and

children.label: ii
children.text: is in current employment that meets H5.30.50.1 below; and

children.label: iii
children.text: holds a visa valid for at least a further 12 months on the date that the person makes a request to travel to New Zealand under H5.25.15(m)(ii); and

children.label: iv
children.text: holds a visa that is eligible to support partners and dependent children (see WF3.1 and V3.10).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: A person who is considered to have a critical purpose for travel to New Zealand under (a) above may be invited to apply under these instructions (see H5.10) for either a:

children.label: i
children.text: a visa appropriate to their circumstances, which will be a visa based on their relationship to their partner or parent who is the highly-skilled worker referred to in (c); or

children.label: ii
children.text: ia variation of conditions for the visa they hold.

units.heading: Requirements for the temporary visa holder’s employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A temporary visa holder described in H3.30.50(c) is considered highly skilled if their current employment is:

children.label: i
children.text: paid at least 1.5 times the median salary (NZD $84,240 per year); or

children.label: ii
children.text: they have a role essential for the completion or continuation of a science programme under a government funded or partially government funded contract, including research and development exchanges and partnerships, and have the support of the Science, Innovation and International Branch at MBIE; or

children.label: iii
children.text: their role is essential for the delivery or execution of one of the following:

children.label: b1
children.text: an approved major infrastructure project, or a government approved event or a major government approved programme, or

children.label: b2
children.text: an approved government-to-government agreement.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Notes: - For the absence of doubt, ‘current employment’ in H5.30.50.1 above does not include an offer of employment. - When considering H5.30.50.1(a), an immigration officer may determine if the current employment of the temporary visa holder meets the requirements of H5.30.50.1(a) for the person in H5.30.50 to be eligible to be invited to apply for a visa.

units.heading: Partner or dependent child of a teacher in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A person will be considered to have a critical purpose for travel to New Zealand if they meet the following requirements:

children.label: i
children.text: the person is currently outside of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the person is the partner or dependent child of a temporary visa holder who is in New Zealand when the expression of interest is made and who is registered with the Teaching Council of Aotearoa New Zealand and is employed as a teacher in Early Childhood Education, or primary, or secondary schooling.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A person who is considered to have a critical purpose for travel to New Zealand under (a) above may be invited to apply under these instructions (see H5.10) for either:

children.label: i
children.text: a visa appropriate to their circumstances, which will be a visa based on their relationship to their partner or parent who is the teacher referred to in H5.25.15(m)(iii); or

children.label: ii
children.text: a variation of conditions for the visa they hold.

units.heading: Calculating remuneration

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Where an annual salary is specified under H5 instructions, remuneration will be calculated according to the salary stated in the employment agreement of the temporary visa applicant or temporary visa holder under H5.30.50.1(a)

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Where an employee is to work more than 40 hours per week, the minimum base salary must be calculated on the basis of a 40 hour week.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Remuneration includes:

children.label: i
children.text: the agreed value of any reasonable deduction from the applicant’s salary or wages for goods or services; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the case of accommodation provided in connection to the employment:

children.label: b1
children.text: the agreed value of any reasonable deduction from the applicant’s salary or wages for that accommodation; or

children.label: b2
children.text: if accommodation is provided by the employer, and there is no deduction from the applicant’s salary or wages for that accommodation, the market rental value of the accommodation provided; or

children.label: b3
children.text: if an accommodation allowance is provided, the amount of that allowance.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Notes: - In relation to H5.30.60 (c)(ii) above, the meaning of accommodation, and the value of accommodation that is included in the definition of ‘remuneration’, reflects the definition of accommodation and the value of accommodation that forms part of a person’s income under section CE 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007. - For the purposes of H5.30.60, remuneration excludes other employment-related allowances (for example tool, or uniform allowances), and bonuses which are dependent on performance.

pages.title: Dependent children of holders of work visas
pages.page_title: U8.20 Dependent children of holders of work visas (13/05/2019)

units.heading: Dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Essential Skills work visa where the employment has been assessed as lower-skilled (WK3.5.1), unless U8.20.1 below applies; or

children.label: ii
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: v
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2); or

children.label: vi
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: vii
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or.

children.label: viii
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.15 to A5.25.

units.heading: Holders of Essential Skills work visas for lower-skilled employment who are able to support student visas for their dependent children

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The applicant (who is the dependent child of an Essential Skills work visa holder whose employment has been assessed as lower-skilled) may be granted a student visa under these instructions if:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant held a visa on the basis of being a dependent child of the Essential Skills work visa holder on 28 August 2017; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the Essential Skills work visa holder has not been subject to a stand-down period (see WK3.20.5).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The applicant (who is the dependent child of an Essential Skills work visa holder whose employment has been assessed as lower-skilled) may be granted a student visa under these instructions if:

children.label: i
children.text: the Essential Skills work visa holder parent previously held a student visa that made them eligible to support a child for a student visa (U8.25); and

children.label: ii
children.text: subsequently held a post-study work visa (WD) based on that student visa; and

children.label: iii
children.text: supported the applicant for a visa based on their relationship while holding a post-study work visa.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$43,322.76 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$43,322.76 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Summary

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless otherwise specified, to be granted a student visa to attend a programme of study of more than three months, applicants must:

children.label: i
children.text: have an offer of a place or, if returning to continue a programme of study, a confirmation of enrolment in an approved programme of study with an education provider in New Zealand that meets student visa requirements (see U3.5, U3.10, and U5.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: be exempted from or have paid tuition fees; and

children.label: iii
children.text: if aged under 18, meet accommodation requirements (see U3.15); and

children.label: iv
children.text: have fulfilled the purpose and met the conditions for any previous or current temporary visas held as set out in E3.15 and E3.20; and

children.label: v
children.text: meet the conditions set out in E3.20; and

children.label: vi
children.text: not be the holder of a current visitor visa granted under Guardians accompanying students to New Zealand instructions (see V3.100).); and

children.label: vii
children.text: hold insurance (see U3.45), unless they are a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) student or a student holding a New Zealand scholarship administered through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All applicants must meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for:

children.label: i
children.text: lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa as set out at E4; and

children.label: ii
children.text: bona fide applicants as set out at E5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: health and character as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have not completed, or will not be completing the programme of study endorsed on their student visa and who wish to change their programme of study and/or education provider must: Note: Applicants who are progressing to further study, for example a student in Year 13 who is progressing to tertiary studies, will not need to meet U3.40.

children.label: i
children.text: meet requirements (a) and (b) above; and

children.label: ii
children.text: meet the requirements set out at U3.40.

units.heading: Payment of costs for Managed Isolation and Quarantine for students who are nominated individuals in COVID-19 Restricted Temporary Entry Immigration Instructions

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The instructions in this section cease to be effective from 29/08/2022

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants who are invited to apply for a student visa on the basis of having a critical purpose for travelling to New Zealand under H5.25.15(c) because they belong to a class of individuals that meets the requirements of H5.30.21(c)(vi), must (if applicable) provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that either:

children.label: i
children.text: they have sufficient funds available to pay for the costs for their stay, if any, in Managed Isolation and Quarantine in New Zealand; or

children.label: ii
children.text: written confirmation from their education provider that the costs for the applicant’s stay in Managed Isolation and Quarantine, if any, will be paid in full or part by that education provider.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Where (a)(ii) applies, but an education provider confirms they will pay only part of the costs for the applicant’s stay in Managed Isolation and Quarantine, the student is required to show evidence they have sufficient funds available to pay the remainder of the costs.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where the applicant must show they have sufficient funds for the purposes of (a)(i) or (b), they must do this by providing evidence of:

children.label: i
children.text: funds held by or on behalf of the applicant (refer U3.50.5 below) to cover the costs for their stay in Managed Isolation and Quarantine in New Zealand; or

children.label: ii
children.text: sponsorship by a person, an organisation or a Government agency which meets generic sponsorship requirements set out at E6.5, to cover the costs for the applicant’s stay in Managed Isolation and Quarantine in New Zealand; or

children.label: iii
children.text: a guarantee of financial undertaking by a third party which covers the costs for the applicant’s stay in Managed Isolation and Quarantine in New Zealand; or

children.label: iv
children.text: notice of the award of a full scholarship that will cover the costs for the applicant’s stay in Managed Isolation and Quarantine in New Zealand.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: For the avoidance of doubt, funds required for the costs for stay in Managed Isolation and Quarantine in New Zealand are separate and additional to the funds required for maintenance under U3.20.25(b) or U3.20.30(b).

blocks.label: note2
blocks.text: Note: An applicant will be subject to pay the costs of their stay in Managed Isolation and Quarantine, unless exempted under clause 6 of the COVID-19 Public Health Response (Managed Isolation and Quarantine Charges) Regulations 2020.

units.heading: Funds held by or on behalf of the student

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Where funds are held by or on behalf of the applicant, immigration officers must be satisfied that the funds are from a genuine source and are genuinely available for the purposes of the person’s requirement to pay for their stay in Managed Isolation and Quarantine.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: When determining whether an applicant has sufficient funds to pay for the costs of their stay in Managed Isolation and Quarantine, immigration officers may consider the period of time for which funds have been held by the applicant and the applicant’s ability to access funds while in New Zealand.

pages.page_title: U3.20 Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand (22/08/2016)

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that they have sufficient funds available to maintain themselves throughout the period of their stay in New Zealand.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence may include but is not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: a notice of the award of a full scholarship; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a completed Sponsorship for Temporary Entry (INZ 1025) form (see U3.20.5); or

children.label: iii
children.text: a completed Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form, which covers a stay in New Zealand for the length of the visa (see U3.20.10); or

children.label: iv
children.text: funds held by or on behalf of the student (see U3.20.20).

units.heading: Sponsorship

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A sponsor for a student visa application must be an acceptable sponsor (see E6.5) and be either:

children.label: i
children.text: a natural person who is a relative or a friend of the applicant; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an organisation or government agency (an individual must be nominated as the authorised contact).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A sponsor for a fee-paying foreign tertiary student who is applying from within New Zealand must have sponsored that student’s initial student visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Sponsors must satisfy an immigration officer that they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet sponsorship obligations); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are sponsoring.

units.heading: Financial Undertaking

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Before the student’s arrival in New Zealand, a financial undertaking may be provided by a third party.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the third party is a person, they must be a relative or a friend of the applicant.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If the third party is not a person, they must nominate an individual as an authorised contact.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The third party providing the financial undertaking must satisfy an immigration officer they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet their financial obligations as set out on the Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are supporting.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Where a third party wishes to continue providing a financial undertaking for the student’s subsequent onshore student visa applications, they may do so if they continue to meet (d).

units.heading: Determining whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To determine whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide, immigration officers may consider:

children.label: a
children.text: the relationship between the applicant and the sponsor or third party;

children.label: b
children.text: any previous breaches of financial obligations set out in undertakings;

children.label: c
children.text: the number of student visa applications they are currently supporting;

children.label: d
children.text: the period of time for which funds have been held by the sponsor or third party; and

children.label: e
children.text: the student’s ability to access funds from the sponsor or third party while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds held by or on behalf of the student

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Where funds are held by or on behalf of the student, immigration officers must be satisfied that the funds are from a genuine source and are genuinely available for the purposes of the applicant’s maintenance requirements.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: When determining whether a student has sufficient funds to maintain themselves throughout their stay in New Zealand, immigration officers may consider the period of time for which funds have been held by the student and the student’s ability to access funds while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking programmes of study lasting less than 36 weeks

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students taking programmes of study lasting less than 36 weeks must provide evidence they have funds of at least NZ$1,250 per month of study available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: This evidence may be sighted after the application has been approved in principle.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking programmes of study lasting 36 weeks or longer

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students taking programmes of study lasting 36 weeks or longer must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that:

children.label: a
children.text: they have NZ$15,000.00 per year available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses); or

children.label: b
children.text: if they are citizens of Samoa and Tonga a written guarantee of maintenance from a relative in New Zealand who is either a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder.

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maternity health services

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Pregnant applicants for a student visa who are due to give birth while in New Zealand must provide evidence that they:

children.label: a
children.text: have funds of at least NZ$9,000 available to pay for maternity health services; or

children.label: b
children.text: have sponsorship by a person, an organisation or a Government agency which meets generic sponsorship requirements set out at E6.5, to cover maternity health services; or

children.label: c
children.text: have a guarantee of financial undertaking by a third party which covers maternity health services (see U3.20.10); or

children.label: d
children.text: are eligible for publicly-funded maternity health services.

units.heading: Conditions of student visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All visas for school students must state: 'primary or secondary school studies'.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the student has provided acceptable guarantees of funds and onward travel, the visa must state: ‘Evidence of financial support not required’ and ‘return/onward ticket not required’.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: All student visas must allow multiple journeys.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Two currency dates must be specified on student visas:

children.label: i
children.text: the date on which the visa expires; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the date on which the permission to travel expires.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions allowing the student to work (see U13).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: See also E3.20 for further student visa conditions.
