pages.title: Summary

units.heading: Summary

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless otherwise specified, to be granted a student visa to attend a programme of study of more than three months, applicants must:

children.label: i
children.text: have an offer of a place or, if returning to continue a programme of study, a confirmation of enrolment in an approved programme of study with an education provider in New Zealand that meets student visa requirements (see U3.5, U3.10, and U5.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: be exempted from or have paid tuition fees; and

children.label: iii
children.text: if aged under 18, meet accommodation requirements (see U3.15); and

children.label: iv
children.text: have fulfilled the purpose and met the conditions for any previous or current temporary visas held as set out in E3.15 and E3.20; and

children.label: v
children.text: meet the conditions set out in E3.20; and

children.label: vi
children.text: not be the holder of a current visitor visa granted under Guardians accompanying students to New Zealand instructions (see V3.100); and

children.label: vii
children.text: hold insurance (see U3.45), unless they are a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) student or a student holding a New Zealand scholarship administered through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All applicants must meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for:

children.label: i
children.text: lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa as set out at E4; and

children.label: ii
children.text: bona fide applicants as set out at E5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: health and character as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have not completed, or will not be completing the programme of study endorsed on their student visa and who wish to change their programme of study and/or education provider must:

children.label: i
children.text: meet requirements (a) and (b) above; and

children.label: ii
children.text: meet the requirements set out at U3.40.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: An applicant who is invited to apply for a student visa on the basis of having a critical purpose for travelling to New Zealand under H5.25.15(c) because they belong to a class of individuals that meets the requirements of H5.30.21(c)(iii), must also meet the requirement set out in U3.50 concerning the costs of Managed Isolation and Quarantine.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Applicants who are progressing to further study, for example a student in Year 13 who is progressing to tertiary studies, will not need to meet U3.40.

pages.title: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand
pages.page_title: U3.20 Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand (31/07/2022)

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that they have sufficient funds available to maintain themselves throughout the period of their stay in New Zealand.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence may include but is not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: a notice of the award of a full scholarship; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a completed Sponsorship for Temporary Entry (INZ 1025) form (see U3.20.5); or

children.label: iii
children.text: a completed Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form, which covers a stay in New Zealand for the length of the visa (see U3.20.10); or

children.label: iv
children.text: funds held by or on behalf of the student (see U3.20.20).

units.heading: Sponsorship

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A sponsor for a student visa application must be an acceptable sponsor (see E6.5) and be either:

children.label: i
children.text: a natural person who is a relative or a friend of the applicant; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an organisation or government agency (an individual must be nominated as the authorised contact).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A sponsor for a fee-paying foreign tertiary or non-compulsory education student who is applying from within New Zealand must have sponsored that student’s initial student visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Sponsors must satisfy an immigration officer that they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet sponsorship obligations); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are sponsoring.

units.heading: Financial Undertaking

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Before the student’s arrival in New Zealand, a financial undertaking may be provided by a third party.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the third party is a person, they must be a relative or a friend of the applicant.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If the third party is not a person, they must nominate an individual as an authorised contact.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The third party providing the financial undertaking must satisfy an immigration officer they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet their financial obligations as set out on the Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are supporting.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Where a third party wishes to continue providing a financial undertaking for the student’s subsequent onshore student visa applications, they may do so if they continue to meet (d).

units.heading: Determining whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To determine whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide, immigration officers may consider:

children.label: a
children.text: the relationship between the applicant and the sponsor or third party;

children.label: b
children.text: any previous breaches of financial obligations set out in undertakings;

children.label: c
children.text: the number of student visa applications they are currently supporting;

children.label: d
children.text: the period of time for which funds have been held by the sponsor or third party; and

children.label: e
children.text: the student’s ability to access funds from the sponsor or third party while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds held by or on behalf of the student

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Where funds are held by or on behalf of the student, immigration officers must be satisfied that the funds are from a genuine source and are genuinely available for the purposes of the applicant’s maintenance requirements.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: When determining whether a student has sufficient funds to maintain themselves throughout their stay in New Zealand, immigration officers may consider the period of time for which funds have been held by the student and the student’s ability to access funds while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking programmes of study lasting less than 36 weeks

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students taking programmes of study lasting less than 36 weeks must provide evidence they have funds of:

children.label: i
children.text: at least NZ$1,667 per month of study available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses) if they are undertaking tertiary or non-compulsory education study; or

children.label: ii
children.text: at least NZ$1,417 per month of study available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses) if they are undertaking compulsory education study.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the student is invited to apply for a student visa on the basis of having a critical purpose for travelling to New Zealand under H5.25.15(c) because they belong to a class of individuals that meets the requirements of H5.30.21(c)(iv), the student must provide evidence they have funds of at least NZ$1,667 per month of study available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a)(ii) and (b) above, if the student is invited to apply for a student visa to undertake secondary study on the basis of having a critical purpose for travelling to New Zealand under H5.25.15(c) because they belong to a class of individuals that meets the requirements of H5.30.21(c)(vi), the student must provide evidence they have funds of at least NZ$1,250 per month of study available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Notes: - This evidence may be sighted after the application has been approved in principle. - Compulsory education study is primary, intermediate, or secondary school study from years 1 to 13.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking programmes of study lasting 36 weeks or longer

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students taking programmes of study lasting 36 weeks or longer must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that:

children.label: i
children.text: they have NZ$20,000.00 per year available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses) if they are undertaking tertiary or non-compulsory education study; or

children.label: ii
children.text: they have NZ$17,000.00 per year available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses) if they are undertaking compulsory education study; or

children.label: iii
children.text: if they are citizens of Samoa and Tonga a written guarantee of maintenance from a relative in New Zealand who is either a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the student is invited to apply for a student visa on the basis of having a critical purpose for travelling to New Zealand under H5.25.15(c) because they belong to a class of individuals that meets the requirements of H5.30.21(c)(iv), the student must provide evidence they have funds of at least NZ$1,667 per month of study available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a)(ii) and (b) above, if the student is invited to apply for a student visa to undertake secondary study on the basis of having a critical purpose for travelling to New Zealand under H5.25.15(c) because they belong to a class of individuals that meets the requirements of H5.30.21(c)(vi), they must have NZ$15,000.00 per year available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses).

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maternity health services

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Pregnant applicants for a student visa who are due to give birth while in New Zealand must provide evidence that they:

children.label: a
children.text: have funds of at least NZ$9,000 available to pay for maternity health services; or

children.label: b
children.text: have sponsorship by a person, an organisation or a Government agency which meets generic sponsorship requirements set out at E6.5, to cover maternity health services; or

children.label: c
children.text: have a guarantee of financial undertaking by a third party which covers maternity health services (see U3.20.10); or

children.label: d
children.text: are eligible for publicly-funded maternity health services.

units.heading: Vocational trainees

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Only the following applicants may be granted a student visa as a vocational trainee:

children.label: i
children.text: Air New Zealand trainees that meet the requirements set out at U6.35.5;

children.label: ii
children.text: Nautical students that meet the requirements set out at U9.5;

children.label: iii
children.text: New Zealand Short Term Training Scholarship (STTS) trainees that meet the requirements set out at U9.15.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Applicants who intend to undertake industry training or a modern apprenticeship, not listed at U4.20(a) above, or U9, must apply for a work visa (see WK).

pages.title: Visas for the length of a programme of study
pages.page_title: U6.35 Visas for the length of a programme of study (31/07/2022)

units.heading: Visas for the length of a programme of study

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students may be granted a student visa for the length of their programme of study, regardless of the period for which they have paid their tuition fees, as specified in:

children.label: a
children.text: Provider Direct – Student (see U6.35.1); or

children.label: b
children.text: Aviation students instructions (U6.35.5).

units.heading: Provider Direct – Student

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Students may be granted a student visa for the length of their programme of study if:

children.label: a
children.text: the student has an offer of a place with an education provider with which INZ has a Memorandum of Understanding for the Provider Direct – Student that allows for the grant of visas for the length of programme of study; and

children.label: b
children.text: the education provider supports the grant of a length of programme of study visa; and

children.label: c
children.text: the student application is submitted through the Provider Direct – Student channel.

units.heading: Aviation students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Aviation students may be granted a student visa for the length of their programme of study if:

children.label: i
children.text: the student has an offer of place from an aviation training provider that is: o certified by the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand; and

children.label: b1
children.text: signatory to the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021 (see U3.5 and U5.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: the aviation training provider supports the grant of a length of programme of study visa; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the full first term of tuition fees have been paid.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence of the aviation training provider’s support to grant a length of a programme of study visa must be provided.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a)(iii), evidence of tuition fee payment is not required where the aviation student is an Air New Zealand trainee and provides a guarantee from Air New Zealand.

pages.title: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand
pages.page_title: U3.20 Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand (07/09/2022)

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maintenance while in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that they have sufficient funds available to maintain themselves throughout the period of their stay in New Zealand.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Evidence may include but is not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: a notice of the award of a full scholarship; or

children.label: ii
children.text: a completed Sponsorship for Temporary Entry (INZ 1025) form (see U3.20.5); or

children.label: iii
children.text: a completed Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form, which covers a stay in New Zealand for the length of the visa (see U3.20.10); or

children.label: iv
children.text: funds held by or on behalf of the student (see U3.20.20).

units.heading: Sponsorship

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A sponsor for a student visa application must be an acceptable sponsor (see E6.5) and be either:

children.label: i
children.text: a natural person who is a relative or a friend of the applicant; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an organisation or government agency (an individual must be nominated as the authorised contact).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A sponsor for a fee-paying foreign tertiary student who is applying from within New Zealand must have sponsored that student’s initial student visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Sponsors must satisfy an immigration officer that they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet sponsorship obligations); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are sponsoring.

units.heading: Financial Undertaking

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Before the student’s arrival in New Zealand, a financial undertaking may be provided by a third party.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the third party is a person, they must be a relative or a friend of the applicant.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If the third party is not a person, they must nominate an individual as an authorised contact.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The third party providing the financial undertaking must satisfy an immigration officer they:

children.label: i
children.text: are bona fide (i.e. are genuinely intending to meet their financial obligations as set out on the Financial Undertaking for a Student (INZ 1014) form); and

children.label: ii
children.text: genuinely hold sufficient funds for each student they are supporting.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Where a third party wishes to continue providing a financial undertaking for the student’s subsequent onshore student visa applications, they may do so if they continue to meet (d).

units.heading: Determining whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To determine whether a sponsor or third party providing a financial undertaking is bona fide, immigration officers may consider:

children.label: a
children.text: the relationship between the applicant and the sponsor or third party;

children.label: b
children.text: any previous breaches of financial obligations set out in undertakings;

children.label: c
children.text: the number of student visa applications they are currently supporting;

children.label: d
children.text: the period of time for which funds have been held by the sponsor or third party; and

children.label: e
children.text: the student’s ability to access funds from the sponsor or third party while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds held by or on behalf of the student

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Where funds are held by or on behalf of the student, immigration officers must be satisfied that the funds are from a genuine source and are genuinely available for the purposes of the applicant’s maintenance requirements.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: When determining whether a student has sufficient funds to maintain themselves throughout their stay in New Zealand, immigration officers may consider the period of time for which funds have been held by the student and the student’s ability to access funds while in New Zealand.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking programmes of study lasting less than 36 weeks

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless (b) applies, students taking programmes of study lasting less than 36 weeks must provide evidence they have funds of at least NZ$1,250 per month of study available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the student is invited to apply for a student visa on the basis of having a critical purpose for travelling to New Zealand under H5.25.15(c) because they belong to a class of individuals that meets the requirements of H5.30.21(c)(iii), the student must provide evidence they have funds of at least NZ$1,667 per month of study available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses).

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: This evidence may be sighted after the application has been approved in principle.

units.heading: Funds required for students taking programmes of study lasting 36 weeks or longer

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students taking programmes of study lasting 36 weeks or longer must provide evidence to satisfy an immigration officer that:

children.label: i
children.text: they have NZ$15,000.00 per year available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses); or

children.label: ii
children.text: if they are citizens of Samoa and Tonga a written guarantee of maintenance from a relative in New Zealand who is either a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a)(i) above, if the student is invited to apply for a student visa on the basis of having a critical purpose for travelling to New Zealand under H5.25.15(c) because they belong to a class of individuals that meets the requirements of H5.30.21(c)(vi), they must have NZ$20,000.00 per year available to maintain themselves during their stay in New Zealand (less prepaid living expenses).

units.heading: Sufficient funds for maternity health services

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Pregnant applicants for a student visa who are due to give birth while in New Zealand must provide evidence that they:

children.label: a
children.text: have funds of at least NZ$9,000 available to pay for maternity health services; or

children.label: b
children.text: have sponsorship by a person, an organisation or a Government agency which meets generic sponsorship requirements set out at E6.5, to cover maternity health services; or

children.label: c
children.text: have a guarantee of financial undertaking by a third party which covers maternity health services (see U3.20.10); or

children.label: d
children.text: are eligible for publicly-funded maternity health services.

pages.page_title: U3.10 Tuition fees (31/07/2022)

units.heading: Tuition fees

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide evidence of full payment of tuition fees for one year or one programme, whichever is shorter.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: For applicants living outside New Zealand, evidence of payment is not required until after the application has been approved in principle.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, aviation students may provide evidence of full payment of the first term as set out under U6.35.5.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (a), the following students are not required to provide evidence of tuition fee payment if they can meet the required exemption and provide evidence as below:

blocks.label: table1
blocks.text: | Exemption | Evidence required ; i | Exempt from tuition fees | Confirmation that the programme of study is exempt from fees or that the student is exempt from paying any fees. ; ii | Students participating in a Study Abroad or Non-award scheme under a study abroad partner agreement with a New Zealand Tertiary education institution | Confirmation from the New Zealand tertiary institution that tuition fees are being paid directly to them from a foreign tertiary institution or authorised third party provider on behalf of the foreign tertiary institution. ; iii | Students holding a New Zealand scholarship administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade | Notice of the award of a full New Zealand scholarship. ; iv | Home country government loan approval at a tertiary institution | Evidence that the loan has been applied for and confirmation from the tertiary institution that the fees will be paid directly to them. ; v | Home country government loan approval at a private training establishment (PTE) for study at Bachelor’s degree and above | Evidence that the loan has been applied for and confirmation from the PTE that the fees will be paid directly to them. ; vi | Foreign government-supported student | Meet the all requirements as applicable under U12.

pages.title: Temporary exemption from the requirement to live with a legal guardian in New Zealand
pages.page_title: U7.25 Temporary exemption from the requirement to live with a legal guardian in New Zealand (31/07/2022)

units.heading: Temporary exemption from the requirement to live with a legal guardian in New Zealand

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Students enrolled in school years 1 to 8, and students aged 13 and under who are enrolled in any other provider (see U3.30.5), may apply for a variation of conditions to their student visa to temporarily exempt them from the requirement to live with their legal guardian in New Zealand as set out at U3.30(b).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A variation of conditions will only be granted where an immigration officer is satisfied that an emergency exists that requires the legal guardian to temporarily return to their home country.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: The applicant must provide evidence that:

children.label: i
children.text: an emergency exists that requires the legal guardian to temporarily return to their home country; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the education provider has approved the alternative caregiving arrangements, consistent with its obligations under the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the legal guardian has purchased a return travel ticket.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The variation of conditions may be granted for the period of time required, up to a maximum of four weeks.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Any failure of the legal guardian to return to New Zealand within the approved period may result in the student visa holder becoming liable for deportation (see U7.10).

pages.title: New Zealand scholarship students
pages.page_title: U11 New Zealand scholarship students (13/05/2019)

units.heading: New Zealand scholarship students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A New Zealand scholarship student receives funding from the New Zealand Government through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade under the following schemes:

children.label: i
children.text: New Zealand Scholarships;

children.label: ii
children.text: New Zealand Short Term Training Scholarships;

children.label: iii
children.text: New Zealand Commonwealth Scholarships;

children.label: iv
children.text: New Zealand English Language Training for Officials;

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The objective of the scholarships is for candidates to gain knowledge and skills in specific subject areas that will assist in the development of their home country.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Recipients are required to return to their home country for at least two years after the completion of their scholarship to apply these new skills and knowledge in government, civil society or private business organisations.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (c) above, New Zealand scholarship students who have completed Short Term Training Scholarships or English Language Training for Officials of less than six months in duration are required to return to their home country for at least one year after the completion of their scholarship.

pages.title: Students holding a New Zealand scholarship undertaking employment
pages.page_title: U11.1 Students holding a New Zealand scholarship undertaking employment (13/05/2019)

units.heading: Students holding a New Zealand scholarship undertaking employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: New Zealand scholarship students may be granted conditions on their student visa to allow them to work during the academic year for up to 20 hours per week, during any holidays within the academic year for up to 20 hours per week, and full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period unless they are studying under the following schemes:

children.label: i
children.text: Short Term Training Scholarships; or

children.label: ii
children.text: English Language Training for Officials Scholarships Note: New Zealand scholarship students may also be eligible for full-time work rights during scheduled vacation periods. See U13.15.10

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: With the exception of the schemes listed under (a), New Zealand scholarship students may be granted work visas at the completion of their programmes of study for qualification-related work experience for the minimum time needed to complete practical work requirements. Note: New Zealand scholarship senior medical and pharmacy students may be granted a work visa for their internship/registration year.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: New Zealand scholarship students are not permitted to:

children.label: i
children.text: work in self-employment; or

children.label: ii
children.text: provide commercial sexual services; or

children.label: iii
children.text: act as an operator of a New Zealand business of prostitution; or

children.label: iv
children.text: invest in a business of prostitution (see E7.40).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Any New Zealand scholarship student, or their partner or dependent children, may only be granted a visa for New Zealand in the two-year period following completion of the student's scholarship, with written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (with the exception of a work visa to complete programme of study requirements or, if the applicant is outside New Zealand, a short-term visitor visa).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Despite (d) above, where a New Zealand scholarship student has completed a Short Term Training Scholarships or English Language Training for Officials of less than six months in duration, the New Zealand scholarship student, their partner or dependent children may only be granted a visa for New Zealand in the one year period following completion of their scholarship or training, with the written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (with the exception of a work visa to complete programme of study requirements or, if the applicant is outside New Zealand, a short-term visitor visa). Note: See WF4.5 for work instructions for partners of holders of student visas who are holding a New Zealand scholarship.

pages.title: Dependent children of holders of work visas
pages.page_title: U8.20 Dependent children of holders of work visas (21/02/2022)

units.heading: Dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2); or

children.label: v
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: vi
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or.

children.label: vii
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.15 to A5.25.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted a Migrant Exploitation Protection work visa (MEPV) must be holding a visa based on their relationship to the MEPV holder to be eligible for a further visa under these instructions.

units.heading: Tertiary aged dependent children of people who may be eligible for a 2021 Resident Visa

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Between 1 January 2022 and 31 December 2023, dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand may be granted student visas if they are:

children.label: i
children.text: residing in New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: aged 25 years or under as at 1 January 2022; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the child of a person who held one of the following visa types as at 29 September 2021:

children.label: b1
children.text: Essential Skills Work Visa

children.label: b2
children.text: Approval in Principle

children.label: b3
children.text: Work to Residence (all categories)

children.label: b4
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search

children.label: b5
children.text: Religious Worker

children.label: b6
children.text: Post Study Work Visa

children.label: b7
children.text: Work Visa granted under section 61 of the Immigration Act 2009 (provided the applicant held another eligible visa type within 6 months of being granted a visa under section 61)

children.label: b8
children.text: Special work visa for victims of people trafficking

children.label: b9
children.text: Migrant Exploitation Protection

children.label: b10
children.text: Special work visa for victims of family violence

children.label: b11
children.text: Silver Fern Practical Experience

children.label: b12
children.text: Other Critical Workers visitor visas (provided the visa was granted for a minimum of 6 months)

children.label: b13
children.text: Critical Health Workers visitor visa (provided the visa was granted for a minimum of 6 months)

children.label: b14
children.text: a Critical Purpose Visitor Visa granted under H5.25.15(j) on the basis of holding an Essential Skills or Work to Residence visa; or

children.label: iv
children.text: the child of a person who was granted a visa between 30 September 2021 and 31 July 2022 if it is:

children.label: b1
children.text: an Other Critical Workers visa (provided the visa was granted for a minimum of 6 months); or

children.label: b2
children.text: a Critical Health Workers visa (provided the visa was granted for a minimum of 6 months).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: People defined in (a) above are considered to be domestic students (see U3.35), and can be granted a visa provided they meet the criteria to be considered a dependent child, being that they are single and:

children.label: i
children.text: aged 17 or younger; or

children.label: ii
children.text: aged 18 to 20 with no child(ren) of their own; or

children.label: iii
children.text: aged 21 to 24 with no child(ren) of their own and are totally or substantially reliant on their parent or their parent’s partner for financial support, whether living with them or not; or

children.label: iv
children.text: aged 25 or older and meets instructions to be included as a dependent child aged 25 years or older as per S6.10.10.1

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants may be granted a student visa for the duration of their parent’s visa, as outlined in (a) above, or until 31 December 2023 (whichever is sooner).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Applicants under these instructions do not need to produce evidence of enrolment (unless are required to do so to qualify for working rights under U13.15.1(g)(i)).

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$43,322.76 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$43,322.76 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

pages.title: Part-time study
pages.page_title: U7 Part-time study (26/11/2018)

units.heading: Part-time study

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: People who are not considered to be full-time students (see U6.1.1) may apply for a visitor visa with a variation of conditions to allow study on a part-time basis.

units.heading: Programmes of study lasting up to 9 months

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: People outside New Zealand may apply for and be granted a variation of conditions to allow study on a part-time basis for a maximum of 9 months from the date of their arrival in New Zealand, provided that they are enrolled in a part-time programme of study certified as one that complies with foreign student requirements (see U3.1) and lasts no more than 9 months, and comply with visitor requirements (see V2.1).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: People already in New Zealand may apply for and be granted a visitor visa with a variation of conditions to allow study on a part-time basis for the balance of their stay up to a maximum of 9 months from the date of their arrival.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If study is the main reason for the applicant being in New Zealand, immigration officers must decline any application to undertake part-time programmes of study lasting longer than 9 months, unless the officers are satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the application has special merit that warrants the application being approved, and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant will comply with the conditions of their visa.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Immigration officers must be satisfied that applicants who wish to undertake part-time programmes of study lasting up to 9 months after their date of arrival:

children.label: i
children.text: are enrolled in and have paid the fees for such a programme of study; and

children.label: ii
children.text: are able to satisfy the standard visitor requirements (see V2.1).

units.heading: Students completing their programme of study

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Despite U7.20 above and U6.1.1, a person who is: may be considered to be a full-time student and may be granted a student visa for the remaining duration of their programme of study if they can meet student requirements (see U3.1).

children.label: i
children.text: in their final semester of a programme of study in New Zealand, that is of at least 2 academic years’ duration; or

children.label: ii
children.text: in their final semester of a programme of study in New Zealand, culminating in a New Zealand qualification that would qualify for points under the Skilled Migrant Category (see SM8)

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: To be eligible for a student visa under these instructions, applicants must not previously have been granted a visa under these instructions.

pages.title: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment
pages.page_title: U13.15 Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment (01/01/2022)

units.heading: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment, a student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work during the academic year, and during any scheduled vacations, including within the academic year.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Students aged 16 or 17 years of age enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment must have written permission from their education provider and written parental consent to be granted conditions allowing work.

units.heading: Work conditions for up to twenty hours in any given week

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa holder may be granted with conditions to work for up to 20 hours in any given week during the validity of the visa if the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1) of at least two academic years’ duration; or

children.label: b
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study, culminating in a New Zealand qualification that would qualify for points under the Skilled Migrant Category (see SM8); or

children.label: c
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study of at least one academic year's duration as part of an approved tertiary student exchange scheme (see E11.45); or

children.label: d
children.text: engaged in a full-time programme of study of at least 24 teaching weeks duration; and

children.label: i
children.text: an immigration officer is satisfied that the primary purpose of the programme of study is to develop English language skills; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the student can provide acceptable English language test results, as set out at U13.15.20 (no more than 2 years old at the time the application is lodged); or

children.label: e
children.text: undertaking full-time English language study of at least 14 consecutive weeks’ duration at an education provider that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the NZQA EER quality assurance system; or Note: When assessing eligibility for work rights under (e) for an applicant who holds a current student visa, all consecutive previous English language study undertaken on this and any previous student visa can be counted towards the 14 consecutive week period provided the programme of study the applicant is applying for: - follows directly from their current study and - is with the same provider as that on their current and any previous student visa.

children.label: f
children.text: undertaking a full-time foundation programme that commenced on or before 28 February 2014 and that programme of study is of at least one academic year’s duration at level four or higher on the New Zealand Qualification Framework at an education provider in Canterbury that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system; or

children.label: g
children.text: undertaking tertiary study as the dependent child of a person who may be eligible for a 2021 Resident Visa (as per U8.20.1) and:

children.label: i
children.text: provides evidence that they are undertaking a full-time programme of study for the duration of their visa (as per the definition in U6.1.1); or

children.label: ii
children.text: is aged 18 or older and has been included as a dependent child in an application for a 2021 Resident Visa.

units.heading: Full time work rights during Christmas-New Year vacation period

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation (summer vacation) period provided that the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: studying full-time (see U6.1.1); and

children.label: b
children.text: enrolled in a programme of study that has a minimum duration of at least two semesters during a period of at least eight months.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: For the avoidance of doubt, applicants who are undertaking tertiary study as a domestic student (U8.20.1) are not eligible to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation period

units.heading: Full time work rights during scheduled vacations

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during all scheduled vacations, if the student is undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1); and of at least one academic year’s duration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) where scheduled vacations are more than one third of the programme of study duration for programmes of study offered by tertiary providers other than universities, full-time work rights may not be granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: An academic year means a programme of study of a minimum of 120 credits during a period of at least eight months (minimum of two semesters)

units.heading: Work conditions for masters by research or doctoral students

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder unlimited work rights if:

children.label: a
children.text: the student is undertaking a Masters by Research or Doctoral degree, and

children.label: b
children.text: the qualification is awarded by a New Zealand tertiary institution.

units.heading: Acceptable English language test results

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following English language test results are acceptable:

blocks.label: table1
blocks.text: Test | Minimum score required ; International English Language Testing System (IELTS) - General or Academic Module | Overall score of 5.0 or more ; Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-based Test (TOEFL iBT) | Overall score of 35 or more ; Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic) | Overall score of 36 or more ; B2 First (First Certificate in English) (formerly Cambridge English: First (FCE)) or B2 First for Schools (First Certificate in English) (formerly Cambridge English: First (FCE) for Schools) | Overall score of 154 or more ; Occupational English Test (OET) | Grade C or higher in all four skills (Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking) *

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: * A score of Grade C or higher in all four skills is required for the OET as there is no overall grade for this test.

pages.title: Definition of a 'domestic student'
pages.page_title: U3.35 Definition of a 'domestic student' (01/01/2022)

units.heading: Definition of a 'domestic student'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of student instructions a 'domestic student' means a domestic student as defined in section 10(1) of the Education and Training Act 2020. The Ministry of Education holds a complete list of who is considered to be a domestic student for the purpose of fee payment and enrollment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary schooling domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending primary and secondary schools and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue;

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents;

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents;

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current school year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending primary and secondary schools and are exempt from paying foreign tuition fees:

children.label: a
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is in New Zealand to study under an exchange programme approved by the New Zealand Government.

children.label: b
children.text: Children whose application for a residence class visa is under consideration and who are the dependent children of any person who is a New Zealand citizen or the holder of a residence class visa.

children.label: c
children.text: Children whose application for New Zealand citizenship is under consideration and who are the dependent children of a New Zealand citizen.

children.label: d
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is onshore and the holder of a valid work visa other than those excluded under U8.20.

children.label: e
children.text: Students who have, or dependent children of any person who has, made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009.

children.label: f
children.text: Dependent children of a foreign student enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme in a New Zealand university.

children.label: g
children.text: Dependent children of any person who, during the current calendar year, last ceased to hold a special temporary visa (see H2).

children.label: h
children.text: Students who have entered New Zealand for the purposes of adoption and:

children.label: i
children.text: whose adoption application before the New Zealand Family Court (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student) is supported by the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki and who has a letter from the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki confirming this support; or

children.label: ii
children.text: who are the subject of an Interim Order of Adoption granted by the New Zealand Family Court under section 5 of the Adoption Act 1955 (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student).

children.label: i
children.text: People who are in the custody of the Chief Executive of the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki; pursuant to any of the following orders:

children.label: i
children.text: an order, pursuant to sections 78, 101 or 238(1)(d) of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989, in favour of the Chief Executive of the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 110 of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989, appointing the Chief Executive of the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki as sole guardian; or

children.label: iii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 33 of the Care of Children Act 2004, whereby a child or young person is placed under the Guardianship of the Family Court or the High Court and the Chief Executive of the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki is appointed as agent of the court with power and discretion to place the child.

children.label: j
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand scholarship administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

children.label: k
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a visitor visa granted under V3.115.

children.label: l
children.text: Dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

children.label: m
children.text: Children granted a student visa under U10.5.

children.label: n
children.text: Students who are in New Zealand to study under an exchange scheme approved by the Ministry of Education (see E11.45).

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector (see U5.20) and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions or limited visa in order to undertake a programme of study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue.

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents.

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents.

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current academic year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Despite (d) above, dependent children aged 21 and over of Diplomatic, Consular or Official staff, who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand, may not be eligible for domestic student status and may be required to pay foreign student fees (see H2.1(b)).

children.label: f
children.text: A person who has made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and who is the holder of a valid temporary entry class visa.

children.label: g
children.text: A person who has been recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and whose application for residence is being processed.

children.label: h
children.text: A person who is enrolled at a tertiary education provider for the purpose of participating in industry training funded under the Industry Training Act 1992.

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector and are exempt from paying foreign tuition fees for foreign students:

children.label: a
children.text: Students enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme, in any New Zealand university (see U5.20).

children.label: b
children.text: A person who is in New Zealand to study under a New Zealand Government approved exchange programme at a tertiary education provider.

children.label: c
children.text: Between 1 January 2022 and 31 December 2023, a person who is:

children.label: i
children.text: residing in New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: aged 25 years or under as at 1 January 2022; and

children.label: iii
children.text: is the dependent child (see E4.1.10(d)) of a person who:

children.label: b1
children.text: on 30 September 2021 held one of the visa types specified at U8.20.1(a)(iii) (being the visas that determine eligibility for a 2021 Resident Visa); or

children.label: b2
children.text: was granted a visa type specified at U8.20.1(a)(iv) between 30 September 2021 and 31 July 2022.

pages.title: Dependent children of holders of work visas
pages.page_title: U8.20 Dependent children of holders of work visas (25/09/2023)

units.heading: Dependent children of holders of work visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Silver Fern Job Search Instructions (see WL2); or

children.label: v
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: vi
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or.

children.label: vii
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted a Migrant Exploitation Protection work visa (MEPV) must be holding a visa based on their relationship to the MEPV holder to be eligible for a further visa under these instructions.

units.heading: Tertiary aged dependent children of people who may be eligible for a 2021 Resident Visa

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Between 1 January 2022 and 31 December 2023, dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand may be granted student visas if they are:

children.label: i
children.text: residing in New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: aged 25 years or under as at 1 January 2022; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the child of a person who held one of the following visa types as at 29 September 2021:

children.label: b1
children.text: Essential Skills Work Visa

children.label: b2
children.text: Approval in Principle

children.label: b3
children.text: Work to Residence (all categories)

children.label: b4
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search

children.label: b5
children.text: Religious Worker

children.label: b6
children.text: Post Study Work Visa

children.label: b7
children.text: Work Visa granted under section 61 of the Immigration Act 2009 (provided the applicant held another eligible visa type within 6 months of being granted a visa under section 61)

children.label: b8
children.text: Special work visa for victims of people trafficking

children.label: b9
children.text: Migrant Exploitation Protection

children.label: b10
children.text: Special work visa for victims of family violence

children.label: b11
children.text: Silver Fern Practical Experience

children.label: b12
children.text: Other Critical Workers visitor visas (provided the visa was granted for a minimum of 6 months)

children.label: b13
children.text: Critical Health Workers visitor visa (provided the visa was granted for a minimum of 6 months)

children.label: b14
children.text: a Critical Purpose Visitor Visa granted under H5.25.15(j) on the basis of holding an Essential Skills or Work to Residence visa; or

children.label: iv
children.text: the child of a person who was granted a visa between 30 September 2021 and 31 July 2022 if it is:

children.label: b1
children.text: an Other Critical Workers visa (provided the visa was granted for a minimum of 6 months); or

children.label: b2
children.text: a Critical Health Workers visa (provided the visa was granted for a minimum of 6 months).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: People defined in (a) above are considered to be domestic students (see U3.35), and can be granted a visa provided they meet the criteria to be considered a dependent child, being that they are single and:

children.label: i
children.text: aged 17 or younger; or

children.label: ii
children.text: aged 18 to 20 with no child(ren) of their own; or

children.label: iii
children.text: aged 21 to 24 with no child(ren) of their own and are totally or substantially reliant on their parent or their parent’s partner for financial support, whether living with them or not; or

children.label: iv
children.text: aged 25 or older and meets instructions to be included as a dependent child aged 25 years or older as per S6.10.10.1

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants may be granted a student visa for the duration of their parent’s visa, as outlined in (a) above, or until 31 December 2023 (whichever is sooner).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Applicants under these instructions do not need to produce evidence of enrolment (unless are required to do so to qualify for working rights under U13.15.1(g)(i)).

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$43,322.76 gross per annum and must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of a parent or parents holding an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Essential Skills work visa holder's current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant's parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite (b) above, dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child's visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$43,322.76 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

pages.title: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment
pages.page_title: U13.15 Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment (09/10/2023)

units.heading: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment, a student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work during the academic year, and during any scheduled vacations, including within the academic year.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Students aged 16 or 17 years of age enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment must have written permission from their education provider and written parental consent to be granted conditions allowing work.

units.heading: Work conditions for up to twenty hours in any given week

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa holder may be granted with conditions to work for up to 20 hours in any given week during the validity of the visa if the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1) of at least two academic years’ duration; or

children.label: b
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study, culminating in a New Zealand qualification at level four or higher on the New Zealand Qualification Framework; or Note: Micro-credentials are not qualifications, even if they are listed on the NZQF. They are therefore excluded when assessing eligibility for work rights under (b).

children.label: c
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study of at least one academic year’s duration as part of an approved tertiary student exchange scheme (see E11.45); or

children.label: d
children.text: engaged in a full-time programme of study of at least 24 teaching weeks duration; and

children.label: i
children.text: an immigration officer is satisfied that the primary purpose of the programme of study is to develop English language skills; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the student can provide acceptable English language test results, as set out at U13.15.20 (no more than 2 years old at the time the application is lodged); or

children.label: e
children.text: undertaking full-time English language study of at least 14 consecutive weeks’ duration at an education provider that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the NZQA EER quality assurance system; or Note: When assessing eligibility for work rights under (e) for an applicant who holds a current student visa, all consecutive previous English language study undertaken on this and any previous student visa can be counted towards the 14 consecutive week period provided the programme of study the applicant is applying for: - follows directly from their current study and - is with the same provider as that on their current and any previous student visa.

children.label: f
children.text: undertaking a full-time foundation programme that commenced on or before 28 February 2014 and that programme of study is of at least one academic year’s duration at level four or higher on the New Zealand Qualification Framework at an education provider in Canterbury that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system; or

children.label: g
children.text: undertaking tertiary study as the dependent child of a person who may be eligible for a 2021 Resident Visa (as per U8.20.1) and:

children.label: i
children.text: provides evidence that they are undertaking a full-time programme of study for the duration of their visa (as per the definition in U6.1.1); or

children.label: ii
children.text: is aged 18 or older and has been included as a dependent child in an application for a 2021 Resident Visa.

units.heading: Full time work rights during Christmas-New Year vacation period

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation (summer vacation) period provided that the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: studying full-time (see U6.1.1); and

children.label: b
children.text: enrolled in a programme of study that has a minimum duration of at least two semesters during a period of at least eight months.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: For the avoidance of doubt, applicants who are undertaking tertiary study as a domestic student (U8.20.1) are not eligible to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation period

units.heading: Full time work rights during scheduled vacations

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during all scheduled vacations, if the student is undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1); and of at least one academic year’s duration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) where scheduled vacations are more than one third of the programme of study duration for programmes of study offered by tertiary providers other than universities, full-time work rights may not be granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: An academic year means a programme of study of a minimum of 120 credits during a period of at least eight months (minimum of two semesters)

units.heading: Work conditions for masters by research or doctoral students

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder unlimited work rights if:

children.label: a
children.text: the student is undertaking a Masters by Research or Doctoral degree, and

children.label: b
children.text: the qualification is awarded by a New Zealand tertiary institution.

units.heading: Acceptable English language test results

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following English language test results are acceptable:

blocks.label: table1
blocks.text: Test | Minimum score required ; International English Language Testing System (IELTS) - General or Academic Module | Overall score of 5.0 or more ; Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-based Test (TOEFL iBT) | Overall score of 35 or more ; Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic) | Overall score of 36 or more ; B2 First (First Certificate in English) (formerly Cambridge English: First (FCE)) or B2 First for Schools (First Certificate in English) (formerly Cambridge English: First (FCE) for Schools) | Overall score of 154 or more ; Occupational English Test (OET) | Grade C or higher in all four skills (Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking)*

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: * A score of Grade C or higher in all four skills is required for the OET as there is no overall grade for this test.
