pages.title: Definition of a 'domestic student'
pages.page_title: U3.35 Definition of a 'domestic student' (19/02/2024)

units.heading: Definition of a 'domestic student'

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: For the purposes of student instructions a 'domestic student' means a domestic student as defined in section 10(1) of the Education and Training Act 2020. The Ministry of Education holds a complete list of who is considered to be a domestic student for the purpose of fee payment and enrolment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary schooling domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending primary and secondary schools and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue;

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents;

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents;

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current school year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Members of the armed forces of any country, members of its civilian component, or crew members of any craft transporting such people to New Zealand, while in New Zealand:

children.label: i
children.text: at the request or with consent of the Government of New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: in the ordinary course of the member's duty or employment.

units.heading: Primary and secondary domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending primary and secondary schools and are exempt from paying foreign tuition fees:

children.label: a
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is in New Zealand to study under an exchange programme approved by the New Zealand Government.

children.label: b
children.text: Children whose application for a residence class visa is under consideration and who are the dependent children of any person who is a New Zealand citizen or the holder of a residence class visa.

children.label: c
children.text: Children whose application for New Zealand citizenship is under consideration and who are the dependent children of a New Zealand citizen.

children.label: d
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is onshore and the holder of a valid work visa other than those excluded under U8.20.

children.label: e
children.text: Students who have, or dependent children of any person who has, made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009.

children.label: f
children.text: Dependent children of a foreign student enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme in a New Zealand university.

children.label: g
children.text: Dependent children of any person who, during the current calendar year, last ceased to hold a special temporary visa (see H2).

children.label: h
children.text: Students who have entered New Zealand for the purposes of adoption and:

children.label: i
children.text: whose adoption application before the New Zealand Family Court (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student) is supported by the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki and who has a letter from the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki confirming this support; or

children.label: ii
children.text: who are the subject of an Interim Order of Adoption granted by the New Zealand Family Court under section 5 of the Adoption Act 1955 (where the Final Order will entitle that student to education as a domestic student); or

children.label: iii
children.text: whose adoption application is through an intercountry adoption process under the Hague Convention on Protection of Children and Co-operation in Respect of Intercountry Adoption 1993 as given effect in New Zealand through the Adoption (Intercountry) Act 1997 and:

children.label: b1
children.text: where at least one of the adoptive parents is a New Zealand citizen, or the holder of a New Zealand residence class visa granted under the Immigration Act 2009; and

children.label: b2
children.text: who has a letter from Oranga Tamariki–Ministry for Children confirming support for the adoption.

children.label: i
children.text: People who are in the custody of the Chief Executive of the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki; pursuant to any of the following orders:

children.label: i
children.text: an order, pursuant to sections 78, 101 or 238(1)(d) of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989, in favour of the Chief Executive of the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki; or

children.label: ii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 110 of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989, appointing the Chief Executive of the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki as sole guardian; or

children.label: iii
children.text: an order, pursuant to section 33 of the Care of Children Act 2004, whereby a child or young person is placed under the Guardianship of the Family Court or the High Court and the Chief Executive of the Ministry for Children, Oranga Tamariki is appointed as agent of the court with power and discretion to place the child.

children.label: j
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a New Zealand scholarship administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

children.label: k
children.text: Dependent children of any person who is the holder of a visitor visa granted under V3.115.

children.label: l
children.text: Dependent children of military visa holders, while the military visa holder is in New Zealand.

children.label: m
children.text: Children granted a student visa under U10.5.

children.label: n
children.text: Students who are in New Zealand to study under an exchange scheme approved by the Ministry of Education (see E11.45).

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people are considered to be domestic students for the purpose of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector (see U5.20) and do not require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions or limited visa in order to undertake a programme of study in New Zealand:

children.label: a
children.text: New Zealand citizens, including students from Tokelau, the Cook Islands and Niue.

children.label: b
children.text: New Zealand residents.

children.label: c
children.text: New Zealand permanent residents.

children.label: d
children.text: People who have a letter from the Protocol Division of the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirming that they are entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1968 or the Consular Privileges and Immunities Act 1971 for the current academic year, until the end of the year in which their diplomatic or consular status expires.

children.label: e
children.text: Despite (d) above, dependent children aged 21 and over of Diplomatic, Consular or Official staff, who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand, may not be eligible for domestic student status and may be required to pay foreign student fees (see H2.1(b)).

children.label: f
children.text: A person who has made a claim to be recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and who is the holder of a valid temporary entry class visa.

children.label: g
children.text: A person who has been recognised as a refugee or a protected person in accordance with Part 5 of the Immigration Act 2009, and whose application for residence is being processed.

children.label: h
children.text: A person who is enrolled at a tertiary education provider for the purpose of participating in industry training funded under the Industry Training Act 1992.

units.heading: Tertiary sector domestic students who require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following people require a student visa, interim visa with study conditions, or limited visa in order to undertake study in New Zealand but are considered to be domestic students for the purposes of attending an education provider in the tertiary sector and are exempt from paying foreign tuition fees for foreign students:

children.label: a
children.text: Students enrolled in any Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programme, in any New Zealand university (see U5.20).

children.label: b
children.text: A person who is in New Zealand to study under a New Zealand Government approved exchange programme at a tertiary education provider.

children.label: c
children.text: Between 1 January 2022 and 31 December 2023, a person who is:

children.label: i
children.text: residing in New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: aged 25 years or under as at 1 January 2022; and

children.label: iii
children.text: is the dependent child (see E4.1.10(d)) of a person who:

children.label: b1
children.text: on 30 September 2021 held one of the visa types specified at U8.20.1(a)(iii) (being the visas that determine eligibility for a 2021 Resident Visa); or

children.label: b2
children.text: was granted a visa type specified at U8.20.1(a)(iv) between 30 September 2021 and 31 July 2022.

pages.title: Dependent children of work visa holders
pages.page_title: U8.20 Dependent children of work visa holders (26/06/2024)

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: v
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or

children.label: vi
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, the eligibility of dependent children of Accredited Employer work visa holders for student visas is set out at U8.20.2 below.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted a Migrant Exploitation Protection work visa (MEPV) must be holding a visa based on their relationship to the MEPV holder to be eligible for a further visa under these instructions.

units.heading: Tertiary aged dependent children of people who may be eligible for a 2021 Resident Visa (REVOKED 26/07/2024)

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Between 1 January 2022 and 31 December 2023, dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to undertake tertiary study in New Zealand may be granted student visas if they are:

children.label: i
children.text: residing in New Zealand; and

children.label: ii
children.text: aged 25 years or under as at 1 January 2022; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the child of a person who held one of the following visa types as at 29 September 2021:

children.label: b1
children.text: Essential Skills Work Visa

children.label: b2
children.text: Approval in Principle

children.label: b3
children.text: Work to Residence (all categories)

children.label: b4
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search

children.label: b5
children.text: Religious Worker

children.label: b6
children.text: Post Study Work Visa

children.label: b7
children.text: Work Visa granted under section 61 of the Immigration Act 2009 (provided the applicant held another eligible visa type within 6 months of being granted a visa under section 61)

children.label: b8
children.text: Special work visa for victims of people trafficking

children.label: b9
children.text: Migrant Exploitation Protection

children.label: b10
children.text: Special work visa for victims of family violence

children.label: b11
children.text: Silver Fern Practical Experience

children.label: b12
children.text: Other Critical Workers visitor visas (provided the visa was granted for a minimum of 6 months)

children.label: b13
children.text: Critical Health Workers visitor visa (provided the visa was granted for a minimum of 6 months)

children.label: b14
children.text: a Critical Purpose Visitor Visa granted under H5.25.15(j) on the basis of holding an Essential Skills or Work to Residence visa; or

children.label: iv
children.text: the child of a person who was granted a visa between 30 September 2021 and 31 July 2022 if it is:

children.label: b1
children.text: an Other Critical Workers visa (provided the visa was granted for a minimum of 6 months); or

children.label: b2
children.text: a Critical Health Workers visa (provided the visa was granted for a minimum of 6 months).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: People defined in (a) above are considered to be domestic students (see U3.35), and can be granted a visa provided they meet the criteria to be considered a dependent child, being that they are single and:

children.label: i
children.text: aged 17 or younger; or

children.label: ii
children.text: aged 18 to 20 with no child(ren) of their own; or

children.label: iii
children.text: aged 21 to 24 with no child(ren) of their own and are totally or substantially reliant on their parent or their parent’s partner for financial support, whether living with them or not; or

children.label: iv
children.text: aged 25 or older and meets instructions to be included as a dependent child aged 25 years or older as per S6.10.10.1

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants may be granted a student visa for the duration of their parent’s visa, as outlined in (a) above, or until 31 December 2023 (whichever is sooner).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Applicants under these instructions do not need to produce evidence of enrolment (unless are required to do so to qualify for working rights under U13.15.1(g)(i)).

units.heading: Dependent children of Accredited Employer work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of an Accredited Employer work visa holder may be granted a student visa if their supporting parent is:

children.label: i
children.text: in a role classified as ANZSCO skill level 1, 2 or 3; or

children.label: ii
children.text: paid at or above 1.5x the Skilled Migrant Category median wage (see SR3.20(a)(ii)); or

children.label: iii
children.text: in a role on the Green List and meets the applicable requirements (see Appendix 13); or

children.label: iv
children.text: in acceptable employment under the Transport Sector or Care Sector Work to Residence policies as defined in SR6.10 or SR7.10.

blocks.label: b

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: v
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or

children.label: vi
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4); or

children.label: vii
children.text: seasonal workers under Specific Purpose Instructions (see WS2.1.1(o)).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, the eligibility of dependent children of Accredited Employer work visa holders for student visas is set out at U8.20.2 below.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: f

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, a dependent child of the holder of a Migrant Exploitation Protection work visa (MEPV) may be granted a student visa under these instructions only if, as at the time they apply, the dependent child is in New Zealand on a visa that was granted on the basis of the visa held by the MEPV holder immediately prior to the MEPV holder’s current visa. blocks.text: Despite (a) above, the eligibility of dependent children of Accredited Employer work visa holders for student visas is set out at U8.20.2 below.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, a dependent child of the holder of a Migrant Exploitation Protection work visa (MEPV) may be granted a student visa under these instructions only if, as at the time they apply, the dependent child is in New Zealand on a visa that was granted on the basis of the visa held by the MEPV holder immediately prior to the MEPV holder’s current visa. If granted, the visa’s duration must be for the same period as the MEPV holder’s visa, and will not include multiple entry travel conditions.

units.heading: Dependent children of Accredited Employer work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of an Accredited Employer work visa holder may be granted a student visa if their supporting parent is:

children.label: i
children.text: in a role classified as ANZSCO skill level 1, 2 or 3 (including roles treated at a higher skill level under WA3.16(d) at the Job Check); or

children.label: ii
children.text: paid at or above 1.5x the Skilled Migrant Category median wage (see SR3.20(a)(ii)); or

children.label: iii
children.text: in a role on the Green List and meets the applicable requirements (see Appendix 13); or

children.label: iv
children.text: in acceptable employment under the Transport Sector or Care Sector Work to Residence policies as defined in SR6.10 or SR7.10 with the exception of the requirement to have completed 24 months of work in New Zealand in that occupation.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite the requirement to determine applications for temporary entry in accordance with the instructions in effect at the time an application is made (E7.10(a)(ii)), the exception set out at (a)(iv) above applies to any application that was submitted before 6 October 2024 and as of that date had not been decided.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of an Accredited Employer work visa holder working in a role at ANZSCO skill level 4 or 5 cannot be granted a student visa as a dependent child, unless:

children.label: i
children.text: on 26 June 2024, they held a visa as a dependent child of the Accredited Employer work visa holder; or

children.label: ii
children.text: on 26 June 2024, they had an application in progress for a visa as a dependent child of the Accredited Employer work visa holder and that application was subsequently granted; or

children.label: iii
children.text: their Accredited Employer work visa holder parent is described in (a)(ii) to (iv) above.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: An Accredited Employer work visa holder whose dependent child is applying for a student visa under these instructions must meet the minimum income threshold specified in U8.20.6 below.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Despite (d) above, the minimum income threshold does not apply if the AEWV holder(s) currently meet the previous income threshold in place on 9 March 2025 (as per U8.20(a)), and on 9 March 2025:

children.label: i
children.text: the dependent child held a visa as a dependent child of the AEWV holder, or had applied for a visa as a dependent of the AEWV holder on or before 9 March 2025 and that application has not been completed; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the dependent child’s parent(s) held an AEWV or Essential Skills work visa, or had applied for an Accredited Employer work visa on or before 9 March 2025 that was subsequently granted; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the maximum continuous stay period that applied to their parent on 9 March 2025 has not yet been reached.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold (see U8.20.6 below).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite U8.20.6(a), dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

units.heading: Minimum income threshold

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$55,844 gross per annum.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of the parent or parents holding an Accredited Employer work visa or an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the Accredited Employer work visa or Essential Skills work visa holder’s current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant’s parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child’s visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Accredited Employer work visas or Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$55,844 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a)(i) above, the minimum income threshold does not apply if the parent(s) currently meet the previous income threshold in place on 9 March 2025 (as per U8.20.6 (a)), and on 9 March 2025:

children.label: i
children.text: the dependent child held a visa as a dependent child of the Religious work visa holder, or had applied on or before that date for a visa as a dependent of the Religious work visa holder and that application has not been completed; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the dependent child’s parent(s) held a Religious Work visa, or had applied on or before that date for a Religious Work visa that was subsequently granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

pages.title: Conditions of student visas
pages.page_title: U6.40 Conditions of student visas (11/02/2021)

units.heading: Conditions of student visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All visas for school students must state: 'primary or secondary school studies'.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the student has provided acceptable guarantees of funds and onward travel, the visa must state: ‘Evidence of financial support not required’ and ‘return/onward ticket not required’.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: All student visas must allow multiple journeys.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Two currency dates must be specified on student visas:

children.label: i
children.text: the date on which the visa expires; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the date on which the permission to travel expires.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions allowing the student to work (see U13).

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: If the student is invited to apply for a student visa on the basis of having a critical purpose for travelling to New Zealand under H5.25.15(c), because they belong to a class of individuals that meets the requirements of H5.30.21(c)(iii), then any conditions allowing travel for a critical purpose must be effective no earlier than 1 April 2021.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: See also E3.20 for further student visa conditions

pages.title: Work conditions for secondary school students
pages.page_title: U13.10 Work conditions for secondary school students (30/03/2015)

units.heading: Work conditions for secondary school students

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For secondary school students, a student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work, for up to 20 hours in any given week and full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation period where the student:

children.label: i
children.text: is a full-time student in Years 12 or 13; and

children.label: ii
children.text: has provided written permission from their school; and

children.label: iii
children.text: has written parental consent.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Where a secondary school student is undertaking a student exchange with an Exchange Provider Organisation (EPO), written permission from the EPO is also required (see E11.55.20).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a)(ii), (iii) and (b) above, secondary school students aged 18 years of age or older do not require parental consent or written permission to be granted conditions allowing full-time work during the Christmas-New Year vacation period.

section_listing: U13.10 Work conditions for secondary school students (02/12/2013)

pages.title: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment
pages.page_title: U13.15 Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment (29/07/2024)

units.heading: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment, a student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work during the academic year, and during any scheduled vacations, including within the academic year.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Students aged 16 or 17 years of age enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment must have written permission from their education provider and written parental consent to be granted conditions allowing work.

units.heading: Work conditions for up to twenty hours in any given week

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa holder may be granted with conditions to work for up to 20 hours in any given week during the validity of the visa if the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1) of at least two academic years’ duration; or

children.label: b
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study, culminating in a New Zealand qualification at level four or higher on the New Zealand Qualification Framework; or Note: Micro-credentials are not qualifications, even if they are listed on the NZQF. They are therefore excluded when assessing eligibility for work rights under (b).

children.label: c
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study of at least one academic year’s duration as part of an approved tertiary student exchange scheme (see E11.45); or

children.label: d
children.text: engaged in a full-time programme of study of at least 24 teaching weeks duration; and

children.label: i
children.text: an immigration officer is satisfied that the primary purpose of the programme of study is to develop English language skills; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the student can provide acceptable English language test results, as set out at U13.15.20 (no more than 2 years old at the time the application is lodged); or

children.label: e
children.text: undertaking full-time English language study of at least 14 consecutive weeks’ duration at an education provider that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the NZQA EER quality assurance system; or Note: When assessing eligibility for work rights under (e) for an applicant who holds a current student visa, all consecutive previous English language study undertaken on this and any previous student visa can be counted towards the 14 consecutive week period provided the programme of study the applicant is applying for: - follows directly from their current study and - is with the same provider as that on their current and any previous student visa.

children.label: f
children.text: undertaking a full-time foundation programme that commenced on or before 28 February 2014 and that programme of study is of at least one academic year’s duration at level four or higher on the New Zealand Qualification Framework at an education provider in Canterbury that:

children.label: i
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: ii
children.text: holds Category One status under the New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system; or

units.heading: Full time work rights during Christmas-New Year vacation period

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation (summer vacation) period provided that the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: studying full-time (see U6.1.1); and

children.label: b
children.text: enrolled in a programme of study that has a minimum duration of at least two semesters during a period of at least eight months.

units.heading: Full time work rights during scheduled vacations

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during all scheduled vacations, if the student is undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1); and of at least one academic year’s duration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) where scheduled vacations are more than one third of the programme of study duration for programmes of study offered by tertiary providers other than universities, full-time work rights may not be granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: An academic year means a programme of study of a minimum of 120 credits during a period of at least eight months (minimum of two semesters)

units.heading: Work conditions for masters by research or doctoral students

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder unlimited work rights if:

children.label: a
children.text: the student is undertaking a Masters by Research or Doctoral degree, and

children.label: b
children.text: the qualification is awarded by a New Zealand tertiary institution.

units.heading: Acceptable English language test results

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following English language test results are acceptable:

blocks.label: table1
blocks.text: Test | Minimum score required ; International English Language Testing System (IELTS) - General or Academic Module | Overall score of 5.0 or more ; Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-based Test (TOEFL iBT) | Overall score of 35 or more ; Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic) | Overall score of 36 or more ; B2 First (First Certificate in English) (formerly Cambridge English: First (FCE)) or B2 First for Schools (First Certificate in English) (formerly Cambridge English: First (FCE) for Schools) | Overall score of 154 or more ; Occupational English Test (OET) | Grade C or higher in all four skills (Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking)*

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: * A score of Grade C or higher in all four skills is required for the OET as there is no overall grade for this test.

pages.page_title: U3.40 Students who wish to change their study conditions (13/05/2019)

units.heading: Students who wish to change their study conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A further student visa or variation of conditions, for the purpose of changing programme of study, education provider and/or study location, will only be granted if an immigration officer is satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant meets the student requirements set out at U3.1; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant has not breached their visa conditions as set out at E3.20; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the original student visa would have been granted for the proposed programme of study, education provider, and/or study location; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the applicant remains a bona fide applicant (see E5.1).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Factors that an immigration officer may take into consideration when determining (a)(iii) and (a)(iv) above include, but are not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: the time elapsed since the original visa was granted;

children.label: ii
children.text: whether the level and/or subject area of the proposed programme of study are significantly different from the original programme of study; and

children.label: iii
children.text: any relevant information held about the previous application(s) including advice from the original issuing branch (see E7.1.1).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have received New Zealand Scholarship funding within the two years prior to their application to change programme of study and/or education provider being made, must also provide evidence that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade supports the change of programme of study or education provider and that any scholarship continues.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Applicants who wish to change their programme of study and/or education provider may provide evidence of payment of tuition fees after the application has been approved in principle.

pages.title: Students holding a New Zealand scholarship undertaking employment
pages.page_title: U11.1 Students holding a New Zealand scholarship undertaking employment (10/12/2022)

units.heading: Students holding a New Zealand scholarship undertaking employment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: New Zealand scholarship students may be granted conditions on their student visa to allow them to work during the academic year for up to 20 hours per week, during any holidays within the academic year for up to 20 hours per week, and full-time during the Christmas-New Year holiday period unless they are studying under the following schemes:

children.label: i
children.text: Short Term Training Scholarships; or

children.label: ii
children.text: English Language Training for Officials Scholarships Note: New Zealand scholarship students may also be eligible for full-time work rights during scheduled vacation periods. See U13.15.10

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: With the exception of the schemes listed under (a), New Zealand scholarship students may be granted work visas at the completion of their programmes of study for qualification-related work experience for the minimum time needed to complete practical work requirements. Note: New Zealand scholarship senior medical and pharmacy students may be granted a work visa for their internship/registration year.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: New Zealand scholarship students are not permitted to:

children.label: i
children.text: work in self-employment; or

children.label: ii
children.text: provide commercial sexual services; or

children.label: iii
children.text: act as an operator of a New Zealand business of prostitution; or

children.label: iv
children.text: invest in a business of prostitution (see E7.40).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Any New Zealand scholarship student, or their partner or dependent children, may only be granted a visa for New Zealand in the two-year period following completion of the student's scholarship, with written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or Education New Zealand (with the exception of a work visa to complete programme of study requirements or, if the applicant is outside New Zealand, a short-term visitor visa).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Despite (d) above, where a New Zealand scholarship student has completed a Short Term Training Scholarships or English Language Training for Officials of twelve months or less in duration, the New Zealand scholarship student, their partner or dependent children may only be granted a visa for New Zealand in the one year period following completion of their scholarship or training, with the written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or Education New Zealand (with the exception of a work visa to complete programme of study requirements or, if the applicant is outside New Zealand, a short-term visitor visa). Note: See WF4.5 for work instructions for partners of holders of student visas who are holding a New Zealand scholarship.

units.heading: Application and evidence

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Applicants must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: a completed student visa application form and fee; and

children.label: ii
children.text: evidence that they have a minimum of $1,250 per month in funds available to maintain themselves during their intended stay in New Zealand; and

children.label: iii
children.text: confirmation from their education provider that they have submitted all required material for the assessment of their qualification.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If an applicant is unable to obtain confirmation from their education provider required for (a)(iii) (for example if the education provider has ceased to operate), confirmation from NZQA that they have submitted all required material for assessment can be provided instead.

pages.page_title: U16.5 Currency and conditions (09/12/2016)

units.heading: Currency and conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Despite U13.15, a student visa holder may be granted under these instructions with conditions allowing work for up to 20 hours in any given week during the validity of the visa.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Visas can be granted up to a maximum period of six months with multiple entry travel conditions.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where the education provider is continuing to operate the original programme of study, education provider and location must be specified on the visa.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: In the event the education provider has ceased to operate, the visa can be granted without a specified programme of study, education provider, or location.

units.heading: Students who wish to change their study conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A further student visa or variation of conditions, for the purpose of changing programme of study, education provider and/or study location, will only be granted if an immigration officer is satisfied that:

children.label: i

children.label: ii

children.label: iii

children.label: iii

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have received New Zealand Scholarship funding within the two years prior to their application to change programme of study and/or education provider being made, must also provide evidence that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade supports the change of programme of study or education provider and that any scholarship continues.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Applicants who wish to change their programme of study and/or education provider may provide evidence of payment of tuition fees after the application has been approved in principle.

pages.page_title: U8.20 Dependent children of work visa holders (08/09/2025)

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: v
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or

children.label: vi
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4); or

children.label: vii
children.text: seasonal workers under Specific Purpose Instructions (see WS2.1.1(m)).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, the eligibility of dependent children of Accredited Employer work visa holders and Specific Purpose work visa holders under the NOL pathway (see WS2.1.1(o)) for student visas is set out at U8.20.2 below.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, a dependent child of the holder of a Migrant Exploitation Protection work visa (MEPV) may be granted a student visa under these instructions only if, as at the time they apply, the dependent child is in New Zealand on a visa that was granted on the basis of the visa held by the MEPV holder immediately prior to the MEPV holder’s current visa. If granted, the visa’s duration must be for the same period as the MEPV holder’s visa, and will not include multiple entry travel conditions.

units.heading: Dependent children of Accredited Employer work visa holders and certain Specific Purpose work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of an Accredited Employer work visa holder or a Specific Purpose work visa holder under the NOL pathway (see WS2.1.1(o)) may be granted a student visa if their supporting parent is:

children.label: i
children.text: in a role classified as ANZSCO skill level 1, 2 or 3 (including roles treated at a higher skill level under WA3.16(d) at the Job Check); or

children.label: ii
children.text: in a role classified as NOL skill level 1, 2 or 3 and listed at Appendix 20; or

children.label: iii
children.text: paid at or above 1.5x the Skilled Migrant Category median wage (see SR3.20(a)(ii)); or

children.label: iv
children.text: in a role on the Green List and meets the applicable requirements (see Appendix 13); or

children.label: v
children.text: in acceptable employment under the Transport Sector or Care Sector Work to Residence policies as defined in SR6.10 or SR7.10 with the exception of the requirement to have completed 24 months of work in New Zealand in that occupation.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite the requirement to determine applications for temporary entry in accordance with the instructions in effect at the time an application is made (E7.10(a)(ii)), the exception set out at (a)(v) above applies to any application that was submitted before 6 October 2024 and as of that date had not been decided.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of an Accredited Employer work visa holder working in a role at ANZSCO skill level 4 or 5 cannot be granted a student visa as a dependent child, unless:

children.label: i
children.text: on 26 June 2024, they held a visa as a dependent child of the Accredited Employer work visa holder; or

children.label: ii
children.text: on 26 June 2024, they had an application in progress for a visa as a dependent child of the Accredited Employer work visa holder and that application was subsequently granted; or

children.label: iii
children.text: their Accredited Employer work visa holder parent is described in (a)(iii) to (v) above.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: An Accredited Employer work visa holder or a Specific Purpose work visa holder under the NOL pathway (see WS2.1.1(o)) whose dependent child is applying for a student visa under these instructions must meet the minimum income threshold specified in U8.20.6 below.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Despite (d) above, the minimum income threshold does not apply if the supporting work visa holder(s) currently meet the previous income threshold in place on 9 March 2025 (as per U8.20(a)), and on 9 March 2025:

children.label: i
children.text: the dependent child held a visa as a dependent child of the AEWV holder, or had applied for a visa as a dependent of the AEWV holder on or before 9 March 2025 and that application has not been completed; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the dependent child’s parent(s) held an AEWV or Essential Skills work visa, or had applied for an Accredited Employer work visa on or before 9 March 2025 that was subsequently granted; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the maximum continuous stay period that applied to their parent on 9 March 2025 has not yet been reached.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold (see U8.20.6 below).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite U8.20.6(a), dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

units.heading: Minimum income threshold

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$55,844 gross per annum.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of the parent or parents holding an Accredited Employer work visa, Specific Purpose work visa holder under the NOL pathway (see WS2.1.1(o)) or an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the supporting work visa holder’s current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant’s parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child’s visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Accredited Employer work visas, Specific Purpose work visas under the NOL pathway (see WS2.1.1(o)) or Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$55,844 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a)(i) above, the minimum income threshold does not apply if the parent(s) currently meet the previous income threshold in place on 9 March 2025 (as per U8.20.6 (a)), and on 9 March 2025:

children.label: i
children.text: the dependent child held a visa as a dependent child of the Religious work visa holder, or had applied on or before that date for a visa as a dependent of the Religious work visa holder and that application has not been completed; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the dependent child’s parent(s) held a Religious Work visa, or had applied on or before that date for a Religious Work visa that was subsequently granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Requirements to be granted a pathway student visa

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To be granted a pathway student visa, an applicant must:

children.label: a
children.text: be offered an eligible study pathway from a qualifying provider(s) (U14.20); and

children.label: b
children.text: meet the general requirements to be granted a student visa as set out at U3.1; and

children.label: c
children.text: meet the additional evidential requirements for pathway student visa set out at U14.5.1.

units.heading: Evidence of meeting requirements

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: In addition to meeting the general requirements to be granted a student visa as set out at U3.1, when applying for a pathway student visa an applicant must provide:

children.label: i
children.text: where there is more than one education provider, a joint letter of support from pathway education providers; and

children.label: ii
children.text: an offer of place (or joint offer) for each programme of study that meets the requirements set out at U3.5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence that tuition fee requirements, as set out at U3.10, for either the first programme of study or first year of study (whichever is shorter) have been met and satisfy an immigration officer that they have the ability to fund any remaining balance of the first programme of study and subsequent programmes of study on the intended pathway; and

children.label: iv
children.text: evidence that the maintenance funds requirements set out in U3.20 for the first year of study on the intended pathway have been met and satisfy an immigration officer that they have the ability to fund any remaining balance of the first programme of study and subsequent programmes of study on the intended pathway.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a)(ii), second and subsequent offers of place for a pathway can be conditional on meeting pre-requisite programme of study entry criteria.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Pathway student visa applicants from a country with a student visa decline rate of more than 20 per cent who intend a study pathway commencing with an English language programme of study and culminating in a qualification at Levels 5 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework must:

children.label: i
children.text: submit an International English Language Testing System test (IELTS) (or equivalent internationally recognised proficiency test) at the time of application; and

children.label: ii
children.text: demonstrate that they only require an improvement of 0.5 of an IELTS overall band score (or equivalent) to meet the English language prerequisite for entry into the intended level 5 to 8 programme of study.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The student visa decline rate for a country is based on statistics, generated over a calendar year (12 months), by Immigration New Zealand. The decline rate and the name of the country are published on the INZ website. For the purpose of this instruction, the internationally recognised English language tests and corresponding IELTS equivalent test scores set out on the INZ website are considered acceptable.

units.heading: Currency and conditions of pathway student visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For the purposes of the pathway student visa pilot, a visa can be granted up to a maximum of five years.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A visa may be granted to expire no more than three months beyond completion of the final pathway programme of study within the maximum currency of five years.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Work conditions for the duration of the pathway student visa will only be granted where the first programme of study meets the requirements as set out at U13.1, U13.10 or U13.15.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If the second or subsequent programme of study meets the requirements set out at U13.1, U13.10 or U13.15, a variation of conditions is required in order to be granted work conditions.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Where (d) applies, a Variation of Conditions or Variation of Travel Conditions (INZ 1020) application form must be completed and submitted with the required fee.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: The holder must make satisfactory progress on the pathway by:

children.label: i
children.text: meeting the conditional pre-requisites for enrolment into a second or subsequent programme of study (E3.20(d)); and

children.label: ii
children.text: commencing the second or subsequent programme of study on a pathway within a 16 week period of completing their earlier programme of study.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Where a first time student has submitted an English language test result as set out at U14.5.1 (c) and been granted a pathway student visa to undertake an English language programme of study culminating in a qualification at Levels 5 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework, the English Language programme of study must be completed within a 20 week period.

units.heading: Changing and complying with pathway student visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: If a pathway student visa holder wishes to move to a different education provider or lower level programme of study than those specified in their visa conditions, they must apply for a new student visa and meet the requirements set out at U3.40.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A variation of conditions, for the purpose of changing a programme of study at the same education provider will only be granted if an immigration officer is satisfied that:

children.label: i
children.text: the applicant meets the student requirements set out at U3.1; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the applicant has not breached their visa conditions as set out at E3.20; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the original student visa would have been granted for the proposed programme of study; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the proposed programme of study is at the same or higher level on the New Zealand Qualification Framework as the original programme of study; and

children.label: v
children.text: the applicant remains a bona fide applicant (see E5.1).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Factors that an immigration officer may take into consideration when determining (b)(iii) and (b)(iv) above include, but are not limited to:

children.label: i
children.text: the time elapsed since the original visa was granted; and

children.label: ii
children.text: whether the level and/or subject area of the proposed programme of study are significantly different from the original programme of study; and

children.label: iii
children.text: any relevant information held about the previous application(s) including advice from the original issuing branch (see E7.1.1).

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Students who have received New Zealand scholarship funding within the two years prior to their application to change programme of study must also provide evidence that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade supports the change of programme of study and that any scholarship continues.

units.heading: Breaching visa conditions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A pathway student visa holder will be considered to be in breach of visa conditions where:

children.label: i
children.text: they fail to meet conditional pre-requisites for enrolment into a second or subsequent programme of study (E3.20(d)); or

children.label: ii
children.text: the time between the completion of one programme of study and the start of a second or subsequent programme of study on a pathway exceeds 16 weeks; or

children.label: iii
children.text: they have submitted an English language test result as set out at U14.5.1(c) and their intended pathway is an English language programme of study culminating in a qualification at Levels 5 to 8 on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework and the English Language programme of study is not completed within a 20 week period.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A breach of visa conditions is "sufficient reason" to make a temporary entry class visa holder liable for deportation, and may result in the issue of a Deportation Liability Notice (E3.60).

pages.title: Provider requirements
pages.page_title: U14.20 Provider requirements (31/07/2022)

units.heading: Provider requirements
Pathway pilot entry criteria

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: To qualify for entry to the Pathway student visa pilot, an education provider must:

children.label: a
children.text: be invited by Immigration New Zealand to be a pilot participant; and

children.label: b
children.text: have signed the Pathway Student Visas - Pilot Participation Declaration agreeing to the requirements as set out at U14.20.10; and

children.label: c
children.text: be either a school, a university or hold a Category One or Two rating under New Zealand Qualifications Authority’s (NZQA) External Evaluation and Review framework; and

children.label: d
children.text: have a minimum 90% student visa application approval rate over the 2014/15 financial year or 2016 calendar year (12 month period); and

children.label: e
children.text: comply with the legislative requirements as set out under the Education and Training Act 2020 to offer programmes of study to foreign students (U5.5 to U5.20); and

children.label: f
children.text: be a signatory to the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021.

units.heading: Eligible pathways

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All pathways must demonstrate academic progression to the second or subsequent programme of study building on the previous study.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All consecutive programmes of study that demonstrate progression are eligible to be included in the pilot with the exception of the following pathways:

children.label: i
children.text: any English language programme of study culminating in any tertiary sector Level 1–4 Certificate on the New Zealand Qualifications Framework (NZQF); and

children.label: ii
children.text: all pathways within and between tertiary sector NZQF Levels 1–4 Certificates; and

children.label: iii
children.text: secondary school culminating in any tertiary sector NZQF Levels 1–4 Certificates.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Breaks between consecutive programmes of study must not exceed 16 weeks

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Only education providers who meet the requirements set out under U14.20.1 can offer a joint pathway in conjunction with one another.

units.heading: Formal agreement between qualifying education providers

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: To ensure a student’s pastoral care needs are met, qualifying education providers who intend offering an education pathway in conjunction with one another must enter into a formal agreement.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The formal agreement must include and set out the following processes and arrangements:

children.label: i
children.text: the application process; and

children.label: ii
children.text: pastoral care obligations; and

children.label: iii
children.text: handover arrangements in transition periods between programmes of study/education providers; and

children.label: iv
children.text: the process if a significant gap exists between completion of a programme of study and the start of a second or subsequent programme of study or in the event some papers are failed and cannot be repeated within a 16 week period; and

children.label: v
children.text: the process if conditional entry requirements for second or subsequent programmes of study are not met; and

children.label: vi
children.text: the process if the student fails to attend and/or make satisfactory progress (E3.20(d)); and

children.label: vii
children.text: the process if the student wishes to leave intended pathway; and

children.label: viii
children.text: the obligation to notify INZ where a pathway student:

children.label: b1
children.text: requires additional time to complete a programme of study and time required is likely to exceed 16 weeks; or

children.label: b2
children.text: fails to meet the conditional entry requirements for a second or subsequent programme of study; or

children.label: b3
children.text: fails to enrol for a subsequent programme of study; or

children.label: b4
children.text: fails to attend and/or make satisfactory progress; or

children.label: b5
children.text: has their enrolment in a programme of study terminated.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Where an education pathway is offered by a single qualifying education provider, the formal agreement processes set out at (b) must be met.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: The signed formal agreement does not have to be submitted with a pathway student visa application, however it must be made available to INZ if requested.

units.heading: Non-compliance with formal agreement requirements or when under active investigation by Immigration New Zealand

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: Where non-compliance, other than of a minor nature, with any of the matters agreed to in the Pathway Student Visas - Pilot Participation Declaration, or where the pathway education provider is under active investigation by INZ for offences committed under part 10 of the Immigration Act 2009 the following process may occur:

children.label: a
children.text: INZ will suspend the processing of any student visa applications related to an existing pathway agreement immediately.

children.label: b
children.text: The non-compliant pathway education provider(s) will be advised in writing of the suspension and will be sent a report detailing the non-compliance, and will be given 30 days to remedy the non-compliance.

children.label: c
children.text: Resolution (or satisfactory progress towards resolution) of the non-compliance to the satisfaction of INZ within the 30 day period will see the suspension lifted and processing of related pathway student visa applications will resume.

children.label: d
children.text: Where a resolution is reached, the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment or the New Zealand Qualifications Authority may conduct an investigation three to six months later to assess the effectiveness of the remediation undertaken. If the remediation is deemed inadequate or ineffective, the suspension can be re-imposed or the provider may be removed from the pathways pilot and current pathway student visa holders may become liable for deportation.

children.label: e
children.text: If INZ is not satisfied that the non-compliance has been addressed or satisfactory progress has been made towards resolution within the 30 day period, the suspension of related student visa processing will continue (until resolution occurs).

children.label: f
children.text: Failure to address or make satisfactory progress towards resolving the non-compliance may result in removal from the pathways pilot, and current student visa holders becoming liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: INZ may rely on the advice of the Ministry of Education and/or the New Zealand Qualifications Authority in determining whether resolution has been reached or satisfactory progress has been made towards resolution.
