pages.title: Dependent children of work visa holders
pages.page_title: U8.20 Dependent children of work visa holders (09/03/2026)

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: v
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or

children.label: vi
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4); or

children.label: vii
children.text: seasonal workers under Specific Purpose Instructions; or

children.label: viii
children.text: seasonal workers under seasonal AEWV pathways (see WA1.10(a)(ii)).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, the eligibility of dependent children of Accredited Employer work visa holders and Specific Purpose work visa holders under the NOL subcategory (see WS2.1.1(o) – instructions effective 8 September 2025) for student visas is set out at U8.20.2 below.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, a dependent child of the holder of a Migrant Exploitation Protection work visa (MEPV) may be granted a student visa under these instructions only if, as at the time they apply, the dependent child is in New Zealand on a visa that was granted on the basis of the visa held by the MEPV holder immediately prior to the MEPV holder’s current visa. If granted, the visa’s duration must be for the same period as the MEPV holder’s visa, and will not include multiple entry travel conditions.

units.heading: Dependent children of Accredited Employer work visa holders and certain Specific Purpose work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of an Accredited Employer work visa holder or a Specific Purpose work visa holder under the NOL subcategory (see WS2.1.1(o) – instructions effective 8 September 2025) may be granted a student visa if their supporting parent is:

children.label: i
children.text: in a role classified as ANZSCO skill level 1, 2 or 3 (including roles treated at a higher skill level under WA3.16(d) at the Job Check); or

children.label: ii
children.text: in a role classified as NOL skill level 1, 2 or 3 and listed at Appendix 20; or

children.label: iii
children.text: paid at or above 1.5x the Skilled Migrant Category median wage (see SR3.20(a)(ii)); or

children.label: iv
children.text: in a role on the Green List and meets the applicable requirements (see Appendix 13); or

children.label: v
children.text: in acceptable employment under the Transport Sector or Care Sector Work to Residence policies as defined in SR6.10 or SR7.10 with the exception of the requirement to have completed 24 months of work in New Zealand in that occupation.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite the requirement to determine applications for temporary entry in accordance with the instructions in effect at the time an application is made (E7.10(a)(ii)), the exception set out at (a)(v) above applies to any application that was submitted before 6 October 2024 and as of that date had not been decided.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of an Accredited Employer work visa holder working in a role at ANZSCO skill level 4 or 5 cannot be granted a student visa as a dependent child, unless:

children.label: i
children.text: on 26 June 2024, they held a visa as a dependent child of the Accredited Employer work visa holder; or

children.label: ii
children.text: on 26 June 2024, they had an application in progress for a visa as a dependent child of the Accredited Employer work visa holder and that application was subsequently granted; or

children.label: iii
children.text: their Accredited Employer work visa holder parent is described in (a)(iii) to (v) above.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: An Accredited Employer work visa holder or a Specific Purpose work visa holder under the NOL subcategory (see WS2.1.1(o) – instructions effective 8 September 2025) whose dependent child is applying for a student visa under these instructions must meet the minimum income threshold specified in U8.20.6 below.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Despite (d) above, the minimum income threshold does not apply if the supporting work visa holder(s) currently meet the previous income threshold in place on 9 March 2025 (as per U8.20(a)), and on 9 March 2025:

children.label: i
children.text: the dependent child held a visa as a dependent child of the AEWV holder, or had applied for a visa as a dependent of the AEWV holder on or before 9 March 2025 and that application has not been completed; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the dependent child’s parent(s) held an AEWV or Essential Skills work visa, or had applied for an Accredited Employer work visa on or before 9 March 2025 that was subsequently granted; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the maximum continuous stay period that applied to their parent on 9 March 2025 has not yet been reached.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold (see U8.20.6 below).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite U8.20.6(a), dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

units.heading: Minimum income threshold

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$55,240 gross per annum.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of the parent or parents holding an Accredited Employer work visa, Specific Purpose work visa holder under the NOL subcategory (see WS2.1.1(o) – instructions effective 8 September 2025) or an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the supporting work visa holder’s current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant’s parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child’s visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Accredited Employer work visas, or Specific Purpose work visas under the NOL subcategory (see WS2.1.1(o) – instructions effective 8 September 2025) or Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$55,240 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a)(i) above, the minimum income threshold does not apply if the parent(s) currently meet the previous income threshold in place on 9 March 2025 (as per U8.20.6 (a)), and on 9 March 2025:

children.label: i
children.text: the dependent child held a visa as a dependent child of the Religious work visa holder, or had applied on or before that date for a visa as a dependent of the Religious work visa holder and that application has not been completed; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the dependent child’s parent(s) held a Religious Work visa, or had applied on or before that date for a Religious Work visa that was subsequently granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

pages.title: Summary

units.heading: Summary

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless otherwise specified, to be granted a student visa to attend a programme of study of more than three months, applicants must:

children.label: i
children.text: have an offer of a place or, if returning to continue a programme of study, a confirmation of enrolment in an approved programme of study with an education provider in New Zealand that meets student visa requirements (see U3.5, U3.10, and U5.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: be exempted from or have paid tuition fees; and

children.label: iii
children.text: if aged under 18, meet accommodation requirements (see U3.15); and

children.label: iv
children.text: have fulfilled the purpose and met the conditions for any previous or current temporary visas held as set out in E3.15 and E3.20; and

children.label: v
children.text: meet the conditions set out in E3.20; and

children.label: vi
children.text: not be the holder of a current visitor visa granted under Guardians accompanying students to New Zealand instructions (see V3.100); and

children.label: vii
children.text: hold insurance (see U3.45), unless they are a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) student or a student holding a New Zealand scholarship administered through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All applicants must meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for:

children.label: i
children.text: lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa as set out at E4; and

children.label: ii
children.text: bona fide applicants as set out at E5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: health and character as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Applicants who have not completed, or will not be completing the programme of study endorsed on their student visa and who wish to change their programme of study and/or education provider must:

children.label: i
children.text: meet requirements (a) and (b) above; and

children.label: ii
children.text: meet the requirements set out at U3.40.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Applicants who are progressing to further study, for example a student in Year 13 who is progressing to tertiary studies, will not need to meet U3.40.

pages.title: Status of education providers and programmes
pages.page_title: U5.1 Status of education providers and programmes (31/07/2022)

units.heading: Status of education providers and programmes

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: All education providers must certify in their offers of places to foreign students (see U3.5) that the programme of study or training scheme offered complies with foreign student requirements for different kinds of education providers (see U5.5 - U5.20).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All education providers offering places to foreign students must be signatories to the Education (Pastoral Care of Tertiary and International Learners) Code of Practice 2021.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Any queries on the status of programmes or training schemes offered by private training establishments should be referred to the Service Delivery Unit, Quality Assurance Division, New Zealand Qualifications Authority (NZQA), PO Box 160, Wellington.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Students will not be granted a student visa to undertake a programme of study or training scheme offered at an education provider that holds a Category Four status under the NZQA’s External Evaluation Review (EER) quality assurance system.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Immigration New Zealand (INZ) may suspend the processing of applications for student visas for study at an education provider where at least one of the following applies:

children.label: i
children.text: the offered programme of study or training scheme does not comply with foreign student requirements as set out in U5.5 to U5.20;

children.label: ii
children.text: the education provider is not complying with its obligations under the Immigration Act, immigration regulations, or immigration instructions;

children.label: iii
children.text: INZ has been informed by education agencies that the education provider is not complying with its obligations under the Education Act and education regulations.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Before a decision is made to suspend the processing of student visas, the following will be taken into account:

children.label: i
children.text: evidence of the non-compliance; and

children.label: ii
children.text: reasons for the non-compliance; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the duration, frequency, and severity of the non-compliance.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: INZ may resume the processing of student visas if it is satisfied that the education provider is complying with its obligations.

pages.title: Currency of student visas
pages.page_title: U6.30 Currency of student visas (02/12/2013)

units.heading: Currency of student visas

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Student visas may be granted for the following periods:

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: for holders of full scholarships and fees scholarships who do not meet the requirements under U6.35, the period of the student's award (up to a maximum of 4 years); and

children.label: i
children.text: for fee-paying foreign students who do not meet the requirements under U6.35, the period for which the student has paid the tuition fees (up to a maximum of 4 years); and

children.label: ii
children.text: for fee-paying foreign students and full scholarship students, who meet the requirements under U6.35, for the length of their programme of study, regardless of the period for which they have paid tuition fees (up to a maximum of 4 years).

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If the programme of study is based on the New Zealand academic year, the visa may be granted for the academic year for which the student has paid, to expire on 31 March of the following year.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If the programme of study lasts for less than one year, or can begin at any time during the year, the visa may be granted to expire no more than one month after the period for which the student has paid.

pages.title: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment
pages.page_title: U13.15 Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment (03/11/2025)

units.heading: Work conditions for students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: For students enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment, a student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work during the academic year, and during any scheduled vacations, including within the academic year.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Students aged 16 or 17 years of age enrolled at a tertiary institution or private training establishment must have written permission from their education provider and written parental consent to be granted conditions allowing work.

units.heading: Work conditions for up to twenty-five hours in any given week

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa holder may be granted with conditions to work for up to 25 hours in any given week during the validity of the visa if the student is:

children.label: i
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1) of at least two academic years’ duration; or

children.label: ii
children.text: undertaking a full-time programme of study, culminating in a New Zealand qualification at level four or higher on the New Zealand Qualification Framework; or Note: Micro-credentials are not qualifications, even if they are listed on the NZQCF. They are therefore excluded when assessing eligibility for work rights under (b).

children.label: iii
children.text: undertaking full-time study as part of an approved tertiary student exchange scheme (see E11.45); or

children.label: iv
children.text: engaged in a full-time programme of study of at least 24 teaching weeks duration; and

children.label: b1
children.text: an immigration officer is satisfied that the primary purpose of the programme of study is to develop English language skills; and

children.label: b2
children.text: the student can provide acceptable English language test results, as set out at U13.15.20 (no more than 2 years old at the time the application is lodged); or

children.label: v
children.text: undertaking full-time English language study of at least 14 consecutive weeks’ duration at an education provider that:

children.label: b1
children.text: is a university; or

children.label: b2
children.text: holds Category One status under the NZQA EER quality assurance system; or Note: When assessing eligibility for work rights under (e) for an applicant who holds a current student visa, all consecutive previous English language study undertaken on this and any previous student visa can be counted towards the 14 consecutive week period provided the programme of study the applicant is applying for: - follows directly from their current study and - is with the same provider as that on their current and any previous student visa.

children.label: vi
children.text: undertaking a full-time Study Abroad programme under a study abroad partner agreement with a New Zealand Tertiary education institution.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite E7.10(a)(ii), immigration officers may apply these instructions to any eligible student visa application that was submitted before 3 November 2025 and as of that date had not been decided.

units.heading: Full time work rights during Christmas-New Year vacation period

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during the Christmas-New Year vacation (summer vacation) period provided that the student is:

children.label: a
children.text: studying full-time (see U6.1.1); and

children.label: b
children.text: enrolled in a programme of study that has a minimum duration of at least two semesters during a period of at least eight months.

units.heading: Full time work rights during scheduled vacations

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder to work full-time during all scheduled vacations, if the student is undertaking a full-time programme of study (see U6.1.1); and of at least one academic year’s duration.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) where scheduled vacations are more than one third of the programme of study duration for programmes of study offered by tertiary providers other than universities, full-time work rights may not be granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: An academic year means a programme of study of a minimum of 120 credits during a period of at least eight months (minimum of two semesters)

units.heading: Work conditions for masters by research or doctoral students

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: A student visa may be granted with conditions to allow the holder unlimited work rights if:

children.label: a
children.text: the student is undertaking a Masters by Research or Doctoral degree, and

children.label: b
children.text: the qualification is awarded by a New Zealand tertiary institution.

units.heading: Acceptable English language test results

blocks.label: p1
blocks.text: The following English language test results are acceptable:

blocks.label: table1
blocks.text: Test | Minimum score required ; International English Language Testing System (IELTS) - General or Academic Module | Overall score of 5.0 or more ; Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-based Test (TOEFL iBT) | Overall score of 35 or more ; Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic) | Overall score of 36 or more ; B2 First (First Certificate in English) (formerly Cambridge English: First (FCE)) or B2 First for Schools (First Certificate in English) (formerly Cambridge English: First (FCE) for Schools) | Overall score of 154 or more ; Occupational English Test (OET) | Grade C or higher in all four skills (Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking)*

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: * A score of Grade C or higher in all four skills is required for the OET as there is no overall grade for this test.

pages.title: Summary

units.heading: Summary

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Unless otherwise specified, to be granted a student visa to attend a programme of study of more than three months, applicants must:

children.label: i
children.text: have an offer of a place or, if returning to continue a programme of study, a confirmation of enrolment in an approved programme of study with an education provider in New Zealand that meets student visa requirements (see U3.5, U3.10, and U5.1); and

children.label: ii
children.text: be exempted from or have paid tuition fees; and

children.label: iii
children.text: if aged under 18, meet accommodation requirements (see U3.15); and

children.label: iv
children.text: have fulfilled the purpose and met the conditions for any previous or current temporary visas held as set out in E3.15 and E3.20; and

children.label: v
children.text: meet the conditions set out in E3.20; and

children.label: vi
children.text: not be the holder of a current visitor visa granted under Guardians accompanying students to New Zealand instructions (see V3.100); and

children.label: vii
children.text: hold insurance (see U3.45), unless they are a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) student or a student holding a New Zealand scholarship administered through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: All applicants must meet the requirements under Generic Temporary Entry Class instructions for:

children.label: i
children.text: lodging an application for a temporary entry class visa as set out at E4; and

children.label: ii
children.text: bona fide applicants as set out at E5; and

children.label: iii
children.text: health and character as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: To determine whether an applicant is likely to breach the condition of a student visa (see E5.1.b(ii)) that the holder must make satisfactory progress in their proposed programme of study, an immigration officer may:

children.label: i
children.text: consider whether the applicant has English language ability consistent with the level and nature of that study; and

children.label: ii
children.text: request the applicant provide evidence of their English language ability as part of this assessment.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Applicants who have not completed, or will not be completing the programme of study endorsed on their student visa and who wish to change their programme of study and/or education provider must:

children.label: i
children.text: meet requirements (a) and (b) above; and

children.label: ii
children.text: meet the requirements set out at U3.40.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Applicants who are progressing to further study, for example a student in Year 13 who is progressing to tertiary studies, will not need to meet U3.40.

pages.title: Dependent children of work visa holders
pages.page_title: U8.20 Dependent children of work visa holders (20/10/2026)

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders who wish to study in New Zealand may be granted student visas unless the work visa holder has been granted a work visa under any one of the following categories:

children.label: i
children.text: Foreign crew of fishing vessels (see WJ); or

children.label: ii
children.text: Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) Work instructions (see WH1); or

children.label: iii
children.text: Supplementary Seasonal Employment (SSE) instructions (see WH3); or

children.label: iv
children.text: Skilled Migrant Category Job Search Instructions (see WR5); or

children.label: v
children.text: Working Holiday Scheme instructions (see WI2); or

children.label: vi
children.text: domestic staff of diplomatic, consular or official staff (see WI4); or

children.label: vii
children.text: seasonal workers under Specific Purpose Instructions; or

children.label: viii
children.text: seasonal workers under seasonal AEWV pathways (see WA1.10(a)(ii)); or

children.label: ix
children.text: India Iconic Work Instructions (see WI21); or

children.label: x
children.text: India Skilled Work Instructions (see WI22); or

children.label: xi
children.text: Independent Professional, or Contractual Service Supplier under Specific Purpose instructions (see WS).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, the eligibility of dependent children of Accredited Employer work visa holders and Specific Purpose work visa holders under the NOL subcategory (see WS2.1.1(o) – instructions effective 8 September 2025) for student visas is set out at U8.20.2 below.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of work visa holders as defined in (a) above are regarded as domestic students (see U3.35) for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools for the period of the parent's work visa.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1) of work visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for dependent children may be waived provided this is covered by the income of the work visa holder parent or by evidence of funds or guarantees submitted with the work visa application of the parent (see W2.15).

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Dependent children of people granted work to residence visas must meet health and character requirements for residence class visa applications as set out at A4 and A5.

blocks.label: g
blocks.text: Despite (a) above, a dependent child of the holder of a Migrant Exploitation Protection work visa (MEPV) may be granted a student visa under these instructions only if, as at the time they apply, the dependent child is in New Zealand on a visa that was granted on the basis of the visa held by the MEPV holder immediately prior to the MEPV holder’s current visa. If granted, the visa’s duration must be for the same period as the MEPV holder’s visa, and will not include multiple entry travel conditions.

units.heading: Dependent children of Accredited Employer work visa holders and certain Specific Purpose work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of an Accredited Employer work visa holder or a Specific Purpose work visa holder under the NOL subcategory (see WS2.1.1(o) – instructions effective 8 September 2025) may be granted a student visa if their supporting parent is:

children.label: i
children.text: in a role classified as ANZSCO skill level 1, 2 or 3 (including roles treated at a higher skill level under WA3.16(d) at the Job Check); or

children.label: ii
children.text: in a role classified as NOL skill level 1, 2 or 3 and listed at Appendix 20; or

children.label: iii
children.text: paid at or above 1.5x the Skilled Migrant Category median wage (see SR3.20(a)(ii)); or

children.label: iv
children.text: in a role on the Green List and meets the applicable requirements (see Appendix 13); or

children.label: v
children.text: in acceptable employment under the Transport Sector or Care Sector Work to Residence policies as defined in SR6.10 or SR7.10 with the exception of the requirement to have completed 24 months of work in New Zealand in that occupation.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite the requirement to determine applications for temporary entry in accordance with the instructions in effect at the time an application is made (E7.10(a)(ii)), the exception set out at (a)(v) above applies to any application that was submitted before 6 October 2024 and as of that date had not been decided.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children of an Accredited Employer work visa holder working in a role at ANZSCO skill level 4 or 5 cannot be granted a student visa as a dependent child, unless:

children.label: i
children.text: on 26 June 2024, they held a visa as a dependent child of the Accredited Employer work visa holder; or

children.label: ii
children.text: on 26 June 2024, they had an application in progress for a visa as a dependent child of the Accredited Employer work visa holder and that application was subsequently granted; or

children.label: iii
children.text: their Accredited Employer work visa holder parent is described in (a)(iii) to (v) above.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: An Accredited Employer work visa holder or a Specific Purpose work visa holder under the NOL subcategory (see WS2.1.1(o) – instructions effective 8 September 2025) whose dependent child is applying for a student visa under these instructions must meet the minimum income threshold specified in U8.20.6 below.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Despite (d) above, the minimum income threshold does not apply if the supporting work visa holder(s) currently meet the previous income threshold in place on 9 March 2025 (as per U8.20(a)), and on 9 March 2025:

children.label: i
children.text: the dependent child held a visa as a dependent child of the AEWV holder, or had applied for a visa as a dependent of the AEWV holder on or before 9 March 2025 and that application has not been completed; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the dependent child’s parent(s) held an AEWV or Essential Skills work visa, or had applied for an Accredited Employer work visa on or before 9 March 2025 that was subsequently granted; and

children.label: iii
children.text: the maximum continuous stay period that applied to their parent on 9 March 2025 has not yet been reached.

units.heading: Dependent children of Essential Skill work visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children (see E4.1.10) of holders of work visas granted under the Essential Skills work instructions (WK) after 30 November 2009 will only be granted a student visa if their parent(s) meet a minimum income threshold (see U8.20.6 below).

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Despite U8.20.6(a), dependent children of Essential Skills work visa holders whose parents have an application being considered under the Samoan Quota or Pacific Access Category must meet the minimum income requirements of those instructions (see S1.10.35 or S1.40.35) to be eligible for a student visa under these instructions.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Dependent children are not required to be assessed against the Essential Skills minimum income threshold if their parent(s):

children.label: i
children.text: have held any temporary work visa before 30 November 2009; and

children.label: ii
children.text: have remained on a valid visa from 30 November 2009 until the date of the dependent child's application under U8.20.

units.heading: Minimum income threshold

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold is NZ$58,240 gross per annum.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: The minimum income threshold must be met and maintained wholly by the salary or wages of the parent or parents holding an Accredited Employer work visa, Specific Purpose work visa holder under the NOL subcategory (see WS2.1.1(o) – instructions effective 8 September 2025) or an Essential Skills work visa.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Evidence must be provided of the supporting work visa holder’s current salary or wages to satisfy an immigration officer that the applicant’s parent(s) meet the minimum income threshold.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: If a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parent(s) may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: If the parent(s) do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their or their dependent child’s visa both the parent(s) and child may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Where both parents hold Accredited Employer work visas, or Specific Purpose work visas under the NOL subcategory (see WS2.1.1(o) – instructions effective 8 September 2025) or Essential Skills work visas, their income may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

units.heading: Dependent children of work visa holders under Religious Worker instructions

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of a holder of a work visa under Religious Worker instructions (WM) will only be granted a student visa if the:

children.label: i
children.text: minimum income threshold is met by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; or

children.label: ii
children.text: religious organisation sponsoring the principal applicant agrees to sponsor the dependent children.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: Under (a)(i) above:

children.label: i
children.text: the minimum income threshold is NZ$58,240 gross per annum; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the minimum income threshold must be met and maintained by the salary, wages or a stipend received by the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iii
children.text: evidence must be provided of the current salary, wages or stipend of the Religious Worker visa holder and their partner; and

children.label: iv
children.text: if a visa application is declined under these instructions and the dependent child becomes unlawful the parents may become liable for deportation; and

children.label: v
children.text: if the parents do not maintain the minimum income threshold for the duration of their visa or their dependent child's visa, both the child and the parents may become liable for deportation.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: Despite (a)(i) above, the minimum income threshold does not apply if the parent(s) currently meet the previous income threshold in place on 9 March 2025 (as per U8.20.6 (a)), and on 9 March 2025:

children.label: i
children.text: the dependent child held a visa as a dependent child of the Religious work visa holder, or had applied on or before that date for a visa as a dependent of the Religious work visa holder and that application has not been completed; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the dependent child’s parent(s) held a Religious Work visa, or had applied on or before that date for a Religious Work visa that was subsequently granted.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: The income of both parents may be combined to meet the minimum income threshold.

pages.title: Dependent children of New Zealand citizens or residence class visa holders
pages.page_title: U8.30 Dependent children of New Zealand citizens or residence class visa holders

units.heading: Dependent children of New Zealand citizens or residence class visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Dependent children of New Zealand citizens or residence class visa holders may be granted a student visa, provided that:

children.label: i
children.text: the parent intends to stay in New Zealand during the same period of time applied for by the dependent child; and

children.label: ii
children.text: the parent supports the application; and

children.label: iii
children.text: either the child’s application for a residence class visa is being considered by INZ or the child’s application for citizenship is being considered by the Department of Internal Affairs, and

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: A visa under these instructions can be granted for a duration of 12 months:

children.label: i
children.text: from the date of arrival, if the applicant is outside New Zealand, or

children.label: ii
children.text: from the date the visa is granted, if the applicant is in New Zealand.

blocks.label: c
blocks.text: If the applicant requires longer to obtain the outcome of their residence or citizenship application, immigration officers may consider granting a further visa for sufficient duration to allow their citizenship or residence application to be completed, as long as the requirements of paragraph (a) above continue to be met.

blocks.label: d
blocks.text: Despite U8.30(a), where the applicant is subject to an overseas adoption order described in section 17(1) and 17(2) of the Adoption Act 1955, a visa cannot, as a result of the adoption, be granted under these instructions unless the adoption is from an ‘exempt country’ (see section 17(3)(b) and (4) of the Adoption Act 1955).

blocks.label: e
blocks.text: Dependent children of New Zealand citizens or residence class visa holders may be granted student visas without the need to produce evidence of enrolment.

blocks.label: f
blocks.text: Guarantees of accommodation and/or maintenance for these dependent children are not required as they are supported by a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Notes: - For the purposes of (d), an ‘exempt country’ is one that is listed at Schedule 1AAB of the Adoption Act 1955. - Where (d) applies, there is no discretion available, either under the Adoption Act 1955, the Immigration Act 2009, or through an ‘exception to instructions’, to grant a visa under U8.30, though an immigration officer may consider granting a visa under other categories of temporary entry instructions.

units.heading: Evidence for dependent children of New Zealand citizens or residence class visa holders

blocks.label: a
blocks.text: Immigration officers must sight evidence of the following:

children.label: i
children.text: the New Zealand citizenship or New Zealand residence status of the applicant's parent; and

children.label: ii
children.text: documents that confirm the applicant's relationship with the parent (see E4.5.10); and

children.label: iii
children.text: that the applicant and parent are intending to stay in New Zealand during the same period of time; and

children.label: iv
children.text: that the New Zealand parent supports the application; and

children.label: v
children.text: the child has applied for a residence class visa or citizenship.

blocks.label: b
blocks.text: If the evidence required by (a) above has been previously provided to INZ as part of a residence class visa application from or including the child, an immigration officer can use that evidence to be satisfied the requirements to grant a student visa are met.

blocks.label: note1
blocks.text: Note: Dependent children holding a visa granted under this category may be able to be considered domestic for the purpose of all tuition fees at primary and secondary schools. See section 10(1) of the Education and Training Act 2020 and the associated notice administered by the Ministry of Education for complete information on domestic students.
